a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Leading Shipowners (company notes)
n: Nippon Yusen Kaisha (Japan Mail S.S. Co.)
t: Founded in October, 1885, the Nippon Yusen Kaisha, which is the premier maritime company of Japan, celebrated the jubilee in October, 1935. The company was established by the amalgamation of two rival concerns, the Mitsubishi and the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha, which were in cut-throat competition with each other. By the amalgamation of the two companies the N. Y. K. inherited 29 steamers and 1 sailing vessels from the Mitsubishi Company and 29 steamers and 10 sailing craft from the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha, making a total of 69 vessels. Of these the 58 steamers totalled 64,610 tons gross and the 11 sailing vessels 4,725 tons gross. Between Japan and New York the Company maintains what is one of the most up-to-date freight services on the oceans to-day. The company put into commission in the Jubilee Year six new motor vessels on its Orient-New York Express Service. These six sister ships are all of 9,000 tons and their speed 18½ knots. Three of them were built in Nagasaki and three in Yokohama. The company owns several motorships on its Pacific run. These are the Chichibu maru (17,500 tons), the Asama Maru (17,000 tons) and the Tatsuta Maru (17,000 tons). These, along with the Taiyo Maru, run a fast fortnightly service from Hong-Kong to Los Angeles and San Francisco, via Honolulu. On the European run the company has also excellent boats, the Terukuni Maru and the Yasukuni Maru being the finest ships on the service. They are both of 11,900 tons gross. As on March 31, 1937 the company owned 87 steamers, totalling 635,280 tons gross . The following is a list of the important N.Y.K. passenger and freight services:— Japan-European Fortnightly Service; Orient-California Fortnightly Service; Japan-Australia Monthly Service; South American West Coast Monthly Service; Japan-Bombay Monthly Service; Japan-China Rapid Express Service. Besides the above the company maintains regular passenger services from Japan to Tsingtao, the South Sea Islands, Tientsin, Formosa, etc., the last two being operated by the N. Y. K. Line. The authorized capital of the company is ¥106,250,000, ¥78,250,000 paid up.

a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Leading Shipowners (company notes)
n: Osaka Shosen Kaisha (Osaka Mercantile S.S. Co.)
t: The Company was established in 1884 by the amalgamation of small shipping companies which had steamers plying between ports in the inland sea. The field of operation has subsequently been enlarged. The following is a list of the important O. S. K. passenger and freight services in operation in the first half of 1937:— South American Monthly Service; New York Rapid Express Monthly Service; East Coast African Monthly Service; Bombay Twice Monthly Service; Calcutta Twice Monthly Service; Australia Monthly Service; South Seas Service (South Seas Subsidized Service, South Seas Voluntary Service, Philippine Service, Saigon-Bangkok Service). The Company also maintains a regular passenger service from Japan to important places in Formosa, China, Korea, Dairen, etc. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 107 steamers aggregating 502,992 tons gross. The authorized capital of the Company is ¥100,000,000, of which ¥62,500,000 is paid up.

a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Principal Tramp-Owners
t: In order to meet an astounding increase in the demand for bottoms during the World War both shipowners and shipyards built one ship after another. Shipyards even went the length of building ships without any order. As the activity of the freight market during the war was spectacular, so the reaction that followed the Armistice was serious. It was for the purpose of relieving the shipowners and shipbuilders of the acute pain caused by a serious break of the price of ships that the Kokusai Kisen Kaisha was organized in 1919 with the surplus of the vessels thus built during the war, through the good offices of the Government. As in July, 1937 the Company operated regular freight services between the Far East and North Europe, New York and Hamburg, Japan and Australia, Japan and East and South Africa, Japan and Bombay, Japan and Formosa. Three 19-knotters which were completed in 1936 have been allocated to the newly inaugurated Far East-North Europe fast service, which maintains four-weekly sailing in conjunction with two new freighters of the N. Y. K. Furthermore, five motor and turbine super-freighters of about 9,200 tons deadweight each are now on order with the shipbuilders in Japan and will all be completed before the end of 1938. The Company owns motor and steam vessels amounting to 300,000 tons gross. Mr. Shinjiro Kurokawa, formerly vice-President of the N. Y. K. is President. The Company is capitalized at ¥80,000,000 and under its able president cleared net profits of over ¥4,160,000 for the year ending December 31, 1936.

a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Principal Tramp-Owners
t: The Company was founded in 1902 by Mr. Kamesaburo Yamashita. The activity of the Company during the World War was worldwide. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 14 ships amounting to 82,400 tons gross. The Yamashita Kisen is the largest of the five major companies operating trampers, the other four being Daido, Mitsui, Kawasaki, Kokusai. In May, 1937 the Company increased its capital from ¥20,320,500 to ¥35,000,000. The Company's shipping operation extends to South Seas, Australia, Europe, North America and Africa. One of its noteworthy service is the transportation of Saghalien timber to Japan and Manchuria beans to Europe.

a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Principal Tramp-Owners
t: The Mitsui Line operates regular and irregular services. The former consists of the direct New York service, the Bangkok service, the Indian service (Bombay and Madras), the Philippine service, Dairen service, the Iran Bay service and the Moji-Yokohama service. The latter represents many ports in Europe, North America, South America, Australia, Africa, British India, the South Seas and Japan. As on March 31, 1937 the Mitsui Line owned 35 steamers amounting to 149,690 tons gross.

a: Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Principal Tramp-Owners
t: The Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha is one of the seven largest shipping companies of Japan. It was founded in April, 1919 with a capital of ¥20,000,000, which is paid up. Principal regular services operated by the Company are the New York Line, San Francisco-Los Angeles Line, Seatle-Vancouver Line, Japan-Australia Line, Europe-Far East Line, Tokyo-Yokohama-Dairen Line, North Korea Line, South America (West Coast) Line, East and South Africa Line, Bombay Line, Asia-Europe-North and South America Line. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 15 ships aggregating 63,351 tons gross.

(Head Office—Hongoku-cho, Nihonbashi, Tokyo). Established 1882. Authorized capital is ¥60,000,000, of which ¥45,000,000 is paid up. Deposits ¥386,748,119.040, of which the Government's are ¥293,178,726.229 including Current Account for ¥162,421,679.281. Advances ¥791,014,808.010 (inclusive of bills discounted), of which ¥232,600,434.380 is to the Government, Reserve fund ¥115,690,000.000, Divid., 10% p.a., Note issue ¥1,640,832,571.500. The Bank of Japan may issue bank notes to any extent against specie reserve of gold and silver; provided that the value of silver shall not exceed one-fourth of the total. The Bank is also authorise dto make fiduciary issue against Government bonds or other specified securities up to ¥1,000,000,000. An additional fiduciary issue over and above this limit may be made; provided, however, that in case such an excess issue is to continue beyond 15 days the Bank shall obtain the approval of the Minister of Finance therefor, and that it shall pay a tax on the same as from the 16th day at a rate not less than [illegible]% p.a. The denominations of convertible notes are ¥1, ¥5, ¥10, ¥20, ¥50, ¥100 and ¥200, but in practice ¥50 and ¥200 have not been issued yet.

(Hypothec Bank of Japan) (Head Office—Marunouchi, Kojimachi, Tokyo). Established 1897. Authorized capital ¥140,920,000.00, ¥116,796,062.50 is paid up. Reserves ¥137,510,997.94, Deposits ¥272,703,658.21, Advances ¥1,309,495,243.73, Issue of Hypothec and other debentures ¥1,054,661,563.00, Divd., 10% p.a. The Nippon Kwangyo Ginko was originally intended to raise funds by issuing debentures and advance them to agriculturalists and industrialists on the security of real estate for a long time at a low rate of interest. The scope of business of the Bank has since been greatly enlarged. The Bank is authorised to issue hypothec debentures with premiums to the amount fifteen times the paid-up capital.

The first agricultural and industrial bank was opened in Shizuoka in the same year as the Hypothec Bank of Japan, or 1897. Its original purpose was also the same as that of the Hypothec Bank, the former serving as a local organ and the latter as a central organ. There were established altogether 46 of these bank, one in each fu and ken, with the single exception of the Hokkaido, the Awa Agricultural and Industrial Bank established in August, 1900 being the last. As in the case of the Hypothec Bank of Japan the scope of business of the agricultural and industrial banks has since been much enlarged. In 1921 a law providing for the amalgamation of agricultural and industrial banks with the Hypothec Bank of Japan was promulgated. Since then twenty-seven agricultural and industrial banks have been merged in the Hypothec Bank of Japan. As at the end of 1935 there were 17 of these banks, their branch offices numbering 63. Their combined capital was ¥84,500,000.00, of which ¥77,750,000.00 was paid up, Reserves ¥70,821,000.00, approximately, Deposits ¥167,834,000.00, Advances ¥580,341,000.00, Bills discounted ¥8,131,000.00, Issue of agricultural and industrial debentures ¥429,543,000.00, Divd., ¥8,581,000.00.

(Head Office—Sapporo, Hokkaido). Established 1899. Authorised capital ¥20,000,000.00, ¥12,500,000.00 paid-up. Reserves ¥15,604,900.00, Deposits ¥108,993,967.327, Advances ¥141,886,882.90, Debenture issue ¥121,715,530.000, Divd., 7% p.a. It was for the purpose of financing colonial industries in the Hokkaido and Karafuto that the Bank was established towards the end of 1899. It is not much different from the Hypothec Bank of Japan and the agricultural and industrial banks in that the Bank makes loans on the security of real estate. What the Bank differs from those banks is that besides making loans on shares and debentures issued by the companies intended to promote the colonal interests of the Hokkaido and Karafuto and taking up the issue of debentures, it makes advances on the security of bills of exchange and documentary drafts and local products. The Bank is authorised to issue Hokkaido Colonial debentures to the amount not more than fifteen times the paid-up capital.

(Head Office—Marunouchi, Kojimachi, Tokyo). Established 1900. Authorised capital ¥50,000,000.00, paid-up. The Industrial Bank of Japan was established in 1900 in accordance with the provisions of the Industrial Bank Act promulgated in March of that year and opened in April, 1902, its object being to finance various industries, railways and harbour construction by advancing loans on securities such as shares, debentures, etc. The scope of business of the Bank has since also been much extended. The Bank is authorised to issue Industrial debentures to the amount of not more than ten times the paid-up capital.

The Bank was established for the purpose of opening up the resources of Taiwan by financing commerce and industry and public enterprises as a central organ for monetary circulation in the island and also extending the scope of its business to South China and the South Seas, thereby serving as an organ of trade between the island and those countries. The Bank has extended the scope of its business not only to South China and the South Seas but also to Europe and America. It is authorised to issue bank notes.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Government also commissioned the Oriental Development Company which entered the field of Manchuria to undertake the task of providing funds required for real estate deals. As a result, the Yokohame Specie Bank was obliged to return to its original field of an exchange bank. Thus, the Yokohama Specie Bank, the Bank of Chosen and the Oriental Development Company have become the three main Japanese banking organizations in Manchuria in their respective fields of activity.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Bank of China was established in 1911 with a capital of 25,000,000 yuan, of which 24,712,200 yuan is paid up. It is the first class bank in China. The Head Office is in Shanghai. Originally it was known as the Huipu Bank Bank which was established in 1908 with a capital of Tls. 10,000,000. Later it was renamed as the Taching Bank. It was after China became a republic and the bank was again renamed the Bank of China that it extended its activity to Manchuria. Its first branch was established in Changchun in 1913. In 1927 it was removed to Harbin in order to meet the growing economic activity in that place.. Prior to this, or in 1919 a branch office was opened in Mukden. Thus, the Bank of China exerted influence over both North and South Manchuria. The situation has changed since the foundation of Manchoukuo. In 1935 in Hsinking there was established the Manchou Headquarters of the Central Bank of China. Although the Bank has many branches and sub-branches with Mukden and Harbin as the centre, it wields no such influence as it once enjoyed together with the former government banks and the frontier banks. Since the independence of Manchoukuo, the Bank has lost the privilege of dealing with public money and of issuing notes, and with the growing credit of the Central Bank of Manchou, it has gradually lost its hold on the exchange business.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Bank of Communications was founded in 1907 as a direct organ of the quondam Post and Telegraph Department of China with the object of promoting the railway, steamship, postal and telegraph services. The authorized capital is 10,000,000 yuan, of which 8,715,600 yuan was paid up. It is one of the two largest special banks of China, the other being the Bank of China. The Bank extended its activity to Manchuria in June, 1908 when it established a branch office at Yingkow. Later branches were opened in Changchun and Mukden. After the inauguration of the Republican regime other branches were set up in Harbin, Kirin and Heilungkiang. At present the branch office is in Hsinking and sub-branches are in Harbin, Kirin, Tsitsihar, Mukden and Yingkow. Harbin and Mukden are still the centre of the activity of the Bank.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Chingcheng Bank was established in May, 1917 with a capital of 10,000,000 yuan, of which 7,000,000 yuan is paid-up. The Head Office is in Shanghai. The Harbin branch was set up in May, 1931. There is also a branch in Dairen.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Tachung Bank was brought into being in March, 1929 with a capital of 4,000,000 yuan, of which 2,600,000 yuan is paid-up. Its Manchu branch is at Harbin.

a: Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks
t: The Bank is capitalized at 3,000,000 yuan and has its Head Office at Tientsin and a branch at Dairen.

The Huifeng Bank, which is an English bank commonly known as the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation, was established in Honkong in 1865 with a capital of 50,000,000 Chinese dollars, of which 20,000,000 dollars is paid up. It shows great activity as an issuing and exchange bank, in South and Central China with Honkong as the centre. With the declining of the activity of Russian banks in North Manchuria, the Bank extended its activity to Harbin. It has branches in Harbin, Mukden and Dairen. It is engaged chiefly in financing industries and the import trade in miscellaneous goods.

The Huachi Bank, an American bank, was established in 1901. In 1926 it was merged in the National City Bank of New York (established in 1812). It is capitalized at $127,500,000 and has reserves for $130,000,000, approximattely. It has branches in Harbin and Dairen. The Bank's advances in Manchoukuo have so far been limited to leading American and European business men and a portion of Manchou capitalists.

The Maichiali Bank is an English bank. It is widely known as the Chartered Bank and has its head office at London. It is capitalized at £3,000,000. It was in 1928 that the Bank extended its activity to Manchuria. It has a branch office at Harbin.

The Bank known at the Banque Franco-Asiatique was established in 1829 in Paris. The authorized capital is 25,000,000 francs. It is surmised that 6,900,000 francs is paid up. It has branch offices at Harbin and Mukden.

Naval Acad. 1888; Staff 1st Sqn.; Captain, Iwate; Chief Staff 2nd Sqn.; Pres. Nav. Gunnery Sch.; Comdr-in-Chief 3rd Sqn.; Chief Nav. Training Dept.; Privy Councillor 1931. Address: 18 Oyama-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Minister of Agr. & Forestry; Mem. House of Peers; b. Dec. 1884. Tokyo; s. of late Raiman Arima. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Prof. of same; M.P. 1924; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & For. 1932-33. Address: 71 Sekine-cho, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Ordnance Vice-Admiral (reserve); Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Tekioku Oxygen Co.; b. 1868, Tokyo; s. of Senkichi Arisaka, architect. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; stayed in France for study of ordnance mfg. for 3 years; on return home, Staff, Tokyo Nav. Arsenal; Chief Arms Mfg. Dept.; Chief Ordnance Dept. Kure Navy Arsenal; served Sino-Japanese, Russo-Japanese and World Wars; visited Europe & Amer. 4 times. Address: 84 Sangenjaya, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Eye-specialist; former Prof. Eye Dept. Osaka Medical Coll.; Pres. Eye-specialists Soc., Osaka; b. Mar. 1881. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Asst. Doctor, Eye-Clinic, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; for 6 yrs. Asst. to late Prof. Axenfeld, Eye-Clinic, Freiburg Univ. Germany; founded Arisawa Eye-Hospital 1914. Address: Kitahama 2-chome, Osaka.

Pres. Meiji Shoten, Meiji Confectoinery Co., Meiji Milk Mfg. Co.; Vice-Pres. Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co., Showa Rubber Co.; Mng.-Dir. Sumatra Kogyo Co.; b. Aug. 1868, Kagoshima; s. of late Ken-ichiro Arishima, M.D.; m. Hayako. Career: started life as Govt. official; apptd. Custom Commr. Taiwan Govt.-Gen.; resigned 1908; joined Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co .and several other firms. Address: 46 Chiyoda-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

b. September 1884, Niigata-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; attended Paris Peace Conf. and Wash. Disarm. Conf.; Dir. Asia Bureau Foreign Office; Minister to Austria; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1932-33; Amb. to Belgium 1934-36; to China, 1936; Foreign Min. 1936-37. Address: 426 Shimo-Ochiai 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. May 1873, Kyoto-fu; s. of late Sanshichi Ariyoshi, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; Councillor Shimane-ken, Hyogo-ken; Home Dept.; sent to Europe 1907; Gov. Chiba-ken 1908; Supt. Gen. Affairs Board, Chosen 1910; Gov. Miyazaki-ken, Kanagawa-ken, Hyogo-ken; Chief, Adm. Board. Chosen; Mayor of Yokohama 1925. Address: 1050 Oyama, Yoyogi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Cons.-Gen. for Colombia; n. Colombian. Address: 32 Bluff, Yokohama.

Pres. Chosen Shokusan Ginko since 1919; Mem. House of Peers; b. May 1878, Nagano-ken; s. of Mitsuhiko Aruga. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogakuin (Law Coll.) 1894; Fin. Inspector, Govt.-Gen. of Chosen; Secr. of same; Chief, Home Affairs Dept. of same; Dir. of present bank 1918. Address: 49 Shokendo-machi, Keijo.

Co. Dir.; b. June 1877, Oita-ken; s. of Eiji Asabuki. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1896; studied economics at London Univ.; joined Bank of Japan 1898; later joined Mitsui Firm 1906; resigned 1908; founded Chiyoda-gumi Ltd. Address: 57 Shimotakanawa, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Vice-Dir. and Chief Absterics & Gynaecology Dept. Ehime Branch Hospital of Japan Red Cross Soc.; b. Nov. 1888, Kagawa-ken; s. of Yutaka Asada, doctor; m. Yoshie. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; with present hospital since 1920. Address: 105 Kiyomachi, Matsuyama.

Vice-Consul at Calcutta; b. July 1896. Ibaragi-ken; s. of Akizu Asahi, poet. Career: joined consular service in 1928 and served at Bombay, San Francisco, Shanghai and London. Address: c/o Japanese Consulate, Calcutta, India.

Dr. of Pharm.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1918; Mem. Imp. Acad. since 1930; b. 1881, Tokyo; s. of Washio Asahina; m. Koto. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; Asst. Prof. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912. Address: 123 Totsuka-machi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Average Adjuster; b. Oct. 1875, Nagoya; s. of Yoshiaru Asai, Govt. official. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; apptd. Mgr. at Chemulpo, Hongkong and Bombay Branches, O.S.K. 1902-16; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Marine & Fire Ins. Co. 1916-24; same, Settsu Marine Ins. Co. 1919-24; established in 1925 jointly with Mr. Ichikawa, Average Adjusting Office in Kobe; Hon. Consul for Uruguay till Mar. 1937. Address: 156 Saishoyama-cho, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir. Ishikawajima Shipbldg. & Engrg. Co. since 1933; b. Nov. 1883, Nagano-ken; s. of Tamanosuke Asakawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; joined Dai-Ichi Ginko; Mgr. Keijo Branch, same. Club: Industry Club of Japan. Address: 108 Kobinata-Suido-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Sculptor; Prof. Tokyo Sch. of Fine Arts; b. May 1883, Oita-ken; s. of Yozo Watanabe; later adopted by Tanehiko Asakura. Career: grad. Sculpture Dept. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1912; went to Borneo Islands 1911. Address: 20 Tennoji-machi, Yanaka, Shitaya-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1932; b. Mar. 1894, Gifu-ken. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; rec'd deg. 1923; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923. Address: 906 Shakujii Tateno-machi, Itabashi-ku, Tokyo.

Co. Dir.; b. Aug. 1891, Tokyo; s. of late Soichiro Asano, businessman. Career grad. Econ. Dept. of Keio Univ.; joined Asano Shipbuilding Co. 1917; Dir. of same 1919; went abroad to inspect shipbldg. ind. 1923; Mng.-Dir. Kanto Hydro-Elec. Power Co. 1925; again visited Amer. 1926-27; completed Saku Hydro-Elec. Power Station 1928. Address: 1 Nagasaka-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Permanent Mem. Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Wholesale Dealer in Dry Goods and Cotton Cloth; b. Feb. 1883, Nagoya; s. of late Jinshichi Asano. Career: served in Russo-Japanese War; Pres. Ishihara Dyeing Ind. Co.; Aud. Taisho Ind. Co.; Momijiya Ltd. Address: 11 Teppo-cho 2-chome, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

Dr. of Pharm.; Dir. Kanazawa Pharm. Coll. since 1931; b. Sept. 1894, Chiba-ken. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Prof. Kanazawa Pharm. Coll. 1925; rec'd deg. 1926; sent to Germany for study 1927-29. Address: 3 Yamazaki-cho, Kanazawa.

Pres. Tsurumi Seitetsu Zosen Kaisha; Advisor Toyo Kisen Kaisha, Toyo Marine Transportation Co., Toyo Shoji Kaisha, Toyo Security Company, Daido Cement Company, Asano Stone Industry Company; Vice-President of Tsurumi Harbor Railway Company; Mng.-Dir. Nippon Cement Co. Ltd.; Dir. Asano Portland Cement Co., Kanto Transportation Co., Kanto Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Keihin Canal Co., Fuji Ind. Co., Asano Kokura Steel Works. Iwaki Colliery, Taiwan Real Estate & Bldg. Co., Asano Bussan Co., Chiyoda Oil Co.; b. Aug. 1889, Tokyo; s. of late Soichiro Asano, one of financial magnates in Japan. Career: completed Kaisei Middle School, Tokyo 1907; grad. Harvard Univ. 1912; attended Int'l Labour Conf. as Capitalist Delegate 1934; visited Siam as Vice-Chairman Japanese Econ. Mission to Siam 1936. Address: 10 Mita Tsuna-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.
Businessman; b. July 1884 s. of late Soichiro Asano. Career: grad. Waseda Univ.; often visited Europe & Amer.; succeeded to his father's estate 1930. Address: 16 Tamachi 5-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; M.P.; Pres. & Editor The Japan Times; Prof. Keio Univ.; Mem. Committee of Tourist Industry; Mem. Foreign Trade Council; b. 1887, Kyoto-fu. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; entered diplomatic service; attended 1st and 2nd League of Nations Assemblies at Geneva 1920 and '21; apptd. Delegate at Information Bureau, Foreign Office 192[?]; 1st Sec. Emb. Constantinople 1925; Councillor of same Emb. 1929; transferred to Belgium 1930; retired 1932; returned to Diet; joined Japan Times Jan. 1933. Address: 28 Naka-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; Chief Secr. Shakai Taishuto Party since 1932; b. May 1891, Oita-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; joined Editorial Staff, Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun; became Dir. Federation of Japan Miners' Assns. which he organized; Central Executive Committee, Nippon Rodo Nominto 1926; Pres. Nippon Taishuto 1930; Chief Secr. Zenkoku Rono Taishuto. Address: 224 Komagome Hayashi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Former Pres. Japan Women's Coll.; b. Jan. 1864, Oita-ken. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ. 1887; studied Phil. at Tokyo Imp. Univ.; taught at Niigata Girls' School, Baika Girls' School, Doshisha Futsu Gakko, etc.; founded Japan Women's Coll. 1894; went to Europe & Amer. to study women's education; was long connected with Imp. Educ. Assn., Secondary Educ., League of Nations Assn., Int'l Educ. Assn., Romaji Promotion Soc. etc. Address: 225 Nishiochiai, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Ataka Shokai; Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Adviser Trade Bureau, Dept. of Com. & Ind since Jan. 1936; b. Apr. 1873, Ishikawa-ken; bro. of Matakichi Ataka. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1895; established present firm 1904; Vice-Pres. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: Miyamorido, Sumiyoshi-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Dir. & Prof. 2nd Higher Sch.; b. Aug. 1878, Miyagi-ken; s. of Gicho Adachi, village headman; m. Tama Shiikawa. Career: grad. Lit. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; with present sch. since 1910. Address: 3 of 12 Geki-cho, Sendai.

D.E.; Pres. Kogyo Kagaku-kai; Prof. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; b. Mar. 1887, Tokyo; s. of Totsuheiji Atsuki. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; rec'd deg. 1919. Address: 21 Maruyama-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Cons. for Argentine at Tokyo; Pres. Kaigai Kogyo K.K.; Dir. Osaka Shosen Kaisha; b. Feb. 1881, Kobe. s. of Toru Atsumi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1902; joined O. S. K. and served at its Kobe, Moji branches; Shanghai, Bombay, Yokohama and Tokyo went to Brazil as Mem. Japanese Economic Mission to Brazil 1935 Address: 80 Shin-machi 1-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.
Hon. Vice-Consul for Narway at Kobe and Osaka since 1937; n. Norwegian; b. Apr. 1902, Oslo. Office Address: 45 Hirano-machi, Kobe.

Diplomatist; Italian Amb. to Tokyo since 1933; b. June 1883, Rome; s. of Francesco Auriti, magistrate. Career: grad. Rome Univ.; entered diplomatic service,; sent to Berne, Madrid, Bukharest and Vienna; Minister to Austria. Address: Italian Emb. Tokyo.

B.A.; D.D.; Religious and Social Welfare Worker; b. Aug. 1873, Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.A.; s. of N. E. Axling, pastor; m. Lucinda W. Burrows. Career: founder of Tokyo Misaki Kaikan, religious, educ. & social welfare institution; one of organizers of Nat. Christian Council in Japan and Secr. of it since its organization; traveled widely in America before Washington Conf. on disarm. also at time of Exclusion Emigration Bill agitation and of Manchurian Incident speaking at interpreter of Japan. Author of "Japan on the Upward Trail" and "Kagawa". Address: 5 of 2 Shirakawa-cho, Fukagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Nihon Univ.; Lecturer Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1928; b. Jan. 1886, Nara-ken; s. of Takeshi Azuma, M.P. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Asst. of same 1917; Prof. Military Intendants' Sch. 1917; Prof. Law & Lit. Coll. Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1924. Address: 28 Shiroyama-cho, Nakano-ku Tokyo.

M.P.; Leader, Seiyukai; b. Apr. 1869, Nara-ken; s. of Yoshitsugu Azuma. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogakuin (Law Coll.), 1890; migrated into Hokkaido with his fellow villagers to engage in colonization work; founded Hokkai Jiji and Hokkai Times; elected Rep. 10 times; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry in Tanaka Cabinet 1927. Address: 273 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Home Minister; b. Oct. 1877, Tokyo; s. of Tokimitsu Yamamoto; later adopted by late Kane Baba. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Secr. Revenue Supt. Bureau; Customs Inspector; Councillor Legislation Breau; Judge Court of Adm. Litigation; Dir. Legislation Bureau; nominated Peer; Pres. Nippon Kogyo Ginko; Finance Minister in Hirota Cabinet 1936-37. Address: 23 Nihonenoki 2-chome, Shiba-ku Tokyo.

Writer; b. Nov. 1869, Kochi-ken; s. of Raihachi Baba. Career: grad. Meiji Gakuin 1893; Teacher, Hikone Middle Sch. and Urawa Middle Sch.; Lecturer Keio Univ.; introduced European Literatures into Japan. Address: 2 Mita Toyooka-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Author; Political Critic; Adviser Shakai Taishuto; b. July 1875, Okayama-ken; s. of Kamesaburo Baba. Career: studied at 2nd Higher Sch.; Doshisha Univ.; Polit. Dept. Waseda Univ.; Editorial Staff Japan Times for 10 years; same, Oriental Review in New York; on return home joined Kokumin Shimbun; went to Paris Peace Conf. as Corr.; participated in organizing parties. Address: 10 Minami-Tera-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mgr. Doitsu Senryo Gomei Kaisha, b. Aug. 1884 at Frankfurt am Main, Germany; m. Otti Forell. Career: grad. Higher Com. Sch. Frankfurt am Main; entered Loepold Cassella & Co.; stayed 8 years in Italy; arrived Japan 1912 representing Cassella Senryo Kaisha and later joined present company. Club: Tokyo Club. Address: Nagai Compound, 11 Konno-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Tokyo Stock Exchange since 1936; b. Nov. 1895, Aichi-ken; s. of Keitaro Ban. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; entered Com. & Ind. Dept.; Commr. Patents Bureau; Chief Mining Adm. Sec. Osaka Mining Supt. Bureau; Commr. Com. & Ind. Dept.; Chief Exchange Sec. Com. Bureau, same; Ind. Adm. Sec., Ind. Bureau; Statistics Sec.; despatched to Europe & Amer. 1935. Address: 21 Shoto-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Merchant; b. 1891, Bremen, Germany. Career: came to Japan 1914; established own business 1921; at present, agent in Japan for several European industrial firms; wrote many essays in the Mitteilungen der Deutschen Gesselschaft fuer Natur und Voelkelkunde Ostasiens, of which he is Vice-President; Secretary of German Chamber of Com. in Japan; Mem. of Asiatic Soc. of Japan. Business Office: Takiyama Bldg. Nishi-Ginza 6-chome, Tokyo. Private Address: 3 Kami-Ogikubo 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Hotel Manager (Adviser for modern hotels in Japan); b. Aug. 1911 in Switzerland; s. of Rudolf Basler, bank mgr. Career: Attended special hotel schools in Switzerland and Mercantile School in London; thorough training in Swiss hotels as cook, waiter, reception clerk, administration, etc.; Lieut.-Quartermaster, Swiss Army. In Japan since 1934. Address: Kawana Hotel, Izu.

n: BASSOMPIERRE, Albert Marie Leon Adolphe de
t: Baron; Belgian Ambassador to Japan; b. Aug. 1873. Brussels; s. of Ernst de Bassompierre, Commr. General, Belgian Army; m. Hélenè de Woot de Trixhe. Career: Dr. Juris. Louvain Univ. 1896; later entered diplomatic service. Address: Belgian Embassy, 33 Shimo-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo

D.C.L.; LL.D.; Legal Adviser, Japanese Foreign Office; b. Feb. 1869, Cumberland, Great Britain; n. British; s. of William-Thomas Baty. Career: grad. Queens' Coll. Oxford; Trin. Coll. Cambridge; English Bar (Inner Temple) 1898; Fellow, Univ. Coll. Oxford 1895-1902; Whewell Scholar, Univ. of Cambridge 1893; Hon. Secr.-Gen. Int'l Law Assn. 1905-1916; organized conferences at Christiania, Berlin, Portland (Me.), Budapest, London, Paris and Madrid; Associate, Institut de Droit Int'l and Academic Diplomatique; former Examiner, Oxford, Liverpool, Manchester, London and Hongkong Univs. Publications: "Int'l Law," "Canons of Int'l Law," "Polarized Law," "Victorious Liability," etc. Address: 9 Urakasumigaseki, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

British Consular Agent; b. July 1867, London; n. British; s. of Edmund Hellyer Bennett. Career: grad. Aske's Hatcham Sch. Surrey, England; arrived at Nagasaki from London in 1887 and joined Holme, Ringer & Co. as Shipping Clerk; established Holme, Ringer & Co. at Jinsen, Oct. 1896 and remained as Mgr. until 1904; established Bennett & Co. 1904. Address: British Consulate, Jinsen, Chosen.

B.S.; American Vice-Consul at Dairen since 1931; b. May 1905, Providence R.I., U.S.A.; s. of G. W. Van Benschoten, doctor. Career: grad. Dartmouth Coll. 1928, Harvard Univ. 1928-29; Vice-Consul, Halifax, Canada 1930; studied at Foreign Service Officers' Training Sch. Washington 1931. Address: American Consulate, Dairen.

B.A. (Allahabad Univ.), B.T. (Aligarh Univ.), Lecturer Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; b. June 1890, Delhi, India; s. of M. T. Berlas, educator; m. A. J. Berlas. Career: taught at several High Schools in India for 20 yrs.; was Dir. of 2 of them; lectured Hindustani in Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. 4 yrs.; Hon. Secr. Red Cross Soc. and St. John's Ambulance Assn. of a local branch 4 yrs.; is a student of Islam and of Japanese culture; contributor to Indian periodicals on the subjects about Japan to enlighten people of his native land. Address: 790 Togoshi-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Consul for Finland; b. July 1878, London; s. of Lester Berrick, merchant; m. Gertrude Mendelson. Career: educated Townley Castle Sch. and continent; came to Japan Nov. 1898; joined Berrick Bros. Yokohama. Address: 199 Yamashita-cho, Yokohama.
D.D.; Missionary; b. Mexico, New York, U.S.A. Address: Aoyama Gakuin, Aoyama, Tokyo.

Vice-Governor, Antung Prov.; b. Nov. 1887, Ehime-ken; s. of Ranzo Betsumiya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Police Chief, Yamagata-ken, Fukushima-ken, Wakayama-ken, Hokkaido & Aichi-ken; Chief, Home Dept. Miye-ken & Kumamoto-ken. Address: c/o Antung Prov. Office, Antung.

Dr. phil.; German Consul at Dairen since 1935; b. July 1880, Muenchen; s. of Theodor Bischoff, director of a railway company; m. Hertha Bischoff, née Zelle. Career: Counsellor of Legation at German Embassy Tokyo 1925-26; Consul at Kobe 1926-34. Address: c/o German Consulate, Dairen.
Mgr. Eastern Export Co. at Kobe; b. 1913, Rangoon, Burma. Address: 11 Isogami-dori 7-chome, Kobe.

Marquis (cr. 1910); Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Board of Councillors, Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Pres. Keijo Spinning Co.; Dir. Chosen Land Improvement Co.; b. June 1861, Bannan, Suigen District, Keiki-do. Career: held important positions in political circles in Chosen since 1892; nominated Peer 1933. Address: 81 Suijin-do, Keijo.

Mem. Board of Councillors, Chosen Govt.; Pres. Chosen Com. Bank; Spec. Mem. Keijo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Feb. 1879, Zenshu; s. of Boku Ki-jun. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Gov. Kogendo and Kita-Kankyodo; Inspector, Oriental Development Co.; Pres. Sannan Bank 1927; Vice-Pres. of present bank 1928; Pres. 1931. Address: 144 Shokakudo, Keijo.

Pres. Soai-kai; Mng.-Dir. Nissen Enterprise Co.; Prop. Nissen Kaikan; b. Apr. 1891, Keisho Nando, Chosen. Career: grad. Mitsuyo Kanbun Shojuku (Chinese Classics Sch.); Nichigo Gakko (Japanese Language Sch.); founded Sokyu-kai (Mutual Relief Society), Soai-kai (Mutual Friendship Society); went to Manchuria and Mongolia to inspect condition of Chosenese; sent to Diet from Tokyo 1932. Address: 1 Umayabashi, Honjo-ku, Tokyo.
Brazilian Consul at Yokohama; b. Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, 1898. Career: grad. Law Coll. Univ. of Rio de Janeiro. Address: 1,500 Araijuku 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo. Tel. Omori 1123.

Journalist; Lecturer; Corr. of Indian Papers; Editor of "New Asia," a monthly paper standing for Complete Independence of Asia; b. Mar. 1886, Bengal, India; n. Indian; Naturalized as Japanese citizen, 1923; s. of Benode Behari Bose, official. Career: grad. Dupleix Coll., French Chandernagore; Morton Inst., Calcutta, India; worked as Chief Clerk, Forest Research Institute, Indian Govt.; joined Indian Govt.; joined Indian Independence Agitation and led revolutionary movement in India 1910-15; was charged by the Indian Govt. with sedition, conspiracy to wage war against the British King, creating disaffection among Indian soldiers for revolutionary purposes, throwing bomb upon and severely injuring Lord Hardinge, Viceroy of India, and a reward of twelve thousand Rupees was announced for his arrest; fled from India as refugee after unsuccessful uprising in 1915 to Japan, where he was ordered to be deported by Japanese Govt., but rescued and protected by Mitsuru Toyama, later Premier Inukai and other Japanese political leaders, and naturalized as Japanese Citizen; is active in Japan for Indian Independence, Asiatic Renaissance and World Peace based on justice and love; built "Asia Lodge," dormitory for Indian and other South Asiatic students, at 401 Yodobashi-machi, Tokyo; published the following books (in Japanese); Prospect of Revolutionary Asia, pages 325; Indian Tales of Wits, pages 340; India in Revolution, pages 428; India in Bondage, pages [?]; Indian Folk Tales, pages 272; Victory of Young Asia, pages 245. Address: 79 Onden 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; LL.D.; Missionary; Chairman Board of Trustees, Friends Girls' Sch.; Sch. of Japanese Language and Culture; b. Oct. 1869, Stuart, Iowa; U.S.A.; s. of Ephraim Bowles; m. Minnie M. Pickert. Career: grad. Penn. Coll., Student Univ. of Chicago; grad. New York Sch. of Social Works; apptd. Teacher in Kansas Public Sch.; same, Indian Sch., Tunesassa, New York; same in Penn. Coll., Oskaloosa, Iowa; missionary in Tokyo since Feb. 1901; representing Soc. of Friends, Philadelphia. Address: 14 Mita Daimachi 1-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. for Panama at Yokohama & Tokyo since 1931; b. Feb. 14, 1910, Panama City; s. of Alejandro Briceno, judge, public notary, diplomat; m. Beatrice Schnahenbeck 1931; profession journalist; consular official. Career; Reporter "Panama-America," "Diario de Panama," "Grafico" and "Accion Comual," 1928-31; served Immigration Dept, Panama Foreign Office 1930; Secr. to Premier Vallarino 1931; Chief of 1st Sec., Dept. of Govt. & Justice 1931; since Mar. 20, 1931 Consul at Yokohama. Address: Panama Consulate, 157 Yamashita-cho, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Hon., B.Sc., C.E., F.R.G.S., LL.D.; Canadian Minister to Tokyo since 1936; b. July 1863 at St. Andrew's, Lhanbryd, Elgin; s. of Rev. Charles Bruce, M.A.; m. 1st, Lady Elizabeth Northcote (deceased), y. d. of 2nd Earl of Iddlesleigh; 2nd. Edith Badgley, d. of late W. A. Molson, M.D., widow of Richard Benedict Van Horne, 1932. Educ.: The Gymnasium, Old Aberdeen; Glasgow Univ. Career: Scientific Staff, Wm. Denny & Bros., Dumbarton, 1883-87; went to Canada 1887; Eng. Staff, C. P. Railway, 1887-95; engaged in mining, British Columbia, 1887-97; Pres. Mine Owners' Assn. of the Interior, 1923-25; Lieut.-Gov., British Columbia, 1926-31; Dir., Consolidated Mining & Smelting Co. of Canada. Address: Canadian Legation, 16 Omote-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Methodist Missionary; b. Aug. 1896, Agosta, Ohio; s. of Rev. E. G. Brumbaugh, Methodist Minister. Career: grad. Oberlin Business Coll. Ohio 1914; Army service, U. S. A. and in France 1917-19; Ohio Wesleyan Univ. Delaware 1920 (B.A.); Sch. of Theol. Boston Univ. 1924 (S.T.B.); Union Theol. Sem. New York 1930 (S.T.M.); Methodist Student Pastor, Harvard Univ. 1923-24; Asst. Pastor, Grace Methodist Church, Dayton, Ohio 1922-23; Missionary in Japan since 1924. Publications: "Religious Values in Japanese Culture." Address: 65 Miyashita-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

B.S. (Colo. Agr. Col.); M.A. (Northwestern Univ.); Amer. Vice Consul at Nagasaki; b. Aug. 1897, Red Cloud, Nebr., U.S.A.; s. of Chas. S. Bruner. Career: U. S. Reclamation Service 1917; U. S. Army 1917-19; Teacher of Science Eaton High Sch. Colorado 1919-20; educ. work in Japan 1920-31; service at present office since 1931. Address: Amer. Consulate Nagasaki.

B.A.; M.A.; B.D.; Ph.D.; Missionary of Presbyterian Church in U.S.A.; engaged in Newspaper Evangelism; b. June 1892, Kobe; s. of Dr. William C. Buchanan, missionary for 44 years in Japan; m. Katharine Baetjer. Career: grad. Fredericksburg Coll. 1912; Washington and Lee Univs. 1914; Presb. Theol. Sem. Chicago 1921; Hartford Sem. Foundation 1934; taught in Hagi Middle Sch. Yamaguchi-ken 1914-16; Yamaguchi Middle Sch. and Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch. 1916-17; Kwansai Gakuin 1917-18; went to U. S. to join army as volunteer 1918; returned to Japan as ordained missionary 1921; joined Asiatic Society of Japan as life member 1921; published "Inari: Its Origin, Development, and Nature" 1935. Address: Ichijo-dori, Muro-machi Nishi, Kyoto.

B.A. (Cambridge Univ. England); Missionary; b. June 1856, Taunton, Somerset, England; s. of William Buncombe, lawyer. Career: ordained in English Church 1883; Curate in Kingston-in-Thames and St. Paul's churches for 5 yrs.; came to Japan as Missionary 1888. Address: 487 Asagaya 3-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

H.B.M. Cons.-Gen. Mukden; b. Mar. 1886, Herriard, Hants, England; s. of Rev. G. H. Butler. Career: entered British Consular service 1908; served at Tokyo, Seoul, Tansui, Osaka, Manila, Yokohama. Address: British Consulate-Gen., Mukden.
Hon. Consul for Japan at Genoa; b. Mar. 1890, Genoa: s. of late Edward Canali. Address: Via Lomellino, 8, Genoa, Italy.

Cotton Controller & Surveyor; b. Aug. 1888, Florence; s. of Andrea Casal, engr. Career: In Japan from 1912 connected with cotton firms until 1921 when became partner F. S. Morse, of which now proprietor; Hon. Secr. & Treas. of Int'l Committee, also Dir. of Int'l Hospital Kobe. Address: Shioya, near Kobe.

Cable Corr. & Ins. Agent since 1928; b. Oct. 1867, London; s. of John Catto; n. Scottish. Career: grad. St. Saviour's Coll. Ardingly; engaged in Ins. business in London and various parts in the East; came to Japan first in 1890; returned to Japan 1902; joined J. Russell Kennedy 1927. Address: 13 Reinanzaka, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

A. B. (Haverford Coll.); Writer & Journalist; b. Feb. 1897, Brooklyn, New York; s. of Ernest V. Chamberlin; m. Sophie Trosten. Career: grad. William Penn Charter Sch. Pa. 1913; Haverford Coll. Penn. 1917; connected with Philadelphia Press, Phila. Public Ledger, New York Tribune 1917-22; Staff Far Eastern Corr. of same in Tokyo since Feb. 1935; Corr. of Christian Science Monitor at Moscow 1922-34; Author of "Soviet Russia" (1930)," "The Soviet Planned Economic Order" (1931); "Russian's Iron Age" (1934); "The Russian Revolution" (1935) etc. Address: 258 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

General; Manchoukuo Prime Minister since 1935; b. 1871. Taian-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Fengtien; apptd. Major-Gen. 1916; Mil. Gov. of Chahar District and Comdr. 16th Div. 1920-22; Dir.-Gen. Nat. Highway Preparation Bureau 1924; War Min. in Ku Wei-chun Cabinet 1927; Min. of Ind. in Fan-Fu Cabinet: Gov.-Gen. Tung Sheng Spec. Dist. Pres. Supreme War Council Nat. Govt.; joined Japanese Army for preservation of peace at Harbin at time of Manchurian Incident; Gov. Heilungkiang Prov. 1932; apptd. Pres. Privy Council and War Minister; Min. (add.), Dept. of Foreign Affairs; Dept. of Mongolia Adm., 1937. Address: Premier's Residence, Hsinking.

General; Chief, Aide-de-Camp to Manchoukuo Emperor; Manchoukuo Privy Councillor; b. 1867 in Kaipinhsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: apptd. Comdr. 55th Brig. of 28th Div.; Commdr. 4th North-East Cav. Div. and Tutelary Envoy in Taoliao 1927. Address: Hsinking.

Lt.-Gen.; Chief Staff & Chief, Mil. Communications Dept., Manchoukuo Defence Dept.; b. July 1893, Changchun-hsien, Kirin Prov.; s. of Gen. Chang Chenkiang. Career: grad. Paoting Mil. Acad. Staff, Heilungkiang Mil. Office and Instructor, Mil. Acad. 1921; Aide-de-Camp, Cav. 14th Brig. 1924; Chief-Staff, Cav. 17th Div. 1926; Comdr. 2nd Brig. Heilungkiang 1929; Bandit Supression Commdr. Fengtien Prov. 1930; Dir. Mil. Supply Bureau, Defence Dept. 1932-35. Address: 15 Chung Chih Lu, Hsinking.

Councillor Manchoukuo Dept. of People's Welfare; b. 1894, Chinchow, Kwantung Prov. Career: grad. Police Training Institute Liaoyang; Staff Finance Dept. Fengtien Prov.; Chief 1st Sec. Fengtien Prov. Stamp Revenue Office; Dir. Mukden Revenue Supt. Bureau; Magistrate Hailung-hsien Fengtien Prov.; Chief Chuangho Salt Fields Fengtien; Councillor Fengtien Prov.; Chief Personnel Sec. of same 1932-35; Dir. Rites & Religious Bureau 1935-37. Address: Dept. of People's Welfare Hsinking.

Dir. Public Health Bureau, Manchoukuo Department of People's Welfare; b. 1891, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Fengtien English Med. Coll.; Surgeon Heilungkiang, Kirin & Fengtien Provs.; Pres. Kirin Prov. Hospital. Address: Dept. of People's Welfare, Hsinking.

Director, Supervisory Bureau Home Office; b. 1891, Itung-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad. Pei-Yang Univ. Tientsin; Magistrate Changchunhsien; Chief Yenki Muni. Adm. Planning Office; Yenki Marine Custom Supt.; Adviser Gov.'s Office, Kirin Prov.; Chief Educ. Dept. of Kirin 1934-36; Dir. Civil Affairs Bureau, Kirin Prov. Address: Home Office, Hsinking.

Chief Dir. Manchoukuo Boy Scouts; b. Feb. 1896, Hopei Prov. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. Tokyo; Magistrate Fu-hsien Fengtien Prov.; Dir. Adm. Bureau Tientsin; Dir. Ind. Bureau Kirin Prov. 1931; Min. of Ind. 1932-35; Foreign Minister; accorded privilege of former post. Address: Hsinking.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 3rd Dist. Garrison (Tsitsihar) since 1932; b. 1900, Noho, Heilungkiang Prov. Career: grad. Paoting Mil. Acad.; Chief, Inf. Garrison; Comdr. Cav. Reg.; Gen. Staff, Heiho Tutelary Dept.; Comdr. Inf. 6th Div. of Heilungkiang. Address: 3rd Dist. Garrison Hdqrs. Tsitsihar.

Vice-Dir. Manchoukuo Forestry Bureau; b. 1885, Payenhsien, Heilungkiang Prov. Career: grad. Higher Police Training Inst. Heilungkiang Prov. 1905; Magistrate, Wangching-hsien 1915; Chief, Police Dept. Peking-Mukden Ry. Bureau 1927; Acting Dir. Kirin-Changchun, Kirin-Tunhua, Ssupingkai-Taonan Ry. Bureaus; Dir. Fishing &Merchant Vessels Protection Bureau Fengtien Prov.; Dir. Weights & Measure Bureau 1935-37 Address: Forestry Bureau Hsinking.

Chief, Plague Prevention Sec. Public Health Bureau, Manchoukuo People's Welfare Dept. since 1932; b. May 1900, Peking; s. of Chao Shih-min, official. Career: Chief, Sanitary Inspection Office, Harbin 1929; Chief, Sanitary Sec. Mukden Muni. Office 1931; Chief, 2nd Sec. Sanitary Dept. & Public Health Sec. Mukden 1932. Address: c/o People's Welfare Dept., Hsinking.

b. 1878, Chinkiang-hsien, Kiangsu Prov. Career: Councillor, Mil. Gov.'s Office, Heilungkiang, 1918; Secr. Gov.'s Office, and Chief Finance Dept. Fengtien Prov. 1921; Civil Affairs Chief, Fengtien Prov. 1932; Vice-Min. of Civil Affairs Dept., 1934-37. Address: Hsinking.

B.A. (Univ. of Califor. 1911); Missionary; b. Nov. 1888, Oakland, Calif. U. S. A.; s. of H. W. Chapman, minister; m. Katherine Arbury Chapman. Career: missionary work of Presbuterian Church in Japan since 1917. Address: Isada, Shingu, Wakayama-ken.

D.D.; Clergyman; b. July 1873, Fauquier County, Virginia, U. S. A.; s. of William Henry Chapman, govt. official; m. Ellen Ritchie Scott. Career: missionary of Amer. Epis. Church in Kyoto Diocese since 1899. Address: Karasumaru, Shimotachiuri-agaru, Kyoto.

Ex-Prime Minister of Manchoukuo; b. 1859, Foochow, China. Career: Consul at Kobe; resided in Lungchow as Kwangsi Frontier Defence Min.; apptd. Inspector-Gen. Kwantung & Anhui Prov. 1907; engaged in business at Shanghai; founded Const. Govt. Prep. Soc. to advocate Const. Govt.; Inspector, Construction of China Ry. & Lienshan Bay Harbor, under Gov.-Gen. Three Eastern Prov. 1909; Gov. Hunan Prov.; Dir. Shanghai Com. Press; Dir. Shanghai Savings Bk.; attended present Manchou Emperor when he was in Tientsin; exerted in establishment of Manchoukuo; Prime Minister & Educ. Min. 1932-35; visited Japan as Spec. Envoy 1934. Address: Hsinking.

Sch. Inspector, Manchoukuo People's Welfare Dept.; b. May 1883 Suihua-hsien, Heilungkiang Prov.; s. of Cheng I-ling, businessman. Career: Pres. North East Univ. of Communications 1927; Govt. Committee, Heilungkiang Prov. 1930; Chief, Educ. Dept. same; Commr. Heilungkiang Prov. Office, and Chief, Educ. Dept. of same, 1932. Address: c/o People's Welfare Dept. Hsinking.

Postal Adm. Bureau of Manchoukuo; b. 1889, Foochow, China; s. of Cheng Hsiao-Hsu, ex-prime Minister. Career: studied at Seijo Sch. Tokyo 1905; grad. Liverpool Univ. 1911; Manager, Kinghua Publishing Co. Peking 1919; Mgr. Tungchi Printing Office, Mukden 1922; Mgr. South Branch, Chihsin Cement Co. Shanghai 1927; Mng.-Dir. Huafeng Enamel Co. Shanghai 1930; Secr. to Prime Min. 1932; Dir. Cap. Constr. Bureau 1935-37. Address: Postal Adm. Bureau, Hsinking.

Aud. Ind. Bank of Manchou since Dec. 1936; b. 1887, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. Tokyo; Magistrate Changchun-hsien, Kirin Prov.; Adviser to Gov. Kirin Prov.; Chief, Yenki Muni. System Adm. Planning Office, Kirin; Dir. Revenue Supt. Bureau Mukden 1932-36. Address: 202 Daido-Daigai, Hsinking.

Councillor & Vice-Chief of Harbin Ry. Factory of S.M.R.; b. Feb. 1900 Shanghai; s. of Chiang Shih-tsuan, Admiral of Changkiang Fleet in Ching Dynasty. Career: Chief Engr., Mukden Arsenal; taught Aviation Sch.; Chief Instructor, Harbin Higher Engrg. Sch.; Prof. Harbin Engrg. Coll.; Sec. Chief, Engrg. Affairs, Chinese Eastern Ry.; Vice-Chief, Head Factory same. Address: 83 Shoshigai-dori, Harbin, Manchoukuo.

Dir. Gen. Monopoly Bureau of Manchoukuo; b. 1899, Yushou-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad. Polit. & Econ. Dept. Chaoyang Univ. Peiping; Magistrate, Mengkiang, Huatien and Yushouhsiens, Kirin Prov. Address: Gen. Monopoly Bureau, Hsinking.

Manchoukuo Privy Councillor; b. Feb. 1891, Kuoerhissuchien Banner. Career: Prince Hoshih, Chelimu League 1902; Mem. House of Commons 1922; Mem. Constitution Draft Committee; Gov. Hsingan Adm. Office 1932-34; Min. of Mongolia Adm. 1934-37. Address: Privy Council Hsinking.
Mayor of Tsitsihar since 1932. Career: grad. Tung Wen Coll. Shanghai; studied in Tokyo; apptd. Foreign Affairs Secr., Heilungkiang Prov. Address: Tsitsihar Muni. Office, Tsitsihar.

Mayor of Mukden; b. 1877, Kaiping-hsein, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Peking Coll. 1909; Gen. Dir. Tsinan Muni. Office; Chief Police Gen. Adm. Office, Tung Sheng Spec. District; Dir. Chinese Eastern Ry. (North Manchuria Ry.) 1932; Police Chief Harbin 1933-35; Metro. Police Chief 1936-37. Address: Muni. Office, Mukden.

Gov. Jehol Prov. since 1937; b. 1896, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Law Coll. Peiping; Secr. Kirin Prov. Office; Dir. Harbin Elec. Bureau; Chief Police Dept. Kirin Prov. 1933-34; Gov. Sankiang Prov. Address: Governor's Residence, Chengteh.

Prof. of German Litt. Keio Univ.; Poet; b. Mar. 1883, Nagano-ken; s. of Naotaro Chino. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Prof. 3rd Higher Sch.; Prof. Nihon Women's Univ. Address: 1071 Nakanobu-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

LL.D. (America); Dentist; Pres. Tokyo Dental Coll.; Japan Dental Assn.; b. Feb. 1870, Chiba-ken; s. of Seinosuke Kato. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; studied at Takayama Dental Inst.; became Corr. Tokyo Shimpo; Teacher of English of middle sch.; Secr. and Lecturer, Takayama Dental Inst.; founded Tokyo Dental Inst. (now Tokyo Dental Coll.) 1900; founded Japan Dental Assn. 1903; author of books on dental science. Address: 496 Sendagaya 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Hiroshima Higher Tech. Sch.; b. Dec. 1881, Yonezawa; s. of Shimizu Cho; m. Maki, d. of Kichihei Suzuki. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; apptd. Prof. Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch. 1908; Yokohama Higher Tech. Sch. 1920; went to U. S. A., Germany & France for study; Sch-Inspector Dept. of Educ. 1927; Dir. Hamamatsu Higher Tech. Sch. 1932-36. Address: c/o Hiroshima Higher Tech. Sch., Hiroshima.
Chancellor; b. Jan. 1884, Germany; m. Paula Dierks. Career: Consular Service since 1905, mostly in the Far East and Japan. Address: German Consulate, 51-B Yamashita-cho, Yokohama.

b. 1893, Kiangsu Prov. Career: Gov. Lingnan-Tao, Kwantung Prov. Councillor Home Dept. & Staff Officer, Kwantung & Kwangsi Inspector-Gen.'s Office in China Dynasty; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Foreign Dept. Address: Hsinking.

Major-Gen.; Comdr. Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army; b. 1902, Mongolia. Career: grad. Hwangpu Mil. Coll. Shiangsu Prov.; studied in Tokyo; Comdr. Mongolia Self Defence Army 1931; Comdr. Hsingan East Sub-prov. Peace Preservation Corps 1932; Chief Staff & Acting Comdr. Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army, 1933. Address: Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army Hdqrs., Pukotu, Manchoukuo.

B.A.; M.A.; Missionary; b. Oct. 1893, Macon, Georgia, U.S.A.; s. of James Jackson Cobb, banker; m. Theodora Cook Atkinson. Career: Prof. at Kentucky Wesleyan Coll. 1915-17; came to Japan 1918; taught at Palmore Institute, Kobe 1919-27 and 1932-33; Evangelistic Work and Principal of Fraser Institute, Hiroshima 1927-31; Principal, Osaka English Sch. since 1933. Address: Eki Kita, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

Dr. phli.; Prof. and Writer; b. Aug. 1875, Bursheid near Cologne, Germany; s. of Edmund Conrady; m. Marie Berg. Career: studied history, polit. econ. and phil. in Bonn, Berlin, Leipzig Univs. 1893-97; Dr. phil. Leipzig 1897-98; lived as writer in London 1898-1900; then in Berlin; author of historical books; served in Great War; came to Japan as teacher of German 1931. Address: c/o Kochi Koto Gakko, Kochi City.
Missionary; b. Apr. 1890, Enfield, Middlesex, England; s. of Ernest Coote; m. Esther Keene. Address: P. O. Box 5, Ikoma, Nara-ken.

Rep. Dir. Dai-Nippon Kali Kaisha. Career: engaged in different kinds of business in London. Africa, Singapore, Java, China; in Japan since 1929. Address: (office) Teikoku Seimei Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo.

A.B. 2nd Secr. American Embassy in Tokyo since 1935; b. Mar. 1902, Washington, D.C.; s. of Dr. Frederick V. Coville, botanist; m. Lilian Grosvenor. Career: grad. Cornell Univ. 1923; entered U. S. foreign service 1926; attache embassy Tokyo 1927-29, vice-consul Kobe 1930; consul Dairen 1930-31, Kobe 1931, Tokyo 1932, Harbin 1932-34; Dept. of State, Washington D. C. 1935. Address: American Embassy, Tokyo.

Journalist; b. Dec. 1885, London; s. of Herbert Robert Cox, company secretary. Career: joined Reuter's London Office 1901; proceeded Bombay 1907; Mgr. Reuter's Colombo Office 1909-11; Mgr. Reuter's Shanghai Office 1912-19; Mgr. Reuter's Far Eastern News Service 1925-33; Reuter's Chief Corr. in Japan since 1934. Address: Reuters Ltd., 9 Ginza Nishi 8-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo.

A.B.; Supervisor, Japan and Manchoukuo Branches of The National City Bank of N. Y.; b. in Camden, Maine, U. S. A.; s. of John C. Curtis. Career: grad. Bowdoin College 1911; Foreign Banking Service since 1911 with Int'l Banking Corp. and The Nat. City Bank of N. Y.; Mgr. Harbin Branch 1921-30; Asst. Vice-Pres. New York Office 1931-32; present post since 1933. Address: c/o The National City Bank of New York, Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Consul-General & Acting Minister for Belgium at Shanghai; b. Sept. 1883, Antwerp. Career: Cons.-Gen. at Harbin; transferred to Shanghai 1927. Address: Belgian Consulate-Gen., Rue Lafayette 1300 Shanghai, China.

Baron; Dir. Society for Int. Cultural Relations; b. Feb. 1892, Omuta City; s. of late Baron Takuma Dan; m. Michiko, d. of Suesaburo Ueno. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; further studied at Harvard Univ. and Lyon Univ.; apptd. Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923; Asst. Prof. 1927; sent to China 1931; resigned 1933; succeeded peerage 1932; decorated with Commander le Crown by Italian Emperor 1929. Address: 344 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co., Yubari Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1875, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Katsuji Danno. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; visited Europe & Amer. and attended Int'l Rotarian Assembly at Denver as Japanese Delegate 1926; sent to Diet 1928. Address: 89 Myogadani-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Merchant; Hon. Treasurer, Indian Trade Assn. at Kobe; b. Aug. 1888, Calcutta. Career: came to Japan 1915; Pres. Indian Club 1921-29; elected its Hon. Mem. 1930; First Indian Resident in Japan received in audience by H.I.J.M. the Emperor 1929; Hon. Secr. & Treasurer Indian Trade Assn. 1925-30. Address: 17, Yamamoto-dori 2-chome, Kobe.

Charge d'Affaires of Peru in Japan and China; b. in Lima, Peru; s. of Dr. Anibal Fernandez Davila, former Vice-President of the Senate of Peru; m. Elsa Beriso. Career: Served in diplomatic service of Peru in Argentine, Colombia, Germany, Holland, Denmark and Japan. Served also in Foreign Office in Lima as Chief of Bureau of Treaties and Conventions. Address: 2, Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers since Apr. 1936; b. July 1878, Morioka; s. of Katsumasa Debuchi, official. Career: grad. P.-G. Course, Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; 3rd Emb. Secr. at Berlin 1907-10; 1st Secr. at Peking 1914; at Washington 1918; Chargé d'Affaires at Berlin 1920; attended 2nd League of Nations Assembly and Washington Conf.; Commr. Shantung Settlement Conf. 1922; Dir. Asia Bureau 1923; Foreign Vice-Minister 1924-28; Ambassador to U. S. A. 1928-33; sent to Australia as Delegate of Good Will Mission 1935. Address: [?] Tamagawa-Oyama-cho, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.
D.L.; Secr. of Emb.; b. Dec. 1904, Ypres, Belgium; s. of Henri Iweins d'Eeckhoutte; m. Zosia Wroblewska. Address: c/o Belgian Embassy, 33 Shimo-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Board of Tourist Industry, Ry. Dept. since July [?]; b. Mar. 1891, Tokyo; s. of Baron Kenjiro Den. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; entered Ry. Dept.; Councillor, Ry. Bureau; Secr. Ry. Dept. 1929; Chief Int'l Sec., Traffic Bureau; went to Europe and America 1922. Address: 147 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M.B.E.; H.B.M. Consul at Harbin; b. Apr. 1897, Tokyo; s. of Walter Dening, teacher and journalist. Career: Austrian Army 1915-19; Brit. Consular Service in Japan from 1920; served Tokyo, Keijo, Dairen, Kobe, Osaka, Manila and Harbin. Address: British Consulate-Gen. Vakzalny Prospekt, Harbin.

D. Jur.; German Ambassador to Tokyo since 1933; b. Apr. 1882, Berlin; s. of Willibald von Dirksen, Peer. Career: grad. Heidelberg and Berlin Univs.; Chargé d'Affaires, Warsaw 1920-21; served Foreign Office, Berlin 1921-23; Consul-Gen. Danzig 1923-25; Dir. Near-East Dept. Foreign Office 1925-28; Ambassador to U.S.S.R. 1928. Address: German Embassy, Tokyo.

Deputy Mayor of Mukden since 1937; b. May 1896; s. of Takichi Dohi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; joined Ry. Dept., S.M.R. Co., same year; Chief of Kaiyuan Local Office, 1926; Hsinknig Local Office, 1927; Chief of Gen. Affairs Sec., Gen. Affairs Dept., Head Office, 1931; Personnel Sec., same, 1932; sent to Europe and America for investigation, 1934; Chief, Shanghai Business Office, 1935. Address: Municipal Office, Mukden, Manchoukuo.

Mng.-Dir. Hotel New Grand; Fujisawa Golf Club; b. 1884, Hyogo-ken; s. of Kusuhei Doi. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1907; joined Toyo Kisen Kaisha; successively Mgr. Hongkong, San Francisco Branches, and Business Mgr. of Head Office; resigned 1926; visited Europe and America to inspect hotel business. Address: 1598 Higashiterao-machi, Tsurumi-ku, Yokohama.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 14th Division since Mar. 1937; b. 1883, Okayama-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1905; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; Staff, Gen. Staff Office, Comdr. Inf. 30th Reg.; Comdr. Inf. 9th Brig.; Chief Mil. Spec. Service Facilities, Mukden 1935; attached Remaining 1st Div. Address: c/o 14th Division Hdqrs. Utsunomiya.

Ph.D.; Dr. Habil. General Secr., Japan-German Cultural Soc. since 1937; b. Oct. 1898 Berlin; s. of Paul Donat, Merchant; m. Elfriede Rehdorf. Career: grad. Berlin Univ. 1924, majored in German literature and philosophy; came to Japan 1925, instructor of German language, Hiroshima Higher School; studied Japanese language & literature; rec'd Dr. Habil. degree from Univ. of Hamburg for Japanology 1936. Address: 2281 1-chome, Araijuku, Omori-ku, Tokyo.
Ingenieur A. et M. Paris; Asst. Com. Attache; b. 1906, Paris. Career: with French Embassy, Tokyo since 1928. Address: 1822 Kaijo Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo.
Mgr. of Butterfield & Swire Dairen; b. Apr. 1897, Ireland; m. 1901. Career: Office British Army; Retired Captain; arrived China 1921. Address: 57 Sakaki-machi, Dairen.

Pianist; b. Nov. 1899, Tokyo; s. of late Edwin Dun, former Amer. Minister to Japan. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Tokyo Acad. of Music; studied music in Berlin 1921-24; apptd. Prof. Toyo Music Sch.; Seijo Gakuen; Arts Dept. Nihon Univ. Address: 8 Sadohara-cho 3-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

B. S. (Dartmouth); Secr. Y.M.C.A. Tokyo; Non Commissioned Officer, Olympic Organizing Committee; b. Nov. 1891, Concord, New Hampshire, U. S. A.; s. of late Hazen F. Durgin; m. Delphine Lazelle. Address: 5 of 7 Fujimi-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

British Pro-Consul, Dairen since 1927; b. 1898, England; s. of James Curtice Ellis, architest; m. Laura E. O'Brien, née Vincent. Career: Educated at Westminster Cathedral Sch. and City of London Coll.; served in Great War 1914-18; entered civil service 1920; seconded to British Far Eastern Consular Service (Japan) 1925; elected Hon. Pres. of Dairen Cosmopolitan Club 1937. Address: c/o British Consulate, Dairen.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1865, Kochi-ken; bro. of Shojo Eguchi, samurai of Kochi Clan. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1887; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mgr. Nagasaki and Moji Branches; Vice-Chief, Mining Dept. Head Office; Mng.-Dir. of same; Vice-Pres. S. M. R. Co. 1931-32. Address: 36 Honmura-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Hsingan East Prov. since 1932; b. 1879, Inner Mongolia. Career: Gov. Eastern Puteha; Councillor, Gov.'s Office of Heilungkiang 1926. Address: c/o Hsingan East Prov. Office, Chalantun, Manchoukuo.

Exchange Broker; b. Oct. 1873, Budapest, Hungary; s. of A. Elked. Career: grad. Com. Acad. Budapest; Officer, Royal Hungarian Cav.; Austrian Jute Spinning Works, Vienna; Credit Lyonnais, Paris, London, etc.; joined Russo-Asiatic Bank, St. Petersburg; Sub-Mgr. in Japan for 14 years; came to Japan 1903, apptd. Adviser, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr. Foreign Dept. 74th Bank; served Park-Union Foreign Bkg. Corp Tokyo; established himself as Foreign Exchange Broker 1921. Address: c/o Elked & Gerdts, 14 Marunouchi 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
Manager, The East Asiatic Co. Ltd. for Kwantung Leased Territory since 1928; b. 1896, Copenhagen. Career: in service of present firm in Manchuria since 1919. Address: The East Asiatic Co., Dairen.

D. Litt.; Educator; b. Oct. 1874, Maebashi; s. of Senjiro Endo; m. Natsuko, d. of late Shuji Izawa. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; Prof. Higher Normal Sch. and Waseda, Toyo, Nihon Kokugakuin and Shukyo Univs. successively since 1900; rec. deg. 1907; founded Sociocological Research Inst. 1907, Research Inst. of Divination Arts 1914; Sugamo Mid. Sch. 1922, Sugamo Com. Sch. 1923 and Sugamo Higher Com. Sch. 1928; has long devoted in promotion of Orientalism, advocated for Stout Educationalism and for exhibition of characteristics of private educ. Address: 2639 Nishi-Sugamo 2-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers since Apr. 1936; b. Mar. 1886, Saitama-ken; s. of Kogoro Endo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Imp. Univ.; Secr. Govt.-Gen. of Chosen; Chief Ind. Dept. Tokyo-fu; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Chiba-ken; Gov. Aomori-ken and Mie-ken; M.P. 1928; Pres. Musashino Ry. Co.; Gov. Kanagawa-ken, Aichi-ken; Chief, Gen. Affairs Bd. of Manchoukuo. Address: 1448 Ikebukuro 3-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Lt.-Col. D'Etat Major; Mil. Attaché, Turkish Embassy Tokyo; b. Sept. 1894, Edirne; s. Yakup Bey Avocat; m. Wasfiye Erdelhun 1904. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Istanbul 1913; Artillery Company Comdr. during World and Independence Wars; grad. Mil. Staff Coll. Istanbul 1926; present post since 1933; Lt. Col. 1935. Address: 306 Yoyogi Sanya, Tokyo.

Hon. Vice-Consul for Norway and Acting Consul for Netherlands at Yingkow since 1922; b. 1884, Yingkow; s. of Charley Farmer, H.B.M. Consular Service. Career: 3 years in Belgium & France during the Great War. Address: The Bund, Yinkow, Manchoukuo.

b. 1892, Kaiping, Fengtien Prov. Career: studied Law and Economy; Court Judge; Adm. Chief Peking-Fengtien Ry. Bureau; Chief Ind. Dept. Fengtien Prov.; Justice Min. 1932-37; accorded privilege of former post. Address: Hsinking.

Chilean Minister to Japan since 1936; b. Mar. 1889, Santiago, Chile; s. of Juan Pelajio Figueroa. Career: Lawyer of Univ. of Santiago de Chile; Attaché, Chilean Leg. in Spain 1919; Com. Counsellor at Leg. in Austria, Hungary 1922; 1st Secr. 1925; Charge d'Affaires 1927; Counsellor at Berlin 1933; Resident Minister to Czechoslovakia 1934; despatched as Delegate to International Conf. and Congress. Address: c/o Chilean Legation, 7 Shirokane-Dai-machi 1-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

B.L., Norwegian Minister in Japan, China, Siam; b. May 1878 at Oslo; s. of August Laurentius Koren, superior army surgeon; m. Gulborg Bing. Career: Secr. For. Office 1902; Consulate-Gen., Kobe 1905; Vice-Consul, Bilbao 1908; Secr. Leg. in St. Petersburg 1909; Acting Consul-Gen. Hamburg 1910; Rotterdam, 1911; Consul, Montreal 1912; Spec. Mission in Tokyo 1917; Consul-Gen. Melbourne 1917; Charge d'Affaires en Pied Lisbon 1921; Minister of 1st Class in Tokyo, Nanking, Bangkok, 1935. Address: Norwegian Legation, 17 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Niigata Higher Sch. since 1932; b. Mar. 1900, near Zemmer Trier Rheinland; s. of Peter Fischer, farmer. Career: grad. Univs. of Berlin, Frankfurt and Paris; served German East Asiatic Society, Tokyo; taught German language to Army officers at Japan's Gen. Staff. Address: Niigata Koto Gakko, Niigata.

B. Ph.; Publisher, The Japan Advertiser and The Trans-Pacific; b. Jan. 1870, Philadelphia, Pa., U. S. A.; n. American; s. of Simon B. Fleisher, manufacturer. Career: grad. Univ. of Pennsylvania 1889. Address: Onden, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Journalist; Managing Editor The Japan Advertiser; Corr. The New York Herald Tribune in Japan since 1929; b. Nov. 20. 1897, Philadelphia, Penn., U. S. A.; s. of B. W. Fleisher, publisher; m. Greta Sundberg of Stockholm, Sweden. Career: educated Charterhouse, Survey, England and Columbia Univ. N. Y. 1919; Corr. with A. E. F. Siberia during War; Corr. United Press in Paris 1921-24; Corr. United Press 2nd Assembly League of Nations; Business Mgr. Japan Advertiser 1924-25; Washington Corr. N. Y. Times 1925-29. Address: The Japan Advertiser, Tokyo.

Businessman; Pres. Frazar Estate Co.; Senior Partner Frazar & Co.; b. Aug. 1867, Shanghai, China; s. of Everett Frazar, merchant. Career: grad. Stevens Inst. of Tech., Hoboken, New Jersey, U. S. A. 1890 with degree M. E.; Pupil of Thomas A. Edison 1891; arrived at Yokohama 1896. Address: c/o Frazar Estate Co., Yaesu Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Dir. C. Itoh & Co.; b. Mar. 1890, Miye-ken; m. Mitsuyo. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1911; joined present firm and served at its head office in Osaka; Mgr. Tsingtao, Tientsin, Hankow Br. successively; Tokyo Br. 1924-36. Address: C. Itoh & Co., Osaka.
Baron; Engineer; Gen. Mgr., Andrews & George Co. for Manchoukuo and Chosen; b. Sept. 1881, Vienna, Austria. Address: Andrews & George Co., Mitsui Bldg., 2 Kamo-cho, Mukden, Manchoukuo.

Ph.D. Lecturer, Manchuria Medical Coll. Mukden; b. Aug. 1902. Career: grad. Berlin Univ. 1925; specialized in Far Eastern languages and history; asst. in Ethographical Museum, Berlin; since 1926 in Manchuria. Address: 5 Shinano-machi, Mukden.

Mng. Dir., I. I. Tschurin & Co. Harbin; b. Nov. 1893 at Kirrlach, Germany; s. of O. Fuetterer; m. Grete Wiechers. Career: educated in Germany 1900-11; joined Shanghai German firm 1911-13; military service at Tsingtao 1913-14; Controller of Hongkong & Shanghai Bank at Mukden and Harbin. Address: 61 Bolshoi Prospect, New Town, Harbin.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Oji Paper Mfg. Co., S. Saghalien Ry. Co., etc.; b. June 1869, Nagano-ken; s. of late Mohei Fujihara. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1891; founded Matsue Nippo; joined Mitsu Bank; transferred to Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr. Shanghai, Amoi, Taihoku Branches and Timber Dept. of same; nominated Peer 1929; made inspection tour of Canada and U. S. A. 1935. Address: 121 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Minister to Chechoslovakia since 1937; b. Mar. 1888, Gunma-ken; s. of Naojiro Fujii. Career grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; Chief Translation, Telegraphic, Personnel, Correspondence Sections, Foreign Office successively; 1st Secr. Embassy London; Consul-Gen. Hamburg; Councillor Emb. Berlin, Washington, London. Address: Japanese Legation, Prague, Czechoslovakia.

D.E.; Civil Engr., Home Dept.; b. Jan. 1889, Miyazaki-ken; s. of Ujisumi Fujii. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Civil Engineer Hyogo-ken, Meiji Shrine Construction Bureau, Earthquake Disaster Relief Office, etc.; Research Engr. Research Bureau of Public Works, Home Dept.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent abroad 1930; sent to Manchoukuo 1934. Address: 382 Totsuka-machi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Academy; b. July 1868, Hyogo-ken; s. of Ichiro Fujii. Career: Prof. 4th Higher Sch.; 8th Higher Sch.; Kyoto Imp. Univ. Address: 53 Omiya Tajiri-machi, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

M.A.; LL.D.; b. Aug. 1892, Prof. Waseda and Hosei Univs.; Instructor Nihon Univ.; b. Aug. 1892, Kagawa-ken; s. of Uhei Fujii. Career: grad. Waseda Univ.; Univ. of Southern Calif.; Boston Univ.; Columbia Univ.; attended Washington Conf. 1921-22; Dir. Nat. League of Univ. Profs. Tokyo since 1932. Address: 11 Otsuka Kubo-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; b. July 1881, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Tozaemon Fujii. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; rec'd deg. 1922; Dir. Aichi Medical Coll; Dir. Attached Hospital; Dir. Nagoya Medical College; retired, 1932. Address: 10 Yokodaikan-cho, Higashi-ku, Nagoya.

M.D.; Surgeon-Gen. (reserve); Pres. Japan Red Cross Hospital; b. Aug. 1881, Oita-ken; s. of Hisabumi Fujinami. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; joined military service; studied in Europe 1917; Instructor, Mil. Medical Coll. Address: 58 Yokodera-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Common Educ. Bureau of Educ. Dept.; b. Apr. 1894, Hiroshima-ken; bro. of Kan Fujino, businessman. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; Commr. Niigata-ken; Commr. Social Bureau; sent to Europe & America 1927; Secr. Social Bureau 1931; Gov. Kagawa-ken 1925; Dir. Tech. Educ. Bureau 1936-37. Address: c/o Dept. of Educ., Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1883, Tochigi-ken; s. of Tomozo Wakatabe, and later adopted by Tomojiro Fujinuma. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Chief Police Dept. Nara-ken, Kagoshima-ken, Kyoto-fu, Osaka-fu; Gov. Ibaraki-ken, Niigata-ken; M.P.; Gov. Tokyo-fu; Metropolitan Police Chief 1932-34; Chief Secr. of Cabinet. Address: 500 Koyama-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Author; Prof. Daito Bunka Gakuin; b. Sept. 1893, Tokyo; s. of Rikitaro Fujisawa, Peer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Official, Dept. of Agr. & Com.; Mem. Permanent Secretariat, League of Nations; Prof. Kyushu Imp. Univ.; Dir. Nippon Bunka Renmei. Address: 191 Gotanda 6-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; b. July 1859 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Kakeyoshi Fujisawa, samurai. Career: learned law at Tokyo and became lawyer through examination, 1880; Mem., Councillor and Chairman, Sendai Municipal Assembly; Permanent Mem. and Pres. Miyagi-ken Pref. Assembly; elected to Diet 13 times; Councillor, Communications Dept.; same, Home Dept. Com. & Industry Minister; Speaker, House of Representatives; Councillor, Meiji Shrine Construction Bureau; Mem., Temporary Legsilation Investigation Committee, etc.; present post since June 1934. Address: 25 Uenohara-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Painter; Court Artist; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. since 1908; b. 1867, Kagoshima; s. of Kempo Fujishima. Career: studied art of painting with Togaku Hirayama, Japanese Painter of Shijo Sch. 1881; with Gyokusho Kawabata; Oil Painting under Hosui Yamamoto; in Paris & Rome as Student of Dept. of Educ. 1905-13. Address: 12 Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Pres. Fujita-Gumi, Taisho Trust Co., Nantei Mining Co.; Dir. Fujita Bank and Fujita Mining Co.; b. Oct. 1868, Osaka; s. of late Denzaburo Fujita. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; went to England for study, 1888; during 10 years stay chiefly studied mining; Dir. Osaka Shosen Kaisha, Japan Fire Ins. Co., Kitahama Bank, Nikkan Gas Co., etc. Address: 41 Sekiguchi Dai-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral; War Councillor since 1936; b. Oct. 1880, Tokyo; s. of late Hisomu Fujita, principal of Kogyokusha Middle Sch.; m. Hisa. Career: grad. Naval Staff Coll.; Vice-Admiral 1929; Captain “Kirishima”; Secr.-Gen. Naval Tech. Dept.; Chief Personnel and Protocol Section of Navy; Chief, Yokosuka Naval Arsenal; Chief, Naval Tech. Dept.; Vice-Navy Minister 1932; Comdr.-in-Chief, Kure Naval Station 1934-36. Address:: 1448 Naka-Meguro 4-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Eastern Manchurian Rayon Pulp Mfg. Co., South Saghalien Petroleum Oil Co., Nagato Coal Mining Co., Dir. Hokkaido Takushoku Co.; consultant, Taiwan Kogyo Co., Nihon Katsudo-shashin Co.; b. Jan. 1873 at Hirosaki City, Aomori. Career: grad. Meiji Univ.; entered business; served as M.P.; later returned to business. Addressff 539 Marunouchi Bldg., Tokyo.

Pres., Fujita Gomei Kaisha; Chairman Kokusan Kogyo K. K.; Vice-Pres. Nippon Yushi (Oil & Fat) K. K.; Dir. Chuo Fire, Marine & Accident Ins. Co.; b. 1889, Yamaguchi-ken; bro. of Yoshisuke Aikawa; later adopted by Fujita family. Career: grad. Chemical Course, Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1915; established Fujita Laboratory. Address: 77 Tango-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Osaka Communications Bureau since 1936; b. Mar. 1889, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Chujiro Fujiwara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; entered Communications Dept.; sent to Europe and America for study; attended World Postal Conf. 1924; Chief, Foreign Mail Section; Dir. Telegraphic Affairs Bureau; Secr., Com. Dept.; Dir. Postal Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo, 1[?]32-35. Address: c/o Osaka Communications Bureau, Nakanoshima, Osaka.

D. Sc.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Meteorologist, Central Meteorological Observatory; Prof. Meteorology, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Oct. 1884, Nagano-ken; s. of Mitsuzo Fujiwhara, official. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; rec'd deg. 1915. Address: c/o The Central Meteorological Observatory, Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Permanent Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Dai-Nippon Sugar Mfg. Co., Shuseisha, Nihon Nat. Cash Register Co.; Dir. Taiwan Takushoku K. K., Musashino Elec. Ry. Co., Kokkwa Conscription Ins. Co., Nikkwa Life Ins. Co., Kyodo Trust Co., etc.; b. 1897, Tokyo; s. of Raita Fujiyama. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Keio Univ. 1922; studied in Europe & America. Address: 14 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.
Mem. House of Peers; b. Aug. 1862, Saga-ken; s. of Kakuzaemon Fujiyama. Career: studied at Keio Univ. Address: 14 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers since Jan. 1937; b. Nov. 1871, Gunma-ken. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ. 1891; journalist 1893-1900; entered Bk. of Japan 1901; attended Paris Peace Conf. 1919; Washington Disarm. Conf. and Geneva Int'l Econ. Conf. 1921; Govt. Delegate, Int'l. Conf. London 1933; Gov. Bk. of Japan 1935-37. Address: 51 Hikawa-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Nanyo Takushoku K. K.; b. Jan. 1877, Osaka; s. of Motomu Fukao. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1899; elected Peer 1928. Address: 30 Ichigaya Naka-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1874, Ibaraki-ken; s. of late Tamegoro Fukasaku. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Univ. 1900; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same, 1912; sent abroad for study, 1916; took degree, 1912. Address: 902 Sendagaya 5-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Nagaoka Higher Tech. Sch. since 1923; b. 1881, Osaka. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; apptd. Prof. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1916; sent to Europe and America for study 1919-21. Address: Gakko-machi, Nagaoka.

Pres. Nambei Takushoku K. K.; b. Nov. 1874, Fukuoka; s. of Isaku Motoki, later adopted by late Nobuzo Fukuhara; m. Shizu. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1899; Dir. and Chief Engr. of Tokyo Works, Kanegafuchi Spinning Co., made inspection tour of Europe and America. Address: 28 Higashi-Shinano-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Shiseido Co. Ltd.; b. July 1883, Tokyo; s. of late Arinobu Fukuhara, company director. Career: grad. Chiba Medical Coll. 1907; studied at Columbia Univ. 1908-11; made special study of mfg. and sales of toilet preparations in New York for many yrs.; on way home toured Europe; started Fukuhara Shiseido with his brother 1916. Address: 278 Chojamaru Kamiosaki, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

b. Sept. 1874, Yokohama; s. of late Genjiro Fukui, merchant. Career: grad. Yokohama Com. Coll.; succeeded to father's business in 1898; connected with Sankyo Co. since 1908; travelled abroad twice; Dir. Sankyo Co., Harley-Davidson Motorcycle Sales Co., Koto Trading Co. Address: 14 Hikawa-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.
Businessman; retired from Mitsui Firm as adviser 1936. (See 1936 issue).

n: FUKUKITA, Yasunosuke 福喜多靖之助
t: Councillor to Dirs. Oji Paper Mfg. Co. since 1933; Dir. Japan Wire Cloth Co.; b. Mar. 1874, Miye-ken; s. of Hedahei Fukukita. Career: grad. Higher Sch. Dept. Doshisha 1898; Stanford Univ. 1904; Non-Official Staff, American Embassy in Tokyo, 1906; made inspection tour of U. S. A. and Canada 1935. Publication: “Cha-no-Yu, Tea Cult of Japan.” Address: 48 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Commissioner of Manchoukuo Customs, Dairen; b. July 1892, Hyogo-ken; s. of Dr. Kosaku Fukumoto. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1905; joined Chinese Customs Service; present post since June, 1932. Address: 3 Iki-machi, Dairen.

Company Director; Pres. Tohoku Shoji Kaisha; Dir. Mito Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1888, Kumamoto-ken. Career: grad. Nagasaki Higher Com. Sch.; joined Yamashita Steamship Co. 1910; Mng.-Dir. same; Dir. Yamashita Gomei Kaisha; Aud. Yamashita Mining Co.; Mng.-Dir. Hanshin Harbor Co. Address: 8 Shimo-Osaki 2-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Compiler, Shain-kai. S. M. R. Co. since 1934; b. Feb. 1898, Niigata-ken; s. of Major-Gen. Tsukasa Kato. Career: studied at Tokyo Seijo Middle Sch.; entered journalism; writer for magazines; author of anthologies, true stories, short stories. Address: 58, Fushimi-cho, Dairen.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. Dec. 1891, Tokyo; s. of Suiken Funabashi, Peer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Bank of Japan; elected Peer 1925; Parl. Councillor of Justice 1934-36. Address: 1908 Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Dir. Mitsubishi Mining Co., Mitsubishi Elec. Mfg. Co.; b. Dec. 1877, Ehime-ken; s. of Nobue Funada; m. Toyo, d. of Seibi Honda. Career: grad. German Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha. Address: 37 Nando-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.
Retired Vice-Admiral. (See 1936 issue.)

Dir.-Gen. Japanese Cotton Mill Owners' Assn., Shanghai since 1926; b. Aug. 1873, Saga-ken; s. of Saikichi Funatsu, farmer. Career: Student Interpreter of Foreign Office; 1894 served in Russo-Japanese War; apptd. Chancellor, Foreign Office, serving at Chefoo, Tientsin, Shanghai, Yingkow, Chicago, New York; Vice-Consul at Nanking 1905; Consul, Hongkong 1908; same, Nanking; Secr. Legation at Peking 1914; Consul-General, Tientsin 1919; Shanghai, 1923. Address: c/o the above association, Yokohama Specie Bank Bldg., Shanghai.
