Dir. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha since 1937; Mgr. Freight Dept. same; Pres. Toyo Kaiun Kaisha; Acting Pres. Nippon Shipping Exchange; b. July 1881, Ehime-ken. Career: Grad. Tokyo Com. Coll. 1905; entered Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; promoted Mgr. Freight Dept. 1926; Japanese Maritime Employers' Del. to Gen. Conf. Int'l Labour Organization at Geneva 1936. Address: Shiomidai-machi 1-chome, Suma-ku, Kobe.

Dir. Accounts Bureau Gen. Affairs Board State Council of Manchoukuo since 1935; b. 1900, Tokyo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1924; entered Finance Dept.; Commr. Building & Repairs Adm. Bureau; Commr. Manchoukuo State Council 1932; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec.; Sec. Chief Personnel Bureau 1934-36. Address: c/o Gen. Affairs Board, State Council, Hsinking.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. Taiwan Army; b. Sept. 1882, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Kan Furusho. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Mil. Staff Coll. 1912; Dir. Personal Bureau War Office; Chief 1st Dept. Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. 11th Div.; Vice-Minister for War 1935-36; Dir. Army Air Service Dept. Address: Taiwan Army Hdqrs. Taihoku.
Mng.-Dir. Showa Coal Co.; b. May 1867, Nagano-ken; s. of Shigetake Furuta. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1891. Address: 555 Denen-chofu 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Justice Minister of Manchoukuo since 1936; b. 1888, Gifu-ken; s. of Shojiro Furuta. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; apptd. Judge, 1916; Procurator Tokyo District & Local Courts; Councillor Justice Dept. 1923; Instructor Police training Inst. 1924; despatched to Europe & America 1928; Judge Supreme Court; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Justice Dept. of Manchou 1933-36. Address: 8 Yashima-dori, Hsinking.

Dir. Sumitomo Honsha Ltd.; Mng.-Dir. Manshu Kokan K. K.; b. Oct. 18[?]6, Kyoto-fu; s. of Kazuma Inoue, later adopted by Furuta family. Career: grad. Mining & Metal. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; joined Sumitomo Firm; Mng.-Dir. Sumimoto Metal Industries Co. Ltd. Address: 359 Nakano, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Court of Adm. Litigation since 1934; b. Feb. 1878, Toyama-ken; s. of Hyotaro Futagami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; Councillor, Communications Dept.; Secr. Com. Minister; Judge, Court of Adm. Litigation; attended World Telegraphic Conf.; Chief Secr. Privy Council. Address: 1373 Kami-Meguro 6-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Co. Dir.; Mng-Dir. Japan Artificial Fertilizer Co.; Pres. Nippon Yushi (Oil & Fat) K. K.; b. June 1868, Ehime-ken; s. of Shinzo Futagami. Career: grad. Law Dept. Chuo Univ. 1895; founded Tokyo Mousseline-de-Laine Spinning Co. 1897; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha 1901; Mgr. Nagoya and Moji Branches; Asst.-Mgr. Coal Dept.; Acting Pres. Super-Phosphate Ind. Assn.; returned to Diet from Ehime-ken 1918. Address: 41 Yarai-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman Miike Nitrogen Ind. Co.; Dir. Mitsui Mining Co.; b. 1871, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Kunio Fuwa. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1859; entered Shibaura Engrg. Works; Prof. 5th Higher Sch.; Engr. Mitsui Mining Co.; went to Europe & America 1911; Chief Yamano Mining Office; Tagawa Mining Office. Address: 513 Yoyogi-Hatsudai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Consul-Gen. of Republic of Ecuador in Japan; b. Jan. 1899, Riobamba, Ecuador. Address: Imp. Apmts. Room 31-32, Consulate-General of Ecuador, 25 Yamashita-cho, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

French Consul-General at Yokohama since 1937; b. Nov. 1878 Provins (Seine et Marne); s. of Maurice Gallois, judge; m. Marie-Rose Pairard. Career: French Embassy Tokyo 1903-18; Consul, Keijo 1918-26; Polit. Sec. Foreign Office, Paris 1927-37. Address: 185 Yamate-cho, Naka-ku, Yokohama.
Honorary Consul for Norway at Kobe and Osaka since 1928; n. Norwegian; b. May 1879 in Vesteraalen, Norway. Address: 45 Harima-machi, Kobe.

Teacher; b. 1894, Oil City, Pa., U. S. A.; n. American; s. of William Jefferson Gealy, Private Secr. to the Chambers' Trust Estate, Oil City, Pa. Career: grad. Allegheny Coll. A.B.; Boston Univ. Sch. of Theology, S. T. B.; Graduate study in Harvard Univ.; Univ. of Basel, Univ. of Berlin; Union Theol. Seminary, S. T. M., Boston Univ. Ph. D.; Minister to Townville, Pa., in the Methodist Episcopal Church, 1921-23; Prof. New Testament, Aoyama Gakuin since 1923; Editor, Japan Christian Year Book, 1935-36. Address: 3 Aoyama Gakuin, Midorigaoka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Financier and Executive; b. 1872, Albany, New York. Career: Dir. Tokyo Elec. Co.; Nipponophone Co.; Columbia Grahmophone Co.; Shibaura Engrg. Works; Japan Steel Products Co.; Corn Products Refining Co., Frazar Estate Co. Address: 527 Yaesu Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Dir. Personnel Bureau Gen. Affairs Bd. Manchoukuo State Council; b. Oct. 1899, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Harushichi Genda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923; entered Finance Dept.; Supt. Sapporo Revenue Office; Chief Fin. Sec. Kwantung Govt.-Gen. 1927-32; Dir. Revenue Bureau Fin. Dept. Address: Nishiki-machi, Hsinking.

1st Lieut. U. S. Army; b. 1899, Scotland, G. B.; s. of William George; m. Ethel Louise George. Career: Enlisted U. S. Army 1917; Rice Institute 1916-17; grad. U. S. Military Academy 1920; Cavalry Sch. 1921; Signal Sch. 1935; served with 57th Inf., 19th Inf., 3rd Cav., 5th Cav., Spec. Duty Hq., 2nd Corps Area, and Aide-de-Camp to Commanding Gen. 1st Division; at present language student attached to American Embassy. Address: c/o American Embassy, Tokyo.

1st Order of Vasa, Sweden; Exchange Broker; b. May 1876, Malmö, Sweden; m. Marie Weinberger. Career: grad. Malmö Högre Almänna Läroverk; after 4 years' com. training in Hamburg, Germany, came to Japan and joined A. Meier & Co. 1896; Partner, same-firm 1910-17; Swedish Vice-Consul, Yokohama 1906-16; Consul 1919; Dir. Winkel & Gedde, Ltd. Kobe & Yokohama 1918-22. Address: c/o Elked & Gerdts, 14 Marunouchi 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Diplomat; Turkish Ambassador to Japan since Mar. 1936; b. 1888, Edirne, Turkey; married d. of S. O. Kermaari, ex-Amb. Career: started his career as Mem. General Staff Off. of Turkish Republic; is a close friend of Pres. Kämal Atatürk; Mil. Attaché in Athens, later Comdr. in Balkan War and Great War; elected Rep.; apptd. Minister to Hungary 1924; to Bulgaria; Amb. to Iran, during the post settled the difficult border trouble. Address: 47 Kamiyama-machi Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

B.A.; French Consul at Mukden since 1937; b. Oct. 1896 at Paris; s. of Paul Germain, agronomist; m. Dubreux. Career: grad. Univ. of Paris, Oriental Language Inst. Paris; Vice-Consul, Peking 1922-26; Consul, Keijo 1926-29; Vice-Consul, Shanghai 1930; Consul, Swatow 1930-31; Nanking, 1931-32; Asst. Consul, Tientsin 1932-35; First Chinese Secr. French Leg. Peking 1935; Consul Adjoint, Embassy, Peking 1935-36. Address: French Consulate, Mukden.

D.E.; Ordnance Vice-Admiral; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1877, Kanazawa; s. of late Takuji Godo. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; entered naval service; Chief Ordnance Dept. Kure Naval Dockyard; Steel Mfg. Dept. of same; Ordnance Testing Dept.; Chief Aviation Dept. Hiro Arsenal; sent to Europe & America 6 times; Chief, Kure Nav. Dockyard 1924; attached to Nav. Tech. Dept. 1927; retired 1928; Dir. S. M. R. Co.; Pres. Showa Steel Works 1934-36; Minister of Com. & Ind. in Hayashi Cabinet 1937; toured U. S. 1937. Address: 36 Kikui-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Mgr. for Japan, Chemical Construction Corp.; b. 1879, Leoben, Austria; s. of Edward Goedicke, Steel Works Mgr. Career: grad. Heidelberg Univ.; went to America; employed in various chemical works. Address: 1733 Fukuzawa-machi, 4-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers since 1911; b. Jan. 1865, Tokyo; s. of late Baron Junzo Goh. Career: went to Germany to study economics 1884; received Ph. D. deg. 1890; entered business 1895; high taxpayer in Tokyo-fu; Pres. Japan and Tokyo Chambers of Com. & Ind. till 1937; retired from active business 1937. Address: 28 Kami-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (merger of Mitsubishi Shipbldg. Co., Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. and Yokohama Dock Co.) since 1935; Dir. Manchuria Air Transport Co. since 1936; b. Nov. 1882, Iwate-ken; s. of Tamasaburo Goko; m. Naoye. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; joined the Mitsubishi; Mgr. Hankow and Wakamatsu Br. Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Dir. and Business Mgr. Mitsubishi Shipbldg. Co. 1928; Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Aircrft Co. 1932. Address: 645 Yamanouchi, Kita-Kamakura, Ohfuna-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Mar. 1884, Oita-ken; s. of late Yoshitomo Goto, official; m. Haru, sister of Viscount Hisaakira Kano. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Chief, Police Dept. Aomori-ken; went to Europe and America for inspection, 1917; Councillor, Home Dept. 1919; Secr. to Home Minister 1920; Dir. Police Bureau, Home Dept. 1922; Secr.-Gen. Taiwan Govt. 1924-28; Pres. Japan Young Men's Assn. 1930; nominated Peer; Agr. & Forestry Min. in Saito Cabinet, 1932-34; Home Min., 1934-36. Address: 29 Konno, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. Co., Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co.; Dir. Sangu Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co., etc.; b. Apr. 1881, Nagano-ken; s. of Kikuemon Kobayashi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Supervision Bureau, Ry. Dept. 1920; resigned and entered business. Address: 49 Hasedo, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Company Director; b. 1891, Oita-ken; s. of Mitsuhiko Goto. Career: grad. Hosei Univ. 1911; joined Yomiuri Shimbun-sha; Chief, Econ. Sec. same; entered business. Address: 35 Kuruma-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.
Secr. Tokyo Club; b. Feb. 1885, Yokohama; s. of William Graham, engr. Career: studied at Winton House, Yokohama; with L. J. Healing & Co. Ltd. 1901-33. Address: 13-F Reinanzaka, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Diplomat; American Amb. to Japan since 1932; A.B. (Harvard Univ. 1902); LL.D. (George Washington Univ. 1926); b. May 1880, Boston; s. of Edward Sturgis Grew. Career: grad. Groton Sch. 1898; Harvard Univ. 1902; travelled extensivley in Europe & the East; Clerk in Cons.-General Cairo 1904; Vice-Consul Cairo 1904-06; 3rd Secr. Amer. Emb. Mexico City 1906-07; St. Petersburg 1907-08; 2nd Secr. Emb. Berlin 1908-11; Secr. Emb. Vienna 1911-12; Secr. Emb. Berlin 1912-16; Counsellor of same 1917; Counsellor Emb. and Chargé d'Affaires at time of break of diplomatic relations with Austria-Hungary Vienna 1917; assigned to Dept. of State Washington May 1917; Acting Chief Western European Affairs Div. Mar. 1918; attended Pre-Armistice Negotiations Versailles as Secr. Amer. Delegation Oct.-Nov. 1918; Secr.-Gen. Am. Commission to negotiate Peace with rank of E.E. & M.P. Paris Nov. 1918; assigned as Am. Secr. on Int'l Secretariat of Peace Conf. Jan. 1919; E.E. & M.P. to Denmark 1920; to Switzerland 1921; Am. Rep., Conference on Near Eastern Affairs Lausanne 1922-23; negotiated and signed Treaty with Turkey 1923; Am. Unofficial Rep. with Temporary Mixed Commn. of League of Nations for control of Traffic in Arms Geneva & Paris 1924; Under Secr. of State 1924-27; served as Chairman Personnel Examining and Sch. Boards of Foreign Service and as Mem. Central Comm. Am. Red Cross; Amb. to Turkey 1927-32. Address: Amer. Emb. Tokyo.

Prof. of Business English, Yamaguchi Coll. of Com.; b. Oct. 1909, Bethlehem, Penn., U. S. A.; s. of Wm. C. Groman. Career: Member of Pennsylvania Young Republican State Execute Committee before coming to Japan; grad. Temple Univ. Coll. of Com.; taught at Bethlehem High Sch. 1932-35; rec'd “Sonin” rank. Address: Shiraishi, Yamaguchi City.

American Consul, Dairen since 1934; b. Mar. 1901, Newark, N. J., U. S. A. Career: grad. Newark Academy; Nat. Univ. of Mexico, 1922; Princeton, (B. A.), 1923; 3rd Secr. Mexico City 1924; Hague and Madrid, 1927; detailed to Conf. of Int'l Chamber of Com. Stockholm, 1927; 3rd Secr. Port au Prince, 1928; 2nd Secr. 1929; Consul 1934. Address: American Consulate, Dairen.
Belgian Consul at Harbin; b. Mar. 1893; m. Gramme Delia. Address: Belgian Consulate, Harbin.
Accountant; b. June 1888, Hackettstown, New Jersey, U. S. A. Career: grad. New York Univ. (B.C.S.); joined Standard Oil Co. of New York; Standard Vacuum Oil Co. Address: 250 Bluff, Yokohama.

Mgr. Hotel New Osaka, Osaka since 1934; b. May 1897, Chiba-ken; s. of Fukutaro Gunji; m. Nobuko. Career: grad. Okura Higher Com. Sch.; joined The Imp. Hotel, Tokyo 1924; was in France, England, Germany, Italy, America to study hotel business 1930-33. Address: 19 Imazu Urakaze, Nishinomiya City.
D.L.; Com. Secr. German Emb. Tokyo; b. Sept. 1896, Bremen. Career: since 1922 in diplo. service at Paris, Addis Ababa, Shanghai, Peking, Geneva; in Tokyo since Apr. 1934. Address: German Emb. Tokyo.

Marquis; Naturalist; b. Feb. 1903, Tokyo; s. of late Marquis Masaaki Hachisuka. Career: grad. Magdalene Coll. Cambridge; went on expeditions to Egypt 1923-24; Arctic Region in Iceland 1925; Corsica Is. 1925 & 1926; French North Africa 1927; Philippine Island 1929; Belgian Congo, Africa 1931. Address: 9, Mita Tsuna-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Adviser Mitsubishi Heavy-Industries Ltd.; b. 1870, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Shinzo Ichinose, later adopted by Sayo Hamada. Career: Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1891; Chief Engine Dept. Nagasaki Works, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; Vice-chief and later Chief of the Works; Mng.-Dir. and then Chairman of the Company; twice went to Europe & Amer. Address: 6 Kudan 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Mar. 1868, Miye-ken; adopted by Seizaburo Hamada. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogaku-in; elected Rep. 12 times; Vice-Speaker House of Rep.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Justice in Tanaka Cabinet 1927-29; speaker 1934-36. Address: 18 Naka-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. phil.; Prof. of German 8th Higher Sch.; b. Nov. 1909, Dresden; m. geb. Grummt Charlotte. Career: grad. Gymnasium; entered Leipzig Univ. Phil. Fakultaet and studied languages of Eastern Asia, Mongolian, Chinese and Japanese; with present sch. since 193[?]. Address: 13 Nakayama-cho 5-chome, Nagoya.

D.L.; Lawyer; b. Sept. 1874, Tokyo; s. of Shinsetsu Hanaoka, later adopted by Kichijiro Hanaoka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; studied Int'l Com. Law in P.-G. Course; joined Takao Kikuchi's Office; rec'd deg. 1918; Hon. Mem. Philippine Bar Assn. Address: 1611 Nogata-machi 2-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Minister of Economics; b. 1893, in Chinchow, Kwantung Province. Career: grad. Nagoya Higher Tech. Sch. 1917; Pres. Toa Ind. Co.; Pres. Asia Flour Mills; Dir. Harbin Exchange; Dir. Harbin Trust Co.; Councillor Heilung-kiang Prov. Office 1931; Dir. Ind. & Fin. Bureaux Heilungkiang Prov. 1932; Mayor of Hsinking 1935-37. Address: Dept. of Economics, Hsinking.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr. Chinkai Naval Station since 1936; b. Oct. 1885, Kochi City. Career: grad. Naval Academy 1905; Naval Staff Coll. 1920; despatched to Europe & Amer. 1926; Chief Instructer Nav. Gunnery Sch. 1927-28; Captain “Haguro” 1929; “Ise” 1930; “Nagato” 1931; Dir. Nav. Gunnery Sch. 1932-34; Comdr. 6th Battle Sqadron 1935; 1st and 3rd Battle Sqdr. 1936. Address: Chinkai Nav. Stan. Chinkai.

Dir. Tokyo Revenue Supt. Bureau since July 1937; b. Dec. 1890, Shimane-ken; s. of Gonzaburo Hara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; entered Finance Dept.; Chief Kokura & Yokohama Revenue Supt. Offices; Bank Inspector; Chief Investment Sec. and Deposits Sec.; Dir. Osaka Revenue Supt. Bureau 1935-36; Econ. Adviser Kwantung Army 1936-37. Address: c/o Finance Office Tokyo.

Pres. Aikoku Life Ins. Co., Japan Air Transport Co.; Chairman Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co.; b. June 1886, Osaka-fu; adopted by Rokuro Hara. Career: grad. 3rd Higher Sch. 1904; Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1907; Japanese Delegate Int'l Chamber of Com. Conf. Washington 1931; went to U. S. as Mem. Japanese Goodwill Mission Mar. 1937. Address: 325 Kitashinagawa 3-chome Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Counsellor Manchoukuo Emb. Tokyo; b. Feb. 1901, Tokyo; s. of Makoto Hara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923; entered S.M.R.; Acting Chief Peking Br.; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Kirin Prov. 1931; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Secretariat, Gen. Affairs Board State Council 1932; Counsellor Manchoukuo Embassy Tokyo 1933; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Jehol Prov. 1934-37. Address: Manchoukuo Embassy Tokyo.

Pres. Osaka Kikai Kosakusho Ltd. since 1933; b. 1882, Saga-ken; s. of Chuzo Kanezaki; later adopted by Hara family. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; invited by Chuan Han Ry. Co., Szechwan, China; Engr. Oita-ken & Saitama-ken; resigned 1923; joined Hunter & Co.; Dir. of present firm 1924; Chairman 1919. Address: Shijidera-machi, Tennoji-ku, Osaka.

Silk Exporter; Pres. Yokohama Koshin Ginko; b. 1868, Gifu-ken; s. of Hisao Aoki; later adopted by Hara family. Career: grad. Tokyo Technical Sch. 1890. Address: 48 Bentendori 3-chome, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Pres. Japan Explosive Co. Ltd., Chosen Spinning & Weaving Co., Ltd., Teikoku Dye-stuff Mfg. Co. Ltd., Kyowa Leather Co.; Dir. Ishin Chemical Ind. Co., Chugai Sangyo Co., Shinshin Concrete Ind. Co., Yingkow Spinning & Weaving Co., Ltd., Manchuria Hemp Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Advisor, Manchuria Tobacco Co., Ltd.; Aud., North Manchuria Gold Mine, Ltd. and Dir. Advisor or Aud. of several other companies. Career: grad. Com. Coll., Waseda Univ., 1909; Mng.-Dir., Kinko-do Publishing Co. Ltd.; and later Pres., same; Aud., Japan Explosive Co. Ltd., 1921; Sr. Mng.-Dir. same, 1923; then present post. Address: 20 of 3, Fujimi-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Privy Councillor; b. Feb. 1867, Nagano-ken; s. of Kosaku Hara, clansman. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Probationer and Councillor, Agr. & Co. Dept.; admitted to bar 1893; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ., Waseda and Chuo Univ., rec'd deg. 1907; Dir. Mitsui Trust Co. 1924; Justice Minister 1927. Address: 2 Fujimi-cho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. June 1875, Shimane-ken; s. of Ikujiro Hara. Career: grad. French Law Dept. Franco-Japanese Law Coll. 1896; Judge, Hiroshima Local Court; Secr. to Justice Min.; Pub. Procurator, Tokyo District Court; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; sent to Europe for study of Jury System, Juvenile Law 1908-13; Parl. Vice-Justice Minister 1934-36. Address: 40 Nando-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Asst. Prof. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. Head Surgeon, Izumibashi Charity Hospital; b. Dec. 1888, Nagano-ken; s. of late Tamijiro Hara. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Asst. of same, 1917-20; studied surgery in Germany and Switzerland 1920-22; rec'd deg. 1924; Dir. and Head Surgeon, Otsuka Sanatorium, 1924-25. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.
Pres. Harada Trading Co.; b. Mar. 1886, Osaka; s. of Genjiro Harada. Career: succeeded to family estate. Address: 37 Yuraku-cho, Nishinari-ku, Osaka.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr-in-Chief 3rd Fleet; b. 1883, Fukui-ken; s. of Jichu Hasegawa. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1903; Nav. Staff Coll.; Secr. to Navy Minister; Nav. Attache Emb. Washington; Chief 1st Sec. Personnel Bureau of Navy; Captain “Nagato”; Chief Staff Yokosuka Nav. Stn.; Comdr. 2nd Submarine Sqn.; Chief 5th Sec. Nav. Tech. Dept. 1930; Vice-Min. of Navy; fought at Shanghai in Sino-Japanese hostilities 1937. Address: 718 Kitashinagawa 3-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

n: HASEGAWA, Tetsutaro 長谷川鐵太郎
t: Pres. Dainichi Elec. Wire Co.; Dir. Yokohama Rubber Co.; Manchoukuo Elec. Wire Co.; Furukawa Electric Co.; b. Jan. 1884, Tokyo; s. of late Viscount Torao Komeda; later adopted by Kiyo Hasegawa. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Mass. Inst. of Tech. and Yale Univ. Address: 118 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

n: HASHIMOTO, Denzaemon 橋本傳左衞門
t: D. Agr.; Prof. Agr. Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. July 1887, Saitama-ken; s. of Genshichi Hashimoto. Career: grad. Agricultural Dept. Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1910; joined Nippon Kangyo Ginko 1910-19; rec'd deg. 1920; went to Europe & Amer. for study; apptd. Lecturer Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1924; Dean 1924-26; 1933-35; Adviser Kwantung Army 1934. Address: 50 Kitashirakawa Ogura-cho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Nippon Oil Co.; b. Sept. 1865, Nagaoka City; s. of Yajuro Hashimoto; m. Chiseko, sister of Asatoro Yamane, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Secr. Privy Council; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Dir. National Debts Consolidation Bureau, Finance Department; Dir. Finance Bureau of same; Vice-Minister of Finance; same of Agr. & Com.; nominated Peer 1912. Address: 353 Nishi-Okubo 2-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Osaka Harbor Land Co., Hamadera Real Estate Co.; Mng.-Dir. Daido Shokusan Co.; b. Feb. 1873; s. of Shigeji Hashimoto. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ. Kyoto; joined Osaka Pref. Com. Museum; Econ. Dept. Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; went to China to research cotton industry; to New York to study trust business. Address: Hamadera-Koen-mae, Osaka-fu.

Painter; Court Artist; b. 1883, Kobe; s. of Kaikwan Hashimoto. Career: studied Chinese Classics & Poems under father; Japanese Painting with Seiho Takeuchi; won Special Choises twice and 2nd Prize 3 times in Educ. Dept. Fine Arts Exhibitions. Address: Ginkakuji-mae, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

n: HASHIMOTO, Manyemon 橋本萬右衞門
t: Acting Partner, Hashimoto & Co.; Dir. Koriyama Godo Bank; Chairman, Koriyama Warehousing Co.; b. June 1892, Fukushima-ken; s. of Manyemon Hashimoto, Peer. Career: studied banking in Europe and America. Address: 747 Takinogawa-machi, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem. House of Peers; b. Mar. 1891, Tokyo; s. of Sanehide Hashimoto; m. Naoko Hashimoto. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Commr. Agr. & Forestry Dept.; Secr. to Prime Minister 1929; Parl. Councillor, Home Dept. 1934-36. Address: 1290 Kaigan-dori, Yuigahama, Kamakura.

Mng.-Dir. Nippon Mutual Savings Bk.; b. Aug. 1870, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kahei Hashimoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; joined Nippon Life Ins. Co. 1895-1921; studied Ins. Sci. at Göttingen Univ.; Dir. Sumitomo Life Ins. Co.; Hyogo Daido Trust Co. Address: 1580 Sumiyoshi-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.
Pres. Settsu Shosen Kaisha; b. Dec. 1882, Osaka-fu; s. of Juichiro Hashimoto. Career: grad. Osaka Com. Sch. 1900; Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1904. Address: 847 Kita-Renge, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Nov. 1868, Oita-ken; s. of Yuzo Hashimoto. Career: grad. Senshu Univ.; Aud. Japan Typewriter Co.; Pres. Nagasaki Iron Works; Dir. Fukagawa Dockyard Co.; same, Hashimoto Trading Co. Address: 6 Motozono-cho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Asano Bussan Kaisha; b. 1874, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Orai Hashimoto. Career: grad. Georgetown Univ. 1910; went to Europe; Chief, Fukuoka Branch, New York Life Ins. Co.; same, Yokohama Branch; Mng.-Dir. Joto Elec. Ry. Co.; Mng.-Dir. Nippon Chuya Ginko; Capitalists Delegate to Sailors' Labor Conf. at Geneva 1920. Address: 11 Omote-cho 4-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Dai-Nippon Brewery Co.; Aud. Tokyo Hat Co.; b. Mar. 1869, Okayama-ken; s. of Zenzaburo Hashimoto, farmer. Career: grad. Mech. Course Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1894; apptd. Chief, Mech. Dept. Nippon Beer Co. in 1906; amalgamating 2 competing beer breweries of Sapporo and Osaka, became Chief, Tech. Dept. of new firm; Dr. Yokohama Glass Mfg. Co. and Nippon Glass Ind. Co. Address 50 Kageoka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Major-Gen.; b. 1882, Miye-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1913; Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in Russia; Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Mil. Attache Legation Poland; Emb. U.S.S.R.; Chief Mil. Press Bureau War Office 1936-37. Address: War Dept. Tokyo.

General; Inspector-Gen. of Mil. Education; High Mil. Councillor; b. July 1879, Tokyo; s. of Yoshikata Hata. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1901; Chief Secr. Gen. Staff; Comdr. 4th Field Heavy Artil. Brigade; Chief 4th Dept. Gen. Staff Office; 1st Dept. same; Artil. Inspector; Comdr. 14th Div. 1933; Chief Army Air Service Dept. Address: War Dept. Tokyo.

Sr. Mng.-Dir. Asano Portland Cement Co., Chosen; Dir. Chugoku Gypsum Co.; b. Feb. 1879; s. of Asaki Hata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; Mgr. Hokkaido Industrial Co. upon graduation; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept., Asano Portland Cement Co., 1917. Address: 1290, Sugamo 6-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Ph. D.; LL.D.; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; Dir. Asamushi Marine Biological Stn. Aomori-ken; Dir. Palao Marine Stn. for Tropical Biology; b. 18[?]6, Aomori-ken; s. of Idzumi Hatai. Career: grad. Tohoku Gakuin; studied Zoology & Neurology at Chicago Univ.; Ph. D. 1903; Prof. Wister Inst. of Anatomy & Biology 1918; studied Zoological Physiology in U. S. A. 1928; LL.D. 1933. Address: 17 Kotodai-dori, Sendai.

Asst. Mng.-Dir. The Domei National News Agency; b. Dec. 1882, Nara-ken; s. of Yoshitoshi Hatakeyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Communications Department; Dir. Nagoya Com. Bureau; same, Postal & Telegraphic Bureau; same, Telegraphic Affairs Bureau; Dir. Taiwan Elec. Power Co. Address: 251 Hyakunin-cho 2-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; b. Feb. 1884, Tokyo; bro. of Ichiro Hatoyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Asst. Prof. same, 1910; studied Civil Law in Germany and France; Prof. Civil Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; rec'd deg. 1917; Attended League of Nations Assembly, Geneva 1917; Econ. Conf. Genoa 1922. Address: [?] Kobinatadai-machi 3-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Leader, Seiyukai Party; b. Jan. 1883, Tokyo; s. of late Kazuo Hatoyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; called to the bar; Chairman, Tokyo Municipal Assembly; Chief Secr., Tanaka Cabinet; Vice-Pres. Enthronement Commission; Educ. Minister in Inukai Cabinet; same in Saito Cabinet 1932-34; went to Europe as mission of “good understanding” manoeuvres on the Sino-Japanese Hostilities, 1937. Address 10 Otowa 7-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Tohoku Kogyo K. K. & Tohoku Shinko Denryoku K. K.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Sept. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Noriaki Hatta. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Engr. Railway Dept.; Dir. Construction Bureau; Vice-Minister of Railway 1926-29; elected Peer 1929; Vice-Pres. S. M. R. Co. 1932-35; Supreme Adviser same 1936-37. Address: 73 Kamifujimae-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; Ph. D.; D. Econ.; Prof. Waseda Univ.; Hon. Consul of Guatemala; b. Jan. 1878, Shiga-ken; s. of Matashichi Hattori. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1902; Princeton Univ.; Berlin Univ.; apptd. Chief Secr. Tokyo Chamber of Com.; Dir. Chamber of Com. of Japan; Pres. Japan Times; Delegate and Vice-Pres. Pan-Pacific Com. Conf. 1922. Address: 11 Waseda-Minami-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Kokugakuin Univ.; b. June 1867, Fukushima-ken; s. of Tohachi Hattori. Career: grad. Philosophy Course, Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Prof. 3rd Higher Sch.; Higher Normal Sch.; Councillor to Education Minister; studied Chinese Classics in China, 1899-1902; Prof. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; rec'd deg.; Dean, Normal Sch. Dept., Peking Univ.; invited to Harvard Univ. as Prof. 1916; went to Europe, 1920; Pres. Keijo Imp. Univ. 1926. Address: 182 Suwa-cho, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. of French Lang. & Litt. at Shizuoka Higher Sch.; b. Feb. 1908, Paris; s. of Armand Hauchecorne, consul at Kobe; m. Odan (Hatsuko). Career: Secr. French Consulate, Kobe 1931-33; with present sch. since 1933; student of Japanese Language, Literature, Music, Arts, History and other Oriental subjects. Address: 36 Kita Ando, Shizuoka.
M. A. (Cantab); Patent Attorney; b. Aug. 1872, Lewisham Kent, England. Career: resident in Japan since 1898; author of “A.B.C. of Go.” Address: 446 Marunouchi Bldg. Tokyo.

Czechoslovakian Minister to Tokyo; b. 1886, Keiv; s. of F. Havlicek, industrialist. Career: grad. Univs. in Prague and Vienna; apptd. Secretary of Legation in Vienna; Private Secr. to Prime Minister in Prague; Councillor of Leg. and Chargé d'Affaires, Berlin; Minister to Brussels. Address: 22 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo

Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Trading Co. since 1934; b. Apr. 1882, Tokyo; s. of Mitsunosuke Hayakawa; m. Hanako. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; joined present firm; Chief, Kobe Branch, Ship Dept.; Gen. Mgr. Head Office. Address: 1113 Zoshigaya 7-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Tokyo Bus Co.; Mng.-Dir. Tokyo Underground Ry. Co.; b. Oct. 1881, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Tsunetomi Hayakawa. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1908; Secr. S. M. R. Co.; Mgr. Koya Railway Co. went to Europe 1914; studied Tube System in London. Address: 1184 Naka-Meguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt. (1921); Pres. Keijo Imp. Univ. since 1935; b. Oct. 1876, Okayama-ken; s. of Jun Hayami. Career: grad. Phil. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; apptd. Prof. Yamaguchi and 1st Higher Schs.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Keijo Law Coll. 1924; studied in Europe and America; Prof. Keijo Imp. Univ. 1926. Address: 5024 Higashi-Shiken-cho, Keijo, Chosen.

Baron; Privy Councillor since 1934; Chairman, Anglo-Japanese Soc.; b. Mar. 1860. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1887; Chief, Com. Affairs Bureau; Ambassador to Italy; Minister to China; Gov. Kwantung Govt.; Amb. to Britain; Grand Master of Ceremonies; went to England as Adviser to H. I. H. Prince Chichibu, 1925; went to Manchoukuo as attendant to Special Envoy H. I. H. Prince Chichibu 1934. Address: 23 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Count; D. Litt.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1874; grand s. of late Count Yasuyuki Hayashi. Career: grad. Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; sent to Europe 1903; Prof. Peers' Sch. 1904; Master of Ceremonies 1906; Prof. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; rec'd deg. 1919; Pres. S. Manchuria Ry. Co. 1932-35. Address: 399 Hatagayahon-machi 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Okura Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; b. May 1866, Oita-ken; s. of Kempei Ishii; later adopted by Toshihisa Hayashi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1890; entered, Railway Dept.; Mgr. Nippon Land & Marine Ins. Co.; Dir. & Mgr. Nihon Fire Ins. Co.; entered Okuragumi, 1909. Address: 18 Ichigaya Kaga-cho 2-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Econ.; Prof. and Librarian, Waseda Univ.; b. Sept. 1883, Okayama-ken; s. of Tanejiro Fujii and adopted by Kumano Hayashi. Career: grad. Law Dept. Waseda Univ. 1905; rec'd deg. 1927. Address: 210 Hatagaya 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Mem. Imp. Academy; Ex-Pres. Keio Univ.; Dir. Radio Corporation of Japan; b. May 1872, Saga-ken; s. of Seishichiro Nakamura, and later adopted by Takisaburo Hayashi. Career: grad. Litt. Dept. Keio Univ. 1895; studied in France 1901-05; Prof. Keio Univ., 1905; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Com.; returned to Diet from Kanagawa-ken 4 times; attended 3rd World Parl. Com. Congress, Belgium; Councillor, Foreign Office; attended Wash. Wisarm. Conf. 1921. Address: 99 Date, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; b. Sept. 1878, Saitama-ken; s. of Reizo Miwa; later adopted by Yusho Hayashi. Career: grad. Tokyo Law Coll. 1897; Judge Tokyo Local Court; Miyagi Court of Appeal; Tokyo Court of Appeal; Procurator Supreme Court; Dir. Criminal Bureau Justice Dept.; Vice-Minister of Justice; Procurator Supreme Court 1927; rec'd deg. 1920; Delegate to Int'l Forgery Prevention Conf. Geneva 1929; Pres. Supreme Court till Mar. 1936; Justice Minister in Hirota Cabinet 1936-37. Address: 13 Minami-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.
M.P.; b. Aug. 1890, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Fukuzo Hayashi. Career: Mem. Hokkaido Assembly; Parl. Councillor of Overseas Affairs 1935-36. Address: 9 Hikawa-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
General on the reserve list. (See 1936 issue).

Mem. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Ujigawa Elec. Power Co.; Ujiden Bldg. Co., Ujiden Securities Co.; Dir. Omi Ry. Co.; Sanyo Elec. Ry. Co., Osaka Bldg. Co., Shinko Land & Bldg. Co., Osaka Togyo K. K.; b. Feb. 1876, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Bunjiro Hayashi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; entered Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Chief Kobe Branch. Address: 214 Okamoto, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Elec. Manufacturing Co. since 1937; b. Aug. 1888, Gifu-ken; s. of Mokuemon Hazama. Career: grad. Post-grad. course, Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1913; joined Shipbuilding Dept., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, 1914; transferred to Kobe works Mitsubishi Elec. Mfg. Co., 1921; Chief of same, 1928; Chief, Business Dept., Head Office, same, 1933. Address: 606, Kita Senzoku-cho, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

A.B.; B.J.; Journalist; b. Apr. 1895, Springfield, Missouri, U.S.A.; s. of James H. Hedges, civil engr. Career: diploma, Western Military Academy, Alton, Illinois, 1912; A.B., Drury Coll. 1917; B. J. Univ. of Missouri, 1919; successively News Editor Miami (Oklahoma) Record-Herald; Corpus Christi (Texas) Caller, feature writer Washington, D.C., Herald; Saff of Japan Advertiser Tokyo and Peking, 1920-31, Managing Editor same 1923-27; Chief Far Eastern Bureau Christian Science Monitor 1927-31; Staff Corr., Tokyo, London Times 1930-31; Contributor to American, English, Japanese magazines; occasional lecturer; Executive Secretary of Press Congress of the World, 1934; Tokyo Corr. Washington D.C., Post and Kansas City (Mo.) Star and Times, 1935; served as Second Lieut. 64th Pioneer Infantry, U.S.A. during World War; Fellow American Geographical Soc.; Member Asiatic Soc. of Japan, Amer. Legion, Theta Kappa Nu, Signa Delta Chi, Phi Alpha Omega, (national pres. same 1917-18), Pi Gamma Mu, Quill and Scroll. Democrat, Congregationalist. Author of “The Kabuki Stage of Japan,” 1929, “What Do Americans Think About Japan (bi-lingual)” 1932, “In Far Japan” 1935. Address: 47 Dai-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

LL.D.; Chargé d'Affaires, Denmark Legation to Tokyo since 1931; b. Apr. 1891, Denmark. Career: grad. Law Coll. Univ. of Copenhagen; served Foreign Office since 1916. Address: 52 Hikawa-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Teacher of German, Matsuyama High Sch.; b. May 1904, Duesseldorf, Germany; s. of Alexander Hessel, engr.; m. Ilse; b. Kraemer. Career: studied at univis. of Muenter, Tuebingen, Zuerich, Bonn, Utrecht till 1928; Pastor in Western Germany 1928-31. Address: 103 Naka Ichiban-cho, Matsuyama.

Rear-Admiral; Comdr. Japanese Nav. Force stationed in Manchoukuo; b. 1886, Aichi-ken. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1906; Nav. Staff Coll.; Captain “Ohi”; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll. & Mil. Staff Coll.; Captain “Asama” & “Hyuga”; Chief Nav. Affairs Propagation Dept. of Navy; Comdr. 1st Battle Sqn.; fought and occupied the South Seas Is. in Great War as Captain of marines; Comdr. 11th Battle Sqn. 1935-36. Address: Japanese Nav. Hdqrs. Hsinking.

Dir. Mining Bureau Dept. of Com. & Ind.; b. July 1894, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Kamesuke Higashi. Career: grad. Econ. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; joined Statis. Bureau, Dept. of Agr. & Com; Patent Bureau Dept. of Com. & Ind.; Dir. Trade Bureau; Com. Affairs Bureau. Address: 191 Gotanda 6-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Higher Normal Sch.; b. 1890, Aomori-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Dir. Dairen Com. Sch.; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. North Manchuria Special District, 1932-34; same, Sankiang Prov. Address: Higher Normal Sch., Hsinking.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1868, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tsuneuemon Higuchi. Career: grad. Law and Econ. Dept. Chuo Univ., 1890; elected Representative 4 times since 1912. Address: 151 Fukazawa-machi 4-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Sept. 1870, Hokkaido; 2nd s. of Hisami Hijikata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined Bank of Japan; sent to England and Belgium; apptd. Examiner, Investigator, Secr., Dir. National Debt Bureau and Mgr., Business Dept.; Pres. Ind. Bank of Japan; Dir. Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Vice-Pres. Franco-Japanese Bank; Pres. Kyoritsu Mining Ind. Co.; Vice-Pres. Bank of Japan; Pres. same 1928-35. Address: 763 Sendagaya 4-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Address: 5 Aoyama Minami-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Min. of Manchoukuo Communications Dept.; b. Oct. 1891, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Kakumatsu Hiraide. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Trader; Pres. Hiramatsu & Co., Inc.; (Fire Ins. Agents; Foreign Mfr's Agents for Japan); b. Jan. 1878 Okayama-ken. Career grad. Tokyo Industrial Univ. Address: 7 Kojimachi 6-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1881, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Fusajiro Hirano. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1910; Corr. Jiji Shimpo; returned to Diet 5 times; Parl. Councillor, Communications Dept. 1934-36. Address: 1033 Nakanobu, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Dir., Tokuyama Soda Ind. Co., Tokuyama Iron Co., Iwai Shoten; b. Dec. 1879, Nagano-ken; s. of Chori Hirano; m. in 1904. Career: grad. Polit. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Baron (cr. 1926); D.L.; Pres. Privy Council; b. Sept. 1867, Okayama-ken; s. of Shin Hiramura, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1888; Judge 1890, Judge Tokyo Court of Appeal; Dir. Mem. House of Peers; Vice-Pres. Japan Physical Education Society; b. Feb. 1879, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Kyubei Hiranuma. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1898; returned to Diet twice; high-taxpayer in Kanagawa-ken. Address: 12 Nishi-Hiraunma-cho 2-chome, Kanagawa-ku, Yokohama.

Chairman Nippon Seitetsu K.K. since July 1937; Mem. House of Peers (nominated Nov. 1935); b. May 1867, Gifu-ken; s. of Tokikoto Tanaka, later adopted by Tadatatsu Hirao. Career: grad. Co. for 40 yrs.; Chairman Kawasaki Dockyard Co. and Dir. of several other firms; went to South America as Chairman Japanese Econ. Mission to Brazil 1935; Educ. Minister 1936-37. Dir. Bank of Japan; b. Apr. 1884, Osaka-fu, s. of Ichigoro Hirase. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907. Address: 10 Komagome Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Adviser, Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. 1864, Okayama-ken; s. of Kengoro Hirata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1888; apptd. Lecturer and Councillor Waseda Univ. 1889; commenced practice in Tokyo, 1890; Lecturer, Law and Jurisprudence, Peers Sch. and Nippon Univ.; went to Europe for study 1897; removed his main office from Tokyo to Osaka 1899; Pres. of Osaka Bar [?]. Address: 80 Hinoue-cho, Kita-ku, Osaka.

Chairman Shibaura Engrg. Works; Dir. Toyo Rayon Co.; b. Oct. 1872, Gunma-ken; s. of Kojuro Hirata. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1893; entered Mitsui & Co.; Mgr. Taiwan Branch; same, Otaru Branch. Address: 228 Togoshi-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

President of Ominato Refrigerator Company; Vice-Pres. Russo-Japanese Fishery Co.; Dir. Taiheiyo Fishery, Co., etc.; b. Nov. 1881, Niigata-ken; s. of Zenji Hiratsuka. Address: 28 Sarugaku, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Hsingchung Kungssu (Kochu Koshi) since Jan. 1936; b. July 1891, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Sataro Hirayama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; entered S. M. R..; Chief, Gen. Affairs Office, Ry. Dept. same; Asst. Gen.-Mgr. Tokyo Branch Office. Address: c/o Kochu Koshi, Dairen.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1935; b. Oct. 1874, Miyagi-ken; s. of Hirotsugu Hirayama. Career: grad. Astronomy Course Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Asst. D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1867, Tokyo; bro. of Jun Hirayama. Career: grad. Astronomy Course, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1888; studied in England & Germany; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Tokyo Astronomical Observatory, 1920. Address: 1 Nagasaka-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.
Pres. Daido Life Ins. Co., Kajima Trust Co.; b. Feb. 1876, Osaka; adopted by Shingoro Hirooka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903. Address: 692 Mori, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.- Dir. Keihin Elec. Power Co.; b. Feb. 1876, Yamanashi-ken; s. of late Hisamitsu Hirose; m. Ei. Career: Chief, Senninsan Iron Works, 1907; Dir. Tokyo Elec. Power Co. 1922; Kanto Hydro-Elec. Dir. Fund Bureau Deposits Dept. Finance Office; b. Nov. 1891, Kanazawa; s. of Kajima Hirose. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Chief Yodobashi Revenue Office; Commr. & Secr. Address: 25 Kamiyama-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Osaka Trust Co.; b. Aug. 1881, Koyto: s. of Ainosuke Hirose. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1905; entered business; Mng.-Dir. Nomura Bank. Address: 136 Yoshino-dori, 1-chome, Toyonaka city, Osaka-fu.

For. Min. Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1878, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tokuhei Hirota. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; Diplo. Probationer, Legation, Peking; Sec. Emb. London; Vice-Dir. Information Bureau Foreign Office; Dir; Europe & America Bureau; Minister to Netherlands; Amb. to U.S.S.R. 1930-32; Foreign Minister in Saito and Okada Cabinets 1933-36; nominated Peer 1937; Prime Minister 1936-37; Pres. Planning Bd. of Cabinet, 1937. Address: Official Residence, Nagata-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Musician; b. June 1892, Kochi-ken; s. of Seiro Hirota, educator. Career: grad. Tokyo Acad. of Music; apptd. Asst. Prof. same sent to Berlin for study. Address: 8 of Ha, 3 Yayoi-cho, Mukogaoka, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen..; Chief, Mil. Tech. Dept. since 1936; b. 1882, Shiga-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1903; resided in Europe during Great War; Chief, Mil. Research Inst. 1932-36. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.
General on the reserve list. (See 1936 Edition).

Hon. Consul for Japan at Budapest; Mng.-Dir. Hungarian Com. Bank; Chief; Fiscal Councillor, to Royan Hungarian Govt.; b. June 25, 1874; m. Aurelie Neustadt. Address: P.O. Box 508, Budapest, Hungary.

D. Sc.; Pres. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Feb. 1870, Aichi-ken; s of Hyozaburo Honda; m. Kane Honda, 1897. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; further studied in Europe; won Imp. Acad. Prize for his research in the steel 1916; invented permanent magnet. Address: 21 Shimizu-dori, Komegafukuro, Sendai.

Writer; b. Dec. 1874, Wakayama-ken; s. of Uhei Honda. Career: grad. Tokyo Senmon Gakko and Hogakuin and later Univ. of Brussels; Secr. to Foreign Minister; Secr. Legation and Embassy; Counsellor of Emb. in London during world War; Minister to Switzerland and Austria; Amb. to Germany 1923-26. Address: 1080 Kamimeguro 7-chome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Dr. of Forestry; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Teikoku Shinrin-kai; b. July 1866, Saitama-ken. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; studied at Munchen Univ (D. General on the reserve list; Former Chief Aide-de-camp to the Emperor. (See 1936 issue.)

Dr. phil.; Vice-Consul at German Consulate-General in Osaka & Kobe; b. Aug. 1900, Heidelberg; s. of Prof. Johannes Hoops. Career: Ph. D. Address: 32/39 Yamamoto-dori 2-chome, Kobe.

Pres. Ind. Bank of Japan; b. 1881, Osaka; s. of Matsu Horai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; joined Sumitomo Bank and served at Tokyo & Yokohama; entered present bank 1913; studied in England & Amer. 1916-24. Address: 476 Yoyogi Hatsudai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Meisei Spinning & Weaving Co., Meisei Rayon Co.; b. Feb. 1882, Okayama-ken;s. of Toshiro Hori. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Mem. House of Peers; Adviser Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Dir. Sumitomo Bank; b. Jan. 1867, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Gohei Hori, later adopted by late Kasumi Hori. Career: grad. Law Coll. Imp. Univ. 1893. Address [?] Hirao, Minomo-mura, Osaka-fu.

Mng.-Dir. Domei National News Agency; b. Feb. [?], Kagoshima-ken; s. of Yukio Hori; m. Fusa, nee Nakajima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1908; entered diplomatic service 1908; Priv. D.L.; Prof. Chuo Univ.; Lawyer; b. 1876, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Kengo Horie. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogakuin; studied Com. Law at Michigan Univ. U.S.A. 1905-08; called to the bar 1920. Address: 80 Date-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Leader, Seiyukai Party; b: May 1882, Fukushima-ken; s. of Ryohei Horikiri. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1903; went to U.S.A., England and Germany to study finance and economics; apptd. Conf.; visited Europe after World War; Parl. Vice-Minister of Finance in Saito Cabinet, 1932-34. Address: 5 Ichigaya Tamachi 2-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Sept. 1884, Fukushima-ken; s. of Ryohei Horikiri. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; entered Home Dept.; Dir. City Planning Bureau; Dir. Engrg. Address: 27 Takata Oimatsu-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

b. 1879, Tokyo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; joined Bank of Japan; Inspector London Branch; Chief Inquiry Bureau, Head Office; Dir. Bank of Japan [?]-37. Address: 830 Simo-ochiai 2-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Teikoku Seishi Kaisha since 1924; b. Nov. 1883, Tokyo; s. of Yurin Horinaga. Career: grad. Okura Higher Com. Sch. 1906; went abroad for study; entered Teikoku Seishi Co. 1916; Mgr. & Dir., same. Address: c/o Teikoku Seishi Kaisha, Osaka Gas Bldg., Hirano-machi, Osaka.

Minobu Forestry Assn. Address: 308 Yoyogi Sanya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. November 1887, Yamagata-ken; s. of Kinichiro Hoshijima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; practised law since 1918; published magazines of Law; elected Rep. 7 times since 1920. Address: 55 Myogadani-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir.-Gen. Manchoukuo Gen. Affairs Bd.; b. 1892, Kanagawa-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Finance Dept.; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Finance Dept. 1932-36; Vice-Finance Minister of Manchoukuo. Address: Tokiwa-cho, Hsinking.

Adviser Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Dec. 1854. Himeji; s. of Kempachi Hoshino. Career: engaged in printing business early; went to U. S. Marquis; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1883, Kumamoto; s. of late Marquis Morishige Hosokawa. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; went to Europe and America. Address: 56 Takata Oimatsu-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Editor, Manshu Nichi-Nichi Shimbun since 1932; b. June 1884, Nagano-ken; s. of Yasozaemon Hosono. farmer. Career: grad. Com. Coll., Chuo Univ. (Tokyo), 1914; served Yamato Shimbun and later Chief Compiler, Kokumin Shimbun. Address: 85, Heiwa-dai, Dairen.

Amb. to Italy; b. July 1883, Tokyo; s. of Masatada Hotta. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Dir. Personnel Bureau Foreign Office; Europe & America Bureau; 1926; Minister to Czechoslovakia; to Switzerland 1934-37. Address: Japanese Emb. Rome, Italy.

Count; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1887, Tokyo; s. of Viscount Chokuju Nabeshima. and later adopted by Seirin Hotta. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Baron; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Prof. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Apr. 1883, Tokyo; s. of Baron Nobushige Hozumi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Maj.-Gen.; Mil. Attaché, Chinese Emb. in Tokyo; b. 1895, Foochow, China. Career: Comdr. Mil. Non-commissioned Officers' Brig. Address: 10 Hinoki-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept.; b. 1876, Chekiang Prov. Career: Chief Secr. Liaoning Prov. Office; Adviser, Heilungkiang Prov. Office; Secr. Chief Executive Office, 1932-34. Address: Imp. Household Dept., Hsinking.

Mayor of Hsinking; b. 1892, Mukden. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Engr. Three Eastern Prov. Arsenal; Councillor Fengtien Prov. Office; Chief Ind. Dept. Fengtien Prov. 1933-34; Gov. Chinchow Prov. Address: Muni. Office Hsinking.
Manchoukuo Privy Councillor; b. 1869, Kweichow Prov. Career: Pres. Peiyang Law Coll. Tientsin; Secr.-Gen. Chief Executive Office, Manchoukuo 1932-34. Address: Hsinking.

M.D.; Prof. of Physiology, Med. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1937; b. Dec. 1896, Tuyama City; s. of Ryuziro Kawamura, later adopted by Hukuda family; m. Tatuko Yosioka. Career: grad. Med. Coll.
