Architect Taiwan Govt.-Gen. since 1919; b. 1879, Gifu-ken; s. of Imashige Ide. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; travelled abroad 1919. Address: 53 of 2 Taisho-machi, Taihoku, Taiwan .

Vice-Admiral; Dir. Nav. Acad.; b. Nov. 1883, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Katsubei Idemitsu. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1906; Nav. Staff Coll. 1916; Resident Mil. Officer, England; Staff Nav. Gen. Staff Office; Chief 1st Sec. Personnel Bureau of Navy; Capt. "Tama," "Yakumo" and "Jungei"; Chief Instructor Nav. Com. Sch.; Aide-de-Camp to the Emperor; Comdr. 1st Submarine Sqn. Address: c/o Nav. Acad. Etajima, Hiroshima-ken.

Mem. House of Peers since 1937; Prop. of Idemitsu Shokai; Pres. Moji Chamber of Com. & Ind. since 1932; Hon. Consul for Manchoukuo at Moji since 1934; b. Aug. 1885; Fukuoka-ken; s. of Toroku Idemitsu, merchant; m. Kikue Yamanouchi. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1909; established present firm. Address: 2937 Hatakeda, Moji City.

Lecturer, Toyo Univ.; Principal, Shoin Girls' Sch., Koyo Middle Sch. & Shoin Girls' Coll.; b. Oct. 1869; Takamatsu; s. of Ihachiro Akagi, later succeeded Iga family; m. Ryu. Career: educ. work since 1896. Address: 116 Eiwa, Fuse-machi, Osaka-shigai.

A.B.; B.D.; S.T.D.; Missionary; b. Nov. 1878, Greencastle, Indiana, U.S.A.; s. of Ferd. C. Iglehart. Career: grad. Columbia Coll., Drew Theol. Sem. New York Univ.; Pastor in New York Conf. 1899-1904; came to Japan, 1904; Teacher Aoyama Gakuin. Address: 6 Aoyama Gakuin, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. San-yu Koshi; b. Dec. 1875, Okayama-ken. Career: came to Manchoukuo 1902; Pres. Mukden Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Mukden Financial Guild; Hoten Nichi-Nichi Shimbun. Address: 10 Kotohira-cho, Mukden.

Pres. Iida G. K.; Takashimaya Ltd.; b. Oct. 1859, Kyoto; s. of Shinshichi Iida. Career: inherited family estate 1888; established Takashimaya-Iida Co. (now Takashimaya Dept. Store); Mng.-Dir. Kyoto Textile Mfg. Co.; Vice-Pres. Kyoto Educ. Assn.; Counsellor, Kyoto Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 1 Yakushimae-cho, Karasumaru-dori Matsubara-agaru, Shimokyoku, Kyoto.

M.D.; Prof. Kyoto Med. Coll.; Chief Med. Dept. Attached Hospital; b. May 1887, Akita-ken; s. of Hikoshiro Iizuka. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1912; Med. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1916; apptd. Asst. Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1922; studied at Collège de France and L'Institut Pasteur. Address: Kami-Goryomae-dori. Karasumaru Higashi-iru, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Writer; Prof. Nihon Univ.; b. Nov. 1894, Tokyo; s. of Yoshijiro Iizuka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; called to the bar; Dir. Ryubunkan Pub. Co.; Mem. Tokyo Pref. Assembly 1924; studied Dramaturgy; Lecturer of History of Stage Dramas at present Univ. 1931. Address: Yato, Koshigoe-machi, Kamakura-gun, Kanagawa-ken.

Attached to Criminal Bureau Justice Dept.; b. 1897. Niigata-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1921; Secr. Justice Dept.; Dir. Criminal Bureau Manchoukuo Justice Dept. 1934-37. Address: c/o Justice Dept. Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Feb. 1880; s. of Tetsu Ikeda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; joined Asahi Shimbun 1909; apptd. Official, Overseas Affairs Dept. 1910; Secr. same Dept. 1911; Chief Police Dept. Gifu-ken 1917; Secr. for Foreign and Home Depts. 1918; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Miyagi-ken 1922; Hiroshima-ken. 1922; Gov. Akita-ken 1924; Dir. Ind. Bureau of Chosen 1924-28; Gov. Hokkaido 1929-31; Pres. Keijo Nippo 1931-32; Parl. Vice-Minister of Com. & Ind. 1936. Address: 2122 Kami-Meguro 4-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Osaka-fu since 1937; b. Feb. 1885, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Naosuke Ikeda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; entered Metropolitan Police Board; Chief, Foreign Affairs Sec., same; Police Chief, Gifu-ken; Chief, Gen. Affairs Sec., Shrines Bureau; Police Chief, Kyoto & Osaka Prefs.; Chief, Home Dept. Hyogo-ken; Dir. of Shrines, Home Dept.; Dir. Police Affairs Bureau, Chosen Govt.-Gen. 1931-36; Gov. Hokkaido 1936-37. Address: Governor's Residence, Osaka.

State-Councillor; Adviser Bank of Japan; b. July 1867; s. of Nariakira Ikeda, banker. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Harvard Univ.; Staff Mem. Jiji Shimpo; joined Mitsui Bank 1895; Mem. National Policy Council; Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; Dir. Mitsui Trust Co.; Councillor Bank of Japan; resigned from Mitsui 1936; Gov. Bank of Japan 1937. Address: 1 Nagasaka-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Supreme Court since 1936; b. Jan. 1879, Saga-ken; s. of Sensuke Ikeda. Career: grad. English Law Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Judge, 1905; Judge, Tokyo Local Court; Chief Judge, Tokyo District Court; Councillor & Public Procurator, Justice Dept.; despatched to Europe & America 1913; Procurator, Supreme Court; Director of Civil Affairs Bureau, Justice Dept.; Chief Judge, Supreme Court 1928-35. Address: 8 Yoyohata Honmachi 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Prof. Kumamoto Med. Coll.; b. Dec. 1883, Mie-ken; s. of Enjiro Ikegami, doctor. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1907; Dir. Fusan Hospital 1916; rec'd deg. 1922. Address: 76 Higashi-Kogai-cho, Kumamoto.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Hon. Mem. Academie des Sciences, Paris; b. May 1886, Tokyo; s. of Tomigoro Ikeno. Career: grad. Botanical Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; apptd. Asst. Prof., later Prof. Agri. Coll. same; studied Botany in Europe 1906; rec'd deg. 1909; Mem. Imp. Academy 1927. Address: 89 Harajuku 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Elec. Power Co.; Chairman Elec. Assn.; b. Mar. 1878, Shiga-ken; s. of Yohei Ikeo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; joined O. S. K. 1912. Address: 16 Shimo-dori 5-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; b. 1879 Tokyo; s. of late Motoi Ikeuchi; m. Nao. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; apptd. Lecturer of same 1913; Asst. Prof. 1915; rec'd deg. 1922. Address: 7 Kojimachi 5-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
D.L.; former Pres. Privy Council. (See 1936 issue.)

Pres. Nagoya Bank since 1936; b. Feb. 1886 in Miye-ken; s. of Zenjuro Ikura. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; entered Bank of Japan 1911, appointed private secretary to Gov. same; promoted Mgr. Nagaya branch 1933. Address: 32 Nunoike-cho, Higashi-ku, Nagoya.

Mng.-Dir. Okura & Co. (Trading) Ltd.; Dir. Mukden Arsenal, Ltd.; b. June 1885, Nagano-ken; s. of Kensuke Imai. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; entered Okura & Co. 1911; Mgr. New York Branch 1916; returned home 1920; Dir. Okura Mining Co. 1922. Address: 6 Shinryudo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers (Imp. nominee); Pres. Matsumoto Chamber of Com. & Ind; Dir. Sericultural Assn. of Japan; Pres. Filature Assn. of Japan, Katakura & Co. Ltd. (Raw Silk Reelers & Exporters). Career: educated in America 1886; went to America 1917 & 1933. Address: Hatsudai, Yoyogi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; attached to Gen. Staff Office; b. Sept. 1882, Aichi-ken; s. of Korekiyo Imai. Career: grad. Mil. Coll. 1904; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Comdr. Inf. 30th Brig.; Chief 1st Dept. Gen. Staff Office 1934; Dir. Personnel Bureau 1935-36; Mil. Affairs Bureau; attached to Mil. Ordnance Dept.; Comdr. 4th Div.; Vice-Chief Gen. Staff. Address: Gen Staff Office, Tokyo.

Chief, Explosive Works, Mukden Ordnance Co. since 1922; b. Nov. 1881, Niigata-ken; s. of Matazo Imai, farmer. Career: grad. Mil. Acad., 1909 and appld. Art. Sub-lieut.; grad. Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; served at Mil. Explosive Works; sent to Europe for study 1921. Address: 7, Aoi-cho, Mukden.

Mem. House of Peers (nominated [?]); b. Feb. 1884, Okayama-ken; s. of Yosaburo Kunishiro; adopted by Zenjuro Imaida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Dir. Kumamoto Communications Bureau; Dir. Post Office Life Ins. Bureau Dir. Elec. Bureau, Osaka City; Vice-Minister of Communications 1928; went to Europe and America 1914; Civil Adm. Chief of Chosen. Address: 230 Kamiosaki 4-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Hon. Consul-Gen. for Luxemburg, Tokyo; Dir. Nippon Seitetsu K. K.; b. June 1867, Gunma-ken; s. of Tsuneko Imaizumi, doctor. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; Engr. Yawata Steel Works, 1896-1910; M.P. 1920-24; sent to Europe and America 7 times; elected Life Mem. Iron & Steel Inst. England 1903; Mem. Verein Deutscher Eisenhuttenleute. Address: 4 Onden 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Mem. Imp. Acad. Secr. Earthquake Investigation Council; b. June 1870, Kagoshima-ken; s. of late Akikiyo Imamura. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1894; Instructor Mil. Acad. rec'd deg. 1905; Prof. Seismology, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923-31. Address: 685 Seijo, Kinuta, Tokyo-fu.

Major-Gen.; Secr.-Gen. Inf. Sch.; b. 1887 Miyagi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1908; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in England & India; Chief Conscription Sec. War Office; Sec. Chief Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. Inf. 57th Reg.; Dir. Narashino Sch.; Comdr. Inf. 40th Brig. 1935-36; Vice-Chief Staff Kwantung Army 1936-37. Address: Infantry School, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Dai-Nippon Spinning Co.; b. Dec. 1879, Nara-ken; s. of Kinzo Imamura, Ex-M.P. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. and Haverford Univ.; joined Settsu Spinning Co. (now Dai-Nippon Spinning Co.). Address: 746 Renge, Morigu, Nishinomiya City, Hyogo-ken.

Chairman Japan Trust Assn.; Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Trust Co.; Dir. Sumitomo Bank, Sumitomo Honsha Ltd., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co.; b. July 1874, Nara-ken; s. of Kinzo Imamura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900. Address: 35 Nango-cho, Nishinomiya City.

Pres. Imamura Bank; Dir. Car & Locomotive Mfg. Co.; Dir. 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co., Tropical Industry Co. and Taiwan Development & Tea Mfg. Co.; b. Nov. 1877, Tokyo; s. of Seinosuke Imamura. Career: studied at Trinity Coll. and Cambrdige Univ. (M.A.). Address: 2808 Kokubunji, Tokyo-fu.

Gov. Karafuto Govt.; b. Nov. 1880; s. of Tsunesada Imamura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Gov. Kokaido, Chosen; Dir. Ind. Bureau of Chosen. Address: Gov.'s Residence, Toyohara, Karafuto.

Pres. Hanshin Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Apr. 1887, Osaka; s. of Shoshichi Ishii; later adopted by Rinzaburo Imanishi. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Com. Sch.; Polit. Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1912; entered business. Address: 24 Honden Sanban-cho, Nishi-ku, Osaka.

Mem. House of Peers; Hon. Consul for Roumania, Belgium, Bolivia, Poland and Portugal at Osaka; Japan Dye-stuff Mfg. Co.; b. Oct. 1862, Kyoto; s. of Risuke Inabata. Career: while in Kyoto Normal Sch. in 1877, was sent to France for study of Applied Chemistry; represented Kyoto Pref. Exhibitions at Intl. Exhibition held at Amsterdam, 1883, investigated chemical and dyeing industry in Holland, England, Germany, Italy, Belgium and Switzerland; established Inabata & Co. 1890 and Inabata Dyeing Works, 1898; attended Intl. Labor Conf., Geneva, 1927. Address: 45 Nanzenji Fukuchi 2-chome, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.
Pres. Inabata & Co.; Vice-Consul for Portugal at Osaka; b. May 1898, Kyoto; s. of Katsutaro Inabata. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. Address: 51 Junkei-machi-dori 2-chome, Minami-ku, Osaka.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; b. Aug. 1890, Tokyo; s. of Baron Shosuke Sato, later adopted by late Kunitane Inada. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tohoku Imp. Univ. & Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Overseas Affairs 1936-37. Address: 15 Aoba-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Prof. Emeritus, Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. Mar. 1874, Aichi-ken; s. of Kenryu Inada. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; studied in Germany; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. & Fukuoka Med. Coll.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918. Address: 9 Surugadai 2-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Intendant to H. I. H. Prince Kan-in; b. May 1870, Shimane-ken; s. of Ryosai Inagaki. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1891; Cav. Sub.-Lieut. 1892; Staff Gen. Staff Office; Aide-de-Camp; Comdr. Cav. 1st Reg.; Attaché Emb. England. Address: 4 Sakae-dori 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mgr. Shizuoka Branch, Nippon Kangyo Ginko; b. 1889; Nagoya; s. of Soshichi Inahata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined present bank; visited Europe and America for inspection, 1921; Asst. Mgr. Kyoto and Osaka Branches; Mgr. Tottori and Nara Branches. Address: 62 of 25 Nishi-Kusafuka-cho, Shizuoka.

D.E.; Chief Internal Combustion Engine Drawing Dept. Kobe Works, Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. Oct. 1892, Tokyo; s. of Masamichi Ino; m. Tomiko, d. of Hikozo Ichikawa. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; immediately joined Mitsubishi Firm; made inspection tour of Europe & America; rec'd deg. 1926. Address: 1843 Takigahana, Mikage-cho, Hyogo-ken.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1886, Fukui-ken; s. of Riemon Inoge. Career: grad. Nihon Univ. 1911; joined Niroku Shimpo; taught Junten Middle Sch.; Secr. to Justice Minister; to Home Minister; Parl. Vice-Min. of Foreign Affairs. 1926-37. Address: 28 Kita-Iga-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Doboku Gakukai; b. Apr. 1876, Sendai; s. of Yoshinori Inouye. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1899; apptd. Asst. Prof. at same; Chief, Civil Engrg. Sec. Kyoto Muni. Office; sent to Europe & America for investigation of water works 1907; on return home Chief, Water Works Sec. Yokohama Muni. Office; Chief, Civil Engrg. Sec. Inawashiro Hydo-Elec. Co.; Dir. Tokyo Elec. Light Co.; Adviser Mitsubishi Mining Co., Nippon Elec. Co. Address: 290 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. June 1873. Kyoto-fu; s. of late Jihei Inouye. Career: grad. Kyoto Com. Sch. 1891; joined present firm; Mgr. Shanghai. Tientsin. London and Hamburg. Address: 74 Shimo-Nibancho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Sr. Mng.-Dir., Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; Dir. and Aud. of several other cos.; b. Jan. 1881. Kokura City, Kyushu; s. of Seizo Inouye. Career: grad. Shimonoseki Com. Sch. 1900; joined Mitsui Bussan K. K. entered present Co., 1911. Address: 132, Harajuku 1-chome. Shibuya-ku. Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Ryojun Engrg. Coll.; b. Dec. 1873, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Nobuatsu Inouye. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Engr. Taiwan Govt., Agr. & Com. Dept., Imp. Steel Works, successively; as Dir. Imp. Geological Survey Bureau and as Pres. Ryojun Engrg. Coll. sent to Int'l Geological Congress held in Austria. Sweden and Canada; rec'd deg. 1917. Address: 96 Shirokane Imazato-cho. Shiba-ku. Tokyo.

Vice-Chairman Japan-Brazil Central Assn.; Advisor. Oriental Development Co.; Peru Cotton Co.; Dir. Nan-a Co.; b. June 1876; s. of Tahei Adachi and later adopted by Tobei Inouye. Career studied at Kogyokusha, Nav. Acad. and Waseda Univ.; studied Colonization Policy and Economics at Vienna and Berlin Univs.; Commissioner, Communications Dept.; Financial Officer. Chosen Govt.; Mng.-Dir. Nanyo Kyokai; Pres. Overseas Development Co. till Apr. 1936. Address: 3553 Mejiro 3-chome. Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Ophthalmologist; Commr., Court Physicians Bureau; b. Mar. 1875, Nagano-ken; s. of Tatsuya Inouye, eye-specialist. Careeer: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied Ophthalmology at P.-G. Course; went to Germany to study at Univs. of Leipzig and Vienna, 1902; medical practice at Inouye Ophthalmological Hospital; studied at Univ. of Berlin and Leipzig 1909; apptd. Prof. Okayama Medical Coll.; Dir. Okayama Ophthalmological Hospital, 1912; rec'd deg. 1914. Address: 66 Nagata-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1887, Tokyo; s. of late Prince Taro Katsura, later adopted by late Marquis Katsunosuke Inouye. Career: grad. Mil. Academy; studied 3 yrs. in Europe and America apptd. Artillery Sub.-Lieut. 1906; Col. 1929; Chief, Mobilization Sec. War Office; Major-Gen. 1934. Address: 42 Miyamura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Koshien Hotel, Sanyo Chuo Hydro-Elec. Co., Nippon Kan-i Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Hanshin Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co., Keihan Elec. Ry. Co., Hanshin Kyuko Bus Co., Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; b. Apr. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Yasujiro Inouye, businessman. Career: grad. Antwerp Com. Coll. Belgium 1902; founded Toyo Paper Mills 1906; apptd. Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co. when the aforementioned firm was merged 1924. Address: 32 Naka 2-chome, Tezukayama, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Co. Dir.; b. Nov. 1881, Shiga-ken; s. of late Goemon Inouye; m. Haru, d. of Jisaburo Hirata, 1912. Career: studied at Elec. Engrg. Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Mgr. Kasagi Hydro-Elec. Co., 1914; Mng.-Dir. Innoshima Elec. Co. 1915; Pres. Omishima Elec. Co. 1920; Standing Auditor Seto-Naikai-Odan Elec. Power Co. (merger of above mentioned 2 companies) till 1924; Dir. Shikoku Hydro-Elec. Co.; Pres. Yoshizaki Ry. Co. 1925-26; Dir. Amanohashidate Cableway Co. 1927; Pres. Hachioji Paper Mfg. Co. since 1931; Toa Commercial Co. since 1934; Jochushi Seizo K. K. since 1935. Address: Ibaraki-cho, Osaka-fu.

Viscount; D. E.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1876, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Yokoku Okamatsu, and later adopted by Takeshi Inouye. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; went to Germany & Amer. for study, 1902; apptd. Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Osaka Higher Tech. Sch.; Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Navy; Ry. Minister 1926-27. Address: 28 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Toyo Univ.; Pres. East Asia Society & Philosophy Society; b. Nov. 1855, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Toshitatsu Tomita; later adopted by Tetsuhide Inoue. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1880; studied in Germany; apptd. Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof.; Dean, Litt. Coll. Address: 109 Omote-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Attorney; b. Nov. 1876, Nara-ken; s. of Seigo Inui. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; studied at Univs. of Berlin and Bonn 1901-05; apptd. Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; Lecturer, Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer and Dir. Hosei Univ.; Lecturer, Keio, Meiji and Senshu Univs.; Pres. Tokyo Bar Assn. Address: 12 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Mfg.-Dir. Imp. Hotel, Tokyo; b. 1887, Ishikawa-ken; bro. of Jintaro Inumaru. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1910; joined S. M. R. Co.; practised and inspected hotel business in China, Europe and America 7 years; joined present hotel 1919. Address: 102 Den-en Chofu [?]-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Minister of Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept. since 1934; b. Mar. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Viscount Yasushi Nomura; later adopted by Irie family. Career: grad. German Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Secr. Privy Council; Dir. Pensions Bureau; Councillor, Imp. Household Dept.; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Dir. Imp. Board of Audit.; Aud. Bank of Japan. Address: Imp. Household Dept., Hsinking.

M.D. Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Vice-Pres. Dojinkai; Chief Dir. Japan-German Culture Society; b. 1865, Niigata-ken; s. of Kyohei Irisawa. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1886; studied in Germany, 1890; apptd. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895-1922; rec'd deg. 1899; Chief, Court Medical Bureau, 1921-22. Address: 226 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Bank of Chosen since 1932; b. Aug. 1886, Nagano-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Inspector, Bank of Taiwan and Bank of Chosen; Secr. Dept. of Com. & Industry; Bank Inspector; retired from Govt. service 1929. Address: 27 Uchikoshi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Hotel New Grand; Pres. Yokohama Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Dir. Mitsui Bank, Int'l Telephone Co., Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Pres. Tokyo Gas Co.; Dir. Yokohama Warehouse Co.; b. Dec. 1869, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Miki Isaka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; went abroad for inspection 1928. Address: 53 Takanawa-Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Lawyer; b. Dec. 1881, Osaka; s. of Koki Isaka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1910; returned to Diet 4 times; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1934-36. Address: 38 Sakurada-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nihon Tabi K. K. and Bridgestone Tyre Co.; b. Feb. 1889, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tokujiro Ishibashi. Career: founded Nihon Tabi K. K. 1918; Bridgestone Tyre Co. 1931; Vice-Pres. Kyushu Medical Coll. at Kurume, 1930; his residence was honoured with Prince Chichibu's stay for few weeks twice in July 1930 and Oct. 1931. Address: 70 Kushihara-machi, Kurume.

Mng.-Dir. & Chief Editor, Toyo Keizai Shimpo-sha (The Oriental Economist); b. 1884, Tokyo. Career: Waseda Univ., 1907; joined Tokyo Mainichi Shimbun, 1908; Editor, Toyo Keizai Simpo, 1911; Dir. same, 1921. Publications: Inflation, Recent Finance & Economics of Japan, History of Banking in Japan, etc. Address: 705 Omachi, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

D. Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc., and Nihon Univ.; b. 1886, Hokkaido; s. of Masanobu Ishibashi. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; studied at Leipzig Univ. Germany; rec'd deg. 1919; won Imp. Academy Prize for Research 1924. Address: 202 Komagome Hayashi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Former Metropolitan Police Chief; b. May 1885, Yamaguchi-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Police Supt. Niigata-ken; Commr. Fukuoka-ken, Aomori-ken & Tokyo-fu; Chief Police Dept. Aomori-ken; Secr. Home Dept.; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Tochigi-ken & Okayama-ken; Chief Secr. Metro. Police Board; Chief Peace Preservation Dept. same; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Kyoto-fu; Gov. Miyazaki-ken & Chiba-ken; Dir. Shrines Bureau 1931-34; Gov. Kanagawa-ken 1935-36; Metro. Police Chief 1936-37. Address: 640 Sendagaya 4-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Sanyo Elec. Ry. Co. since 1934; Dir. Sinki and Sin-mei Motorcar Cos.; b. 1877; s. of Yasushige; m. Uta. Career: joined San-yo Ry. Co. 1901; after it was nationalized, continued service; Dir. Sendai and later Kobe Ry. Bureaus; sent to Europe & Amer. 1909; to Siberia and Manchuria, 1918-19; Dir. Kobe Municipal Elec. Bureau 1927. Address: 1466 Shironomae, Mikage, Hyogo-ken.

Viscount; b. Feb. 1845, Niigata-ken. Career: Studied Med. Sci. under Kensen Yanagi; Mil. Surgeon 1871; Mil. Surgeon-Gen.; Chief, Med. Sec., War Office; Chief, Field Sanitation Office in Sino-Japanese War; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Japan Red Cross Soc.; Privy Councillor till 1936. Address: 17 Ageba-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Dir. Industrial Guild Central Assn.; Dir. Rural Regeneration Soc.; b. Jan. 1884, Tokyo-fu; s. of Viscount Tadanori Ishiguro. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Chief Tenancy Sec.; Dir. Agr. Bureau; Sericultural Bureau 1927; Agr. Bureau 1929; went to Europe & America 1914-15; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 17 Ageba-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.
Pres. Ishihara Industry & Marine Transportation Co., b. Jan. 1888; s. of Chotaro Ishihara, Kyoto. Career: grad. Ritsumeikan Univ. 1913. Address: 3 Fujimi-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Prof. Ophthal. Dir. of Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Ujimoto Ishihara. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; sent to Germany to study med. sci. 1912-14; rec'd deg. 1916; apptd. Surgeon Lieut.-Col. 1906; attached to 2nd Inf. Reg., 1st Garrison Hospital Tokyo; Instrucor Army Surgeon Sch.; Dir. 2nd Garrison Hospital; Surgeon-Gen. 1926; Commmr. Dept. of Overseas Affairs 1930. Address: 35 Miyasato, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Stage Dancer; Prop. Ishii Bac Dance Studio; b. Dec. 1892, Akita-ken; s. of Ryukichi Ishii. Career: completed Akita Middle Sch.; entered Opera Dept., Imperial Theater; studied dance under Enrico Rossi and song with Madam Tamaki Miura; made public performances at Berlin, Muenchen, Leipzig, Paris, Olmuts, Prague, Lords, Posen, Warsaw, Ostende and at New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, San Francisco. Address: 62 Jiyugaoka, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. East Asia Bureau Foreign Dept. since 1937; b. Feb. 1887, Fukushima-ken; s. of Bungoro Ishii, agriculturist. Career: grad. Com. Dept. Toa Dobun Shoin 1908; served S. M. R. Co. 1908-11; joined Foreign Dept. 1915; service as Eleve-Consul at Canton, Tientsin, San Francisco; Secr. of Emb. & Leg. U.S.A., England, Mexico; Chief 3rd Sec. Com. Bureau; Consul-Gen. Kirin [?] Shanghai; Minister to Siam 1936-37. Address: Foreign Office Tokyo.

Dir. The Dai-ichi Ginko, Ltd.; b. June 1874, Tokyo; bro. of Yoshio Momoi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1895; entered 1st Bank; promoted to Vice-Pres. same; Pres. 1931-35. Address: 5 Takajo-machi. Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Privy Councillor since 1929; b. Mar. 1866. Chiba-ken; adopted s. of Hoyu Ishii. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; apptd. Attaché at Paris 1891; 1st Secr. of legation; Dir. Com. Bureau; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs; Ambassaror to U.S.A. and France; Foreign Minister; ennobled, 1911; Mem. House of Peers 1916; Delegate, Naval Disarm. Conf. 1927. Address: 15 Aoba-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Member of Imperial Academy of Fine Arts; Lecturer on free-hand drawing Tokyo Imperial Univercity; b. Mar. 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Teiko Ishii, artist. Career: studied art under his father, later with C. Asai and F. Nakamura; went abroad twice, 1911-12 and 1923; exhibited works in "Bunten" since 1907; organized "Nikakwai" art soc. with friends; organizer also of "Issui-kwai". Address: 1035 Nippori Watanabe-cho, Arakawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Asahi Shimbun-sha; b. Aug. 1889, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1912; Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1914; Dir. Public Peace Section. Metropolitan Police Board; Secr. and Councillor, Taiwan Govt.; visited Europe & America 1920-22. Address: 6307 Oi Kaneko-machi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Kangyo Ginko; b. 1881, Mie-ken; s. of Shiro Ishii. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1906; joined Bank of Chosen, 1910; promoted to Mgr.; Dir. Chosen Shokusan Ginko, 1920. Address: 110 Kamimeguro 1-chomee, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Pres. Ishii Iron Works Ltd.; b. Mar. 1880, Yokohama; s. of Minekichi Uchida; later adopted by Chokichi Ishii. Career: established present firm, 1919; Dir. Crane Mrg. Co.; Pres. Takaoka Gas Co.; took 30 patents. Address: 49 Nanpeidai-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

n: ISHIKAWA, Hidezurumaru 石川日出鶴丸
t: M.D.; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. 1878, Toyama-ken; s. of Inue Ishikawa. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; studied in Germany, Russia and England. Address: 55 Takanohananobo-machi, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.
Pres. Shufu-no-tomo-Sha; b. 1887, Oita-ken; s. of Matazo Ishikawa. Career: engaded in publishing business for many years; Vice-Pres. Kokumin Shimbun. Address: 9 Surugadai 2-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Pres. Nihon Imono Gakukai; b. June 1879, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Yutaka Ishikawa. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; Staff. Kure and Hiro Nav. Arsenals; Chief, Engine-Construction Dept., Hiro Nav. Arsenal; Chief Sc. Research Dept., Nav. Tech. Research Lab.; Attached to Nav. Construction Dept.; despatched to Europe & America; rec'd Imp. Acad. Prize for his study on Alloys and Castings 1919; rec'd deg. 1920. Address: Nikawa, Ryogen-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Kyoto Elec. Light Co.; b. Nov. 1882, Tokyo; s. of Kunisaburo Ishikawa. Career: grad. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; apptd. Auditor Daishojigawa Hydro-Elec. Co.; Mt. Atago Elec. Ry Co.; Mt. Kurama Elec. Ry. Co.; went to Europe and America. Address: Sohokuji, Higashimonzen-cho, Kyoto.

Architect; b. Feb. 1894, Kobe; s. of Kisaburo Ishimoto. Career: grad. Archit. Course, Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; went abroad for inspection, 1922-23; apptd. Lecturer, Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1926; with Dr. Yasushi Kataoka, established Kataoka-Ishimoto Archit. Office, 1927; founded Ishimoto Archit. Office, 1931. Address: 96 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Aug. 1875, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Kichirouemon Ishino, farmer; m. Kikuko, formerly Prof. of Tokyo Ladies Higher Normal Sch. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Sci. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; went to Europe and Amer. for study 1913-17; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1918; Dean, Sci. Coll. 1928-30; sent to Europe & Amer. 1927-28. Address: 428 Yabushita-machi, Tonodan, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.
M.D.; Dir. Muni. Hygienic Inst. of Tokyo; b. Mar. 1884, Okayama-ken; s. of Shizuyoshi Ishikawa. Career: grad Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910. Address: 47 Kamitakata 1-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Prof. Meiji Univ.; b. 1881, Tokyo; s. of Hakaru Ishiwara. Career: grad. Physical Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; Instructor, Artillery & Engrg. Sch.; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1907-21; rec'd deg. 1916. Address: 1118 Kamimeguro 7-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Minister of Finance; b. Oct. 1891, Tokyo; s. of Toshiichi Ishiwatari, Peer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; Chief Saiwaibashi Revenue Office; Commissioner Revenue Superintendent Bureau; Chief of Indirect Tax Section Tokyo & Osaka Rev. Supt. Bureaus; Chief Nat. Loans Sec. Finance Bureau; Chief Nat. Tax Sec. Taxation Bureau; Dir. same Bureau; Mem. Cabinet Research Bureau 1936; Dir. Revenue Bureau Fin. Office. Address: 125 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; b. July 1866, Fukushima-ken; s. of Wasaburo Ishizuka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Adviser Korean Govt.; Chief-Councillor Taiwan; Civil Adm. Chief Kwantung; Dir.-Gen. Residency-General, Korea; Chief Agr. Com. & Ind. Depts. of Chosen; Pres. Oriental Development Co.; Mem. House of Peers 1916; Governor-Gen. Taiwan 1929. Address: 71 Haramachi 2-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.
F. C. A., O. B. E.; Chartered Accountant; b. 1891 in London. Career: joined firm of Maurice Jenks, Percival & Isitt, London, Kobe, Tokyo and Yokohama. Address: 23 Kitano-cho 2-chome, Kobe.

Lt.-Gen.; Comdr. 10th Div.; b. 1871, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1905; Mil. Staff Coll.; apptd. Staff 11th Div.; attached to Gen. Staff Office; Chief Staff 1st Div.; Chief 2nd Sec., Mil. Training Dept.; Chief 2nd Dept. Gen. Staff Office; Mil. Attaché, Emb. China 1933. 36; Dir. Mil. Affairs Bureau 1936-37. Address: 10th Div. Hdqrs., Himeji.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Nov. 1868; s. of Yenji Isomura. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1889; entered Communications Dept. 1890; Bank of Japan, 1894; joined Mitsui Firm, 1896. Address: 30 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. E.; Research Engr. Sibaura Engrg. Works Ltd.; b. Feb. 1885, Wakayama-ken; s. of Hannosuke Issiki. Career: grad. Elec. Engrg. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; made study of Elec. Engrg. especially of Lightening Protection. Address: 601 Koenzi 4-tyôme, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Lt.-Gen.; Comdr. 5th Div.; b. 1885, Tokyo-fu. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1904; Mil Staff Coll. 1916; Comdr. Inf. 14th Reg. 1921; attaché Gen. Staff Office 1922; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Asst. Mil. Attaché Legation China 1924; Staff 33rd Brig. 1927; Comdr. 33rd Inf. Reg. 1928; Staff Kwantung Army 1929; Dir. Army Press Bureau; attached to Gen. Staff Office 1933-34; Supreme Adviser to Manchoukuo 1934; Chief Staff Kwantung Army. Address: 5th Div. Hdqrs., Hiroshima.
D.L.; Prof. Keio Univ.; b. Dec. 1879, Hiroshima-ken; s. of late Riro Itakura. Career: grad. Law Dept. Keio Univ. 1903. Address: 403 Togoshi-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.
Pres. Kawasaki Dockyard Co.; b. Mar. 1880, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of late Yataro Itani. Career: was Pres. Hokkaido Mining Co. Address: 111 Yamamoto-dori 4-chome, Kobe.

Prof. of Econ. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. Feb. 1899, Toyama-ken; s. of Matsujiro Itani, journalist. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; went to Paris, Geneva, Vienna, Berlin for studies; Expert to 10th Assembly, League of Nations 1929; Expert, Int'l Conference of Tariff Holidays 1930; Delegate to Pacific Conf. at Shanghai 1931. Address: 57 Takata Oimatsu-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Mayor of Otaru; b. May 1885, Otaru, Hokkaido; s. of late Miyakichi Itaya. Career: grad. Com. Dept. Waseda Univ.; Pres. Itaya Mercantile Steamship Co., Karafuto Bank; Dir. South Sea Mail Steamship Co.; Executive Partner, Kurohime Steamship Co.; Pres. Hokuman Savings Bank; Mng.-Dir. Hokkai Hydro-Elec. Co.; High Taxpayer in Hokkaido. Address: 29 Ironaimachi 6-chome, Otaru, Hokkaido.

D. E.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Waseda Univ.; b. 1867, Yonezawa; s. of Sukeyuki Ito. Career: grad. Archit. Course, Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; Engr. Ise Shrine Construction Office; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; rec'd deg. 1901; went to China, India and Turkey 1902; Prof. 1905-28. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

n: ITO, Jirozaemon 伊藤次郎左衞門
t: Pres. Nagoya Pottery Co.; Dir. Aichi Watch, Clock & Elec. Machine Mfg. Co., Nihon Wireless Telegraph Co.; Adviser, Matsuzakaya Dept. Store; b. 1878, Nagoya; s. of Jirozaemon Ito. Career: succeeded father's business, 1924; went to U.S.A. for investigation. Address: 3 Chaya-machi 3-chome, Nagoya.

D. E.; Consulating Mechanical Engr.; Prop. Ito Industrial Office; Acting Partner, Tokyo Weighing Machine Mfg. Co.; Mng.-Dir. Showa Hikoki K. K.; b. Mar. 1873, Fukuoka-ken; s. of late Kanae Ito, samurai. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1989; entered Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; inspected shipbuilding and mechanical works in England, 1911-12; studied internal combustion engines in Europe, 1912-14; investigated start-turbines in Sweden and England, 1916; ivestigated submarine-boats and airplane engines in England and France, 1917-18; apptd. Vice-Pres. Kobe Works, of the firm, 1917; founded and became Pres. Mitsubishi Internal Combustion Engine Works; Kobe (later Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. which was merged into present Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd.), 1918; retired 1922; invented and patented Ito's Bridge Manoeuvering Apparatus and Ito's Propeller-blade Milling Machine. Address: 6 Marunouchi 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Chief, Hosokura Mine, Mitsubishi Mining Co.; b. January 1883; s. of Hanjiro Ito; m. Sono. Career: grad. Metallurgy Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1910; immediately joined Mitsubishi Co. and served at its Ikuno. Akebono, Okuyama, Makimine and Osarizawa Mines; Chief Chosen Mining Office. Address: Uguisuzawa-mura, Kuwabara-gun, Miyagi-ken.

Writre; Councillor of Radio Corp. of Japan; b. Oct. 1892, Tokyo; s. of Hiroshi Ito. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1913; joined Tokyo Jiji Shimpo; Corr. in Europe & America; Dir. & Chief Editor of the paper; author of books on naval affairs. Address: 6223 Oi Kaneko-machi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Min. to Poland until 1937; b. Aug. 1885, Ehime-ken; s. of Michioki Ito. Career: grad. P.-G. Course, Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; apptd. Elève-Consul; Diplomatic Probationer; 1st Secr. of Legation and Embassy, Councillor of Embassy; resided in Italy, France. China and Switzerland; rec'd deg. 1932; attended 11th League of Nations Assembly, 1930, and Gen. Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1931. Address: Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Vice-Minister of Educ. since June 1937; b. May 1891, Aichi-ken; s. of Yukichi Ito. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; Commr. Iwate-ken; Secr. to Educ. Minister; Secr. Educ. Dept.; Chife Engrg. & Supplementary Educ. Sec. Tech. Educ. Bureau; Chief Students' Dept.; Dir. Higher Educ. Bureau; Pub. thought Educ. Bureau. Address: 881 Shimo-Meguro 4-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Japan Leather Co., Shoes Mfg. Co.; b. Sept. 1896, Tokyo; s. of Haruo Ito. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; studied in England. Address: [illegible] Kudan 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Jokogyo K. K.; b. Aug. 1879, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Ishisuke Ito. Career: grad. Shipbuilding Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha 1905; studied in England 1905-09; Engr. Mitsubishi Nagasaki Dockyard; Chief, Business Dept. same; Mng.-Dir. same. Address: 126 Hara-machi. Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Kaibogikai; b. Dec. 1861, Ehime-ken; s. of Kijiro Ito. Career: joined Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Mgr. Branches at Yokohama, Shanghai and London; Mng.-Dir. later Pres. of same; Dir. Nisshin Steamship Co.; Special Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Japan Times & Mail. Address: 543 Kuzugayatsu, Komachi, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

Mgr. Mitsui & Co. Ltd. London; b. Dec. 1887, Tokyo; m. Shioko Sasaki, cousin of Marquis Y. Sasaki. Career: Mgr. Deutsche Bussan A. G. Berlin; Mgr. Mitsui & Co. Ltd. Sydney; same, Otaru. Address: c/o Mitsui & Co. Ltd. Royal Mail House, 14/19 Leadenhall St., London. E. C. 3.; (home address) 63 Shoto-machi, Shibuya-ku. Tokyo.
Pres. C. Itoh & Co.; Tientsin Spinning Co., Kureha Spinning Co.; b. 1886, Shiga-ken; s. of late Chubei Itoh. Career: succeeded to family estate 1903. Address: Sumiyoshi-mura. Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.-Dir. C. Itoh & Co.; Aud. Tientsin Spinning Co.; b. 1883. Career: Chairman Japan Cotton Merchants Union; Japan Cotton Goods Export Assn.; Mng.-Dir. Japanese Assn. for Export of Cotton Goods to India; Jap. Assn. for Exprt of Cotton Goods to Netherlands East Indies; went to Brazil as Mem. Japan Econ. Mission to Brazil 1935. Address: Sumiyoshi, Mukc-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Matsue Bank; Dir. Izumo Elec. Co.; b. Nov. 1879, Shimane-ken. Career: completed middle sch.; inherited family estate, 1910; his statue was erected at his native place for the merit in exploiting natural resources in the localty 1934. Address: Yakawa-mura, Nita-gun, Shimane-ken.

Former Priv. Secr. to Educ. Minister; b. June 1892. Tambaichi, Nara-ken; 5th s. of Takayoshi Iwai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; served at its London Branch, 1919-25; travelled in Europe 1927-28; returned to Home Office; was charged with laying out Ishiyama Works. Toyo Rayon Co. 1926-27; Acting Mgr. Provision Dept. Mitsui Head Office 1929-31; Gen. Mgr. Brazil Coffee Propaganda & Sales Hdqrs. in Japan 1932-34; went to South Amer. as Mem. Japanese Econ. Mission to Brazil 1935; while in London studied paintings and sculpture for 6 years and was recommended as Hon. Associate of Royal Soc. of Brit. Artists; author of "Outline of Tenrikyo." "Cherry Leaves" (London MacDonald 1922), etc. Address: 196 Horinouchi 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Secr. Saiseikai (Charity Medical Assn., under foundation of Imp. Court); b. Feb. 1904; s. of Baron Tomoharu Iwakura; m. Yoshiko, e. d. of Count Takatsugu Todo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1927; entered Dept. Home Affairs and later Dept. of Imp. Household. Address: 10, Hachiyama-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Pub. Procurator, Miyagi Court of Appeal since 1936; b. Feb. 1881, Saga-ken; bro. of Shigeyoshi Iwamatsu. Career: grad. Law Coll. 1910; Public Procurator, Tokyo, Nagano, and Chiba Local Courts; Chief Public Procurator, Chiba Local Court; Chief Public Procurator, Higher Court, Taiwan Govt.; Yokohama Local Court, Aug. 1929; Public Procurator, Supreme Court; Tokyo Court of Appeal; Dir. Prison Affairs Bureau 1934-36. Address: 1 Katahira-cho Omachigashira, Sendai.

Journalist; Pres. Domei News Agency; b. Sept. 1883, Tokyo; adopted s. of late Seiichi Iwanaga. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1909; served S. M. R. Co. and Govt. Ry. of Japan; became Mng.-Dir. Kokusai News Agency, later Shimbun Rengo-sha. Address: 232 Kami-Osaki 4-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Lecturer, Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Apr. 1869, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Choku Iwasaki, physician. Career: grad. Geol. Course, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Prof. Kumamoto Higher Tech. Sch.; Lecturer, Agri. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: Tsukaguchi Jutakuchi, Tachibana-mura, Kawabe-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Vice-Pres. Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; s. of Baron Hisaya Iwasaki. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; went to England for study 1922; with present firm since 1926; visited South America for inspection 1930. Address: 7 Tatsuoka-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; b. 1865, Kochi-ken; s. of late Yataro Iwasaki. Career: grad. Pennsylvania Univ. 1891; made inspection tour of economic conditions in Europe & America. Address: 1 Yushima Kiridoshi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Pres. Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Dir. Mitsubishi Bank, Yokohama Specie Bank, Mitsubishi Mining Co., Mitsubishi Trust Co., Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; b. Aug. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Yanosuke Iwasaki. Career: grad. 1st Higher Sch.; studied at Cambridge Univ.; made tour of inspection in Europe and America; succeeded to peerage 1908. Address: 2 Torijzaka-machi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers (nominated 1931); b. Apr. 1875, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Hikoshichi Hiyama, later adopted by Kinzo Iwata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; journalistic work 1899-1909; called to the bar 1909; Mem. Legislation Consideration Committee, Imp. Econ. Conf., Tenancy System Inquiry Board etc.; rec'd deg. 1916. Address: 12 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Sumatra Industrial Co. since 1925; b. 1889, Chiba-ken; s. of Kisuke Iwata. Career: grad. Chiba Higher Horticultural Sch. 1912; served Nanyo Rubber Plantation Co. & Nanyo Development Co.; Dir. Nihon Rubber Co. 1920. Address: c/o Sumatra Industrial Co., Sumatra Is., Dutch East Indies.

Minister to Columbia since 1934; b. Mar. 1888, Tokyo; s. of Atsuo Iwate. Career: grad. Consul Course, Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1913; Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer, Consul, Sec. of Foreign Office; Chief of Corr. and Translation Sections; 1st Sec., Legation, Canada; Consul-Gen. Honolulu 1931; Councillor, Embassy, Italy, 1933-34. Address: c/o Japanese Legation, Bogota, Columbia.

Mgr. Tokyo Branch & Councillor, S. M. R. Co.; Mem. Committee of Tourist Ind.; b. 1888, Tokyo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; joined S. M. R. 1927; Chief Shogai Sec. Ry. Dept.; Vice-Gen. Director & Chief, Transport Dept. Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Railway till 1936. Address: c/o S. M. R. Tokyo Branch, Toranomon, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Nov. 1869, Nagano-ken; bro. of late Shuji Izawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; entered official service; Governor, Wakayama-ken, Ehime-ken, Niigata-ken; Metropolitan Police Chief; Gov.-Gen. of Taiwan, 1924; Mayor of Tokyo, 1926. Address: 2517 Nishisugamo 2-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

D.L. Non-official Staff, S. M. R. Co.; b. Oct. 1873, Hokkaido; s. of Rintaro Izumi, farmer; m. Hatsuyo. Career: studied at Sapporo Agri. Coll. Lake Forest Coll. (B.A.), 1906; Univ. Wisconsin (M.A.), 1907; Columbia (Graduate Sch.), 1909-13; apptd. Prof. Keijo Imp. Univ. etc. Address: 566 Tenzanton, Dairen.

Business Mgr. Manchuria Spinning & Weaving Co.; b. Nov. 18[?]6, Yokohama City; s. of Yoshiyuki Tojo (Captain, N.Y.K.) and later adopted s. of Yakichi Izumi (Chief Engineer of N. Y. K.). Career: grad. Econ. Coll., Keio Univ., 1911; entered Yokohama Raw Silk Co., served at New York, Tokyo, Hankow, Nagoya Branches, resigned same and entered Fuji Gas Spinning & Weaving Co. 1924. Sub.-Mgr. Business Dept. same; then present post. Address: 1 Suehiro-cho, Liaoyang, Manchoukuo.

Pres. Osaka Oxygen & Hydrogen Co.; director of several firms; b. Apr. 1883, Osaka; adopted s. of Seisuke Izumi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908. Address: Kyobashi 3-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

M.D.; Dir. Izumiyama Hospital; b. Jan. 1895, Aomori-kne; s. of Matsusaburo Izumiyama, banker. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; apptd. Asst. of same, 1921; Lecturer, 1927; rec'd deg. 1927; Sub-Dir. Miyagi Hospital of Japan Red Cross, 1927; Head Surgean, Hosei Hospital, 1929. Address: 2 Odori Minami 4-chome, Toyohara-machi, Karafuto.

Dr. phil. (Leipzig); Prof. 3rd Higher Sch. since 19[?]; and Lecturer Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1930; b. June 18[?]; Peipzig; m. Hertha Jahn. Career: Teacher at German High Schools until 1924; came to Japan 1924; taught at Yamaguchi Higher Sch. 1924-2[?]; at Shizuoka Higher Sch. 1930-34; 1st Higher Sch. 1934-37. Address: Koto Gakko Kansha, Yoshida Honmachi, Kyoto.

Merchant; Chairman, A. Cameron & Co., Ltd.; b. 1889, Kobe; n. British (both parents and grandparents Welsh); s. of H. D. James, sea captain; m. Winifred Hannah Jones, 1911. Career: educated in Kobe and Liverpool; Chairman, Kobe & Osaka Foreign Chamber of Com. 8 years; British Assn. of Japan Kobe Branch 3 years; Mem. of Council Japan-British Soc. of Kansai; Pres. S. P. C. A. 5 years; Consul-General for Sweden at Kobe & Osaka; Mem. Kobe Harbour Improvement Enquiry Commission, Committee of Hyogo Pref. Assn. of Tourists, Japan-Canada Trade Assn., Merit of Imp. Donation Foundation, Saiseikai; Adviser, Sannomiya Social Relief Committee, Kobe Ward Tourists Assn. Decoration: O. B. E. Recreation: all branches sport. Clubs: Kobe Club, K. R. A. C., Rokko Golf Club, Osaka Club, Mengyo Club, Club Concordia, Shioya Country Club Address: 1 of 121 Aza-Nishinota, Shioya, Akashi-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Permanent Mem. Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Broker, Yokohama Exchange; b. Jan. 1871, Ehime-ken; s. of Kenshichi Joko. Career: Pres. Federation, Yokohama Ind. Assn., Yokohama Silk Exporters Assn.; Japan Silk Industry Assn.; Mng.-Dir. Yokohama Traders' Assn. Address: 171 & 173 Bluff, Yokohama.

Merchant; b. Apr. 1878, Osaka. Career: Chairman, Nickel & Lyons, Ltd.; Kobe Int'l Committee; Mem. of Committee, Kobe & Osaka Foreign Chamber of Commerce; Pres. Kobe Regatta & Athletic Club. Address: Shioya near Kobe.

Pres. Gadelius & Co., Osaka; b. January 1886 Lund, Sweden. Career: Grad. Elec. Engrg. Course Royal Technical Univ. Stockholm 1909; Elec. Engr. at Swedish Gen. Elec. Co. 1909-17; rep. same in Japan from 1912; joined Gadelius & Co. 1917 as Mgr. Kobe Office; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Office 1932. Address: 158 Yamamoto-dori 4-chome, Kobe.

Pres. Joshima Termite Research Institute; Non-official Staff, Dept. of Rys.; b. Feb. 1889, Saga-ken; s. of Denzo Joshima, timber merchant. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll., Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1915; Lecturer, Meiji Coll. of Tech.; established Kyushu Elec. Chemical Ind. Co., 1916; concentrated his efforts for five years towards the prevention of termite damage, discovering a means for this end in 1932; then established present Research Institute. Address: 1650 Hanazono-cho, Fukuoka City.

Pres. Manchoukuo-Japanese Cultural Assn.; b. 1874 in Peiping. Career: Foreign Affairs Commissioner, Yingkow; Chief Finance Dept. Heilungkiang Prov.; Kirin Prov.; Pres. Kirin Provisional Bank 1925; Adviser to Kirin Prov. Office; Pres. Central Bank of Manchou 1932-36. Address: Hsinking.

Count; Mem. House of Peers; Chairman Soc. for Int'l Cultural Relations; Hon. Dr. of Law (Weslyan Univ. Conn. and Amherst. Coll. Mass.) Chairman Nippon Seikosho; Aud. Nippon Seitetsu K. K.; b. May 1865, Kagoshima; s. of late Count Sukenori Kabayama. Career: grad. Amherst Univ. Mass. U.S.A.; founded Kokusai News Agency 1914, presiding over same until it was merged into Nippon Shimbun Rengo Agency 1926; Vice-Pres. America-Japan Soc. since 1924; attended World's Parl. Com. Conf. London as Japan's Delegate 1926 & 1935; London Nav. Conf. as Adviser to Japanese Del. 1929. Address: 215 Gotanda 6-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Int'l Telephone Co.; b. July 1868, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Sukeo Kabayama, samurai. Career: grad. 1st Higher Sch.; studied at Columbia Univ.; grad. Law Coll. Yale Univ. and its P.-G. Course (LL.D.); entered War Office, 1895; Secr. to Premier and Education Minister; Pres. Toyo Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. S. Manchuria Ry. Co.; Chief Secr. of Yamamoto Cabinet. Address: 28 Oban-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Partner Okura & Co.; Pres. Japan Chamber of Com. & Ind., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind., Japan-Manchou Business Assn., Tokyo Rapid Transit Ry. Co., Toyo Mousline Mfg. Co., Chin-Fu Ry. Co.; Vice-Pres. Int'l Assn. of Japan; Chairman Okura Doboku K. K., Shantung Mining Co., East Asia Ind. Co.; b. Sept. 1867, Miye-ken; s. of Watari Kadono. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1884; Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1891; studied in Europe & America 1891-95; served Sanyo Ry. Co. 1897-98; Okura & Co. London 1898-1907; Mem. Dr. Dan's Mission to Europe & Amer. 1921-22; Genoa Econ. Conf. 1922; London World Econ. Conf. 1933; Simla Conf. 1933; Chairman Econ. Mission to Europe & America 1937. Address: 51 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

b. 1877. Wanping-hsien, Hopei Prov. Career: grad. Polit. & Econ. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1909; Legal Advisor, Peking-Mukden Ry. Bureau; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. Tsingtao-Tsinan Ry. Admin. Bureau; Adviser, Ind. Dept. Kirin Prov.; Chief, Secretariat, Gen. Affairs Bureau, Ind. Dept. 1932-35; Dir. Patents Bureau, Manchoukuo Ind. Dept. 1935-37. Address: Hsinking.

Dir. Oriental Development Co.; b. Aug. 1885, Yamanashi-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; apptd. Taxation Officer 1914; Chief, Taxation Offices at Urawa, Nagasaki & Kobe; Chief. Gen. Affairs Section, Kobe Customs 1918; sent to Canada & U. S. A. 1921; Secr. Finance Dept. & Chief, Savings Bank Section 1923; Supt. Nagasaki Customs 1929; Chief, Kumamoto Revenue Supt. Office 1931. Address: 8 Takane-cho Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1892, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Gisaku Kuboi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; entered Okura-gumi; studied Law in Germany 1922-24; called to the Bar; Parl. Councillor of Navy 1934-36. Address: 718 Kita-Shinagawa 4-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Acting Partner, Kubota-gumi; b. May 1907; Tokyo; s. of late Yukichi Kubota, contractor for civil engrg. & building. Career: studied at Waseda University; succeeded father's business. Address: 155 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

Baron; D.E.; b. Apr. 1881, Tokyo; s. of late Baron Yuzuru Kubota. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; studied Ry. & Bridge Construction in America 4 years; entered Ry. Dept.; Chief, Tokyo Construction Office; Dir. Nagoya and Tokyo Ry. Bureau; Dir. Traffic Bureau 1929; Vice-Minister of Ry. in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 35 Kanatomi-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Privy Councillor since 1932; b. Sept. 1865, Okayama-ken; s. of Zenshi Kubota, teacher. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1891; entered Home Dept.; Councillor, Home Dept.; Secr. Agr. & Com. Dept.; Dir. Sanitary Bureau, Home Dept; Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation; Pres. same. Address: 169 Denyen-Chofu 4-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

President of Nichiro Gyogyo Kabushiki Kaisha (Russo-Japanese Fishery Company), Hakodate Cold Storage Co.; Director of Taiheiyo Fishery Co.; b. May 1873, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Hiroshi Uchida; m. Aiko Zushi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1896; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; served Kobe, Hongkong & Hankow Branches; Mng.-Dir. Sakai Celluloid Products Co. 1907; Dir. Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co. 1910; Mng.-Dir. Hazami Mining Co. 1913; Pres. Fuji Paper Mfg. Co. 1918; Pres. Hayakawa Elec. Power Co., etc. Address: [?] Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Dir. Nippon Mining Co.; Mgr. Saganoseki Smelter of same; b. Sept. 1885, Ehime-ken; s. of Satoshi Shinozaki, later adopted by Yasukazu Kubota; m. Yasuko, d. of Chikashi Daito. Career: grad. Metall. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; became Engr. Hitachi Mines; same Saganoseki Smelter 1916; rec'd deg. 1932. Address: Saganoseki Seirenjo, Kita Amabe-gun, Oita-ken.

n: KUBOTA, Tokujiro 久保田篤次郎
t: Mng.-Dir. Nissan Jidosha Kaisha; Aud. Kubota Iron Works; b. 1891, Osaka-fu; s. of Gonshiro Kubota. Pres. Kubota Works. Career: grad. Osaka Tech. Coll. 1912; Mng.-Dir. Jitsuyo Jidosha K. K. 1921-26; Mng.-Dir. Dat Jidosha K. K. 1926-31; Dir. Tobata Foundry Co. 1931-33; Mng.-Dir. Jidosha Seizo K. K. 1933-34. Address: 75 Denyen-Chofu 3-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

n: KUBUSHIRO, Ochimi Mrs. 久布白落實
t: B.D.; Gen. Secr. Japan Women's Temperance Union; b. Dec. 1882 in Kumamoto; d. of Rev. Shinjiro Okubo; m. Rev. Naokatsu Kubushiro. Career: grad. Joshi Gakuin, Tokyo 1902; Pacific Theological Seminary, Berkeley Calif. 1909; in National W. C. T. W. since 1916. Address: 278 Eifuku-cho, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Cultural Sec. Bureau of Information & Publicity Manchoukuo Foreign Offices. Career: Cons. Harbarovsk 1921; Dir. Bd. of Commr. Harbin Municipality; Cons. Blagovechensk 1932. Address: Foreign Dept., Hsinking.

Ph. D.; S. J.; Prof. Jochi Daigaku; b. Mar. 1886, Hollabrunn, Austria; n. Austrian; s. of Count Leo Kuenburg, Councillor of Govt. Career: studied Law at Vienna Univ., Theology at Innsbruck Univ. Philosophy at Munich and Freiburg Univs. 1904-21; apptd. Prof. of Phil. Innsbruck 1922; came to Tokyo 1925. Address: c/o Jochi Daigaku, Kioi-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Navigations Bureau Dept. of Communications; b. 1885, Chufu, Shantung Prov. Career: grad. Peers' Coll. 1903; Chief Ssupingkai-Taonan Ry. Police Dept. 1916; Dir. Peking Highways Bureau; Vice-Dir. State Highways Bureau; Dir. Pub. Works Bureau Kirin Prov. Address: Dept. of Communications Hsinking.

Dir. & Mgr., Kwantoshu Onoda Cement Co.; b. Mar. 1894, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Tomozo Fujino, farmer; later adopted into Kuniyoshi family. Career: Applied Chemistry Course, Engrg. Coll., Kyushu Imp. Univ., 1918; joined Onoda Cement Co., 1919; sent to Europe and America for study, 1924; Mgr. Dairen Branch, same, 1930. Address: Choushuitzu, Dairen suburb.

B.A.; Chinese Consul-General at Taihoku; b. Mar. 1893. Tientsin; n. Chinese; s. of Y. F. Kuo. Career: grad. Econ. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Secr. Ministry of Foreign Affairs 1929-31; Consul-Gen. Yokohama 1932-33. Address: Chinese Consulate-Gen., Taihoku.

M.D.; Dir. Maternity Hospital Japan Red Cross Soc. since 1927; b. Dec. 1881, Morioka; s. of Gen-ichiro Kuji. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; went to America for study 1907; Head, Obstetrics and Gynecology Dept. Iwate Hospital 1908-13; Med. Officer, Chosen Govt. Hospital 1913; Prof. Keijo Med. Coll. 1916; sent to Europe 1919-21; Prof. Kanazawa Med. Coll. 1923. Address: 11 Ebisu-dori 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chief 3rd Sec. Amer. Bureau, Foreign Office; Acting Minister to Portugal since 1932; b. Aug. 1893, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Yasujiro Kumabe, samurai; m. Matsuko, d. of late Eikichi Asawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo, Imp. Univ. 1919; started diplomatic career 1919; Consul Marseilles; Secr. Leg. Mexico & Emb. Turkey; attended Gen. Assembly of League of Nations 1923; Mem. Turkish Straits Adm. Commission 1931-32; Acting Min. to Portugal 1932-37. Address: Foreign Dept., Tokyo.

Dir. 6th Higher Sch.; b. 1873, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Gohei Kumamoto, landowner; m. Sumeko. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; sent to Europe & America for study of educ. 1918. Address: 371 Kunitomi-cho, Okayama City.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 4th District Army of Manchoukuo; b. in Liaoyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Academy Tokyo, 1911; Chief Staff, Kirin Mil. Training Academy; Chief, Defence Army, Kirin Prov.; Chief Staff, Defence Dept. 1932-34; Vice-Minister of Defence & Dir. Horse Adm. Bureau 1934-35. Address: 4th Army Hdqrs., Harbin.

Mem. House of Peers; Company Director; b. Jan. 1871, Kanazawa City; s. of Yukinori Kurachi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1894; entered Home Dept.; and later, Foreign Dept.; apptd. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs. Address: 170 Harajuku 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir.-Gen. Kogyo Chosa Kyokai; Mng.-Dir. Kogyo Tosho K. K.; b. Nov. 1887, Shiga-ken; s. of Toshiro Kurahashi. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Tech. Sch. 1909; studied in U. S. A. 1916-19; attended Int'l Econ. Conf. 1927, 11th Assembly of League of Nations 1930 and 16th Int'l Labor Conf. 1932; Lecturer Meiji Univ.; Dir. Nippon Power Assn. Tokyo Police Welfare Soc.; Japanese Fed. of Exporters Assn. etc. Address: 70 Shimo-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1869, Kagoshima-ken; adopted s. of Jiro Kurasono. Career: grad. Nihon Univ.; elected M.P. 5 times since 1924, Parl. Vice-Min. of Ry. 1935-36. Address: 3 Ichigaya Kaga-cho 1-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Minister to Roumania & Yugoslavia since 1837; b. Mar. 1890, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Shuntaro Kurihara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Elève-Consul Mukden, Lyons; Diplomatic Probationer Spain; Manchoukuo; attended Peace Conf. Paris; Consul Foochow, Hsinking; Secr. Foreign Office; Chief Corr. & Translation Sec. 1929; Consul-Gen. Hsinking 1932-33; Tientsin 1934; Dir. Research Bureau Foreign Office. Address: Japanese Legation, Bucharest, Roumania.

Vice-Consul, Japanese Consulate-Gen., Harbin since 1936; Chief, Mutankiang Branch Office, same; b. Oct. 1897; s. of Hidekusu Kurimoto. Career: grad. Tung Wen Coll., Shanghai 1919; served as journalist two years; entered Asia Bureau, Foreign Office 1922; served at Fuchow, Kirin, London, Changtien, Chihfeng. Address: Branch Office, Japanese Consulate-Gen., Ningan-hsien, Pinkiang Prov., Manchoukuo.

Pres. Kurimoto Iron Works; Mem. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. 1875. Wakayama; s. of Hanjiro Kurimoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; attended Int'l Labor Conf. as Capitalist Delegate 1930. Address: 35 Uyenomiya-cho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka.

Viscount (1912); Privy Councillor; b. Nov. 1851, Tokyo-fu; s. of Koemon Kurino. Career: entered Foreign Office 1881; Dir. Research Bureau; Polit. Bureau; Minister to U.S.A. Italy, France, Russia; Amb. to France 1906; ennobled Baron 1907. Address: 4 Hinoki-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Police Bureau Lungkiang Prov.; b. 1898, Ishikawa-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Judicial Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Justice Dept. 1932-33; Judge North Manchuria Spec. Dict. High Court 1934-35; Vice-Chief High Procurators' Office Chinchow Prov. Address: Lungkiang Prov. Office Tsitsihar.

Minister to Sweden; b. 1886, Fukui-ken; s. of Shunichi Kuriyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Diplo. Probationer Emb. France; Secr. Foreign Dept.; Chief 1st Sec. Treaty Bureau; Chief 3rd Sec.; 1st Class Secr., later Councillor Emb. France 1927; Dir. Treaty Bureau. Address: Japanese Legation, Stockholm, Sweden.

Marquis; Privy Councillor since 1924; Mem. House of Peers: former feudal lord of Fukuoka Clan; b. May 1867, Fukuoka; s. of Nagatomo Kuroda. Career: grad Cambridge Univ. (M.A.) 1887; ennobled 1884; Master of Ceremonies 1889; Vice-Pres. House of Peers 1894. Address: 1 Fukuyoshi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Colonel; Japanese Resident-Mil. Officer, India since 1935; b. 1887, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1910; Mil. Staff Coll.; Staff, Mil. Trading Dept.; Comdr. Inf. 59th Reg.; Sec. Chief War Office. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.

Co. Dir.; Mem. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Kurokawa & Co. Ltd.; b. Jan. 1893, Tokyo; s. of Tokubei Kimura, later adopted by Koshichi Kurokawa. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1915; became Broker, Osaka Stock Exchange 1921. Address: 8 Uehonmachi 8-chome, Tennoji-ku, Osaka.

Pres. Kokusai Kisen Kaisha Ltd. since 1927; b. July 1875, Yamagata-ken; s. of Masachika Kanai, samurai; adopted by Yotaro Kurokawa. Career: grad. Aoyama Gakuin Coll. 1894; joined N.Y.K. 1894; Asst. Mgr. Shanghai Branch 1911; Mgr. Foreign Service Dept. Head Office 1916; Mgr. Kobe Branch 1920; Vice-Pres. 1923; resigned 1924; Delegate on Shipping Affairs, Peace Conf. Paris 1919; Pres. Japan Shipowners' Assn. 1922-26. Address: 14 Shoto, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo,

Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1885, Kyoto; s. of Buemon Kurosaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; entered Legislation Bureau; promoted to Councillor, and Chief, 2nd Sec. same; Dir. Legislation Bureau in Saito Cabinet 1933-34. Address: 1 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Mfr. & Trader (Office Appliances); b: January 1875, Tokyo. Career: spent his younger days in U. S. A. and travelled abroad extensively. Address: 2 Ginza 6-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. Phone: Ginza 1639.

Amb. to Belgium since Apr. 1936; b. Mar. 1886, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Sobei Kurusu. Career: grad. Consular Course Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; Consul Chicago; Consul-General Manila; 1st Secr. Legations Chile and Greece; Embassy Italy, Consul-General Hamburg; Minister Peru; Dir. Com. Bureau. Address: c/o Emb. of Japan, Brussels, Belgium.

Pres. Manchuria Gold Mining Co. since 1935; b. May 1882, Fukui-ken; s. of Tokio Kusama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Finance Dept.; Commr., Revenue Supt. Bureau; Financial Commr. Russia; Secr. Finance Dept.; Chief, Nat. Tax Sec.; Director of Finance Bureau Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Inspector, Bank of Chosen & Oriental Development Co.; Mayor of Nagasaki 1931-33. Address: c/o Manchuria Gold Mining Co., Hsinking.

Dir. Gen. Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Chairman Meiji Life Ins. Co.; Dir. Society for Int'l Cultural Relations; Mem. Spec. Ind. Deliberation Committee; Dir. Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Mitsubishi Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Mitsubishi Trust Co.; Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; Nihon Wireless Telegraph Co.; b. Feb. 1867, Tokyo; s. of Magosaburo Kushida. Career: studied at Daigaku Yobimon & Pennsylvania Univ. 1890; served Mitsubishi Bank 1894-1937. Address: 17 Nagata-cho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Pres. Osaka Imp. Univ.; b. Jan. 1871, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kunitaro Kusumoto, physician. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Teacher Osaka Higher Med. Sch. 1905; sent to Germany for study 1906; Prof. Osaka Med. Coll. 1919; Dean 1924. Address: Hirata, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

D. Sc.; Prof. Kyushu Imp. Univ. since 1918; b. 1878, Tokyo; s. of Aishin Kuwaki. Career: grad. Sci. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; apptd. Asst. and later Lecturer of same; studied Physics at Berlin Univ. Address: 10 Jigyo Nishi-machi, Fukuoka City.

D. Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. June 1874, Tokyo; s. of Aishin Kuwaki. Career: grad. Phil. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Prof. 1st Higher Sch. 1899; Lecturer, later Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Litt. Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1906; sent to Europe and America for study 1907-09; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Mem. Imp. Academy 1923; travelled abroad, [?] and 1930; Lecturer, Waseda Univ. Address: [?] Kita-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo,

Lt.-Gen.; attached Ordnance Central Dept.; b. Oct. 1885, Hiroshima s. of late Takadai Kuwaki. Career: grad. Mil. Staff Coll. 1914; sent to Russia 1917; to Europe 1920; Greece as Mil. Attaché 1921; apptd. Instructor Mil. Staff Coll. 1922; Comdr. Field Artillery 2nd Reg. 1928; 3rd Brig. 1932; Staff Taiwan Army 1934; Chief 1st Dept. Gen. Staff Office 1936-37. Address: 31 Kita-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Minister to Netherlands since 1937; b. Mar. 1884, Kagawa-ken; s. of Yasuzo Kuwashima. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1906; Secr. Foreign Office and Tokyo Reconstruction Bureau; 1st Secr. Emb.; Consular service Mukden, Hankow, Bombay, Chicago; Councillor Emb. Washington; Consul-Gen. Honolulu; Tientsin 1930; Dir. East Asia Bureau Foreign Office. Address: Japanese Legation, The Hague, Netherlands.

Prof. Osaka Sch. of Foreign Languages for 15 years; b. Feb. 1872, Peking, China; s. of Kwan Chang-shan, official. Career: Teacher at Japanese Legation & Garrison in Peking for 11 years; at Yokohama Specie Bank, Div. Hdqrs. and S. M. R. Local Office in Liaoyang for 5 years; Prof. Otaru Higher Com. Sch. for 8 years. Address: 1368 Himematsu, Sumiyoshi-cho, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Councillor, and Member of Board of Engineers, Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. Dec. 1888, Kanazawa; 3rd. s. of Tetsusaburo Kyuno; m. Ayako, d. of Hidemi Matsunami 1915. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; immediately joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Diesel Engine Designer at Kobe Works, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co. till 1916; Aero-Engine Designer at Mitsubishi Internal Combustion Engine Co. up to 1920; Chief Engr. and Vice-Pres. of Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. 1920-34; pioneer maker of Japanese Diesel engine and aero-engine; made great contribution towards completion of building Japanese Navy and Army airplanes. Address: 275 Asagaya 3-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.
American Consul at Mukden; b. 1891 of Amer. Parents in Turkey. Career: U. S. Foreign Service since 1911. Address: American Consulate-Gen., Mukden.

M.A. (Glasgow); M.D. (Edinburgh); Medical Missionary; b. Aug. 1870, Kilmarnock, Scotland; s. of David Landsborough, Minister of the Gospel; m. Marjorie Ellen Learner. Career: grad. Kilmarnock Academy 1887; Glasgow Univ. 1890; Edinburgh Univ. 1895; arrived in Formosa as Medical Missionary under Presbyterian Church of England 1895. Address: Shokwa, Taiwan.
Hon. Consul for Norway at Dairen; Merchant; b. Feb. 1898; s. of F. Larkins; m. Dulcie Howell. Address: c/o W. H. Winning & Co., P. O. Box 134 Dairen.
Teacher at Jochi Daigaku; b. Nov. 1898, Nieheim i/Westf. Germany; s. of Georg Lassalle, judge. Career: engaged in relief work at Mikawashima, Tokyo. Address: c/o Jochi Daigaku, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Diplomatist; Charge d'Affaires of Peru in Japan and China; b. Oct. 1892, Lima, Peru; n. Peruvian. Career: studied in England and Peru; diplomatic service of Peru in U. S. A., Ecuador, Colombia, Bolivia and Japan; also in Foreign Office in Lima. Address: Peruvian Legation, 13 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

B.A.; Bishop of Sendai; b. May 1902, Quebec, Canada; s. of Joseph E. Lemieux, merchant. Career: studied at the college of Ste Anne de la Pocatiere; entered the Dominican order in 1923; studied at Rome, 1928; at Oxford, 1929; arrived in Japan, 1930; apptd. missionary in charge of the Catholic parish at Miyamae-cho, Hakodate; apptd. bishop of Sendai April 1936; consecrated at Sendai June 1936. Address: Tenshuko Kyokai, 161 Moto-Terakoji, Sendai-shi, Miyagi-ken.

Mech. Engr.; Krupp rep. in Japan; b. April 1877 at Koenigsberg, Germany. Career: Mng.-Dir. of Factory in Russia before Great War; joined Krupp; came to Japan 1928. Address: Seinenkai Apt., Iriarai-machi, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Merchant; Tokyo Mgr. Schoeller-Bleckmann Phoenix Seiko G. K.; b. May 1903, Yokohama; s. of Eduard Levedag; m. F. Mary Crossley. Career: German Sch. Yokohama; St. Joseph's Coll. Yokohama; Oberrealschule Muenster & Bonn Germany; University Bonn; entered business 1926; Klausmayer & Co. Bonn, Roemhild A. G. Weimar, Pressa Exhibition Cologne; joined present firm at Vienna, Austria 1928; attached to Japan end of same year. Address: 58 Nichinoya, Kitagata, Yokohama.

Dir. Manshu Takushoku Kaisha; b. 1878, Heishan-hsien. Fengtien Prov. Career: Secr. Mil. Gov.'s Office, Heilungkiang Prov.; Dir. Forestry Bureau and Chief, Gold Mining Bureau, Kirin; Dir. Adm. Bureau, Kirin-Hailung Ry. 1926; Chief Secr. Kirin Prov. Office 1932-33; Chief, Civil Dept. Kirin Prov. 1933-34. Address: Kirin Prov. Office, Kirin.
Pres. Supreme Procurator's Office, Manchoukuo; b. 1877. Honan Prov. Career: grad. Hosei Univ. Tokyo; Judge, Fengtien Supreme Court. Address: Supreme Procurator's Office, Hsinking.

Manchoukuo Communications Minister; b. 1895. Shenyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov.; s. of Li Yungwoo. Career: grad. Russian Com. Sch. 1920; Sino-Russian Law & Polit. Univ. Harbin; Chief Secr. Harbin Municipal Administration Bureau; Vice-Director, same; Advisor to North Manchuria Railway Administration Office, Fengtien Prov.; Sino-Soviet Conf. Office; Consul.-Gen. Vladivostok; Dir. Educ. Adm. Bureau, Harbin 1927; Dir. N. M. R. Adm. Bureau; Supt. same; Chief Dir. N. M. R. 1932-35. Address: c/o Communications Dept. Hsinking.

Lieut.-Gen.; Chief of Mukden Central Mil. Training Sch.; b. 1884, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Tokyo; apptd. Major-Gen. 1920; Chief Staff Mongolia Frontier Comptroller Gen.'s Office 1931; Gen. Staff Taoliao Guards Army 1932; Dir. Gen. Staff Bureau Defence Dept. 1933-35; Vice-Minister of Defence 1935-37. Address: Central Mil. Training Sch. Mukden.

Pres. Manchoukuo Supreme Court since 1932; b. 1884, Minhou-hsien, Fukien Prov. China. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. Tokyo; Dir. Bureau of Special Sch. Affairs, Education Dept., China 1912; Pres. High Court, Peking. Address: Supreme Court, Hsinking.
District Mgr. Manchoukuo & Korea Nipponophone Co. Ltd.; b. May 1899, Kobe; s. of H. Lindstrom, missionary; m. Ernestine Gardiner. Address: c/o Nipponophone Co., Ltd. 212 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

Chief Secr. Legislative Council, Manchoukuo; b. in Liaoyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mukden Law Coll.; studied law in Japan; Chief, Hsingho-tao, Tsitsihar 1921. Address: Legislative Council, Hsinking.

b. 1879, Chekiang Province; s. of Lo Shu Hsun. Career: Inspector Agr. Coll.; Pres. Agr. Bureau Hupei Prov. 1900; sent to Japan for educ. research 1901; Advisor of Educ. Canton & Kwangsi Provs. 1902; Kiangsu Prov. 1903; Councillor Educ. Dept. 1908; sent to Japan for Agr. Research 1909; Privy Councillor 1932; Pres. Supervisory Council till 1937; accorded privilege of former post. Address: Hsinking.
Acting Consul of Esthonia at Harbin; b. Dec. 10, 1897, Tartu, Esthonia. Address: 11 Fifth Linie, Harbin.

Major-Gen.; Chief Staff, Manchoukuo 5th District Army since 1934; b. Apr. 1885, Hankow, Hupei Prov. China; s. of Lu Hu. Career: grad. Mil. Academy, Japan 1901; studied Mil. Artillery & Engrg. Sch. Japan 1904; Art. Col. 1906; Major-Gen. and Chief, 1st Sec. Gen. Staff Office 1909; Lieut.-Gen. & Vice-Chief Staff 1911; attached to Kirin Prov. Guards Army 1932-34. Address: c/o 5th Army Hdqrs., Chengteh, Jehol Prov., Manchoukuo.

Manchoukuo Minister of Industry; b. 1890, Fushun, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Kiangsu Law Coll.; Vice-Pres. Mukden Assembly; sent to Washington Conf. as Rep. Three Eastern Provs. 1923; went to Russia 1923; Chairman Soviet-Chinese Conf. & Mukden-Soviet Conf.; Pres. Chinese Eastern Ry. 1924; Gov. Chinese Eastern Ry. 1927-29; Mayor of Harbin & Gov. North Manchuria Spec. Dist. 1932-34; Pinkiang Prov. Dec. 1934-May 1935; Civil Affairs Min. 1935-37; Fin. Min. May 1937. Address: Dept. of Ind., Hsinking.
Gov. Tunghua Prov. Career: Editor Taitung Daily, Dairen; Dir. Com. Affairs Bureau Foreign Dept. 1932-35; Secr. to Prime Minister. Address: Governor's Residence, Tunghua.

Pres. Minseito; M.P.; b. 1861, Akita-ken; s. of Nagahide Machida. Career: grad. Daigaku Yobimon (now Tokyo Imp. Univ.); published magazine "Toyo Keizai Zasshi"; went to Europe; joined Bank of Japan; Yamaguchi Bank; became Dir. of same; sent to Diet 8 times from Akita-ken; Councillor, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Agr. & For. Minister; Min. of Com. & Ind. 1934-36. Pres. Hochi Shimbun. Address: 73 Minami Enoki-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Consul for Greece at Kobe; merchant; b. Nov. 1885, Glasgow, Scotland; n. British; s. of late James John MacNaughton, civil engr. Career: grad. Kelvinside Acad. Glasgow; arrived in Japan 1909; Asst. Findlay Richardson & Co. Yokohama & Kobe; served in World War 1917-19; returned to Japan 1919; Hon. Vice-Cons. for Greece 1921; Cons. 1921; commenced business on his account 1924. Address: Nippon Bldg. 79 Kyo-machi, Kobe.

M.A., M.B.E., F.R.G.S.; Comm. Secr, British Embassy Tokyo; b. 1886 at Inverness, Scotland; m. Agnes Elsie Davidson Bruce. Career: entered consular service 1909; served at Kobe, Hakodate, Yokohama, Shimonoseki, Oslo, Honolulu, Manila. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Sept. 1884, Hyogo-ken; s. of Shirobei Maeda. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1907; Mem. County Assembly; elected M.P. since 1924; Councillor Finance Dept. 1931; Parl. Vice-Min. of Com. & Ind. 1936-37. Address: 3 Shin-machi 3-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

b. October 1887, Mie-ken; adopted s. of Ryu Maeda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Councillor; sent to Europe & America for inspection 1924; Dir. Osaka Region; Dir. Traffic Bureau; Dir. Ry. Adm. Bureau, 1934-37. Address: 4312 Oi Yamanaka-cho, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Dir. Branch Hospital, Japan Red Cross, Osaka; b. 1877, Fukui-ken; s. of Shohaku Maeda, samurai. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904; served, Red Cross Hospital; rec'd deg. 1910. Address: 29 Nishino-cho 1-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

D.E. (1930); Prof. of Architecture, Tokyo Univ. of Engrg. since 1931; b. Dec. 1880, Kyoto; s. of Shohaku Maeda, doctor. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; served Kwantung Prov. Civil Adm. Office; Engr. Kwantung Govt. 1905; Prof. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1907; despatched to England as Commr. British-Japanese Exhibition, and later Student of Educ. Dept. 1909. Address: 1040 Nippori 9-chome, Arakawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Manchuria Telephone & Telegraph Co.; b. 1883, Mie-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Chief, Telephone Section Communications Bureau, Com. Dept.; Dir. Sendai Com. Bureau, 1927; Dir. Tokyo Com. Bureau. Address: 286 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Editorial Writer, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Dir. Pacific Problems Research Committee; Dir. Tokyo City Adm. Research Committee; Councillor Social Bureau Home Dept.; b. 1884, Tokyo. Career: grad. German Law Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Priv. Secr. to Home Minister; Asst. Mayor of Tokyo 1921-23; Govt. Delegate to Int'l Labor Conf. Geneva 1923-26. Address: 18 Hikawa-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Lt.-Gen.; Comdr. 8th Div.; Mem. House of Peers; b. June 1885; s. of Toshiaki Maeda and later adopted by Toshitsugu Maeda. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Mil. Staff Coll.; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll.; studied in Germany; served British Army in World War; went to England again as Mil. Attaché; Comdr. Inf. 2nd Reg. Imp. Guard Div. 1930; Comdr. Inf. 2nd Brig. 1933; Chief 4th Sec. Gen. Staff Office 1935; Dir. Mil. Staff Coll. 1936-37. Address: 8th Div. Hdqrs., Hirosaki.

Prop. of Watch, Jewelry, & Spectacles Store; b. Apr. 1890, Nagasaki; s. of Tsurumatsu Maeda. Career: served Army Adm. Office at Yingkow during Russo-Japanese War, 1904; grad. Chinese Language Sch. 1908, and Russian Lang. Sch. 1910; engaged in business at Vladivostok, 1912-18; opened shop at Harbin 1917; Mem. Harbin Chamber of Com. & Ind. since 1932. Address: 47 Mostowaya St., Harbin.

M.P.; b. Feb. 1882, Wakayama-ken; bro. of Shoichi Maeda. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogakuin (Law Coll.); French Dept. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang.; German Dept. Doitsu Kyokai Sch.; practised at the bar; sent to Diet 7 times since 1917; Dir.-Gen. Seiyukai; Dir. Chuo Shimbun, East-India Ind. Co., Hayakawa Elec. Power Co., Keijo Elec. Ry. Co.; Pres. Legislation Bureau in Tanaka Cabinet 1927; Com. & Ind. Minister in Inukai Cabinet 1931-32; Ry. Min. in Hirota Cabinet 1936-37. Address: 28 Mikawadai-machi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.
Mng.-Dir. Oriental Can Mfg. Co.; b. May 1885, Nagano-ken; s. of Enji Maezawa. Career: grad. Fisheries Institute and entered business. Address: 199 Higashi-Osaki 3-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. of Law and Polit. Sci.; Consul for Italy at Harbin; b. June 1883, Pinerolo, Italy; s. of Giulio Maffei, lawyer; m. Marinette Poncet-Zbindene. Career: Consul for Italy in Cordoba, Hankow; Bratislawa, Daker. Address: Italian Consulate 93 Sungarisky Pr., Harbin.

D.L.; Advisor Tokyo Asahi Shibun; Prof. Meiji Univ.; Lecturer Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. Dec. 1878, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Oregon and Iowa State Univs.; Chief Editor Tokyo Asahi Shimbun. Address: 915 Zoshigaya 6-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Sc.; Dean, Sc. Coll. Osaka Imp. Univ.; Emeritus Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; Prof. Tokyo Engrg. Coll.; Mem. Chem. Phy. Research Inst.; b. 1874, Kyoto; s. of Toshitami Majima. Career: grad. Chem. Course, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; studied Chemistry in England & Germany; rec'd deg. 1909; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1910; Dean, Sc. Coll. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1930; won Imp. Academy Prize for study of Lacquer. Address: Jurakuso, Takarazuka-kogai, Hyogo-ken.

M.P.; Lawyer; b. May 1885, Gifu-ken; s. of Ihei Makino. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Secr. Communications Supt. Bureau; Secr. to Educ. Minister; joined the bar; sent to Diet 7 times; Councillor Com. & Ind. Dept.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Com. in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 50 Shimo-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
Count; Ex-Lord Keeper of Privy Seal. (See 1936 issue.)

Dr. of Econ.; Prof. of Sci. of Finance, Waseda Univ.; Adviser, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun-sha; b. Jan. 1879, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Teizo Makino; m. Kikuko Saigo, 1910. Career: Waseda Univ.; apptd. Teacher, Kumamoto Com. Sch.; Official, Agr. & Com. Dept.; joined Asahi Shimbun-sha 1911, and served as Corr.; Chief, Political Econ. and Editorial Depts.; rec'd deg. (Tokyo Imp. Univ.) 1928; author of many books on econ. subjects. Address: 562 Sendagaya-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

B.D.; Dir. Katei-gakko (Reformatory for Boys) since 1933; b. July 1871 in Nishi Oji-mura, Shiga-ken; s. of Anryu Makino; m. Shigei Sawamura. Career: grad. Doshisha, Kyoto; Yale Div. Sch., New Haven Conn.; preacher Kyoto Cong. Churches; apptd Vice-Pres. C. E. World Union 1917-19; Councillor for Social Works at Dept. Interior Affairs, S. M. R. Co.; Osaka Pref. Gov. 1919-1933. Address: 767 Kami-Takaido 3-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo

Dir. La Fédération Equestre Imperial du Japon, Int'l Equestrian Assn., Tokyo Riding Club; b. Mar. 1887, Tokyo; s. of Kiyonari Makita. Career: studied English Litt. at Waseda Univ.; became Pres. Makita Orimono G. K.; Com. Councillor Toyokuni Bank; with Count Matsudaira, founded La Fédération Equestre Imperial du Japon and Int'l Equestrian Assn. Address: 10 Horie-cho 3-chome, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Pres. Showa Hikoki Kogyo K. K.; Dir. Nihon Seitetsu K. K.; b. Sept. 1871, Osaka; s. of Toranojo Makita. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; entered Mitsui Mining Co.; went to Europe & America for observation 1898; Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Mining Co. 1913; Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha 1932. Address: 43 Kita-Higakubo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Pres. Nagasaki Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; b. Jan. 1882. Nagasaki-ken; s. of Ishichi Makiyama, samurai. Career: grad. Polit. & Econ. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1906; elected M.P. 7 times since 1917; Parl. Vice-Minister of Navy 1917. Address: 9 Onden 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Mitsui Bank; Dir. Showa Bank; b. July 1883. Tsuyama, Okayama-ken. Career: grad. Aoyama Gakuin; entered Mitsui Bank; studied abroad; Mgr. Nagoya Branch. Address: 176 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D.E. (1891); Mem. House of Peers (nominated 1927); Pres. Nihon Kogaku-kai; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo & Kyushu Imp. Univs.; b. Nov. 1861, Tokyo; s. of Hajime Mano. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo 1881; Asst. Prof. of Alma Mater 1882; studied at Glasgow Univ. 1886-89; on return home became Prof.; Judge Patents Bureau; Dir. Tech. Educ. Bureau, Educ. Dept. & Prof. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Pres. Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1913. Address: [?] Yoyogi Hon-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Journalist; b. Aug. 1911, Brussels, Belgium; s. of Sibyl-Strum Elie Marcuse, journalist. Career: former sailor; entered Shanghai Office of Havas News Agency as Asst.-Editor 1932; now Tokyo Corr. of Havas, and several other French publications. Address: c/o The Domei Tsushin-sha, Dentsu Bldg., Ginza, Tokyo.

S.T.D.; J.C.D.; D.D.; Most Rev., Titular Archbishop of Doclea, Apostolic Del. to Nippon since 1933; b. Jan. 1895 at Rome, Italy; s. of Louis Marella, official, Holy See. Career: studied at Pontifical Roman Seminary, Rome; Univ. of Appolinaris; Royal Univ. of Rome; ordained priest, 1918; consecrated bishop, 1933; official of Sacred Congregation of Propaganda, Rome; Counsellor, Apostolic Del. Washington U.S.A. Address: Apostolic Delegation, 12 Shinryudo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

B.A.; M.A.; Ped. D.; Lecturer, Osaka Univ. of Com. since 1931; b. Apr. 1875, Farmington, Ill., U. S. A.; s. of Chas. M. Martin, doctor; m. Esther B. Ludwig. Career: grad. Cornell Coll. Iowa 1898; studied at Univ. of Chicago, Boston Univ., Harvard Univ., Columbia Univ. and Univ. of London; missionary work at Tientsin 1900; at Nagasaki and Kumamoto 1900-04; Teacher at Wiley High Sch. 1906-08; Asst. Prof. Dakota Wesleyan Univ. 1908-13; Prof. Coll. of the Pacific, Calif. 1913-14; Aoyama Gakuin 1914-30; Yencheng Univ. 1930-31. Address: 67 Aotani-machi 2-chome, Nada-ku, Kobe.

Principal Dairen 2nd Middle Sch.; b. Oct. 1885, Yonezawa City; s. of Tokujiro Maruyama; m. Nobu. Career: grad. Hiroshima Normal Coll. 1908; Assist. Prof. of same 1909; Teacher Dairen Middle School 1917-23; went to Europe and America for study and inspection 1926-27. Address: 43 Suisen-cho, Dairen.
Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Bank; b. 1880, Yamagata-ken; s. of Jiemon Ito; later adopted by Toku Maruyama. Career. grad. Law Dept. Keio Univ. 1906. Address: 10 Takane-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Colonel; Sec. Chief, Gen. Staff Office since 1936; b. 1883, Nagano-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1912; Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in England; Resident-Mil. Officer, India; Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Mil. Attaché, Embassy, England 1934-35. Address: c/o Gen. Staff Office, Tokyo.
