Mem. House of Peers; b. Sept. 1883, Hiroshima-ken; bro. of Mokichi Maruyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; entered Metropolitan Police Board; Dir. of Public Peace Dept.; sent to Europe & America to study police affairs, 1917; Dir. Police Affairs Bureau, Chosen Govt.; Asst.-Mayor of Tokyo 1926; Met. Police Chief 1929-31; nominated Peer, 1934. Address: 96 Owada-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor, and Member of Board of Engineers, Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. Nov. 1886, Aichi-ken; 2nd s. of Murajiro Mase; m. Fusa, d. of Hikokichi Shinmi. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Chief Engrg. Dept. Mitsubishi Internal Combustion Engine Co. Ltd.; Chief Engrg. Dept. Kobe Works, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; pioneer maker of Japanese Diesel engine specially noted for submarine diesel engine; rendered distinguished services in introducing the L type submarine, its building and development. Address: 66 Asagaya 5-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Yashima Automobile Co. Ltd.; b. 1881, Nagasaki. Career: grad. Ecole d'Etoile du Matin, Tokyo; London Mgr. Takata & Co.; Mgr. Foreign Dept. same Tokyo; established present firm 1925, representing Chrysler Export Corp. for the Japanese Empire. Clubs: Rotary Club, Tokyo Club. Address: 170 Harajuku 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Journalist & Author; b. Jan. 1879, Newburgh, N.Y., U.S.A.; s. of John A. Mason, newspaper proprietor; m. Edith Hannah Halbert. Career: grad. Barnard Sch. N. Y. and Coll. of New York City; London Editor & later European Mgr. United Press 1899-1908; New York Corr. London Daily Express 1908-31; War Critic, United Press 1914-18; Collaborator on Foreign Affairs, La Prensa, Buenos Aires since 1925; Chairman, New York Phil. Soc. 1929-31; Vice-Pres. India Academy of America 1930-35; Mem. Advisory Committee on Japanese Studies, Columbia Univ. N. Y.; Publications; Com. Progress in the Philippine Islands (with Dr. Regidor Jurado), 1905; Creative Freedom 1926; The Creative East 1928; Kami Nagara no Michi, 1933 (English language edition, "The Meaning of Shinto," 1935); Sozo no Nihon, 1934. Address: Imperial Hotel, Tokyo.

M.P.; Pres. Jitsugyo-no-Nihon-sha; b. Oct. 1869, Niigata-ken; s. of Seishiro Masuda. Career: grad. Waseda Univ.; joined Yomiuri Shimbun; Editor, Economic & Financial Sec., same; established present firm 1900; Vice-Speaker, House of Rep. 1931; elected Representative 6 times. Address: 125 Hara-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Daido Elec. Power Co., Showa Electric Power Co., Tateyama Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Daido Fertilizer Co.; Dir. Kamioka Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; b. Feb. 1869; s. of late Giemon Masuda, Shizuoka-ken. Career: Secr. to Count Shimpei Goto; once elected Representative. Address: 48 Jochi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Adviser, Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. Nov. 1847; s. of Takayoshi Masuda, samurai. Career: apptd. Kiheinokami (Cav. Inspector) and Zohei-Gonnokami (Ordnance Inspector) of Shogunate; Vice-Pres. Senshu Kaisha; participated in establishment of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and apptd. Pres.; Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; created Baron for merit of his contributions to commerce. Address: 731 Itabashi, Odawara, Kanagawa-ken.

Baron; Pres. Taiwan Sugar Mfg. Co.; b. Sept. 1875, Tokyo-fu; s. of Takashi Masuda. Career: grad. Com. Inst. of Antwerp, Belgium; Dir. Imp. Theater, Morinaga Confectionery Co., Chiyoda Fire Ins. Co., Nippon Brick Co., etc. Address: 15 Hirakawa-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
Vice-Pres. Ind. Bank of Manchou; b. Mar. 1884; s. of Tokunori Matsubara, Okayama-ken. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch.; Vice-Pres. Bank of Chosen. Address: Ind. Bank of Manchou, Hsinking.

D.L.; Lecturer, Tohoku Imp. Univ., Tokyo Imp. Univ., Chuo Univ., Senshu Univ.; b. Oct. 1877, Fukui-ken; s. of Kazushiro Matsubara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; Consul at Chicago and Hsinking; Secr. Foreign Dept., 1912; 2nd Secr. Legation; 1st Secr. same; Chief, Translation Section Foreign Dept.; Councillor of Embassy, Germany. Address: 531 Sendagaya 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. & Chairman Chem. Div. Nat. Research Council; Vice-Pres. Int'l Union of Chem.; b. May 1872, Nagoya; s. of Yasoichi Matsubara. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; studied at Univs. of Manchester and Berlin 1903-06; apptd. Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; Prof. 1909; Dean. Sc. Fac. 1929; Emer. Prof. 1933; attended as Govt. Delegate 2nd Int'l Convention of Int'l Catalogue of Sc. Litt. London 1905, and 6th Int'l Congress of Applied Chemistry Rome 1906, as Delegate of National Research Council, General Assembly of Int'l Research Council, Brussels 1926; General Assemblies of International Union of Chemistry, Washington 1926, and Madrid 1934; is mem. of several Committee of Ministry of Educ., etc. Address: 10 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Tumen Customs; b. 1884, Kanazawa, Japan. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served at Customs, Tientsin, Dairen, Shanghai and Tsingtao; present post since 1932. Address: c/o Tumen Customs, Tumen, Manchoukuo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; b. Nov. 1892, Saga-ken; s. of late Baron Masahisa Matsuda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Uuiv. 1918; apptd. Judge, Marine Court of Inquiry; Secr. Colonization Bureau of Cabinet 1924; Secr. Taiwan Govt. 1931; sent to Europe, America & Africa 1930; Gov. South Sea Govt. 1932; Dir. Monopoly Bureau Chosen 1933-34. Address: 1008 Nishigahara, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Planning Bureau Gen. Affairs Board Manchoukuo State Council; b. 1900. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1921; entered Finance Dept.; Commr. same; Dir. Accounts Bureau 1932-36. Address: State Council Hsinking.

LL.D.; Lafayette Coll.; Rutgers Coll. and Univ. of Missouri (U.S.A.); Imp. Household Minister since Mar. 1936; b. Apr. 1877, Tokyo; s. of late Katamori Matsudaira, Lord of Aizu Clan. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; attaché, Embassy, London 1902; Staff, Treaty Revision 1911; 2nd Secretary Legation, Peking 1912-14; Consul-General Tientsin 1914; Chief, Diplomatic Mission in Siberia 1918; Mem. Inter-Allied Ry. Committee, Siberia 1919; Dir. Europe & America Bureau, Foreign Office 1920; Secr.-Gen. Japanese Delegation, Disarm. Conf. Washington 1921; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 192[?]; Ambassador to U.S.A. 1925-28; Delegate to Gen. Assembly League of Nations 1929 and 1930; same to London Naval Conf. 1930; same to Gen. Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1932; Amb. to England 1929-36. Address: 16 Shoto, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Pres. House of Peers since June 1937; Chairman Japan Central Sericultural Assn. since Jan. 1936; Pres. Teikoku Horse Improvement Assn.; Imp. Supporters' Assn. for Soldiers; Vice-Pres. Teikoku Horse-Race Society, Saisei-kai (The Imperial gift foundation); Dir. Daito Bunka Kyokai; b. Dec. 1874, Tokyo; s. of Yoritoshi Matsudaira. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; Law Dept. Waseda Univ. 1897. Address: 15 Komagome 4-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Grand Master of Ceremonies; b. Mar. 1882, Tokyo; s. of late Yoshinaga Matsudaira. Career: grad. Oxford Univ. (Balliol Coll.), England; Master of Ceremonies; K.C.V.O., C.B.E. and other foreign decorations; went to London as Chief Suite Prince Chichibu 1937. Address: 8 Fujimi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. South Seas Development Co.; b. Jan. 1876, Fukushima-ken; s. of Kyuhei Matsue. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1899; studied in Louisiana Univ.; entered Japan Sugar Mfg. Co.; Chief, Osaka Factory; established Toroku Sugar Mfg. Co. 1910; Mng.-Dir. same; Mng.-Dir. Niitaka Sugar Mfg. Co. 1916; Mng.-Dir. present firm; despatched to Europe by Agr. & Com. Dept. for study 1903-06. Address: 111 Fujimae-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

b. May 1891, Miye-ken; s. of Bunshi Matsui. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; Commr. Chiba-ken; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Mem. Cabinet Research Bureau; Dir. Resources Bureau 1935-36; Tohoku Rehabilitation Affairs Bureau 1936; Dir. Resources Bureau of Cabinet. Address: 176 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

General; Supreme Comdr. of Japanese Troops in Shanghai; b. 1878 in Aichi-ken; s. of Takekuni Matsui. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1892; Staff Kwantung Army Hdqrs; Chief 2nd Section Gen. Staff Office; Staff Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. 11th Div. 1929; Comdr-in-Chief Taiwan Army 1933-34; Supreme War Councillor. Address: 2147 Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Dir. Maison Franco-Japonaise; b. Mar. 1868; s. of Yasuzo Matsui, Osaka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; 3rd Secr. Legation; 2nd Secr. same; 1st Secr. same; Councillor, Foreign Office; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs; Foreign Min. 1924; Ambassador to England; Delegate, Paris Peace Conf. 1916. Address: 52 Shimo-Rokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Agr.; Dir. Chiba Horticultural Coll. since 1931; b. Dec. 1883; s. of Tsunesaburo Matsui. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; taught at Coll. of Agr. & Forestry Morioka and Utsunomiya 1909-23; Sch. Inspector, Dept. of Educ. 1928. Address: Matsudo-machi, Chiba-ken.

Former Pres. Kyoto Imp. Univ. since 1933; b. 1873. Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tsukuda Matsui. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; studied chem. at Glessen & Liverpool Univs.; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Pres. of same till June 1937. Address: 19 Kitasono-cho, Shimokamo, Kyoto.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Vice-Pres. Police Assn. and Fire-Prevention Assn.; Dir. Japan Red Cross Society, Civil Educ. Soc. and Central Social Welfare Assn.; Adviser of Central Inst. of Police Training; b. Sept. 1866, Hiroshima-shi; s. of Yurin Matsui, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; apptd. Police Supt.; Chief, Yotsuya Police Station; Chief, 1st, 2nd Dept. and Fire Dept. Metropolitan Police Board; Procurator, Chosen Govt.; Gov. Shizuoka-ken and Aichi-ken; sent to Europe and America for inspection of police and fire protection services; rec'd deg. 1910. Address: 3141 Oi Kashima-cho, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor Concurrently Chief Document Sec. of Dept. of Communications of Manchoukuo; b. 1803, Nagoya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1927; entered S. M. R. Co.; Chief 3rd Sec., Ry. Bureau, Communications Dept. 1932; Secr. Privy Council 1932-36; Councillor Manchoukuo Embassy Tokyo 1936-37. Address: c/o Dept. of Communications Hsinking.

M.P.; Pres. Taiwan Steamship Co., Japan-Soviet Oil Co.; Rep. Mgr. Matsu Shokai; b. Dec. 1865; s. of late Prince Masayoshi Matsukata. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied at Oxford, Yale and Paris Univs.; Secr. to Prime Minister; Pres. Kawasaki Dockyard Co.; Special Mem. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind.; visited U.S.S.R. on business 1932; established Matsukata Japan-Soviet Oil Co. 1933. Address: 20 Yamamoto-dori 4-chome, Kobe.

Dir. Taiwan Development Co.; Pres. Taiwan Elec. Power Co.; b. Feb. 1872, Ehime-ken; s. of Sohei Matsuki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; Councillor Communications Dept.; Dir. Railway Dept.; Councillor Tokyo City; Dir. Elec. Bureau; Chief Dir. Yamashita Gomei Kaisha 1918; Vice-Pres. Yamashita Steamship Co.; Dir. Uraga Dock Co.; Vice-Pres. Capital Reconstruction Board. Address: 4 Shoin-cho 2-chome, Taihoku.

Dir. Legislative Bureau, General Affairs Board State Council of Manchoukuo; b. Mar. 1898, Yamagata-ken; s. of Kiyonao Matsuki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1922; joined S. M. R. Co.; apptd. Legal Adviser to Kwantung Army 1931; Dir. Legislation Bureau Manchoukuo 1932; Councillor of same 1933-35. Address: 8 Keiminro, Goshiki-gai, Hsinking.

Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. Manchuria Development Co. since 1936; b. July 1890, Tokyo; s. of Tokutaro Matsukuma. Career: grad. Chuo Univ. 1913; entered Monopoly Bureau; Vice-Councillor, same; transferred to Cultural Works Dept. Foreign Office; Mem. Japanese Delegation to Naval Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1927; despatched to Europe & America; 1st Secr. Japanese Embassy, Manchoukuo 1934-35; Counsellor, same 1935. Address: c/o Manchuria Development Co., Dairen.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Prof. Chuo Univ.; Lawyer; b. Oct. 1877, Tokyo; s. of Soichiro Matsumoto, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; Councillor, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to Europe to study com. law; rec'd deg. 1910; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Vice-Pres. S. M. R. Co.; Pres. Legislation Bureau; Pres. Kansai Univ. joined the bar; Com. & Ind. Minister in Saito Cabinet 1934. Address: 1 of 2 Marunouchi 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Yingkow Waterworks and Electric Co.; Pres. Yingkow Chamber of Com.; Dir. Shinko Bank; b. Nov. 1869, Tokyo. Career: grad. Tokyo Law Coll.; established Yingkow Waterworks & Electric Co. Address: 3 Yoshino-cho, Yingkow, Manchoukuo.

Chairman, Rumoye Ry. Co., Wakamatsu Harbor Co.; Pres. Kurosaki Pottery Ind. Co., Kyushu Hydro-Electric Co.; Director Nihon Seitetsu K. K., Mitsui Trust Co.; Auditor Yasukawa Electric Works; President of Showa Coal Co.; Rep. Director Meiji Spinning Co.; b. Oct. 1870, Fukuoka-ken; s. of late Baron Keiichiro Yasukawa, and later adopted by Sen Matsumoto. Career: suceeded family estate 1923. Address: 1071 Nakahara Tobata City, Fukuoka-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Oji Securities Co.; Dir. Karafuto Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1882, Osaka-fu; s. of Toyojiro Matsumoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; entered Finance Dept.; joined Industrial Bank of Japan 1915; Dir. of same bank 1920-30; was in America and China for 4 years. Address: 27 Kitatani, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Dec. 1886, Okayama-ken; s. of Yoshio Kawakita. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Gov. Shizuoka-ken, Kagoshima-ken, Fukuoka-ken; Dir. Social Work Bureau Home Dept.; Dir. Police Affairs Bureau 1932-34. Address: 1051 Naka-nobu-cho, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

D.Litt. (1899); Ph. D. (1900, Yale Univ.); Mem. Imp. Acad.; Prof. Nippon Women's Univ.; Dir. Inst. of Child Study; b. Sept. 1866, Gunma-kn; s. of Tasuku Iino; later adopted by Kanjuro Matsumoto. Career: grad. Phil. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; studied Psychology in Yale Univ. U.S.A.; Prof. Tokyo Higher Nor. Sch.; Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Pres. Kyoto Muni. Paintings Coll., Kyoto Applied Fine Arts Sch.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to Europe & America 1918 & 1924. Address: 15 Kobinatadai-machi 2-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Nitto Flour Mill Co., Japan-Manchoukuo Flour Mill Co., Matsumoto Cereals & Fertilizer Co., Taiwan Paper Manufacturing Co., Japan-Manchoukuo Pulp Co.; Vice-President of Eastern Manchurian Rayon Pulp Mfg. Co.; Dir. Kokubo Rayon Co.; b. May 1878, Saitama-ken; s. of Heizo Matsumoto, businessman. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1900. Address: 87 Kobinata-Suido-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Foreign Affairs; b. Sept. 1887, Nagano-ken; s. of Yaesaku Matsumoto. Career: grad. Toa Dobun Shoin 1909; Corr. Yamato Shimbun; Private Secr. to late Count Komei Kato; Asst. Mayor of Tokyo; Parl. Councillor, Foreign Office [?]. Address: 3 Naka 3-gokan, Marunouchi [?]-chome, Tokyo.

Pres. Fujikura Elec. Cable Works and Fujikura Kogyo Co., b. Nov. 1868, Tochigi-ken; s. of Kumakichi Fujikura, landlord. Career: went to America to inspect elec. wire mfg. industry; established Fujikura Cable Works with his brother; Vice-Pres. Nippon Elec. Assn.; Head, Kanto Branch of same. Address: 47 Tenma-cho 1-chome, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Sept. 1883, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Reizo Matsumura, farmer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Commr., Kanagawa-ken, Saga-ken, Tottori-ken; Governor, Oita-ken 1923; Dir. Police Bureau, Home Dept. 1924; nominated Peer 1926; Vice-Minister of Com. & Ind. 1931. Address: 448 Nishiokubo 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1883, Toyama-ken; s. of Waichiro Matsumura. Career: grad. Polit. Econ. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1906; Corr. Hochi Shimbun; sent to Diet from Toyama-ken; Secretary to Agr. & Forestry Minister; Parl. Councillor, Agr. & Forestry Dept. 1932-34. Address: 91 Sakashita-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Ishikawajima Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; Ishikawajima-Shibaura Turbine Co.; Dir. Ishikawajima Aircraft Co.; Jidosha Kogyo K.K.; Vice-Admiral (reserve); b. Oct. 1874, Tokyo; s. of Yasutane Matsumura. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1896; sent to England & Amer.; Staff, Standing Fleet 1903; grad. Nav. Staff Coll. 1907; resided in France 1908; Commdr. "Kasuga" 1911; during World War Staff Despatched Sqn. to Pacific 1914; Nav. Attaché, Emb. Paris; Captain "Tokiwa" & "Hiei"; Chief Staff 2nd Sqn.; Chief, 1st Sec. Nav. Training Dept.; Comdr. 5th Sqn.; Chinkai Nav. Port; retired active service 1926. Address: 955 Daita 2-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Dec. 1882, Tochigi-ken; s. of late Kozo Matsumura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; joined Furukawa Gomei; apptd. Chief, Purchasing Section, Furukawa Mining Co.; Dir. Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co.; Asahi Elec. Industry Co.; Parl. Councillor of Com. & Ind. 1932-34. Address: 39 Hachiyama-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Yonei Shoten Ltd. since 1919; Acting Partner, Meiji Gomu Seizosho; b. May 1881, Tokyo. Career: grad. Law College Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; joined Yonei Shoten 1909; founded Meiji Gomu Seizosho 1919. Address: 30 Shimo-Rokubancho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Member of House of Peers; b. Jan. 1880, Osaka; s. of Shimpei Matsumura; m. Emi, d. of Baron Tatsuo Yamamoto. Career: Dept. Chief, Legislation Bureau; Dir. Stock-Farming Bureau, Dept. of Agr. & Com.; Dir. Com. Bureau; Dir. Fisheries Bureau; Dir. Agr. Bureau; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry 1931; nominated Peer 1933. Address: 39 Kami-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; D. Agr.; Emeritus Prof. Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; b. Mar. 1872, Akashi City; s. of Jihei Matsumura; m. Moto. Career: grad. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1896; studied in Berlin, Germany; Prof. of Entomology, Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1902-[?]; Emeritus Prof. since [?]. Address: 1[?] Ohyama-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Acting Vice-Consul, Hangchow, China; b. May 1894, Kobe. Address: Japanese Consulate Hangchow, China.

Minister on the Waiting List; b. Apr. 1883, Saga-ken; s. of Seiichi Matsunaga. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Diplomatic Probationer at Peking; Eléve-Consul at Seattle and Ottawa; Dir. Treaty Bureau; Minister to Netherlands 1930; to Austria & Hungary 1933-36. Address: c/o Gaimusho, Tokyo.

n: MATSUNAGA, Yasuzaemon 松永安左衞門
t: Pres. Toho Elec. Power Co., Niigata Elec. Power Co., Oigawa Elec. Power Co.; Vice-Chairman Japan Ind. Assn.; Dir. Tokyo Elec. Light Co., Oji Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Dec. 1875, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Yasuzaemon Matsunaga, brewer. Career: grad. Law Dept. Keio Univ. 1896; apptd. Mgr. Hirosaki Hydro-Elec. Co. 1906; founded Toho Elec. Power Co. 1910; established new firms of electric, gas, brick, oil, vehicles, etc. in Kyushu; Pres. Hakata Chamber of Com. & Ind. 1917; elected to Diet from Fukuoka 1917; went to Europe & Amer. to inspect ind., polit. and econ. conditions after the War 1919; Pres. Elec. Assn. 1924. Address: 367 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L. Mem. Imp. Acad.; Prof. and Chief, Com. Dept. Nihon Univ.; Vice-Pres. Harbor Assn. and Nav. Assn.; Pres. Japan Univ. Profs.' League; b. Jan. 1868, Osaka-fu; s. of Niemon Matsunami. Career: studied at Doshisha Kyoto; grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; apptd. Code Investigation Comm.; Advisor to Navy Office on Int'l Law of War; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll. 1896; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; rec'd deg. 1901; Vice-Chairman Int'l Maritime Conf. London [?], Paris 1900 & Göthemburg 1924. Address: 17 Naka-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Chief Director of Seiyukai; b. Dec. 1883, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Chohachi Matsuno. Career: sent to Diet 6 times since 1920; Dir. Kikuchi Elec. Ry. Co., Nippon Dempo News Agency, Ryubunkan Publishing Co.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Home Dept. in Inukai Cabinet 1931. Address: 2 Mita Tsuna-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Matsuoka Steamship Co., Matsuoka Farm Hokkaido; Dir. Kureha Spinning Co., Tokyo Steel Mfg. Co.; Hon. Polish Consul in Osaka; b. Sept. 1888, Hyogo-ken; s. of Shuzo Matsuoka. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. Address: 1611 Daiso, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

Baron; D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Temporary Industry Rationalization Bureau; Dir. Toyo Kyokai Univ. and Kyocho-kai; etc.; b. Nov. 1876, Tokyo; s. of Baron Yasuki Matsuoka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; apptd. Prof. same; Govt. Delegate, Int'l Labour Conf.; Mem. City Planning Committee and Econ. Finance Inquiry Committee; Dir. Indo-China Assn.; Dean, Toyo Kyokai Univ.; attended World Peace Conf. Switzerland 1914. Address: 24 Zaimoku-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. (Wisc. Univ., U.S.A.); Editor-in-Chief, Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi; b. 1880, Aomori-ken; s. of Totaro Matsuoka, Lawyer. Career: grad. Polit. Sc. Dept. Keio and Wisc. Univs.; Lecturer Tokyo and Kobe Univs. of Com., Keio Univ., Kagoshima Higher Agr. & Forestry Sch.; Commr., Taiwan Govt.; Head, Financial Dept. Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; Pres. Keijo Nippo. Address: Hibarigaoka, Kawanishi-machi, Kawabe-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Painter of Japanese style; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; Mem. Imp. Acad. of Arts; b. Sept. 1881, Hyogo-ken; s. of Misao Matsuoka. Career: grad. Japanese Painting Dept. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1894; Asst. Prof. same 1907; Prof. same; Examiner, Imp. Academy of Arts Exhibition since 1919; won Special Honor 3 times in Educ. Dept. Fine Arts Exhibitions; won Imp. Academy of Arts Prize at 10th Exhibition 1929. Address: 122 Zoshigaya, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. S. M. R. Co. since 1935; b. Mar. 1880, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Sanjuro Matsuoka. Career: went to America 1892; grad. Oregon Law Coll. Oregon, U. S. A., 1900; élève Consul, Shanghai; Commr. Kwantung Govt. 1906; 3rd Secr. Legation Brussels 1907, China 1908; Consul at Shanghai 1908-09; 2nd Secr., Embassy, Washington 1913; 1st Secr. same 1916; Commr. Foreign Office 1917; Secr. to Foreign Minister 1917-18; sent to Europe & America 1918; Mem. of Suite Japanese Legation to Peace Conf. 1919; despatched to Foochow, China 1919; Consul-Gen. Canton, China 1920-21; apptd. Dir. S. M. R. Co.; Vice-Pres. same 1927-29; joined Seiyukai Party 1930; elected M.P. from Yamaguchi-ken, 1930 & 1932; despatched to Shanghai by Govt. at time of Shanghai Incident 1932; Japanese Chief Delegate to League of Nations Assembly; resigned M.P. 1933. Address: c/o S. M. R. Co., Dairen.

Mng.-Dir. Nomura Bank; Dir. Nomura Gomei Kaisha, Nomura Securities Co.; b. 1882, Miye-ken, bro. of Torakichi Matsumura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1904; joined Sumitomo Bank; Mgr. Hankow, Shanghai & London Branches. Address: 1930 Shinotsubo, Mikage-machi, Hyogo-ken.

Dir. Communication Bureau Foreign Office since 1936; b. Jan. 1888, Hyogo-ken; s. of Sadayori Matsushima. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1912; entered Foreign Office; Secr. Emb. France 1926; Secr. Leg. Greece 1930; Mem. of Suite, Japanese Delegation to 2nd League of Nations Assembly 1921; Econ. Conf. Genoa 1922; 1st Secr. Emb. Manchoukuo 1932; Chief 1st Sec. Com. Bureau Foreign Office 1935. Address: 854 Koenji, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. Chinchow Prov.; b. 1890, Tottori-ken; s. of Sawajiro Matsushita. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1915; Commr., Monopoly Bureau, Taiwan Govt.; Chief, Police Dept. Zenra-Nando & Kankyo-Nando, Chosen; Chief, Home Dept. Kankyo Nando, Zenra-Hokudo & Keisho-Nando, Chosen 1931-34; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Chientao Prov. Address: Chinchow, Prov. Office, Chinchow, Manchoukuo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Jan. 1872, Ehime-ken; s. of Moto Matsuura, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Secr. to Educ. Minister; Councillor, Educ. Dept.; Dir. Higher Educ. Bureau; Chief, Exam. Committee of Civil Service; Pres. Kyushu Imp. Univ. Address: 49 Myogadani-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Intendant to Prince Kaya; b. Aug. 1884, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Torasaku Matsuura. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1904; served Russo-Japanese War; Comdr. Inf. 13th Reg.; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Mil. Training Dept.; Comdr. Inf. 12th Brig.; Dir. Personnel Bureau War Office; Dir. Mil. Inf. Sch.; Comdr. 10th Div. Address: c/o Prince Kaya's Mansion, Samban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Prof. and Dean Faculty of Sci., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Oct. 1884, Oita-ken; s. of Tengai Sumie, priest; m. Matsue Matsuyama. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1911; apptd. Lecturer 1913; Asst. Prof. 1916; Prof. 1922; ordered to Europe and America 1919-21; Dean Faculty of Sc. 1936. Address: 2 of 33 Tanaka Sekiden-cho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

Consul-Gen. at London since 1927; Com. Councillor, Embassy at London; b. June 1882, Nagano-ken; s. of Rokuro Nakamura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1903; joined Nozawa-gumi, later Chugai Trading Co.; attended 4th and 5th Gen. Assemblies of Int'l Trade Conf. Stockholm 1927. Address: Embassy of Japan, London.

M.P.; Reserve Engrg. Sub-Lieut.; b. Mar. 1884, Wakayama-ken; s. of Tsuneji Matsuyama. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; studied in America; served at Tokyo Pref. Office 1910; Chief Engr. Kawasa Farm & Taisho Water Utilization Assn. Chosen 1915; elected M.P. 6 times; Parl. Councillor Foreign Office 1936-37. Address: 835 Sendagaya 5-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Japan Mining Assn. since 1926; Standing Mem. Fuel Assn.; Mechanics Research Inst.; b. 1887, Nagano-ken; s. of Tatsusaburo Karaki; adopted by Kameya Matsuzawa. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; joined Nippon Oil Co.; Chief Mining Sec. 1917; Foreign Affairs Sec. 1921; resided in America 1922; went to America and Dutch East Indies on inspection tour of petroleum industry. Address: 41, Kamiyama-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Prop. of Matsuzawa Shokai; b. 1889, Nagano-ken. Career: engaged in business of chemicals, construction materials and of plumbery work. Address: 20 Kanbu-dori, Dairen.
General on the Reserve List. (See 1936 issue).

Dr. Juris.; Dr. Polit. Economy; Dir. Maison Franco-Japonaise since 1936; Prof. l'Universite de Grenoble; b. Mar. 1900 at Linnoges, France; s. of Felix Mazeaud, Councillor Court of Cassation. Career: Received degree of Dr. Juris. 1921; Dr. Polit. Economy 1924; advocate Court of Appeals, Lyon 1919-1925. Appt. Prof. Univ. Grenoble 1928; titular Prof. same 1930; titular Prof. of Comm. Law same 1930. Address: Maison Franco-Japonaise, 3, Surugadai 2-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Canadian Govt. Trade Comm. at Kobe; b. June 1901, Union Bay, B.C., Canada; n. British; s. of C. A. McLane. Career: grad. Univ. of British Columbia, Vancouver, B.C. (B.A.); Univ. of Calif. Berkeley, U.S. (M.A.); Com. Intelligence Service, Dept. of Trade & Com. Ottawa 1928. Address: P. O. Box 230 Kobe.

M.D.; b. Apr. 1884, North Carolina, U.S.A.; n. American; s. of James Erasmus McSparran, Clergyman. Career: grad. Virginia Public Sch.; Randolph-Macon Academy; Randolph-Macon Coll.; Medical Univ. Richmond, Va.; Medical Sch. Vienna Univ.; hospital and private practice in Virginia 5 years; 19 years practice in Japan. Address: 7 Nihon Odori, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Dr. Jur.; Attache, German Embassy Tokyo since 1937; b. June 1909 at Strassburg (Alsatia); s. of Dr. Otto Meissner, Secr. of State, Chief Presidential Chancery German Fuhrer. Career: studied at Cambridge Trinity Coll. Grenoble, Lausanne, Heidelberg, Gottingen; entered Foreign Service 1934; served at Embassy, London and Foreign Office, Berlin; served Army, promoted Lieut. of Res. Address: German Embassy, Tokyo.

Pres. German East Asiatic Society, Tokyo; Pres. K. K. L. Leybold Shokwan, Tokyo & Osaka; b. Mar. 1885, Hamburg; n. German. Career: arrived in Japan, 1906, since then actively concerned in trade business between Germany and Japan; Partner in the following firms; G. K. Kenzai-sha, Tokyo & Osaka; P. Schmitz & Co. Tokyo; Chien Hsin Engrg. Co. Ltd. Shanghai, Hongkong; Simon, Evers & Co. G.m.b.H. Hamburg; author of several books regarding Japanese grammar and things Japanese. Address: 5861 Oi Kaneko-machi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Teikoku Sanso K. K.; Agent for "L-Air Liquide" in Japan, China and Manchoukuo; Hon. Consul for Belgium; b. Feb. 1892, Paris; n. French; s. of Jules Melchior, Vice-Admiral; married. Career: Capitaine de Corvette de reserve. Address: 23 Nakayamate-dori 5-chome, Kobe.
Major; Peruvian Military Attache in Tokyo; b. Aug. 1902; m. Lima. Career: Sub-Lieut. 1924; Captain 1928; Major 1934. Address: 50 Aoyama Minami-cho 1-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Journalist and Foreign Trade Delegate; b. Sept. 1894, Budapest; n. Hungarian; s. of late Ferdinand Joseph Metzger. Career: studied Catholic Theol. and Oriental lang. at Pázmány Univ. Budapest 1914; Lecturer on Japanese Lang. and Litt. at Royal Hungarian Oriental Acad. Budapest 1916; served Foreign Office Austro-Hungarian Monarchy; Examiner "Dolmetsch School" (Mil. Interpreter Service) Imp. & Roy. Austro-Hungarian Army Hdqrs. 1918; Sworn English Interpreter Royal Courts of Justice Budapest 1921; Secr. and Interpreter of Imp. Japanese Consulate in Budapest 1922; Secr. "Commission de la Delimitation de la Frontière" Japanese Delegation 1923; came to Japan as Corr. for Hungarian newspapers 1929; Corr. for Hungarian Official Press Agency, Agence Telegraphique Hongroise S.A. 1931; Delegate Hungarian Foreign Trade Office; Spec. Corr. "Corriere Della Sera" in Milano 1936. Address: 354 Moto-machi, Honmoku, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Spec. Imp. Household Editorial Bureau; Mem. House of Peers; Mem. Compiling Bureau of Historical Materials of Meiji Restoration; b. 1865, Himeji; s. of Teisuke Koda; later adopted by Katsuaki Mikami. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Lecturer Tokyo Women's Higher Normal Sch. 1892; Prof. same; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dean Litt. Coll. same rec'd deg. 1899; resigned 1926. Address: 169 Komagome Hayashi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Prop. Mikimoto Pearl Store; b. Jan. 1858, Miye-ken; s. of Otokichi Mikimoto. Career: invented cultivated pearl and engaged in its export throughout world; awarded Supreme Hon. Grand Medal at St. Louis Exhibition Paris; elected Peer 1924; made inspection tour of Europe & America. Address: 2 Ginza 4-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo.

A.B.; D.D. Missionary; b. Aug. 1881, Salem, Virginia, U.S.A.; s. of Lewis G. M. Miller; m. Martha Meta Harder. Career: grad. Roanoke Coll. Va. 1901; Phila. Theol. Sem. 1907; came to Japan 1907; since 1920 Dean of Kyushu Gakuin. Address: Kyushu Gakuin, Kumamoto.

I.E.G. (1923); E.S.E. (1925); Rep. Compagnie Generale de Telegraphie Sans Fil and Associated Compagnies; b. Apr. 1902, Athis-Mons near Paris; s. of Amand Millot; m. Emma Gabriel. Career: grad. Higher Elec. Sch. of Paris; entered present firm July 1925; present post since 1926. Address: 15 Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.
Journalist; Chief Tokyo Bureau Associated Press of America; b. June 20, 1883, New York. Address: 1 Ginza Nishi 7-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo.
Teacher at 8th Higher Sch.; b. Apr. 1911, Caridff, England; s. of W. Courtnay Milward, doctor. Address: 13 Nakayama-cho 5-chome, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

Dep. Mayor of Tokyo; b. 1886, Toyama-ken; s. of Chozaburo Minabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Councillor Home Dept.; Secr. Home Dept.; Chief Executive Sec. Pref. Bureau Home Dept.; Gov. Yamanashi-ken; Okayama-ken; Dir. Civil Engrg. Bureau Home Dept.; Gov. Miyagi-ken, Aichi-ken; Vice-Educ. Min. 1934-36. Address: 15 Setagaya 1-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Tokyo Court of Appeal; b. Mar. 1875, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Hiroo Minakawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. 1903; entered Justice Dept.; attached to 4th Army Hdqrs. during Russo-Japanese War; Judge, Osaka, Kokura, Tokyo Local Courts; attended Int'l Criminal Law Conf. Brussels 1910; studied in France, Germany, and Switzerland 1910-13; Secr. Justice Dept.; Public Procurator, Supreme Court; Dir. Personnel Bureau Justice Dept.; Chief Public Procurator, Hiroshima and Nagoya Appeal Courts; Vice-Minister of Justice in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 42 Miyamura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Chief, Gen. Affairs Sec. Lungkiang Prov. since 1935; b. Sept. 1902, Yamagata-ken; s. of Moemon Minakawa. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1928; joined Tokyo Asahi Shimbun 1930-32; studied at Tatung Coll. 1932; attached to Tailai-hsien; Councillor Tailai-hsien 1933-35. Address: 5 Kanko-gai, Tsitsihar.

Dir. Bureau of Educ. Manchoukuo Dept. of People's Welfare; b. 1896, Yamagata-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; entered Justice Dept.; Public Procurator Sendai Local Court, Tokyo Public Procurator's Office; Chief Secr. and Dir. Personnel & Decoration Bureau, State Council 1933-34; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Chinchow Prov.; Chief Gen. Affairs Bureau Dept. of Educ. Address: Dept. of People's Welfare, Hsinking.

Privy Councillor since 1936; b. Oct. 1869, Toyama-ken; s. of Kakuhei Iwama, and later adopted by Heikichi Minami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Secr. of Cabinet; Gov. Fukuoka-ken; Vice-Minister of Educ.; Gov.-Gen. of Taiwan 1932; Communications Min. in Saito Cabinet 1932;34; Mem. House of Peers. Address: 6 Sakaedori 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Gen. (reserve); Gov.-Gen. of Chosen; b. Aug. 1874, Oita-ken; s. of Kihei Minami. Career: grad. Military Academy 1895; Mil. Coll. 1903; Instructor, Mill. Coll.; same, Naval Staff Coll.; same, Mil. Cavalry Sch.; Comdr. Cavalry 13th Reg.; Pres. Mil. Cav. Sch.; same, Mil. Acad.; Comdr. 16th Division; Vice-Chief, General Staff; War Minister in Wakatsuki Cabinet 1931; Supreme War Councillor; Ambassador to Manchoukuo 1934-36. Address: Gov.-Gen 's Residence, Keijo, Chosen.

Pres. Taihei Fire Ins. Co., Toyo Fire Ins. Co.; Tokyo Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. Dai-Ichi Fire Ins. Co., Yasuda Bldg.; b. Jan. 1881, Oita-ken; s. of Takaji Minami. Career: grad. Law Dept. Kwansai Univ. 1901; entered Chiyoda Life Ins. Co.; promoted to Chief, Kyoto Branch & Research Dept., same; invited by Yasuda Hozensha as Councillor 1923; Dir. & Mgr. Tokyo Fire Ins. Co.; Mng.-Dir. same 1925; Vice-Pres. same 1931; Pres. same 1931. Address: 555 Koenji 4-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Oil Painter; Mem. Imp. Acad. of Arts; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; b. Sept. 1883, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Keizo Minami. Career: grad. Western Painting Dept. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1907; studied in England 2 years; in France 2 years; visited Italy; won 2nd Prizes in Educ. Dept. Fine Art Exhibitions. Address: 3 Hyakunin-machi, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc.; b. Jan. 1870, Gunma-ken; s. of Kurazo Minegishi. Career: Teacher, Tokyo Pref. Normal Sch. 1894; Maebashi Middle Sch. 1897; Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1898. Address: 1345 Ikebukuro 3-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Finance Bureau Taiwan Govt.-Gen. since Feb. 1936; b. 1887, Aichi-ken; s. of Kyugoro Mineta. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; entered Fin. Dept.; Commr. Revenue Supt. Bureau; Commr. Custom House; Dir. Nagasaki Customs; Dir. Kumamoto Revenue Supt. Bureau; Dir. Nagoya Revenue Supt. Bureau 1934-36; made inspection tour of Europe & China. Address: c/o Taiwan Govt.-Gen., Taihoku.
Former Mem. House of Peers. (See 1936 issue).

Gov. Kwantung Prov. since 1936; b. Feb. 1892, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Tomokuni Minoike. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Govt. service; Secr. & Chief Educ. Dept. Hiroshima-ken; Chief Civil Adm. Office Dairen 1929-35; Chief Police Sec. Kwantung Bureau 1935. Address: Kwantung Prov. Office Dairen.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; Dir. Boy Scouts of Japan; b. Jan. 1897, Tokyo; s. of late Yataro Mishima, Peer. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; Secr. Count Makino, Envoy at Peace Conf.; Japanese Delegate of Boy Scouts to 2nd Jamboree, Copenhagen, Denmark; elected Peer 1931 Comdr. Despatched Boy Scouts to Manchoukuo 3 times in 1931, 1932 and 1933; same Despatched Boy Scouts to Shanghai 1932. Address: 110 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Pres. Taihoku Imp. Univ.; b. Jan. 1876, Morioka; s. of Shunjiro Mita, physician. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same; sent to Germany and France for study; rec'd deg. 1914; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. & Dean Med. Coll. of present Univ. Address: Taihoku Imp. Univ., Taihoku.

Mem. President's Council Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Dir. Furukawa Elec. Co., Chosen Anthracite Co.; Japan Aluminium Co.; b. Oct. 1871, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Keiichiro Mitani. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; entered Mitsubishi Co. 1896; Mgr. Shanghai, Nagasaki and Karatsu Branches; Mgr. Coal Dept. Tokyo Head Office; when Mitsubishi Mining Co. was established in 1918, was elected Mng.-Dir., Chairman; Mng.-Dir. Japan Ind. Assn., etc. Address: 255 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Governor Kirin Prov. Manchoukuo since 1936; b. 1887, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1909; Gendarmerie captain 1920; Comdr. Mukden Detachment, Japanese Gendarmerie 1931; Commr. Fengtien Prov. 1932; Chief, Police Dept., Fengtien Prov. 1934-36; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Kirin Prov. 1936-37. Address: Kirin Prov. Office, Kirin.

D.E.; Dir. Electro-Technical Lab. Communications Dept.; Engr. Imp. Household Dept.; Prof. Waseda Univ.; b. Mar. 1885, Toyama; s. of Seizo Mitsuda. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; apptd. Engr. Com. Dept. 1913; went to America & England to study electricity. Address: 1289 Higashiterao, Tsurumi-ku, Yokohama.

Special Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Chairman, Mitsubishi Warehouse Co., Ryoka Warehouse Co.; Kyodo Express Co.; Pres. Japan Warehouse Assn.; b. Apr. 1876; s. of Takejiro Mitshashi, Tokyo. Career: Pres. Hiroshima Mercantile Marine Sch.; Engr. Hiroshima-ken; served in Russo-Japanese War. Address: [?] Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mitsui Mines Ltd.; b. Jan. 1875, Kyoto; bro. of Motonosuke Mitsui and later adopted by Tokujiro Mitsui. Career: grad. Yokohama Com. Coll.; entered Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; served at London Branch; Pres. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. Address: 1 Nagasaka-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.
D. Sc.; Prof. of Chemistry, Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1893, Tokyo; s. of Prof. Kakichi Mitsukuri. Career: grad. Chemical Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 40 Nakasugiyama-dori, Sendai.

Chemist; Composer; b. Oct. 1895, Tokyo; s. of Prof. Gempachi Mitsukuri. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1921; studied in Europe 1921-25; Physical Chem. at Kaiser Wilhelm Research Inst. Berlin; educated Musical Composition by George Schumann; served Nav. Tech. Research Inst.; founded New Musical Composers' Assn. 1930; Japanese Secr. of Intl' Soc. for contemporary music. Address: Naval Club, Hiratsuka, Kanagawa-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Taiwan Warehouse Co.; Dir. Taiwan Stone Co., Tokai Motor-car Transportation Co.; b. Sept. 1879, Himeji; s. of late Major-General Hiroyoshi Mitsumaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904; joined Bank of Taiwan. Address: 8 Tsukiji-cho 1-chome, Taihoku.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Nippon Dempo Tsushin-sha; b. Sept. 1866, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Yuki Mitsunaga. Career: Corr. Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; established Nippon Kokoku K. K.; changed the name of firm to Nippon Dempo Tsushin-sha; Mng.-Dir. same; went to America & Europe for investigation 1921. Address: 19 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku,

Dr. of Forestry; Prof. Forest Chem. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Apr. 1885, Wakayama-ken; s. of Yasujiro Miura. Career: grad. Forestry Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; studied 2 years in Europe & America; Lecturer Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Prof. 1926. Address: 17 Sakuragaokamachi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Commr. Imp. Household Dept; Pres. Doai Memorial Hospital; b. Mar. 1864, Fukushima-ken; s. of Dosei Miura. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1887; studied in Berlin, Marburg, Heidelberg and Paris Univs. 1890; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; Mem. Imp. Acad. 1906; accompanied Prince Saionji to Europe 1918; attended the Crown Prince to Europe 1921. Address: 1 Surugadai 2-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Author; Univ. Prof.; b. Nov. 1903, Aomori-ken. Career: grad. Litt. Coll., Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1931. Literary Works in Japanese: "History of Christian Martyrdom," "Treaties on Modern Literary Thought," "Treaties on Outline of Theatrical Performance," etc. Address: 13 Kayaba-cho 2-chome, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo.
M.D.; Sc. D.H.; Prof. Manchuria Medical Coll.; b. Mar. 1[?]96, Kobe; s. of Koya Miura, Doctor. Address: 17 Inaba-cho, Mukden.

Pres. Marumiya; Dir. Chi[illegible]ibu Cement Co.; b. May 1871, Tokyo; s. of Zembei Miwa. Career: studied Chinese Classics in His Private Sch.; succeeded father's position; engaged in mfg. "Mitsuwa" toilet soap and other toilet goods. Address: 17 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

n: MIYAGAWA, Hyakutaro 三宅川百太郞
t: Dir. N. Y. K.; Adviser Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Auditor Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. June 1869, Aichi-ken; s. of Seizaburo Miyagawa. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1892; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mgr. Hankow, Shanghai, Wakamatsu and Moji Branches; Chief Shipping Dept. and Oriental Dept.; Spec. Mem. Yokohama Chamber of Co. & Ind. Address: 25 Showa-dori 2-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Gov. Inst. for Infectious Diseases; b. Feb. 1885, Aichi-ken; s. of late Sukeemon Miyagawa; m. Yasuko. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Prof. same 1927; Dir. Infectious Disease Inst. 1934. Address: 78 Kamifujimae-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Dean, Engrg. Coll. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Aug. 1883, Saitama-ken; s. of Tojiro Miyagi, landowner; m. Chiyo. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; apptd. Prof. Sendai Higher Tech. Sch. 1909; studied Mechanical Engrg. in England and America 1919-20; again went to Europe and America for study 1930. Address: 28 Kitayoban-cho, Sendai.

Pres. Nisshin Spinning Co.; Dir. Kawasaki Trust Co., Toa Hemp-Dressing Co.; Japan Industrial Club, Japan Trades Assn.; b. Jan. 1879; s. of Shotaro Kobayashi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; Mem. Tokyo Muni. Assembly. Address: 10 Isarago-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Mem. House of Peers; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. Career: apptd. Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Acting Principal, Tokyo Medical, Sch.; served Home Dept.; Dean, Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chairman, Sch. Hygiene Advisory Assn.; Councillor, Japan Exhibition; sent to Philadelphia as Vice-Pres. of World Medical Congress; nominated Peer 1891. Address: 81 Takehaya-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr. (1915) Prof. Agr. Coll. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. since 1918; b. Jan. 1882, Tokyo; s. of Yasumasa Miyake, official; m. Yuko Nishio. Career: grad. Sapporo Agr. Coll. 1905; Asst. Prof. Agr. Coll. Tohoku Imperial Univ. 1908; studied Agrl. Chem. in Europe 1914-17; despatched to Europe & Amer. 1927-28; Dean, Agr. Coll. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1934-36. Address: 2 Kita Sanjyo Nishi 18-chome, Sapporo, Hokkaido.

Minister to Chile; b. Sept. 1888, Wakayama-ken; s. of Shin-ichiro Miyake. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1912; apptd. Elève-Consul, Councillor, Foreign Office; Chief. 3rd Secr. Treaty Bureau; 1st Secr. of Legation; Consul-Gen. Batavia 1927; Calcutta 1933-36. Address:: c/o Japanese Legation, Santiago. Chile.

Cultural Critic; D. Litt.; b. May 1860, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Tsunenori Miyake. Career: grad. Phil. Course, Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1883; Asst. Prof. same; Lecturer, Tokyo Tech. Sch.; published "Japan & Japanese" with Juko Shiga; went to Europe, America and South Sea Islands. Address: [?] Yoyogi Hatsudai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; b. June 1873, Chiba-ken; s. of Atsutoshi Miyama. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to England, Germany and America to study Applied Chem. Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Central Chem. Lab. Govt.-Gen. of Chosen; Pres. Keijo Higher Tech. Sch.; Engr. & Chief Chem. Elec. Dept. Patent Bureau. Address: [?] Kita-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Tea Producer; b. Sept. 1877, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Shohei Miyamoto, farmer. Career: Pres. Shizuoka-ken Pref. Assembly 1923 and 1927; Dir. Shizuoka-ken Tea Assn. since 1924; Japan Tea Promotion Committee since 1925; sent to Diet from Shizuoka-ken 1932, 1936, 1937. Address: Asahina-mura, Ogasa-gun, Shizuoka-ken.

Official; m. Yuko Nishio. Career: grad. Sapporo Agr. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1887; served in Foreign Office as Assistant in Law Bureau 1887-92; Secr. Legation at Washington 1892-94; Secr. and Charge d'Affaires at Berlin and Brussels 1894-99; Minister Resident in Diplomatic Service 1900-06; Counsellor, Embassy at Washington 1906-08; retired from diplomatic service to practise law 1909; in addition to law practice, Special Corr. Carnegie Endowment for Int'l Peace since 1910; Hon. Mem. American and Canadian Bar Assns. 1918; visited London and Paris as guest of Bars of England and France; Associate Mem. Bar Assn. City of New York 1918; apptd. by President Coolidge, American Non-national Mem. Permanent Int'l Commission provided for by Treaty of 1914 between U.S.A. and Uruguay for advancement of peace 1928; Hon. Mem. Mexican Academy of Jurisprudence and Legislation 1935. Address: 22 Aoyama Minami-cho 4-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Company Director; b. Feb. 1895; s. of Kamejiro Miyazaki; m. Sadako Kizu 1919. Career: Dir. Takaoka Bank, Takaoka Com. Bank, Takaoka Elec. Light Co., Takaoka Whipped Cotton Co.; Hokuichi K. K.; Hokuriku Trust Co. and Takaoka Rice Exchange; Pres. Takaoka Trust Co. and Takaoka Rice Exchange; Pres. Takaoka Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 26 Yamai Hon-machi, Takaoka, Toyama-ken.

Councillor, Embassy, Turkey; b. Apr. 1892, Ehime-ken; s. of Shinjiro Miyazaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Com. & Ind. Bureau, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Secr. Foreign Dept.; Secr. of Embassy; Chief, 1st Sec. Europe & American Bureau 1926; 1st Secr. Embassy, Paris 1932; 1st Sec. Emb. London 1934-36. Address: Japanese Embassy, Istanbul, Turkey.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Academy; b. Nov. 1861, Tokyo; s. of Tomoe Miyoshi. Career: grad.Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; studied Botany in Germany; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Uni. 1895; Pres. Attached Botanical Garden, 1922. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; b. Feb. 1871; s. of late Taizo Miyoshi, Peer. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1895; served Kyushu Ry. Co.; toured Europe & Amer. to study transportation business; joined Mitsubishi Firm 1908. Address: [?] Ichigaya Nakano-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Major-Gen. (Reserve); Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1878; s. of Count Naomasa Mizoguchi. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1898; apptd. Artillery Sub.-Lieut.; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief Art. Sec. War Office; Mem. Mil. Tech. Committee; attached to Divisions at Hiroshima, Zentsuji, Utsunomiya and Nagoya; fought in Russo-Japanese War; elected Peer 1924; Councillor, War Office 1925; Parl. Vice-Minister of War 1929-30. Address: 164 Onden, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Retired Captain (Navy); Author; b. Oct. 1877, Matsuyama; s. of late Mitsuyuki Mizuno. Career: grad. Nav. Acad.; went to Europe & Amer. for inspection during World War; to Germany after the War. Address: 143 Kamiuma, Komazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Jan. 1868, Tokyo; s. of Ryuzaburo Mizuno, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; apptd. Councillor, Home Dept. 1894; Secr. to Home Minister; Dir. Shrines Bureau and Engrg. Bureau; Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; Home Minister 3 times; Educ. Minister 1927-28; accorded treatment of a minister. Address: 61 Shirokane Sarumachi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Feb. 1867, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Tonosuke Mochizuki; adopted by Shunkichi Mochizuki. Career: studied Law, Economics and Politics at Kogyokusha, Kyoritsu Gakko and Meiji English Language Sch.; engaged in mining industry; sent to Diet 12 times since 1898; Councillor, Agr. & Commerce Dept. in Hara Cabinet; Communications Minister in Tanaka Cabinet 1927; Home Minister 1929-30; Com. Minister 1935-36. Address: 307 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Pharm. Mng.-Dir. Momotani Juntendo; Dir. Momoi Shoji Co.; b. Sept. 1889; Wakayama-ken; s. of Masajiro Momotani. Career: grad. Pharm. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; established Momotani Toilet Article Lab. 1913; went to France to inspect toilet article factories 1920; Mem. Pharm. Exam. Committee, Home Dept. 1927; Aud. Osaka Pharm. Sch. 1932. Address: 12 Minami-machi Naka 1-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

D.E.; Pres. Eisei Kogaku Kyokai; b. June 1880, Sendai; s. of Kosei Moniwa. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; Chief Engr. Nagoya Municipal Water Works; Lecturer, Nagoya Higher Tech. Sch.; Engr. Home Dept.; Engr. Reconstruction Bureau 1924; rec'd deg. 1919; went to Europe & America 1919. Address: 323 Arai-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; B.D.; Missionary; b. May 1898, Osaka; s. of J. Wallace Moore; m. Grace Eagleton. Career: Pastor at Caddo, Okla. U. S. A. 1922-24; Japan Mission of S. P. Ch.; Southern Presb. Ch. 1924. Address: Niban-cho Asahi-machi, Toyohashi.

Mng.-Dir. Isorite Kogyo Co.; b. Sept. 1876, Kyoto; s. of Gembei Mori. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; apptd. Kobe Branch Mgr. Sumitomo Warehouse Co.; Business Mgr. Sumitomo Steel Works; Mgr. Sumitomo Wakamatsu Colliery Office; Mng.-Dir. Japan Sheet Glass Co. 1923-27; Auditor, Sumitomo Fertilizer Co. 1927-31. Address: 83 Tezukayama Naka 1-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

M.P.; b. 1873, Nagasaki-ken. Career: grad. Polit. & Econ. Dept. Tokyo Senmon Gakko; started life as journalist; Corr. Nagasaki Shimpo, Nagasaki Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; Editor Nagasaki Shimbun; elected M.P. 5 times; Parl. Councillor Agr. & Forestry Dept. 1934-36. Address: 76 Nakakojima-cho, Nagasaki.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1874, Osaka and later adopted by late Heibei Mori. Career: grad. Kyoritsu Medical Sch. Osaka; connected with several business firms and societies; Pres. Federation of Osaka Industrial Assns.; Hon. Consul for Turkey; High Tax-payer in Osaka-fu. Address: 30 Junkeimachi-dori 3-chome, Minami-ku, Osaka.

Pres. Tokyo Clearing House; Deputy-Chairman Yasuda Bank; Dir. Mitsui Trust Co.; Yasuda Trust Co.; Auditor, S. M. R. Co., Nippon Wireless Telegraph & Telephone Co., Tokyo Credit Bureau; Dir. Yasuda Hozensha; b. Feb. 1873, Tottori-ken; s. of Jinjuro Mori. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1897; joined Yokohama Specie Bank and served at Head Office, Shanghai, London and Yingkow Branches; Mgr. Kobe Branch; Asst. Mgr. London; Dir. Bank of Taiwan; Pres. of same. Address: 47 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Elec. Ind. Co., Showa Mining Co., Karafuto Coal Mining Co., Showa Fertilizer Co.; Mng.-Dir. Toshin Elec. Co.; Dir. Saigawa Elec. Power Co.; b. Oct. 1884, Chiba-ken; s. of Tamekichi Mori; m. Asako, sister of Viscount Tadaharu Okubo. Career: succeeded father's business. Address: 6 Kioi-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Mar. 1887, Shiga-ken; s. of Shuku Mori, landowner. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. 1909; Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; sent to Europe to study Theory of Ins. 1914-17; elected Fellow of Ins. of Actuaries 1907; Asst. Prof. of Ins. & Com. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Prof. 1919; Councillor 1923-33; Dean, Econ. Coll. 1931-33; despatched to Europe & America to inspect econ. conditions 1934; Hon. Mem. of American Assn. of Univ. Teachers of Ins. 1934. Address: 30 Ichigaya Nakano-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. 15th Bank; Chairman, Imp. Warehouse & Transportation Co.; b. Mar. 1877, Fukushima-ken; s. of Sozaemon Mori, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; apptd. Secr. Finance Dept. 1903; went to Europe and America on official mission 1908-10; Dir. Bank Bureau & Finance Bureau, Finance Dept.; Vice-Pres. Bank of Taiwan 1920; Dir. S. M. R. Co. 1922. Address: 45 Shoto, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

n: MORRI, Yasotaro 毛利八十太郞
t: Executive Ed. Japan Times & Mail; b. Mar. 1882, Tokyo-fu; s. of Yoshiharu Morri. Career: went to America for study; on returning, joined Japan Mail (present Japan Times (& Mail); reporter, Kokusai Times; joined Osaka Mainichi Shimbun-sha, 1922; present post since 1937. Address: c/o Japan Times & Mail, Uchisaiwai-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Ph. D.; Chief Dir. Women's Econ. Coll. and Bunka Fukyu-kai Foundation; b. Mar. 1877, Kyoto; s. of Jun-ichiro Masuyama, later adopted by Katsuzo Morimoto. Career: grad. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. and John Hopkins Univ. Baltimore, Md., U.S.A.; sent to America to study Economics and Finance 1914; went to Europe and America as student and lecturer; Professor of Tohoku Imperial Univ. 1918; same. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. until 1933; built first apartments in Japan. The Bunka Apts. Address: Bunka Apts., Ochanomizu, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

n: MORIMURA, Ichizaemon 森村市左衞門
t: Baron; Pres. Japan Traders Assn.; Morimura-gumi; Chairman Fuji Elec. Power Co.; Dir. Yokohama Specie Bank, Fuji Gas Spinning Co., Tokyo Rubber Ind. Co., 1st Life Ins. Co.; b. Dec. 1873, Tokyo; s. of late Baron Ichizaemon Morimura. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1892; stayed in America 9 years for study; joined Morimura-gumi; succeeded peerage 1920. Address: 33 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Secr.-Gen. of Taiwan; b. 1886, Nara-ken; s. of Mampei Morioka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; entered Govt. service; Gov. Shimane-ken, Aomori-ken, Ibaraki-ken, Tochigi-ken; Dir. Police Bureau of Chosen; Dir. Pub. Peace Bureau Home Dept. 1931-32. Address: 4 Sendagaya-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Mukden; b. Mar. 1885, Okayama-ken; s. of late Risaburo Morioka. Career: grad. Toa Dobun Shoin; Vice-Consul Canton 1919; sent to Peking as Mem. Envoy to settle Shantung Question 1922; Vice-Consul Tsingtao; Consul Ichang 1923; Nanking 1925; Chefoo 1927; Mukden 1929; Commr. Kwantung Govt.; Consul Antung 1930; Kirin 1932-37. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen. Mukden.

Dir. Colonization Bureau, Manchoukuo Ind. Dept. since 1936; b. Mar. 1902, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Nobuzo Morishige. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1925; Commr. Kwantung Govt.; Commr. Overseas Dept. 1935-36. Address: c/o Ind. Affairs Dept., Hsinking.

M.D.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Apr. 1868, Kyoto; s. of Gensen Morishima. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1894; studied Pharmacology in Germany; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1900; Dean, Medical Coll. same; Emeritus Prof. same 1928. Address: 36 Koyama Horiike-cho, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Councillor Embassy in China; b. Feb. 1896, Kanazawa City; s. of Hikoo Morishima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Foreign Office; Consul Mukden; Consul-Gen. Harbin; 1st Secr. Emb. Berlin; Dir. East Asia Bureau. Address: Japanese Embassy, Peking, China.

Chairman Dai-Nipon Celluloid Co.; b. Aug. 1865, Hyogo-ken; s. of Seihachi Morita. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Secr. Home Dept.; Dir. Sanitary Bureau, same; Dir. Com. & Ind. Bureau, Agr. & Com. Dept.; resigned and entered business. Address: 38, Dai-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Ry. Bureau, Manchoukuo Communications Dept.; b. 1896, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1924; served Mukden Office, S. M. R. Co.; present post since 1932; sent to Europe & America. Address: c/o Communications Dept., Hsinking.

Mng.-Dir. Moritani & Co.; b. May 1889, Okayama-ken; s. of Gohei Moritani, businessman. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1913; Econ. Dept. Columbia Univ. N. Y.; succeeded business of his father who founded present firm. Address: Gofukubashi 2-chome, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Nov. 1884, Miyagi-ken; s. of Tokuro Moriya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Official, Home Dept.; Secr. Chiba-ken and Aichi-ken 1913; Inspector and Councillor, Home Dept. 1917; Chief Secr. and Chief, Gen.-Affairs Sec. Chosen Govt.; Chief, 2nd Sec., Social Bureau, Home Dept.; Govt. Delegate, Int'l Labour Conf. Geneva 1925; Chief, Social Sec. Social Bureau 1926; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry. Address: 74 Nishigahara-machi, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor of Emb.; b. Nov. 1893, Miyagi-ken; s. of Tokuro Moriya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Legal Secr. Kwantung Govt. 1920; Secr. Treaty Bureau Foreign Office 1923; Mem. Delegation to Chinese Tariff Conf. Peking 1925-26; attached Delegation to Extraterritorial Commn. Peking 1925-26; 2nd Secr. Emb. London 1926; 1st Secr. 1929; 1st Secr. Legation China 1930; Consul-Gen. Foochow 1932-34; 1st Secr. Emb. Manchoukuo 1934. Address: Foreign Dept., Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral (Reserve); Pres. Japan-Mexican Soc.; Pres. Dai-Nihon Kokusui-kai; b. June 1870, Saga-ken; s. of late Takemitsu Moriyama; m. Wakako. Career: grad. Naval Academy 1892; served in Sino-Japanese War; resided in France 1899-1902; fought in Russo-Japanese war as Staff, 4th Sqn.; Nav. Attaché Emb. France 1907-10; attended 2nd Int'l Peace Conf. 1907; 100th Anniversary of Independence of Chile; served in World War as Comdr. Despatched Sqn. to America; retired 1923. Address: 1430 Kami-Meguro 6-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Prof. & Dir. of Library, Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sci.; b. June 1883, Niigata-ken; s. of Yasuhei Morohashi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1908; ordered to China for study 1919; rec'd deg. 1929. Address: 24 Nishi-Ochiai-cho 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; b. May 1858; s. of Eizo Inomata, and later adopted by Nao Motoda. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ.; sent to Diet from Oita-ken 16 times; Vice-Speaker and Speaker, House of Rep.; Communications Minister; Ry. Minister; Pres. Colonization Bureau; Committee, Ry. Council. Address: 7 Kojimachi 5-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. June 1879, Yokohama; s. of late Morimichi Motono; m. Yae [illegible]attori. Career: grad. Elec. Dept. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1902; sent to France for study 1903; went to America and Europe 1913; attended Int'l Illuminating Congress U. S. A. 1928; apptd. Dean Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1932. Address: 21 Shogoin Entomi-cho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

D.E.; Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd.; b. Aug. 1882, Tokyo; s. of late Dr. Yujiro Motoyoshi. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; Councillor, same; Chief, Designing Dept. of its Nagasaki Works; Chief, Nagasaki Works; Lecturer, Kyushu Imp. Univ.; went to Siam as Vice-Chairman Japanese Econ. Mission to Siam 1936. Address: 9 Momozono-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D. Econ.; Prof. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ.; Mem. Trade Promotion Investigation Committee; b. March 1888, Ehime-ken; s. of Magoichi Mukai, landowner. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. 1914; apptd. Asst. of Alma Mater 1914; sent to Europe & Amer. to study econ. 1919-22. Address: 342 Denyen-Chofu 3-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Permanent Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Jan. 1885; s. of Tadashiro Mukai. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; joined present firm and served as Mgr. Dairen and London Branches. Address: 433 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Shanhaikwan Customs; b. 1897, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1922; entered Hypothec Bank of Japan; served S. M. R.; Chief Record Sec. Manchoukuo State Council 1932-37. Address: Shanhaikwan Customs, Manchoukuo.

Baron; Diploma of Imp. Coll. London; Ordnance Rear-Admiral; Chief Elec. Sec. Nav. Tech. Research Dept.; b. Oct. 1891, Tokyo; s. of Vice-Admiral Shinkichi Mukoyama; m. Mitsuko. Career: grad. Elec. Engrg. Course Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; P.-G. Course, City and Guilds (Engrg.) Coll. South Kensington, London; L'Ecole Superieure d'Electricité (Section de Radio Telegraphie) Paris; succeeded to peerage 1911; apptd. Chief Nav. Ordnance Officer 1914; sent to England & France 1918-21; Inspector Nav. Ordnance 1930; Chief Elec. Dept. Kure Nav. Arsenal 1930. Address: 72 Benten-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Bachelor of Sc.; Consulting Mining Engr.; Pres. Mikuni Co.; Mng.-Dir. Munakata Trading Co.; Dir. Yamamoto Trading Co., Koun Steamship Co., Osaka Pharm. Co., The Sumoca K. K.; Nanyo Gomu Takushoku Co.; b. Aug. 1901, Osaka; s. of Masazo Munakata. Career: grad. Lafayette Coll. Easton; Bethlehem Prep. Sch., Bethlehem, Pa. U. S. A.; entered business. Address: 740 Sumiyoshi-machi, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Minister to Siam since June 1937; b. Jan. 1888, Aomori-ken. Career: grad. Spec. Consular Course Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1911; diplo. and cons. service at Changchun, Harbin, Honolulu, New York, Peking, London, Calcutta, Shanghai and Sydney. Address: Japanese Legation, Bangkok, Siam.

Vice-Pres. Kokusai Kisen Kaisha since 1936; b. Nov. 1895; Shiga-ken; s. of Yonesaburo Murakami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; entered Ry. Dept.; Secr. Ry. Dept.; Chief, Documents Sec. Secretariat; Secr. to Ry. Minister; Councillor, Ry. Region; Dir. Kobe & Osaka Regions; Dir. S. M. R. Co. 1930-34. Address: 100 Sakura-machi, Dairen.

Chief Secr. Privy Council; b. Aug. 1883, Tottori-ken; s. of Ken Murakami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Dept. of Com. 1907; served Privy Council 1916; Judge Court of Adm. Litigation 1927-34; Lecturer Chuo Univ.; Prof. of Civil Law Senshu Univ. Address: 12 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Nissan Jidosha Kogyo K.K.; b. Sept. 1878, Hiroshima City; s. of Masaji Murakami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904; joined Kisha Seizo Kaisha; Mgr. same; joined Tobata Foundry Co. 1918; Dir. same 1929; Pres. Kokusan Kogyo K. K. Address: 33 Ichigaya Kaga-cho 2-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

b. April 1889, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Yoshinori Murakami. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1910; apptd. Secr. Embassy at London; Consul and Commr. Kwantung Govt.; Secr. Tokyo Reconstruction Bureau; Consul-Gen. at Hongkong and Hamburg; Chargé d'Affaires, Embassy at Stamboul, Turkey 1931; Min. to Peru, Ecuador & Bolivia 1933-37.

Chief, Manchoukuo Koshan Agr. Experimental Stn. since 1934; b. Aug. 1896, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Tozaburo Murakoshi; m. Miyeko. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1921; entered Kungchuling Experimental Stn. of S. M. R. Co. and studied agr. physics at its Dept. of Agronomy; sent to England, America, Germany & France for study 1929-30; made special study at Dept. of Agr. Engrg. of Wisconsin Univ. Address: Koshan Agr. Experimental Stn., Koshan Lungkiang Prov.

Musician; b. June 1881, Hakodate. Career: Orchestra Conductor of Yamato Hotel under management of S. M. R. Co.; went 3 times to Europe and America to study music; composed the National Song of Manchoukuo; performed music twice in the presence of Manchoukuo Emperor. Address: 2 Yamashiro-cho, Dairen.
Lt.-Gen.; Pres. Mukden Arsenal Ltd. since 1934; b. Sept. 1887, Aichi-ken; s. of Genshu Hiraiwa; m. Tetsuko. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1898. Address: 17 Hagimachi, Mukden.

Vice-Min. of Com. & Ind.; b. Dec. 1890, Aichi-ken; s. of Shichisaburo Murase. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Secr. of Cabinet; Councillor Legislation Bureau; Dir. Resources Bureau; Dir. Com. Affairs Bureau; Dir. Patent Bureau. Address: 196 Hayashi-cho, Komagome, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Banker; b. 1886, Kagawa-ken; s. of Tomitaro Murata; m. Hanako. Career: grad. German Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; entered Justice Dept.; joined Yokohama Koshin Ginko 1921. Address: 1218 Yuigahama, Kamakura.

Pres. Osaka Shosen Kaisha since 1934; Japan Shipowners' Assn; Chairman Settsu Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. Kokusai Tsuun Kaisha, Osaka Building Co., Kitanihon Steamship Co., Nisshin Steamship Co., Nikka Life Ins. Co.; Nanyo Kaiun K.K.; Kokusai Unyu K.K.; Nichihaku Menka Co.; Nichiman Sangyo Co.; Aud. Sumitomo Chem. Co.; b. Oct. 1878; s. of Shozo Murata, Tokyo. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1900; joined O. S. K.; Mgr. Taiwan Dept. and Ocean Dept.; Mng.-Dir. 1920; Vice-Pres. 1929. Address: Shinotsubo, Mikage-cho, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Nippon Yushi (Oil & Fat) K. K.; b. Jan. 1885, Tottori-ken; s. of Kinji Murayama; m. Hisa Hirata. Career: gra. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1909; joined Nippon Flour Mills, Ltd.; later with Saiga Elec. Co. and Tobata Foundry Co.; toured abroad 1921; Mng.-Dir. Kitsukawa Engrg. Works 1922; Mng.-Dir. Tobata Cold Storage Co. 1927; Godo Marine Products Ind. Co. Osaka; Mng.-Dir. Nippon Shokuryo Kogyo K.K. 1834. Address: 4 Onden 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Dir. Tokyo Muni. Honjo Hospital; Lecturer Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Oct. 1883, Miyagi-ken; s. of Sadakazu Saito; later adopted by Gengo Murayama. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; became Vice-Dir. present hospital; studied in Europe & America; served Epidemic Hospital established temporarily just after the Earthquake disaster 1923 by Red Cross Soc. and Kyochokai. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Import & Export Merchant; Mng.-Dir. M. Musabhoy & Co. Ltd.; b. Feb. 1896; s. of M. Musabhoy, merchant. Career: grad. Bombay Univ. Mng.-Dir. M. Musabhoy & Co. Ltd. Kobe 1918-21; Dir. Swadesh Match Mfg. Co. Ltd. Bombay 1923-26; present post again since 1927. Address: 328 Sannomiya-cho 1-chome, Kobe.

n: MUSHAKOJI, Kimitomo 武者小路公共
t: Viscount; b. August 1882, Tokyo; s. of Viscount Saneyo Mushakoji. Career: grad. Law College of Tokyo Imperial University; appointed Diplomatic Probationer; Consul at Shanghai; Secretary of Embassy in Germany; Councillor, Embassy, Belgium; Minister to Denmark; Deputy Delegate to 11th Assembly, League of Nations, Geneva 1930; attended Disarm. Conf. 1931; Minister to Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark; Amb. to Turkey; Ambassador to Germany; Concluded German-Japan Anti-Comintern Agreement Nov. 1936. Address: Japanese Embassy, Berlin.

Colonel; Captain, Japanese Inf. Forces, Peking since 1936; b. 1884, Saga-ken. Career: grad Mil. Academy 1911; Mil. Staff Coll.; Staff, Mil. Affairs Sec. War Office; Sec. Chief Gen. Staff Office. Address: c/o Japanese Garrison Hdqrs., Peking China.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. May 1889, Tokyo; bro. of Marq. Naomitsu Nabeshima, Peer; later adopted by late Naoakira Nabeshima. Career: grad. German Dept. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. 1911; studied at Taulant Univ. Saxony; made inspection tour of Europe & America; elected Peer 1925; Secr. to Justice Minister 1927; Parl. Councillor of Navy 1932; Parl. Vice-Min. of Home Affairs 1936-37. Address: 8 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov. 1876, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Keisuke Nagai, scholar. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; sent to Germany to study physiology under Prof. Verworn of Göttingen Univ. 1903-06; apptd. Asst. Prof. of Alma Mater 1906; Prof. 1913; Dean of Med. Faculty 1934; rec'd deg. 1911; sent to Europe and America for inspection, and attended 13th Word Conf. of Physiology as Japan's Delegate 1929; Mem. Nat. Research Council. Educ. Dept.; Mem. Ins. Sanitary Investigation Committiee, Home Dept.; Temporary Mem. Sch. Sanitary Invest. Com.; Examiner. Med. & Dental Practitioner Exam. Address: 70 Yamamoto-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.
Ex-Consul-Gen. at Chientao; b. July 1883, Niigata-ken; s. of Yoshitomi Nagai. Career: grad.. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: c/o Matsuya Hotel, 3 Kojimachi 4-chome, Tokyo.

Ex-Amb.; b. 1877, Nagoya; s. of Matsuemon Nagai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; entered diplomatic service; 3rd Secr. Emb. Washington 1907; Cons.-Gen. San Francisco 1909; Secr. Foreign Office and Chief, Telegraph Sec. 1914-17; Councillor Emb. 1918; Dir. Com. Bureau; 1922; Minister to Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland; Amb. to Belgium 1928; Delegate Gen. Assembly League of Nations 1927-29; attended London Naval Conf. 1929; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1930; Amb. to Germany 1933-34; Chief Delegate to London Nav. Conf. 1935. Address: 28 Higashi Shinano-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Communications Minister since 1937; b. Apr. 1881, Kanazawa; s. of Noboru Nagai, samurai. Career: grad. Polit. Econ. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1905; studied at Manchester Coll. Oxford; sent to Diet 6 times; Councillor Foreign Office; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs; Prof. Waseda Univ.; Overseas Minister in Sato Cabinet 1932-34; Chief Dir. Minseito Party 1936-37. Address: 507 Sendagaya 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.E. (1933); Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1933; b. July 1894; s. of Noboru Nagai. Career: grad. Applied Chemistry Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920-193[?]. Address: 10 Nishi-kata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Major-Gen.; Chief Staff Western Defence Hdqrs.; b. 1888, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1910; Mil. Staff Coll.; Instructor Inf. Sch.; Comdr. Inf. 25th Reg.; attached to Kwantung Army Hdqrs.; Chief Staff Japanese Garrison in China 1935; Comdr. Ho-yo Fortress. Address: c/o Western Hdqrs., Kokura.

Dir. Nippon Cast Steel Co.; b. Jan. 1877 in Tokyo; s. of Yuzuru Nagamine; m. 2nd. d. of Shizusaburo Matsutani. Career: grad. Course of Mech. Engrg. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904. Address: 51 Yokodera-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Teikoku Sanchi Soko K.K.; b. June 1877, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Yakichi Nagamine. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1901; Mgr. Shanghai Branch, Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mgr. Ryoka Warehouse Co.; Mgr. Osaka Branch, Mitsubishi Trading Co. Address: [?] Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral; Comdr.-in-Chief Combined Fleet and First Fleet; b. June 1880, Kochi-ken; s. of Harukichi Nagano. Career: grad. Naval Staff Coll.; Pres. Nav. Acad. Etajima; Vice-Chief Naval Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief Yokosuka Nav. Stn. 1933-34; Admiral 1934; Delegate to London Nav. Conf. 1935; Navy Min. 1936-37. Address: 229 Ishikawa-machi, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Kobe Gas Co.; Kawasaki Dockyard Co.; Oriental Hotel and Velvet Soap Co.; b. Oct. 1870, Hyogo-ken; s. of Hikobei Nagao. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1891; joined Kanegafuchi Spinning Co.; promoted to Mng.-Dir., later Vice-Pres. of same; Pres. of same 1930. Address: 132 Okamoto, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; D.Sc. (Tokyo Imp. Univ.); Sc. D. Honorary (Cambridge Univ.); Ex-Pres. Osaka Imp. Univ.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; Mem. Imp. Acad.; b. June 1865, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Jisaburo Nagaoka. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp.; Berlin Univ.; occupied important position among Profs. of Imp. Univ. 1896-1926; Pres. Radio Committee; went abroad on official service 8 times. Address: 10 Komagome Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

D. L.; Ex-Ambassador to France; Judge, Permanent Court of International Justice; b. Jan. 1878, Yamaguchi-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; apptd. Minister to Netherlands; Dir. Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office; Ambassador to Germany; Ambassador to France 1932-33; Chief Delegate to Japan-Dutch Conf. 1934. Address: 88 Hanazono-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

b. March 1886, Kuwana, Miye-ken; s. of Teizo Nagase, printer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Secr. Forestry Bureau; Commr. Patent Bureau; Secr. Agr. & For. Dept.; Dir. Fisheries Bureau 1927; Dir. For. Bureau; Chief Rice Dept.; Dir. Agr. Bureau; Vice-Min. of Agr. & For. Address: 90 Togoshi-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nagase Kao Soap Co.; b. Feb. 1905, Tokyo; s. of late Tomiro Nagase. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ.; succeeded family estate 1911; visited Europe and America, South Seas and Australia 1926-28. Address: 2 Bakuro-cho, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Minister of Justice; b. June 1880, Ogaki; s. of Shugo Nagashima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; Judge 1913; Councillor, Justice Dept. 1916; Public Procurator, Supreme Court 1927; Dir. Civil Affairs Bureau; Pres. Sapporo Court of Appeal; Pres. Hiroshima Court of Appeal 1934-35. Address: 129 Hinode-cho 1-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Mgr. Passenger Dept. Nippon Yusen Kaisha; b. Apr. 1882, Nagano-ken; s. of Naminosuke Nagashima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1906; joined N. Y. K. and served at Yokohama and London; Mgr. Supplies Dept. Head Office. Address: 6 Wakagi-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Japan Boy Scouts; Takushoku Univ.; Imp. Educ. Assn.; b. July 1876, Hyogo-ken; s. of Jitsutaro Nagata, samurai. Career: grad. 3rd Higher Sch.; apptd. Dir. Kaito Middle Sch.; Commr. Oita-ken, Ishikawa-ken, Kumamoto-ken and Iwate-ken; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Fukuoka-ken; Police Affairs Dept. Kyoto-fu; Gov. Miye-ken; Dir. Police Bureau, Home Dept.; nominated Peer 1918; Mayor of Tokyo; Min. of Overseas Affairs 1936-37. Address: 83 Zoshigaya-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Pres. Shizuoka Minyu Shimbun; b. June 1885, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Rokusaburo Nagata. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1908; entered Manshu Shimbun; Chief Tientsin Branch, Dairen Steamship Co.; elected M.P. 6 times; Parl. Councillor of Navy 1936-37. Address: 397 Kashiwagi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Executive Office, Furukawa Elec. Co.; Nippon Elec. Wire Co. and Nippon Submarine Cable Co.; b. Oct. 1885, Ehime-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Furukawa Gomei Kaisha 1911. Address: 225 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. June 1883, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Jirohei Nagawa. Career: grad. Meiji Law Coll. 1903 and Hosei Univ. 1906; apptd. Judge 1904; Judge Tokyo, Chiba and Maebashi District Courts; practised at the bar 1917; sent to Diet 5 times from Hiroshima-ken; Parl. Vice-Minister of Ry. 1932-34. Address: 3015 Oi Kashima-cho, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Pres. Tokyo Imp. Univ., Cancer Investigation Society; b. Apr. 1878 Tokyo; s. of Sensai Nagayo. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; apptd. Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied Pathology in Germany 1907; rec'd deg. 1911; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dean Med. Faculty 1932-34; Dir. Govt. Inst. for Infectious Disease 1919-32; attended Tropical Pathology Conf. 1921; visited America by invitation of Rockefeller Foundation; Int'l Cancer Research Assn. London; Serum Conf. Copenhagen; Health Conf. League of Nations Geneva; Leper Conf. Paris. Address: 88 Ichibei-cho 2-chome, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. July 1859, Niigata-ken; s. of Hisayuki Naito, farmer. Career: grad. Pref. Sch. at Kashiwazaki and Takashima Sch. Yokohama; founded Japan Oil Co. May 1888, over which presided until 1926; sent twice as Non-commissioned Staff, Agr. and Com. Dept. to Europe and America to study oil business; sent to Diet twice; Councillor, Tokyo Reconstruction Bureau; Mem. Imp. Econ. Conf.; nominated Peer 1925. Address: 36 Zaimoku-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Sanchoku Ry. Co., Sanchoku Kaihatsu Co.; Vice-Pres. Nippon Elec. Power Co.; Mng.-Dir. Chosen Elec. Power Co.; Dir. Hakone Tozan Ry. Co; b. Apr. 1881, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Johei Naito. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Toa Dobun Shoin 1904; entered Toho Elec. Power Co. 1922; Vice-Chief Investigation Dept.; Dir. & Chief Nagoya Branch; Mng.-Dir. Nippon Elec. Power Co. 1929. Address: Inojiri, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

D. Sc.; Prof. Archit. Dept. Waseda Univ.; b. June 1886, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Koshiro Naito, farmer. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Consulting Engineer for construction of Kabuki-za, Meiji Life Ins. Bldg., Tokyo Kaijo Bldg., Nippon Ginko Bldg., etc. Address: 76 Wakamatsu-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Ritsumeikan Univ.; b. Jan. 1866, Kyoto; s. of Rokuzaemon Nakagawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; Secr. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Secr. to Prime Minister; Secr. of Cabinet; Secr. to Educ. Minister; Commr., Karafuto Govt.; Dir. Kajima Bank; Vice-Pres. Dai Nippon Life Ins. Co.; Pres. Bank of Taiwan. Address: 19 Suwa-machi, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Japan Red Cross Soc.; Lord-in-Waiting Kinkei Hall; b. Mar. 1875, Sendai; s. of late Soichi Nakagawa; m. Sada, sister of Baron Kaichi Omori. 1903. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; entered Home Dept.; apptd. Councillor, Fukushima-ken, Hyogo-ken; Secr. and Chief Home Affairs Dept. Saitama-ken and Kanagawa-ken; Gov. Osaka-fu; Dir. Sanitary Bureau Home Dept., Tokyo Reconstruction Bureau 1929-30. Address: 43 Mejiro-cho 4-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co., Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. Co.; b. 1881, Nara-ken; s. of Yukiyasu Nakagawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Ry. Bureau, Communications Dept.; Councillor Ry. Dept.; Secr. to Ry. Minister; Dir. Traffic Bureau, Ry. Dept.; Vice-Minister of Railway; studied in Europe & America; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 33 Naka-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. (Yale Univ.); Pres. Yokohama Rubber Co., Furukawa Elec. Co.; Dir. Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; Vice-Pres. Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Nov. 1874. Shiga-ken; s. of Matasaburo Akatsuka; later adopted by Ishimatsu Nakagawa. Career: grad. Yale Univ. Address: 46 Takanawa Minami-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Committee of Sanitary Assn. Home Dept.; b. July 1857; s. of late Manjiro Nakahama, samurai. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1881; Pres. Fukushima Med. Coll.; Prof. Okayama Med. Coll.; Pres. Kanazawa Med. Coll.; established Kamakura and Kaisei Hospitals. Address: 120 Denenchofu, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Japan Dental Coll.; b. May 1876, Nagano-ken; s. of Nizaemon Nakahara. Career: passed Exam. for Dental Practitioners 1889; founded present College; Studied in America; received Sc.-D. (Maryland Uni. U. S. A.) 1916; decorated for merit of his service in dental education, 1924; attended Int'l Dental Congress 1931. Address: 2737 Kichijoji, Musashino-machi, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Seitetsu K.K.; b. Jan. 1879, Kumamoto-ken; bro. of Torarokuro Nakai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Chief, Documents Sec. Agr. & Com. Dept.; Chief, Accounts Sec.; Dir. Patent Bureau; Forestry Bureau; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Com.; Pres. Imp. Steel Works. Address: 108 Kitami Seijo, Kinuta-mura, Tokyo-fu.

Pres. Nakai Yoshiten (paper) Co.; b. July 1875 at Kyoto; s. of Saburobei Nakai. Career. participated in Russo-Japanese war; awarded Junior Grade of the 7th Court Rank and 6th Class Order of Merit. Address: 66 Shimo Negishi-machi, Shitaya-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Chairman, Hokkai Soda Co.; Tokyo High Pressure Ind. Co.; b. Oct. 1870, Shimane-ken; s. of Sadaki Matsui; later adopted by Ichima Nakai  Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; Engr. Osaka Cement Co.; entered Mitsui Mining Co. 1903; Dir. same 1922; rec'd deg. 1915. Address: 28 Konno-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Minister of Rys.; M.P.; b. Jan. 1884, Gunma-ken; s. of Kumekichi Nakajima. Career: grad. Nav. Engrg. Coll; Nav. Staff Coll.; established Nakajima Aircraft Co., Leader of Seiyukai Party. Address: 2 Ichigaya Kagacho 1-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nakajima Aircraft Co.; b. Mar. 1890, Gunma-ken; bro. of Chikuhei Nakajima, M.P. Career: grad. Mercantile Marine Sch. 1916; joined Nakajima Aircraft Co.; Vice-Pres. same; went to Europe & America 3 times. Address: 1433 Kamiigusa-machi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. June 1886, Kochi-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; entered Fin. Dept.; Councillor Monopoly Bureau; Secr. to Finance Minister; Secr. to late Premier Yuko Hamaguchi, Parl. Councillor, Ry. Dept. in Wakatsuki Cabinet 1931; Parl. Vice-Min. of Finance 1936; elected M.P. 4 times. Address: 3 Mukogaoka Yayoi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

n: NAKAMIGAWA, Saburoji 中上川三郎治
t: Mng.-Dir. Chiyoda Life Ins. Mutual Co.; Dir. South America Development Co.; b. Aug. 1886, Tokyo; s. of Hikojiro Nakamigawa; m. d. of late Sanji Muto. Career: grad. Keio Univ. Address: 52 Isarago-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Wholesale Dealer in Toilet Articles, Soaps and Groceries; b. Feb. 1888, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Ryuzo Nakamura; m. Kimiyo Ejima. Career: after Russo-Japanese War, came to Harbin to engage in commerce. Address: 83 Mostowaya, Harbin.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr. Maizuru Naval Depot; b. 1884, Kochi-ken. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1905; Nav. Staff Coll.; Captain "Naka"; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; Staff Nav. Gen. Staff; Tech.-Commr. Nav. Disarm. Conf. London; Capt. "Nagato"; Chief Staff 2nd Sqn.; Dir. Nav. Educ. Bureau; Comdr. Training Sqn.; Chief 1st Dept. Nav. Gen. Staff; Dir. Nav. Staff Coll. 1935-36. Address: Naval Depot Maizuru.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1882, Tokyo; s. of late Baron Satoru Nakamura. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Ry. Dept.; apptd.
