Engr. 1907; sent to America for study, 1913; Chief, Construction Offices of Shinsho, Akita and Atami lines; Chief, Planning Section, Constr. Bureau; Dir. Constr. Bureau, 1926-29. Address: 30 Uenohara, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; High Mil. Councillor; Comdr. of Tokyo Garrison and of the Eastern Defence Hdqrs. concurrently; b. Aug. 1881, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Yoshifusa Nakamura, samurai. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Adjutant War Office; Comdr. Inf. 39th Bridg.; Chief Staff Chosen Army; Dir. Personnel Bureau War Office; Comdr. Garrison in North China 1932-34; Comdr. 8th Div. 1934; Chief Staff Mil. Training Dept. 1935; Acting Inspector-Gen. of Mil. Educ. 1936; War Minister 1937. Address: Tokyo Garrison Hdqrs.

Pres. Komatsu Seisakusho Ltd.; b. Aug. 1876, Shizuoka-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1902; entered N.Y.K.; served Kobe Branch 1903; joined Inawashiro Hydro-Elec. Power Co. 1912-23; toured Europe & America; joined Komatsu Seisakusho 1924. Address: 373 Hyakunin-machi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

n: NAKAMURA, Rikitaro 中村利器太郎
t: Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Dir. Mitsukoshi Ltd.; Niko Dept. Store; b. Mar. 1872 Tokyo. Career: grad Keio Univ. 1889; Chairman of Mitsukoshi until Sept. 1937. Address: 41 Kotaki-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1869, Fukui-ken; s. of Masanori Nakamura, teacher. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; Prof. 1st Higher Sch. 1895; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; studied Crystallography & Optics in Germany 1903-06; rec'd deg. 1909; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911 went to Europe & America during Great War; Mem. Imp. Acad. 1925; Dean, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1926-30. Address: 59 Sasugaya-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. & Mng.-Dir. Nippon Flour Mills Co. Ltd.; Pres. Toyo Flour Mills Co. Ltd., Mukden; b. Sept. 1876, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Tojuro Nakamura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1899; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr. Osaka & Kobe Branches; Dir. Nippon Flour Mills Co. Ltd. Address: 16 Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Sanwa Bank since 1933; b. Feb. 1878, Oita-ken; bro. of Hyotaro Katagiri, samurai; adopted by Sachitane Nakane 1892. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; joined Bank of Japan, and served at Business Bureau and Agency in London; Chief, National Treasury Bureau; Mgr. Osaka Branch; Dir. 1928-33. Address: 9 Natsugi-machi, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Japan Power Assn.; b. May 1879, Miye-ken; s. of late Yosuke Nakanishi; m. Fumiko, d. of Dr. Tameyuki Amano. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; entered Communications Dept.; Dir. Nagoya Com. Bureau 1919; attended 7th World Postal Conf. Madrid as Japan's Chief Delegate and made tour of Europe & Amer. 1920-21; Dir. Elec. Bureau 1923; retired 1927. Address: 145 Tsunohazu 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Kokusai Transportation Co., Godo Transportation Co., Taihoku Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Vice-Pres. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Mng.-Dir. Japan-Manchoukuo Ind. Assn.; b. May 1882, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Yoshichi Nakano. Career: succeeded father's business 1915; Mng.-Dir. Naikoku Transportation Co. 1923; Pres. 1924. Address: 1 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Feb. 1886, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Taijiro Nakano. Career: grad. Polit. Econ. Dept. Waseda Univ.; Editorial Writer, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Editor, Toho Jiron; Pres. Kyushu Nippo; Councillor, Finance Dept.; Vice-Minister of Communications; Leader Kokumin Domei 1933-35. Address: 808 Yoyogi Hon-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Nippon Oil Co.; b. Jan. 1869, Niigata-ken; s. of Teikichi Nakano, farmer. Career: grad. Law Dept. Waseda Univ. 1891; joined present firm 1893. Address: 416 1-chome, Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Kanagawa-ken since 1936; b. Mar. 1888, Okayama-ken; s. of Saburo Fukui, M.P. Career: grad. German Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Chief, Educ. Sec., Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Police Chief, Shiga-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept. Fukushima-ken, Tochigi-ken & Osaka-fu; Gov. Saga-ken, Miyazaki-ken, Tochigi-ken & Miyagi-ken; Dir. Social Bureau 1935. Address: Governor's Residence, Yokohama.

Mng.-Dir. Japan Sugar Producers' Assn. since 1936; b. 1884, Nagasaki-ken; bro. of Seiichi Nakase. Career: grad German Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; served Taiwan Govt.-Gen.; Chief, Com. & Ind. Sec.; Chief, Taichu Com. Museum; Chief, Staple Products Sec.; Dir. Monopoly Bureau, Taiwan; Gov. Taihokushu; Dir. Industrial Bureau, Taiwan; despatched to French Indo-China by the Foreign Office 1925. Address: c/o Japan Sugar Producers' Assn., 2 Marunouchi 1-chome, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 16th Div.; b. 1883, Oita-ken. Career: grad Mil. Acad. 1904; Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in France; attached to Mil. Arsenal; Comdr. Field Artil. 7th Reg.; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Comdr. Maizuru Fortress; Dir. Narashino Mil. Sch. 1933-36; Comdr. Gendarmerie 1936-37. Address: 16th Div. Hdqrs. Kyoto.

Pres. Nakashima & Co., Kanazawa Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Jan. 1881, Kanazawa; s. of late Tokutaro Nakashima. Career: Pres. Kanazawa Cultural Assn.; Kaga Paper Mfg. Co., Ishikawa-ken Agr. Co.; Dir. Kano Godo Bank, Kanazawa Elec. Tramway Co., Third Trust Co., Showa Trading Co. Address: 8 Jikken-cho, Kanazawa City.

Dir. Mukden Postal Adm. Supt. Bureau since 1932; b. 1898, Kanazawa; s. of Otokichi Nakashima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Commr. Communications Dept. Address: Niiro, Sankeiro, Mukden.

Councillor, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. since 1932; b. Feb. 1898; s. of Shinsuke Nakayama, farmer. Career: grad. Tungwen Coll. Shanghai 1920; joined Mitsui & Co., 1920; Dairen Fire & Marine Ins. Co. 1922. Address: c/o Shengyang-hsien Office, Fengtien Prov. Manchoukuo.

Dir. Radio Corp. of Japan; b. Jan. 1874, Niigata-ken; s. of Seikichi Nakayama. Career: grad. Tokyo Post and Telegraph Coll.; entered Communications Dept. 1892; went to Europe and America to investigate telephone business 1896; apptd. Elec.-Engr. Communications Dept.; representing Govt. attended 3rd Int'l Wireless Telegraph Convention, London 1912; became Adviser, Ministry of Communications, Chinese Govt. 1913; Mng.-Dir. Tokyo Branch, Radio Corp. of Japan 1928-34; went abroad to inspect radio 1930. Address: 514-2 Koyama-machi, Ebara-ku Tokyo.

Prop. Nakayama Taiyodo (mfrs. of "Club" toilet articles etc.), Nakayama Chem. Lab., Nakayama Culture Inst.. Platon Co. (mfrs. of "Platon" stationary); b. Dir. Tokyo Stock Exchange; Pres. Sagami Ry. Co.; Dir. Uraga Dock Co.; b. May 1873. Nagoya; s. of Denmei Namba, samurai. Career; grad. Keio Univ. 1893. Address: 48 Aoyama Minami-cho 2-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Kobe Pier Co., Amagasaki Real Estate Co., Nikka Oil Mfg. Co., Nihon Raw Cotton Co.; Mng.-Dir. Taisho Hemp Mfg. Co.; Dir. Sanyo Chuo Hydro-Elect. Power Co.; b. Nov. 1878; s. of Shigemitsu Nango, Peer. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1900; inherited family estate 1912. Address: 3 Hamahigashi, Mikage-machi, Hyogo-ken.

Chief Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. July [?], Gunma-ken; s. of Shinrokuro Nanjo, samurai. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1892; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr. London and Osaka Branches. Address: 14 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Engineer-in-Chief Manchoukuo Communications Dept.; Dir. Hydro-elec. Constr. Bureau; b. Dec. 1876, Kobe; s. of Masanosuke Naoki. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served as Engr. Tokyo Muni. Office. Spec. Constr. Dept. Fin. Dept., Home Dept.; Chief Osaka Harbor Dept.; Chief. Osaka City Planning Dept.; Dir.-Gen. Tokyo Reconstr. Bureau 1923; Chief, Reconstr. Bureau Home Dept. 1924; resigned 1925; Dir. Chief Engr. Obayashi-gumi; Dir. Manchoukuo Public Works Bureau. Address: 102 Jogoro, Hsinking.

Baron; Gen. (retired); Privy Councillor; b. Apr. 1868, Tochigi-ken; s. of Hikoichiro Nara; m. Mitsu, d. of Yoshinobu Umeda. Career: Apptd. Artillery Sub.-Lt. 1889; Chief Artil. Sec. Mil. Affairs Bureau, War Office; attached Embassy in Germany; Comdr. Japanese Garrison in China; Chief Staff Japanese Garrison in Tsingtao; Dir. Mil. Affairs Bureau; Chief Aide-de-Camp to H.I.M.; served Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese Wars. Address: 160 Kashiwagi 1-chome, Yodobashi, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Life Assurance Co.; Chairman Life Assurance Co.'s Assn.; b. June 1885; s. of Ryuzo Naruse. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; entered Govt. service 1910; Chief Secr. House of Peers; Commr. of Enthronement Ceremony 1927; Mng-Dir. of present firm 1932. Address: 135 Aoyama-Minami-cho 6-chome, Tokyo.

D. Agr.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Rural Reconstruction Committee, North Eastern District Development Committee, Japanese Council, I.P.R., Imp. Agri. Assn.; Manchoukuo Immigration Assn.; Japan-Germany Culture Inst.; b. June 1888, Tokyo; s. of Hatsumi Nasu. Career: grad. Agri. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Asst; Prof. same 1917; rec'd deg. 1923; Prof. 1923; sent to Europe & America. Address: 415 Setagaya 4-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor Chinghsing-hsien, Lungkiang Prov. since 1934; b. Jan. 1902; s. of Hyakusuke Negoro. Career; grad. Keio Univ. 1927; made tour of inspection to China; joined political movement in Heilungkiang Prov. 1932; Commr. Heilungkiang Prov. Address: Chinghsing-hsien Office Lungkiang Prov., Manchoukuo.
Engineer; b. Mar. 1886, June, Germany; m. Shizue. Address: 60 Tsuji, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

Journalist; b. 1882, Graach, Germany. Career: Clerk, Provincial Bank, Germany; came to China 1902; Prop. & Editor, "Hankow Daily News" 1908-17; Editor "North China Standard," Peiping 1920-26; returned to Germany 1926; Editorial Staff, "Uebersee-Post," Leipzig 1927-28; English Editor "Transocean" Wireless News Service 1929; Editor, English Edition, "Berliner Tageblatt" 1930-31, returned to Far East 1932, representing "Deutsches Nachrichtenbuero. Now representing Manchuria of "Eildienst fuer Aussenhandel & Auslandswirtschaft," correspondent "Ostasiatische Rundschau" and other German newspapers, Deutsche Ostmesse, Koenigsberg. Publications: "A Dairy of the Chinese Revolution," "Industrial Follies of China." Address: No. 4 Yung Ho Li, Jan Ching Hou, Mukden.

Adviser, Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Member of House of Peers; Acting Partner, Nezu Gomei Kaisha; Pres. South Chosen Ry. Co. Taihei Life Ins. Co., Tobu Ry. Co., Tokyo Subway Co., Showa Fire Ins. Co., Fukoku Conscription Ins. Co.; Chairman, Nankai Ry. Co.; Dir. Nihon Chemical Ind. Co., Aikoku Life Ins. Co., Yokohama Warehouse Co.. Japan Air Transport Co., Chichibu Ry. Co., Chinfoo Ry. Co., Ashikaga Spinning Co., Iwaki Cement Co., Seibu Ry. Co.; b. June 1860, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Toemon Nezu. Career: elected M.P. 3 times; established Musashi Higher Sch.; nominated Peer 1926. Address: 115 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
Merchant; b. May 1883, Mark, Germany. Career: arrived China 1913. Address: Kokosheki-cho, Dairen.

n: NIIDA, Masutaro 仁井田益太郎
t: D.L.; Lawyer; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1868, Fukushima-ken; s. of Oncho Niida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; Judge 1896; studied Civil Procedure Code in Germany 1897-1900; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1900; rec'd deg. 1901; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined the bar; nominated Peer 1934. Address: 215 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Com. Affairs Bureau Dept. of Com. & Ind.; b. Mar. 1897, Niigata-ken; s. of Keijiro Niikura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1920; Secr. Mine Adm. Bureau Dept. of Agr. & Com.; Chief Mining Law Sec. Osaka Mine Adm. Bureau; Dir. Trade Bureau Dept. of Com. & Ind. Address: 64 Nishigahara, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Asano Bussan Kaisha; Dir. Nihon Hodo (Pavement) Co., Showa Iron Works, Okano Valves Mfg. Co.; Spec. Committee Resources Research Bureau of Cabinet; b. Mar. 1884, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Seiichi Ninomiya. Career: grad. Meiji Law Coll. 1904; stayed in America 14 yrs.; Mgr. Oriental Trading Co.; Mem. Seattle Chamber of Com.; returned 1915; Acting Partner Daikoku Shokai; joined Asano Co. 1919. Address: 422 Shimo-Ochiai 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Embassy, Moscow since 1936; b. Apr. 1893, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Taichizaemon Nishi; m. Fukiko. Career; grad. Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; diplomatic service at Embassy in Russia and Consulates in New York and Hsinking; Chief, 1st Sec. Com. Affairs Bureau, Foreign Office; same, Europe & America Bureau 1932-34; same, Europe & Asia Bureau 1934-36; Consul-General, Tsingtao. Address: Japanese Embassy, Moscow.

Mgr. New York Branch Yokohama Specie Bank; b. Nov. 1886; s. of Masaaki Nishi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1908; joined present bank; served at its Dairen, Shanghai, New York, Buenos Aires, Hankow and Soerabaya Branches. Address: c/o Yokohama Specie Bank, New York.

M.D. (1917); Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1922; b. Jan. 1885, Tokyo; s. of late Seiichi Nishi. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; studied in Germany 1911-15; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1915-22. Address: 1642 Shimo-Ochiai 4-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Aug. 1870, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Yasunori Nishida. Career: grad. Phil. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1894; Teacher Ishikawa-ken Mid. Sch.; Prof. Yamaguchi Higher Sch.; 4th Higher Sch.; Peers' Sch.; Kyoto Imp. Univ. Address: 32 Tanaka Asukai-machi, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

Dir. Matsumoto Higher Sch.; b. Feb. 1873. Tochigi-ken; s. of Masanobu Nishikawa, official; m. Sei, d. of Kwanpo Araki, court artist. Career: grad. Science Dept. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1898; Teacher & Secretary, of same; Sch. Inspector of Educ. Dept.; Dir. Kochi Higher Sch. 1927-32. Address: Asama, Matsumoto-shigai, Nagano-ken.

Mng.-Dir. Nomura Life Ins. Co.; Dir. Nomura Bank; b. 1885, Osaka; s. of Isaburo Nomura. Career: grad. Kansai Com. & Tech. Sch.; entered Sumitomo Bank; went abroad 1926; entered Nomura Bank 1927; Mgr. Tokyo Branch. Address: 73 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. & Ph. D. (Columbia Univ.); D. Sc. (Tokyo Imp. Univ.); Adviser, Osaka Mainichi Pub. Co.; Mng.-Dir. Social Welfare Corps of same; Mem. Japan Writers' Assn.; Writer; b. Mar. 1883; s. of Genitsu Nishimura, farmer. Career: grad. Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch.; Columbia Univ. N. Y., U. S. A.; apptd. Prof. Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; joined Osaka Mainichi Shimbun 1928; stayed in Manchuria & China 7 years; Europe & America 7 years for investigation  Address: Minami-Toshimamura, Toyono-gun, Osaka-fu.

Lieut.-Gen.; b. 1881, Tottori-ken; s. of Shigetake Nishio. Career: grad. Mil. Academy; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll.; Comdr. Inf. 40th Reg.; Chief, 1st Sec. Mil. Training Dept.; Comdr. Inf. 39th Brig.; attached to Mil. Arsenal 1930; Chief, 4th Dept. Gen. Staff Office; Chief Staff, Kwantung Army 1934-36; Vice-Chief Gen. Staff Office 1936-37; Comdr. Imp. Guards Div. 1937. Address: 24 Mikawadai-machi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Auditor, Manchuria Telephone & Telegraph Co. since 1933; b. March 1882, Gunma-ken; s. of Shogo Nishiyama, official. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ.; entered Finance Office; Dir. Finance Bureau, Kwantung Govt. Address: 6 Takasaki-machi, Ryojun.

Mgr, Hsinking Branch, Fukusho & Co.; head, Kirin, Ssupingkai, Tumen Branch offices same; Mng.-Dir. Hsinking Colliery Co.; Auditor, Hsinking Automobile Co.; b. Nov. [?] in Osaka; s. of Jimbei Nishiyama. Career: grad. Osaka Foreign Language Sch. 1925; joined Fukusho & Co.; Chief, Warehouse Sec. same; Insurance Sec., same; Harbin Branch Office, same. Address: 42, Yashimadori, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

D.E.; Dir. & Chief Engr., Nippon Elec. Co.; Dir. Manshu Communications Co.; b. Aug. 1893, Matsusaka City; e.s. of Yasubei Niwa. Career: Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916; joined Communications Dept., same year; entered Nippon Elec. Co., 1924; rec'd Imp. Reward and an Imp. Commemoration Reward by Imp. Acad. and Society for Protection of Industrial Property, respectively, for invention of the N. E. type Television. Address: 1590 Ekoda 4-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Rear-Admiral; Chief, Naval Affairs Propagation Dept. since 1935; b. 1888, Hokkaido. Career: grad. Naval Academy 1907; Naval Staff Coll.; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; despatched to Europe & America; Tech. Commr. Gen. Disarm. Conf. Geneva; Chief, Extra Research Sec. Mil. Affairs Bureau of Navy. Address: c/o Navy Office, Tokyo.

M.D.; Pres. Mukden Hospital, Japan Red Cross Society since 1930; b. Sept. 1891 in Aichi-ken; s. of Kuichiro Noda, fertilizer merchant. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1918; apptd. Surgeon-Lieut., Army Dept., 1919; rec'd deg. 1929; Surgeon Lieut. Colonel 1933; sent to Europe and America for investigation, 1936. Address: 30 Naniwa-dori, Mukden.

D.L.; Counsellor, German Embassy, Tokyo; b. Sept. 1887, Zittau, Germany. Career: since 1920 in the diplomatic service; Councillor, Legation, Sofia; Chief, Polish Sec. Foreign Office, Berlin 1927-33; arrived in Japan Sept. 1933. Address: German Embassy, Tokyo.

Journalist; Corr. for the Far East: L'Intransigeant (Paris); b. St. Louis, Mo. U.S.A. Aug. 1882; s. of Henry Martyn Noel, banker. Address: 1191 Horiuchi, Hayama. Business Office: The Japan Times, Tokyo.

Spec. Staff, Kokusai Unyu K. K.; b. May 1881; s. Kiyemon Nogi, merchant. Career: served Ry. Dept. for 30 years; retired as Chief of its Nagoya Traffic Office 1928; joined present firm as Councillor; Dir. 1930-35. Address: 26 Suisen-cho, Dairen.

Pres. Nippon Nitrogen Fertilizer Co., Asahi Bemberg Co., Nihon Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Chosen Nitrogen Fertilizer Co., Nippon Magnesium Metals Co., etc.; b. July 1873, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Koreyuki Noguchi. Career: grad. Elec. Course, Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; established Sogi Hydro-Elec. Co. 1904. Address: c/o Nippon Chisso Hiryo K. K., Soze-cho, Kita-ku, Osaka.

Publisher; Pres. Dai-Nippon Yuben-kai Kodan-sha; Hochi Shimbun-sha; Dir. Nippon Paper Mfg. Co.; Aud. Chugai Printing Co.; b. Dec. 1878, Gunma-ken; s. of Yoshio Noma. Career: grad. Gunma-ken Normal Sch.; Spec. Training Sch. of Teachers, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served as Teacher of Primary Sch. and Middle Sch.; Sch.-Inspector Okinawa-ken; Secr. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Publisher of magazines "Yuben," "Kodan Club," "Fuji," "Shonen Club," "Fujin Club," "King," "Gendai," "Shojo Club" and "Yonen Club." Address: 19 Otowa 3-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral (reserve); Pres. Peers' Sch.; b. Dec. 1877, Wakayama; s. of Kisaburo Masuda, samurai; adopted by Masatane Nomura; m. Hideko. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1898; despatched to Austria & Germany; Staff Nav. Affairs Bureau Navy Dept.; Secr. to Navy Minister; Attaché Emb. U.S.A.; Captain "Yakumo"; attended Peace Conf. and Washington Conf.; Staff Nav. Gen. Staff; Dir. Nav. Instruction Bureau; Vice-Chief Nav. Gen. Staff; Comdr. Training Sqn.; Comdr.-in-Chief Kure Nav. Stn.; Comdr. 3rd Sqn. 1932; Comdr.-in-Chief Yokosuka Nav. Stn. 1932-33; War Councillor. Address: 40 Nanpeidai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nomura Bank; Vice-Pres. Nomura Gomei Kaisha, Nomura East Indies Development Co.; Dir. Nomura Securities Co., Osaka Trust Co., Nomura Life Ins. Co.; b. 1887, Osaka; s. of Joko Nomura. Career: grad Osaka Higher Com. Sch.; Birmingham Univ. England. Address: 1875 Kannonjibayashi, Sumiyoshi-mura, Hyogo-ken.

Rear-Admiral; Chief Staff, Combined Fleet since 1935; b. 1886, Kagoshima-ken. Career: grad. Naval Academy 1907; Naval Staff Coll.; Staff, Naval Construction Dept.; Captain "Chogei"; Naval Attaché, Embassy, Germany; Capt. "Haguro" and "Kaga"; Dir. Naval Submarine Sch.; Commdr. 2nd Submarine Battle Sqn.; despatched to London Disarm. Conf.; resided in Germany. Address: c/o Navy Office, Tokyo.

D.E.; Pres. Ominato Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Dir. Tokyo Underground Ry. Co., Nambu Ry. Co., Shonan Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Jan. 1859, Gifu-ken; s. of Akira Nomura. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1881; rec'd deg. 1888; Chief Engr. Ry Dept.; Pres. Civil Engrg. Society; Imp. Ry. Assn.; S. M. R. Co.; made inspection tour of Europe & America twice. Address: 35 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; High Tax-payer in Osaka; Acting Partner Nomura Gomei Kaisha; Pres. N. V. Nomura Oost-Indische Cultuur Maatschappij; Dir. Osaka Gas Co., Fukushima Spin. Co.; Adv. Nomura Securities Co., Nomura Bank, Nomura Life Ins. Co., Sugimura Warehouse Co., Nikka Spinning & Weaving Co.; Aud. Osaka Trust Co.; b. Aug. 1878 in Osaka; s. of Joko Nomura. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Com. Sch. 1897, entered business; received decoration from French Govt. 1928. Address: 21 Bingo-cho 2-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

Chairman Mitsui Life Ins. Co.; b. 1880, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Hanji Noyori. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Mitsui & Co.; Business Mgr. same; Chief Osaka Branch. Address: 469 Kami-Osaki 1-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Prop. Nozawa Shoten; Rep.-Dir. Nippon Asbestos-Slate Mfg. Co., Showa Cement Co.; Chairman, Taikyu Spinning Co.; Dir. Higo Filature Co.; b. June 1871, Shiga-ken; s. of Tazaemon Tonoike, brewer. Career: served at Raw Silk Dept. Mogi Shoten, Yokohama; went to Brazil 1895; started import of Indigo into Japan 1897, and Asbestos-Slate 1906, at Kobe; established Nippon Asbestos-Slate Mfg. Co. 1912; elected Mem. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind. 1921; Rep.-Dir. Asbestos-Slate Co.; Dir. Kobe Raw Silk Co. and Higo Filature Co. Address: 2 of 11 Kitanagasa-dori 3-chome, Kobe.

M.D.; Sc. D.; Principle, Teikoku Girls' Medical Special Sch. (Teikoku Joshi Igaku Yakugaku Senmon Gakko) since 1925; Pres. Nukada Hospital (Internal diseases); b. Dec. 1886 in Okayama-ken; s. of Atsuta Nukada; physician; m. Katsura Koga. Career: grad. Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; M.D. degree 1919; Lecturer, Alma Mater, 1923; Sc. D. degree 1925. Address: 1722 Araijuku 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Merchant (Nutter & Co.); Vice-Cons. for Portugal; b. May 1870, Greenford, Middlesex, England; s. of Elliot Smith Nutter, merchant; m. Tome Sakamoto who became a British Subject. Career: educated at University College School, Gower Street, London. Address: Dairi, Moji City.

Pres. Oana Elec. & Mfg. Co.; Mng.-Dir. Nippon Wireless Telegraph & Telephone Co.; Dir. Nippon Carbonic Acid Gas Co.; Nippon Bean-Mash Company; b. April 1881, Nagano-ken; s. of late Yasaburo Oana. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; studied at Technische Hoch Schule, Karlsruhe, Baden, Germany 1910-13; Engr. Tokyo Elec. Power Co. 1905-07; Chief Elec. Engr. Asano Cement Co. 1907-09; Chief Engr. and Mgr. Fukuhaku Elec. Ry. Co. (now Toho Elec. Power Co.) 1909-10; established Oana Seisakusho 1914; Lecturer, Waseda Univ. Address: 5 Hashiba 2-chome, Asakusa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Agr. Affairs Bureau; b. Dec. 1891, Saga-ken; s. of Shoroku Inatomi; later adopted by Matakichi Obama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Sec. Chief Agrl. Bureau; Chief Fishery Sec. Fisheries Bureau 1928; Chief Secr. to Minister of Agr. & Forestry; Dir. Agrl. Bureau 1934; Investigator Cabinet Investigation Bureau. Address: 44 Sumiyoshi-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. & Mng.-Editor Chugai Shogyo Shimpo; b. Dec. 1889, Shimane-ken; s. of Ichiro Obama. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Waseda Univ.; Secr. to Speaker, House of Rep. 1915; joined Masuda Trading Co. 1917; Editorial Staff Chugai Shogyo Shimpo 1921. Address: 388 Unoki-machi, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. South Manchuria Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1885, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; joined present firm; sent to Germany and America for study 2 years; Chief, General Affairs Sec. Tokyo Branch of the firm 1919; Head, Finance Sec. 1925; Auditor 1927; toured Europe and America 8 months; Head Shanghai Office 1929; became Mng.-Dir. Hanshin Harbour Co.; Dir. Japan-Manchou Warehouse Co., Shantung Mining Co., Shoko Glass Co., Toyo Nitrogen Industry Co. Address: 18 Goban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Utsunomiya; b. Apr. 1886, Shimane-ken; s. of Kameshiro Ochiai. Career: grad. Law Dept. Nihon Univ. 1910; apptd. Commr. Tokushima-ken; Yamanashi-ken; Chief Police Affairs Dept. Oita-ken, Miye-ken, Nagano-ken; Chief Home Dept. Gunma-ken, Ishikawa-ken, Akita-ken, Aichi-ken, Kanagawa-ken; Gov. Tokushima-ken; Dep.-Mayor of Tokyo. Address: 30 Taira-cho, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. 1889, Tokyo-fu; adopted s. of Nobutoshi Oda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1915; entered Bank of Japan; toured China & Europe; joined Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Secr. to Ry. Minister 1926; Foreign Councillor 1929; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry in Saito Cabinet 1933-34. Address: 52 Ichigaya Yakuoji-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

D. L.; Mem. House of Peers; Mem. Imp. Acad. Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. since 1931. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; studied in England, France & Germany; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Dean Law Coll. same; attended Int'l Acad. Assembly 1920; Judge Permanent Court of Int'l Justice Hague. Address: 3 Kami-nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Pres. Hitachi Seisaku-sho, Ltd.; b. 1874, Tochigi-ken. Career: grad. Elec. Engrg. Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; joined Kuhara Mining Co. Ltd. 1906; Sr. Mng.-Dir. Hitachi Seisaku-sho, Ltd. 1920; present post since 1929. Address: 140 Komagome Higashi Katamachi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Bank Ltd.; Dir. Sumitomo Bldg. Co. etc.; b. Feb. 1880, Niigata-ken; s. of Keisaku Ohdaira; m. Matsu, d. of Isaburo Tokumasu. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1902; joined present bank. Recreation: Golf. Clubs: Osaka Club, Osaka Bankers' Club. Address: 50 Kitabatake Naka 2-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Chief Ed. Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Asahi Shimbun; b. 1888, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Michihei Ogata. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1911; joined Asahi Shimbun; Dir. Osaka Asahi Shimbun 1928; studied in Europe & America 1920. Address: 331 Hyakunin-cho 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Jan. 1883; s. of Koreyoshi Ogata, physician. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; went to Germany for study 1910-13; apptd. Asst. Prof. of Alma Mater 1913; Prof. Pathological Anat. Address: 435 Komagome 3-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

L.D.; M.P.; b. June 1876, Okayama-ken; s. of Tomoaki Ogawa, physician. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; apptd. Asst. Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904 and later promoted to Prof., Dean, Econ. Coll. same Univ. 1922-24; elected to Diet from Okayama-ken 7 times; Dir. Minseito; Vice-Minister of Finance in Hamaguchi Cabinet; Com. & Ind. Minister in Hirota Cabinet 1936-37. Address: 32 Sakurayama-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Prof. Ryojun Engrg. Coll. since 1934; b. Sept. 1893, Tokyo; s. of Prof. Umesaburo Ogawa. Career: grad. Mech. Engrg. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Chief Engine Designing Sec. Nagoya Works, Mitsubishi Aircraft Co. Address: 7 Akabane-cho, Ryojun.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. May 1870, Kyoto; s. of Atsushi Asahi, later adopted by Komakitsu Ogawa. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; Engr. Agr. & Com. Dept. 1897; went to France 1900; to Manchuria 3 times during Russo-Japanese War; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1908; Dean, Sc. Coll.; resigned 1930. Address: 467 Tonodan, Bishamon-cho, Kyoto.

M.D.; Prof. Nagoya Med. Univ. since 1931; b. Jan. 1875, Nagano-ken; s. of Sadahei Oguchi, merchant. Career: grad. Saisei Gakusha; served Sino-Japanese War as Surgeon-Sub.-Lieut. 1895; Surgeon Captain during Russo-Japanese War 1904-05; Surgeon-Major 1910; Instructor Army Med. Sch. 1911; Prof. S. Manchuria Med. Coll. 1912; sent to Europe 2 years; rec'd deg. 1916; Dir. & Prof. Aichi Med. Coll. 1926; Mem. Int'l Council of Ophthalmologie since 1929. Address: 22, Hazama-cho, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

Mem. House of Peers; Rep. Dir. Sumitomo Honsha Ltd.; Chairman Sumitomo Mining Co., Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd., Sumitomo Elec. Wire & Cable Works, etc.; b. Mar. 1875, Kanazawa; s. of Masamichi Ogura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Commr. of Civil Engrg. Home Dept. 1897; Councillor Yamaguchi-ken 1898; resigned 1899 to join Sumitomo Firm; travelled in Europe & America 1900-02. Address: 24 Aioi-dori 1-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir. Manshu Paint Co. since 1919; b. Sept. 1882, Aichi-ken; s. of Yakichi Oguri. Career: grad. Com. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1907; served Nisshin Oil Mfg. Co. for many years. Address: Komatsudai, Hoshigaura, Dairen.

Pres. Chugoku Bank, Kurashiki Silk Fabric Co., Kurashiki Spinning Co.; Kurashiki Chuo Hospital; Ohara Art Museum; b. July 1880, Okayama-ken; s. of Koshiro Ohara, company dir. Career: established Ohara Agr. Research Inst. 1914; Ohara Social Problems Research Inst. 1919; Kurashiki Labour Science Research Inst. 1921. Address: Shinkawa-machi, Kurashiki, Okayama-ken.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Jan. 1877, Niigata-ken; s. of Keijiro Tanaka; adopted by Tomotada Ohara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; apptd. Judicial Probationer; Judge, Tokyo District Court, 1904; Public Procurator, Chiba Local Court; Tokyo District Court 1908; Councillor, Dept. of Justice 1919; Chief Public Procurator, Yokohama Local Court 1920; made official tour through U.S.A. and Europe 1921-22; Chief Public Procurator, Tokyo District Court 1921; Nagasaki Court of Appeal 1923; Public Procurator, Supreme Court 1924; Vice-Minister of Justice 1927; Pres. Tokyo Court of Appeal 1931-34; Justice Minister 1934-36. Address: 23 Naka-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Director-General, Foreign Office, Manchoukuo; b. 1893, Gifu-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer; 1st Secr. of Legation; Consul-Gen. Harbin 1931; Manchoukuo Vice-Min. of Foreign Affairs; went to Europe & America, 1937. Address: Foreign Office, Hsinking.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Dec. 1885, Toyama-ken; s. of Hachisaburo Ohashi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; entered Communications Dept.; Secr. to Com. Min.; Dir. Postal Affairs Bureau 1925; Dir., Finance Bureau 1928; Chief Secr. of Hayashi Cabinet; Pres. Cabinet Research Bureau 1937. Address: 67 Nagata-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. of House of Peers; Adviser Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Mgr. Soc. for Int'l Cultural Relations; Pres. Chosen Kogyo Co., Ohashi Honten, Keijo Elec. Co.; Chairman Dai-Nippon Brewery Co.; Manshu Pulp Ind. Co.; Elec. Chem. Ind. Co., Chosen Smokeless Coal Co.; Dir. S. Chosen Ry. Co., Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Ins. Co., Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Nihon Yusen Kaisha, Japan Air Transport Co., Japan Dyestuff Mfg. Co., Tokyo Fire Ins. Co.; b. July 1863, Niigata-ken; s. of Sahei Ohashi. Career: studied at Dojinsha; published Hokuetsu Shimpo; established Hakubunkan; founded Ohashi Library; elected to Diet from Tokyo 1902; nominated Peer 1926. Address: 22 Sanban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
Corr. "Petit Parisien" and "Le Jour," in Japan. Address: 6 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Ex-Mayor of Yokohama; b. July 1887, Kagawa-ken; s. of Michiji Ohnishi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Chief, Police Affairs Dept. Kagawa-ken; Secr. & Councillor Chosen Govt.; Chief Home Affairs Dept. Keisho-Hokudo; made inspection tour of Europe 1924; Secr. Reconstruction Bureau 1926; Deputy Mayor of Tokyo 1926; same of Yokohama 1929; Mayor of Yokohama 1931-35. Address: 71 Aoyama Kita-machi 4-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Asahi Glass Co., b. Apr. 1884, Tokyo; s. of Nizo Ohno. Career: grad. Ceramic Ind. Course Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1906; joined present firm; apptd. Factory Dir. same; Lecturer Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch., Meiji Semmon Gakko; Engrg. Coll. Kyushu Imp. Univ.; Mem. Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 1336 Higashi 1-chome, Magome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Civil Adm. Chief of Chosen; b. Oct. 1887, Saitama-ken; bro. of Eizo Ohno. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; entered Home Dept.; Secr. Social Bureau; went to Europe & Amer. 1923; Gov. Tokushima-ken & Gifu-ken; Dir. Local Affairs Bureau, Home Dept.; Metro. Police Chief 1932; Japanese Del. to 15th Int'l Labour Conf. 1916; Econ. Adviser to Kwantung Army 1935; Dir.-Gen. Kwantung Bureau 1935-36. Address: c/o Chosen Gov.-Gen., Keijo, Chosen.

M.P.; Pharmacist; Leader, Seiyukai; b. May 1870, Aichi-ken; s. of late Kiroku Ohguchi, druggist. Career: grad. Tokyo Pharmacy Sch.; Medical Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Mayor of Toyohashi; Mem. Aichi Pref. Assembly; returned to Diet 8 times; Dir. Toyohashi Elec. Co.; Pres. Toyohashi Shimbun; Mem. Toyohashi Chamber of Com.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Finance. Address: 16 of 2 Kohinatadai-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

B.S.; M.A. (Columbia Univ. New York) Librarian; b. 1898, Kyoto; s. of Sanjiro Ohsa, businessman; m. Kazuko, d. of Sadaji Otogawa of Kyoto. Career: studied at Coll. of English Literature, Doshisha Univ. 1918-21; School of Library Service & Teachers Coll. Columbia Univ. 1926-28; B.S. 1927; M.A. 1928; Librarian Dairen Lib. S.M.R. Co. 1921-29; Head Librarian Fushun Lib. of same Co. 1929-36; Asst. Dir. Dairen Lib. 1936. Address: Dairen Library, Dairen.

Vice-pres. Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Dir. Osaka Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Chairman, Marine Affairs Assn.; b. 1876, Ibaragi-ken; s. of Iyonosuke Oda, later adopted by Mizuho Ohta. Career: Mercantile Marine Sch. 1896; studied in Europe and America; joined present firm 1900; made inspection tour of Europe and America 1913; attended 1st Int'l Labour Conf. at Washington 1919. Address: 592 Aoki, Honjo-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

L.L.B.; Councillor S.M.R. Co.; b. Mar. 1893, Okayama-ken; s. of Usaburo Ohta, farmer; m. Setsuko. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined present firm 1917; Manager, Yingkow, Antung and Mukden Offices successively; went to Europe and America for study 1930-31; Mgr. Tsitsihar Office; Supervisor; transferred to Tientsin Office 1935. Address: c/o Tientsin Office, S.M.R. Co., Tientsin.

Pres. Yamaichi Securities & Finance Co.; b. Jan. 1890, Okayama-ken; s. of Daishiro Ohta. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; joined present firm 1917; Dir. 1921; Mng.-Dir. 1926-1936. Address: 1 Toyowake-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Dir. Nisshin Steamship Co.; Overseas Development Co.; Mem. Nat. Resources Investigation Committee; Nat. Park Committee; Overseas Trade Committee; Japan-Amer. Trade Council; Mng.-Trustee Japan Tourist Bureau; Councillor Imp. Marine Affairs Assn.; Navy Assn.; South Seas Assn.; b. Mar. 1874, Fukui-ken; s. of Fumoto Ohtani. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1896; joined N. Y. K. and served in its branches at London, Hongkong, Singapore, Culcutta, New York; travelled in interest of N.Y.K. over Australia, Malay Peninsula, Dutch Indies, British India, French Indo-China, Siam, Philippines, South Africa, etc.; attended Int'l Maritime Law Conf. London, Paris, Gothemburg, etc. as Japanese Delegate 1920-23; Mng.-Dir. N.Y.K. 1923; Vice-Pres. 1929-35. Address: 275 Chojamaru, Kami-Osaki, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Aug. 1888, Hyogo-ken; s. of Mampei Ohuchi; m. Sasayo Takeda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Secr. Finance Dept.; Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1919. Address: 385 Hyakunin-machi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Chem. Ind. Co., Dir. Nippon Sheet Glass Co., Kyushu Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Victor Talking Machine Co. of Tokyo; etc; b. Sept. 1884, Tokyo; s. of Gannojo Nagai. Career: grad. Elec. Engrg. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Engr. Electric Bureau, Communications Dept. 1911; Lecturer, Engrg. & Tech. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1911; joined Sumitomo Firm 1913; apptd. Mgr. Executive & Adm. Dept. 1925; Mgr. Gen. Affairs Dept. 1930. Address: 1447 Shiro-nomae, Mikage-machi, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Retired Gen.; b. Sept. 1863, Yamaguchi; s. of Matahei Oi. Career: grad. Mil. Academy, 1883 and Mil. Staff Coll. 1888; Staff Gen. Staff Office; Staff 2nd Division; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll.; Secr. to War Minister; Attaché, Embassy, Berlin; Comdr. Inf. 18th Brig.; Comdr. 12th Div.; 8th Div.; Vladivostok Expeditionary Force; Supreme War Councillor. Address: 74 Izumi-machi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral; Chief Nav. Air Service Hdqrs.; b. 1883, Niigata-ken; s. of Ryogo Oikawa. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1905; Aide-de-Camp Crown Prince; Captain "Tama"; Chief 1st Sec. Nav. Gen. Staff; Head Instr. Nav. Acad.; Staff, Naval Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief 1st Nav. Air Corps 1932; Dir. Nav. Acad. 1933; Comdr.-in-Chief 3rd Sqn. Address: 91 Nishi-Okubo 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Aerological Observatory; b. Mar. 15, 1874, Saga-ken; s. of late Tokichi Oishi; m. Kane, d. of late Horinori Ito. Career: Physical Course, Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Expert, Central Meteorological Observatory; sent to France & Germany for study, 1911-13; to America, 1919 and to Europe, 1927 on official tour. Address: Official Residence, Tateno, Onogawa-mura, Tsukuba-gun, Ibaraki-ken.

Mayor of Nagoya; Adviser Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. May 1867; s. of Tazo Oiwa. Career: grad. Tokyo Hogaku-in 1891; elected to Diet from Aichi-ken 1915. Address: 74 Minami Ise-machi 3-chome, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Pres. Japan Zoology Society; b. Nov. 1868, Tokyo; bro. of Tsunetaro Oka. Career: grad. Zool. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; studied Zool. Bot. and Geol. in Freiburg & Leipzig Univs. Germany; rec'd deg. 1895; Prof. Yamaguchi Higher Sch.; Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1897. Address: 17 Ichigaya Kawada-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Dairen Suburban Real Estate Co.; Dir. Manchuria Cultural Assn.; b. Mar. 1858, Miye-ken; s. of Kaheiji Oka, fish wholesaler. Career: apptd. Pres. 105th Bank, Tsu City, 1879; President of Miye Chamber of Commerce 1881; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1887; Mgr. Tokyo Elec. Light Co. 1894; went to China, 1901, and engaged in shipping business between Japan and China; served in World War 1934; Pres. Dairen Credit Bank 1924; joined S. M. R. Co. Address: 2 Yamashiro-cho, Dairen.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1868 Okayama-ken; s. of Kisaburo Itami, and later adopted by Yasutaka Oka, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1891; Gov. Akita-ken and Tottori-ken; Dir. Police Bureau; Metropolitan Police Chief; nominated Peer 1914. Address: 58 Aoyama Minami-cho 5-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Journalist; Chairman, Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi; b. Sept., 1873, Osaka; s. of Yoshisuye Oka. Career: grad Polit. Dept. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; apptd. Councillor, Legislation Bureau; same, Dept. of Agr. & Com.; Chief Ind. & Com. Section of same 1913; Dir. Ind. & Com. Bureau, Dept. of Agr. & Com.; apptd. Japanese Govt. Rep. to Paris Peace Conf., and became Member of Committee for Codification of Labor Charter of Versailles Treaty in Paris 1918; Mem. of Committee for the Revision of Treaty of Commerce; represented Government at 1st International Labor Conf. Washington 1919; Govt. Repr. at Paris and Geneva for revision of economic boycott clauses in League of Nation's Pact; visited China, South Seas, Europe and America to investigate financial and economic conditions; made great contribution towards completion of making Laws on Trade Unions, Factory and Petty Insurance; became Dir. Osaka Mainichi Pub. Co. 1927; Editor, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi. Address: 276 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. South Manchuria Tech. Coll. since 1930; Pres. Manchuria Archt. Assn.; b. Nov. 1889, Sendai; s. of Arau Oka. Career: grad. Archit. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; entered S.M.R. Co.; despatched to Europe and America for Inspection 1921-2; Prof. South Manchuria Tech. Coll. 1925-30. Address: 180 Togendai, Dairen.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. Aug. 1884, Tokyo; s. of late Viscount Nagamoto Okabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; joined diplomatic service; Attaché, Emb. England & Amer.; Chief 2nd Sec. Asia Bureau Foreign Office; Deputy Grand Master of Ceremonies; Parl. Vice-Minister for War; Vice-Pres. Japan-Manchou Cultural Soc. Address: 10 Tango-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Nippon Industrial Rubber Co.; b. May 1884 at Fukuoka City; s of Satoru Okabe, council mem. Fukuoka city; m. in 1911. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Comm. Coll. 1905; took up official post at Sango-koshi Rubber Estates at Johore; resigned 1912; established Johore Rubber Plantation Co., Pres. till 1934 when company amalgamated into N.I.R.C. Address: 225 Sanyamachi, Yoyogi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor Lansi-hsien, Pinkiang Prov.; b. June 1904. Matsuyama; s. of late Okutaro Okada, soldier. Career: Chief Documents Sec. Civil Dept. Heilungkiang Prov.; Chief, Accounts Sec. Civil Dept. Pinkiang Prov. Address: Councillor's Residence, Lansi-hsien, Pinkiang Prov., Manchoukuo.

Pres. Yingchengtzu Colliery Co. & Seiseki Mining Co.; b. Mar 1887. Okayama-ken; s. of Isaburo Okada, farmer. Career: grad. Chuo Univ. 1918; Dir. Godo Tobacco Co., 1926-36; Mng.-Dir. Peipiao Colliery Co. 1933-35; Dir. Manshu Kogyo K.K. 1933-36. Address: 18 Tokiwa-cho 1-chome, Hsinking.

Dir. Antung Customs; b. 1898. Yamagata-ken. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; entered Chinese Customs; Non-Commissioned Staff, Dairen Customs 1932; Sec., Chief, same 1932-35; Dir. Chengteh Customs Jehol Prov. 1935-37. Address: Antung Customs, Manchoukuo.

Minister to Argentina since 1937; b. Apr. 1882, Yamagata-ken; s. of Kanenobu Okada, Official. Career: studied at Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. and Waseda Univ.; Commr. Foreign Office; 3rd Secr. Emb. London; 2nd Secr. Leg. Sweden; Consul Antung; Consul-Gen. Chientao; Consul-Gen. Honolulu 1932-34; Dir. Cultural Works Bureau. Address: Japanese Legation, Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Ex-Prime Minister; Retired Admiral; b. Jan. 1868. Fukui-ken; s. of Kitoda Okada. Career: grad. Naval Acad. 1889; Nav. Staff Coll.; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; Comdr., "Yaeyama" & "Asahi," Dir. Nav. Torpedo Sch.; Captain "Kasuga" & "Kashima," Chief Ordnance Dept. Sasebo Nav. Arsenal; Comdr. 1st Torpedo-flotilla 2nd. Sqn.; 3rd Torpedo-flotilla; Chief 2nd Sec. Nav. Tech. Dept.; Dir. Personnel Bureau of Navy; Dir. Sasebo Nav. Arsenal; Chief Nav. Tech. Dept.; Comdr.-in-Chief Combined Fleet & 1st Sqn.; Comdr.-in-Chief Yokosuka Naval Station; Navy Minister 1927; resigned 1929; Prime Minister 1934-36. Address: Tsunohazu, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Painter of Western Style; Court Artist; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; Mem. Imp. Academy of Arts; b. 1869, Tokyo; s. of Motooki Ishio; later adopted by Masazo Okada. Career: grad. Toyo Eiwa Gakko; studied oil painting under Kiyoteru Kuroda; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1896; studied in France 1897; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1902; went to Europe 1930. Address 96 Date-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Hokkaido Colonial Bank; since 1936; b. March 1885 in Shiga-ken; s. of Itsujiro Okada; m. Nobu, 1st d. of Suzaemon Baba. Career: elected Dir. Oriental Development Co. 1925; apptd. Financial Superintendent, Govt. Taiwan 1932. Address: Hokkaido Colonial Bank, Sapporo.

Gov. Hyogo-ken since 1936; b. Nov. 1886, Tokyo; s. of Ryuzo Kemi. Career: grad. English Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Commr. Shizuoka-ken & Aichi-ken; Secr. Reconstruction Bureau; Gov. Chiba-ken, Yamaguchi-ken & Nagano-ken; Dir. Local Affairs Bureau, Home Dept. 1935. Address: Governor's Residence, Kobe.

M.P.; b. Nov. 1878 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kimpei Okada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Gov. Saitama-ken, Nagano-ken and Kumamoto-ken; Dir. Police Bureau Home Dept.; elected to Diet from Okayama-ken; Dep.-Mayor of Tokyo; Vice-speaker House of Rep. 1936-37. Address: 31 Nagata-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Dir. Central Meteorol. Observatory & Imp. Marine Obs.; b. Aug. 1874, Chiba-ken; bro. of Kintaro Okada. Career: grad Physic. Course, Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; Expert Central Meteorol. Obs. 1894; Dir. Kobe Marine Meterol. Obs. 1920; Dir. Central Meteorol. Obs. 1920. Address: 2 Takehira-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Bank; Dir. Buzen Bank; Aud. Sumitomo Honsha Ltd., Nippon Sheet Glass Co.; b. Dec. 1883, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1906; joined Sumitomo Bank; Mgr. Shimonoseki, Nagoya, & Tokyo Branches. Address: 102 Nango-cho, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Vice-Chairman Nippon Central Sericultural Assn. since Jan. 1936; Pres. Weights and Measures Assn. of Japan; Dir. Trade Assn. of Tokyo; b. Sept. 1871, Osaka-fu; s. of Jotaro Okamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; apptd. official, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Dir. Forestry, Com. Affairs, Com. & Ind. and Agr. Bureaus; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Com.; Dir. Patent Bureau; attended 3rd Labor Conf. as Govt. Delegate. Address: 1613 Araijuku 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Yamaguchi Com. Coll.; b. Jan. 1881, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Jiroyemon Okamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1907; Dir. Mito Com. Sch. 1912; Chief Secr. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1915-1922; Dir. Wakayama Com. Coll. 1922-1932. Address: 2303 Shimmichi, Yamaguchi City.

Cartoonist; Guest Mem. Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; b. June 1886, Hakodate; s. of Takejiro Okamoto. Career: grad. Western Painting Dept. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1910; went to Europe 1929. Address: 3 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Cons.-Gen. Shanghai since May 1937; b. Aug. 1892, Kyoto-fu; s. of Buzaemon Okamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; service in Emb. London; Staff 1st Sec. Europe & Amer. Bureau; 2nd Secr. Emb. Wash.; Consul Seattle; Chief 2nd Sec. Europe & Amer. Bureau 1931-34; Dir. Finance Bureau 1934-36; Dir. Amer. Bureau 1937. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen. Shanghai.

b. Dec. 1883, Kyoto-fu; s. of Buzaemon Okamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Eleve-consul Shanghai 1910; Consul; 2nd Secr.; 1st Secr. Embassy England; Councillor Emb. Italy 1927; Min. to Iran. Address: c/o Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 2nd Div.; b. 1884, Tokyo; m. Chieko, sis. of Keiichi Kato of Aomori-ken. Career: Military Academy 1905, Mil. Staff Coll.; Adviser to Sun Chuan-fang; Chief, Mil. History Compiling Sec. Gen. Staff Office; Chief Mil. Research Dept.; Chief 2nd Dept. Gen. Staff Office; Vice-Chief Staff Kwantung Army. Address: 2nd Div. Hdqrs., Sendai.

Co. Dir.; b. Sept. 1870, Shigaken; s. of Shigai Okano; m. Tsuya, d. of Vice-Admiral N. Ogura. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Com. Sch.; joined Mitsui & Co.; Dir. Nagoya Weaving Mills Co., Toyoda Weaving Machinery Co., Dai-Nippon Colliery Co.; Pres. Yashu Mining Co., Koshiji Mining Co., Japan-China Spinning & Weaving Co., Int'l Wireless Telephone Co., Nichiran Trading Co. Address: 1 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku Tokyo.

Pres. Okaya & Co.; Nippon Savings Bank; Dir. Aichi Ginko, Aichi Tokei Denki K. K.; b. Aug. 1887, Nagoya; s. of Sosuke Okaya, Peer. Career: grad. Nagoya Com. Sch. 1906; inherited family estate 1926. Address: 50 Ebisu-machi, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

Adviser Kobe Chamber of Co. & Ind.; Chairman Kobe Bank Ltd.; Pres. Okazaki Steamship Co., Kobe Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Asahi Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Shinei Silk Co.; b. May 1884, Saga-ken; s. of Tadahide Ishimaru, later adopted by Tokichi Okazaki. Career. grad. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. 1906; Pres. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind. till Mar. 1937. Address: Mizuno-machi, Suma-ku, Kobe.

Viscount; D. Sc.; Pres. Chemical & Physical Research Institute; b. 1878, Tokyo; adopted s. of Nobuyoshi Okochi. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ 1903; rec'd deg. 1914; often elected Peer since 1915. Address: 1 Yanaka Shimizu-cho, Shitaya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. The Yokohama Specie Bank; b. Oct. 1878, Tokyo; s. of late Toshimichi Okubo, statesman. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; entered present bank 1903; Mgr. London Branch; Dir. 1926. Address: 11 Mukoyama-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Japan-German Cultural Society; Mem. Compiling Bureau of Historical Materials of Meiji Restoration; Dir. Japan Red Cross Society; b. Apr. 1866; s. of late Toshimichi Okubo, statesman. Career: grad. Yale Univ.; studied at Halle, Heidelberg and Berlin Univs.; Secr. to Home Minister 1896; Gov. Oita-ken, Tottori-ken and Osaka-fu, Address: 5 Minami-Iga-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem. House of Peers; Hon. Pres. Waseda Univ.; Advisor, Hochi Shimbun; Pres. Japan Civilization Society; Japan-Indian Assn.; b. Aug. 1871, Tokyo; adopted s. of late Marquis Shigenobu Okuma. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; studied in Cambridge Univ.; Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; Hon. Pres. Waseda Middle Sch.; Secr. to Prime Minister; M.P. 1915. Address: 115 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Daido Match Co.; Nippon Match Joint Sales Co.; Nippon Carb. Ind. Co.; Dir. Kyushu Elec-Transmission Co., Toyo Nitrogen Ind. Co., Manchou Chem. Ind. Co., Japan Gasoline Co.; b. Nov. 1879, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Hampei Okumura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; went to Europe & Amer. 1922. Address: 81 Sakuragaoka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Kochu Koshi since Dec. 1935; b. May 1894, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Toshichi Okumura. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; entered Research Dept. S. M. R.; Chief, Kirin & Peiping Offices, Research Sec. Tokyo Branch, Enterprising Sec. Address: c/o Kochu Koshi, Dairen.

Mgr. Calcutta Branch, Mitsubishi Trading Co.; b. 1892. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1915; joined present firm; went to Brazil as Mem. Japanese Economic Mission to Brazil 1935. Address: c/o Mitsubishi Trading Co., Calcutta, India.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; adviser, S. M. R. Co.; President of Manshu Immigration Association; b. July 1882, Tokyo; s. of Baron Heizo Okura, Lieut.-Gen. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; apptd. Engr., Ry. Dept.; joined S. M. R. Co.; Mgr. Traffic Dept., later Dir. & Mgr. Planning & Development Dept.; resigned 1931. Address: 1504 Yoyogi Tomigayacho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Pres. Okura-gumi; Chairman, Imperial Hotel; Dir. Locomotive & Car Mfg. Co., Nippon Elec. Battery Co., Imp. Theatre, Akita Timber Co.; b. June 1882; s. of late Kihachiro Okura, businessman. Address: 20 Shimoniban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers since 1931; b. Aug. 1883, Tokyo; s. of late Baron Shoichi Omori. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; official, Chiba-ken, Gunma-ken, Shiga-ken; apptd. Chief, Police Dept. Shiga-ken. Tochigi-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept. Iwate-ken, Yamagata-ken, Ibaraki-ken, Gunma-ken. successively; Gov. Gunma-ken and Shimane-ken; sent to Europe and America for study 1923; Parl. Vice-Minister of Home Affairs. Address: 235 Shuku-machi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Civil Affairs Bureau Justice Dept. since 1933; b. June 1887, Miye-ken; s. of late Yotaro Omori; m. Kinuko. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Judge Tokyo District Court; Councillor Justice Dept.; Repr. and Judge Mixed Arbitral Tribunal; stationed at London 1922-26; Judge Supreme Court; Lecturer Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. S. M. R. Co.; Chief Supervisory Dept. Kwantung Bureau; Chief Mil. Communications Supervisory Dept. Kwantung Army; b. Feb. 1872, Fukui-ken; s. of Sonoe Omura. Career: grad. Sapporo Agr. Sch. 1896; Engr. Hokkaido Colliery Co.; despatched to Europe & Siberia to investigate railways; Engr. Govt. Railways; Dir. Ry. Bureau Chosen Govt.-Gen. 1925; despatched to Siberia as Mem. Int'l Ry. Supervisory Comm. and to Peiping as Adviser of Chinese Govt. Address: S. M. R. Official Residence, Hoshigaura, Dairen.

M.D.; Prof. Psychiatry, Manchuria Medical Coll. since 1917; b. June 1885, Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Psychiatrical specialist. Address: c/o Manchuria Med. Coll., Mukden.

Lawyer; Co. Dir.; b. Nov. 1897, Okayama-ken; s. of Rikuta Ono, farmer; m. 1925. Career: grad. Law Coll. Chuo Univ. 1918; practised law 1920; edited law paper; came to Manchoukuo 1922; Mem. Dairen Muni. Assembly since 1924; Pres. Dairen Stock & Trust Co.; Dir. Nichiman Kogyo Co.; Dairen Girls' Senshu School; Manshu Hosei Gakuin; Antung Exchange; Aud. of Dairen Merchandise Exchange. Address: 12 Tajima-cho, Dairen.

Mng.-Dir. Fuji Minobu Ry. Co.; Pres. Toyo Recreation-Ground Co. Teikoku Mishin Co.; Dir. Hokkaido Godo Elec. Co.; b. Jan. 1879, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Hachizaemon Ono, landowner. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905. Address: 46 Nanpeidai-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Consul-Gen. for Bolivia and Hon. Consul for Guatemala at Yokohama; Pres. Ono Shoten, Ltd.; Dir. Teikoku Sericulture Warehouse Co., Yokohama Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Dai-Ichi Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; b. January 1890, Yokohama; s. of Mitsukage Ono. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1915; went to America and Canada to inspect com. and ind. Address: 4481 Oyado, Honmoku-machi, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Mng.-Dir. Toyo Fertilizer Co.; President of Rasa Industrial Co.; Dir. Nippon Smelting Co., Showa Gosei Kagaku Co.; b. Oct. 1880, Oita-ken; s. of Doun Ono, physician. Career: grad. Law Dept. Waseda Univ.; join Furukawa Gomei Kaisha. Address: 625 Kita-senzoku-cho, Omori-ku, Tokyo.
(See Terashima, Kozo).

n: ONOZUKA, Kiheiji 小野塚喜平次
t: D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Academy; b. Dec. 1870, Niigata-ken; s. of Heikichi Onozuka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial University 1895; went to Europe and America for study; apptd. Dean, Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. of same, 1928-34; rec'd deg. 1902. Address: 36 Kobinatadai-machi 2-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Okura & Co. (Mining) Ltd.; b. Mar. 1887 in Osaka-fu, s. of Komakichi Osaki, merchant; m. Chiyoko, d. of Kataro Ishikura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Comm. Sch. (present Univ. of Comm.). Address: 26 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dep. Mayor of Harbin; b. 1901, Kagoshima-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined S. M. R. 1925; apptd. Commr. Gen. Affairs Board Manchoukuo State Council 1932; Councillor Manchoukuo Legation Tokyo; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. State Highways Bureau 1933-36; Councillor Hsingan North Prov. 1936-37. Address: Muni. Office, Harbin.

Major-Gen.; Mil. Attache, Embassy, Germany since 1934; b. Apr. 1886, Nagoya; s. of late Lt.-Gen. Kenichi Oshima; m. Toyoko, d. of late Inejiro Tajiri. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1897; Mil. Staff Coll.; Assist. Mil. Attache, Emb. Germany; Staff, Artil. Inspectorate; Sec. Chief, Gen. Staff Office. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Berlin.

Mng.-Dir. Sumitomo Bank since 1932; b. Jan. 1887, Gunma-ken; s. of Naosaku Oshima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; entered present Bank; Vice-Chief, New York Branch; Chief, Foreign Dept. Head Office 1922; Mgr. 1925. Address: 1454 Shironomae, Mikage-machi, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Chief Dir. Imp. Educ. Assn.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. and Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sci.; b. Nov. 1880, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Masayoshi Oshima, landlord. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; Dir. Tokyo City Educ. Bureau; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Thought Problem Investigation Committee. Address: 52 Komagome Sendagi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Major-General (reserve); Gov. Mutankiang Prov.; b. 1884, Tokyo; s. of late Gen. Yoshimasa Oshima. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1905; Aide-de-Camp to the Emperor of Japan; Comdr. Inf. 16th Reg.; Chief Staff, 4th Div.; Comdr. Imp. Guards 2nd Brig. 1934-35; Dir. Police Bureau Civil Dept. 1936-37. Address: Mutankiang Prov. Office, Mutankiang, Manchoukuo.

D.E.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1882, Hyogo-ken; s. of Shoji Kurosawa, and later adopted by Rokuro Oshima. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; went to America to study Applied Chem. 1915; toured Europe and Amer. 1922; attended World Coal Conf. 1926; World Power Confr. Berlin 1920; same Wash. 1936. Address: 121 Yoyogi Sanya-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral; War Councillor; b. May 1876, Aichi-ken; s. of Tohei Osumi. Career: grad. Naval Academy, 1897; Secr. to Navy Minister; Captain "Asahi"; Embassy Attache in France; Comdr-in-Chief, 3rd Squadron; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr.-in-Chief, 2nd Sqn.; Navy Attache in France; Comdr.-in-Chief, 3rd Squadron; Min.; Supreme War Councillor; against Navy Min.; 1933-36. Address: 57 Shimo-Takanawa-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr.; Prof. Agr. Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. 1885, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Muraji Osugi. Career: grad. Agrl. Chem. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; studied in America 1916; rec'd deg. 1920; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1923. Address: 52 Jodoji Nishida-machi, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

D. Econ.; M.P.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Finance; b. Nov. 1886, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Mankichi Ota. Career: grad. Econ. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; joined Hochi Shimbun, 1919; apptd. Vice-Pres. of same; resigned 1928; sent to Diet, 1930, '32, '36; Parl. Councillor of Finance. Address: 2616 Sanno 1-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

President Osaka Electric Ry. Co., Godo Elec. Co.; Dir. Kokuto Ry. Co., Hanwa Elec. Ry. Co., Toyo Elec. Engrg. Works, Daido Elec. Power Co.; b. Oct. 1874, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Kageaki Ota. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; entered Ry. Dept.; resigned and entered business. Address: 3 Kori Tomoroki-mura, Kita-Kawachi-gun, Osaka-fu.

n: OTAGURO, Jugoro 太田黒重五郎
t: Pres. Kyushu Elec. Ry. Co., Kyushu Real Estate Co., Shinto Elec. Ind. Co., Nobeoka Elec. Co., Chikugo Elec. Co., Showa Elec. Light Co., Hakata Elec. Ry. Co.; Dir. Chuo Elec. Co.; Adviser, Kyushu Elec.-Transmission Co.; b. June 1866, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Tatsuo Komaki, later adopted by Korenobu Otaguro. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; Mgr. Osaka Com. Museum; entered Mitsui Bussan Kaisha 1894; Mng.-Dir. Shibaura Engrg. Works; Pres. Kyushu Hydro-Elec. Power Co. Address: 22 Higashiogi-machi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.
Farmer; b. Dec. 1876, Kyoto; s. of Koson Otani, priest; once married but his wife passed in Jan. 1911. Address: Yokujitsuso, Shusuishi, Dairen-shigai.

Minister of Overseas Affairs; Mem. House of Peers; b. Aug. 1886, Kyoto; s. of late Count Koson Otani; m. Yasuko, d. of Viscount Hidenobu Koide. Career: elected Peer 1931. Address: 57 Myogadani, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Shochiku K. K. (theatrical & cinema); b. Dec. 1877, Tokyo; s. of Eikichi Otani. Career: Adviser Kabuki-zu; Business Mgr. same; Pres. same; established Shochiku Theatrical Co. 1929. Address: 23 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

President of Manchoukuo Home Office; b. 1893, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. German Law Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; Commr. Home Dept.; Chief Police Affairs Dept. Fukuoka-ken 1931; Metro. Police Bd. 1932; Chief Home Dept. Nagasaki-ken 1932-34; Chief Econ. Dept. Kanagawa-ken 1935; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Civil Affairs Dept. 1936-37. Address: Home Office, Hsinking.

Rear-Adm. (reserve); Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Elec. Engrg. Co.; b. Feb. 1874, Hyogo-ken; s. of Mampei Ouchi. Career: grad. Naval Engrg. Coll.; Naval Staff Coll.; entered Navy Office; Chief Engr., Sasebo Naval Arsenal; Mgr. Kobe Works, Mitsubishi Elec. Engrg. Co. Address: 14 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

B. Lit.; Teacher; b. Jan. 1880, Louisiana, U.S.A.; s. of Samuel Smith Oxford. Career: grad. Daniel Baker Coll.; Eastman Sch. of Com.; taught at Daniel Baker Coll, Brownwood, Texas, 3 years; Inst. Ingles, Santiago, 2 years; Palmore Inst. Kobe, 25 years. Address: Palmore Institute, 23 Kitanagasa-dori 4-chome, Kobe.

Mayor of Shizuoka since 1935; b. Sept. 1870, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Ihei Ozaki. Career: grad. Shizuoka Middle Sch.; promoted to Captain in Mil. Service; elected M.P. 3 times since 1912; Mem. House of Peers 1925. Address: 60 Anzai-machi 3-chome, Shizuoka.

M.P.; b. Nov. 1859, Miye-ken; s. of Yukimasa Ozaki, samurai. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Editor Yubin Hochi Shimbun, Niigata Shimbun; Commr. Statistics Bureau; sent to Diet from Miye-ken 20 times since 1890; Councillor Foreign Office; Minister of Educ.; Minister of Justice; Mayor of Tokyo; made inspection tour of Europe after World War 1919; again went to Europe & Amer. 1931-33. Address: 1774 Hiro, Zushi-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

Wholesale Dealer in Woollen Goods and Upholstery; b. Mar. 1896, Tottori-ken; s. of Yotaro Ozawa, farmer. Career: engaged in present business since 1912. Address: 18 Awaji-machi 3-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

Vice-Dir. North Chosen Ry. Supt. Bureau, S. M. R.; b. Apr. 1888, Ishikawa-ken; s. of late Tokuhei Ozawa. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1911; joined present firm; Chief, Land Transportation Dept. Harbour Office 1919; went to Europe & America for study 1924; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. Anshan Iron Works 1926; Chief, Work Sec. Planning Dept. 1930; Chief, Harbour Sec. 1931. Address: 11 Hokeido, Seishin, Chosen.

Pres. Hanshin Iron Works, Kobe Gas Co., Amagasaki Gas Co., Kobe Elec. Mfg. Works, Velvet Soap Mfg. Co., Tokiwa Co. Ltd.; Dir. Sanyo Hide & Leather Mfg. Co., Japan-Brazil Colonization Co., Nippon Woollen Cloth Co., Oriental Hotel Ltd.; Maya Cable-way Co.; b. Apr. 1879, Kobe; s. of Kiichiro Ozone; m. Kiyo, sister of Tanehiko Yoshida. Career: became Kobe Muni. Councillor; Standing Mem. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 5 Sakuragi-cho 3-chome, Suma-ku, Kobe.

Mng.-Dir. & Chief Engr. Manshu Colliery Co. since 1934; b. Apr. 1893, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mining & Metallurgical Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1923; served at Fushun Coal Mines. Three Eastern Prov. Arsenal: Chief Engr. Sian Coal Mines; Councillor Hokang Coal Mines; Pres. Sian Colliery Co.; Adviser Mukden Agr. & Mining Office; Secr. of Manchoukuo Privy Council. Address: Hsinghua-kai Si Ssu-ma-lu, Hsinking.
Hon. Vice-Consul for Finland at Dairen; Merchant; b. Dec. 1888, Germany. Address: 212 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

Councillor Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept. since 1937; b. 1871, Manchuria. Career: Chief Home Affairs Dept. Chief Executive Office 1932-34; Privy Councillor 1934-37. Address: Imp. Household Dept. Hsinking.

Gov. Fengtien Prov. since 1934; b. Sept. 1892, Fengtien Prov.; s. of Pao Fu-jun. Career: grad. Mukden Mil. Acad. 1914; served Mukden Mil. Gov.'s Office; Chief Mil. Affairs Sec.; Mukden Mil. Provisions Dept. 1922; Spec. Committee Chinese Eastern Ry.; High Adviser Tung Sheng Spec. Dist. 1929; Vice-Min. of Civil Affairs 1932-34. Address: Gov.'s residence, Mukden.

M.D.; Medical Practioner; b. 1874, Ennenda, Glarus, Switzerland; n. Swiss; s. of Emil Paravicini, physician. Career: studied at Swiss Schools and Univ.; after receiving degrees in Switzerland, served as Asst. and Locumtenens at Univ.-Clinics and Hospitals of Basle, Berne, Zurich, Engadine, and German Hospital, London; P.-G. work in Germany, France, U.S.A.; in charge of Sanatorium near Zurich; practised in Switzerland and Milan; in Yokohama and Tokyo since 1905; Med. Officer to Brit. Emb. Tokyo 1921-28; visited prisoners' camps on behalf of Int'l Red Cross Committee during World War; delegate of same Committee at Red Cross Conf. 1926, 1934 and 1937 in Tokyo; Swiss Del. at World Educ. Conf. Tokyo 1937. Address: 772 Honmoku 3-chome, Yokohama.

American Vice-Consul at Dairen since 1937; b. July 1902, Newport, Rhode Island, U. S. A.; s. of Pierre Paul Pasquet; m. Suzanne Rambaut. Career: American Consulate General, Paris, 1925-31; vice-Consul, Paris, 1931-34; Glasgow, Scotland, 1934-37. Address: 35 Yanagi-machi, Dairen.
Teacher Fukushima Higher Com. Sch.; b. July 1892, Peking, China; s. of Po Jui-hsun. Address: 12 Seiyozan, Fukushima-shigai.

Danish Consul at Kobe & Osaka; b. 1876, Stourbridge, Worcestershire, England; s. of Horace Pearce, merchant. Career: grad. Hereford Coll. Herefordshire England; Fruit Farming in California 1894-98; served in Sale & Co. Yokohama 1899-1908; engaged in trade as Pres. "Pearce & Co." Yokohama 1908; removed to Kobe 1923; Danish Consul 1929. Address, (home) 66 Kitanocho 4-chome, Kobe. (Office) 92 Yedo-machi, Kobe.

M.A. (Univ. of San Francisco, Calif.); Bibliographer & Prof. of English; b. Jan. 1897, Windsor, Vermont, U.S.A.; s. of Karl W. Perkins; m. Ione Bendel. Career: for 15 years, business executive; Prof. of English Daisan Koto Gakko since 1935; Co-founder and first research fellow of "Soc. for Oriental Studies" of San Francisco, Calif. Address: Sanko Kansha, Kyoto.

H. B. M. Cons.-Gen. Seoul Korea since Feb. 1935; b. June 1882; s. of Eccleston A. E. Phipps; m. Aline M. Purvis. Career: apptd. Student Interpreter in Japan Oct. 1903; H. B. M. Vice-Cons. Tokyo 1915; Cons. Tamsui 1920; Honolulu 1925; Kobe 1932. Address: Brit. Consulate-General Keijo Chosen.

Major-General; C.B., D.S.O.; British Military Attache in Tokyo 1921-26 and since 1936; b. Mar. 1880 in London; s. of Sir Francis T. Piggott, barrister-at-law; one time legal adviser to Prime Minister Ito of Japan 1888-91; later attorney-gen. of Mauritius; chief justice of Hongkong; m. Jane Smith. Career: educ. at Cheltenham Coll., Royal Military Acad., Woolwich; Captain 1911; Major 1916; Colonel 1923; Major-Gen. 1935; served in Great War; General Staff, War Office London 1914, 1920-21, 1927-30; Deputy Mil. Secr. to Sec. of State for War 1930-35. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo.

Prof. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; Hon. Consul for Portugal at Tokyo; b. Nov. 1893, Cabanas, Conselho do Carregal do Sal. Portugal; s. of F. do Nascimento Pinto, army officer; m. Tsurue (Japanese). Career: Instituto Superior de Agronomia de Lisboa. Address: 32 Honcho-dori 5-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. phil et dipl. ès Lettres; Prof. Lecturer of Yamaguchi Higher Sch. & Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch.; b. Nov. 1896, Ohlau, Germany; s. of Prof. Dr. Karl Preibisch. Career: graduate of Magdeburg Coll.; Captain of German Army 1914-19; studied Philosophy and Roman Philology at Halle and Muenster, Siena (Italy), Sevilla (Spain), Paris et Besancon (France); Governor of Princes of Hessia; Prof. of High Schools; German Coll. at Athens (Greece). Address: Koto Gakko Kansha, Itoyone, Yamaguchi City.

B.A.; M.A.; Writer; b. 1887 in Canada; s. of Albert M. Price; m. Mary Virginia Selden. Career: grad. Western Res. Univ.; post grad. Columbia Univ., New York Univ.; editorial staff The Survey; editor World Outlook, etc.; studied Indian labour question in S. America; War reconstruction service in France, Italy; dir. motion picture expedition, Sahara desert; ethnographic studies of Battaks of Sumatra etc.; author "Ancient Peoples at New Tasks," "The Negro Round the World," "Study of American Influence in the Orient," "Japan's New Horizons" etc. Address: 2132 Isshiki, Hayama, Japan.
Pres. Rud. Ratjen & Co. Tokyo, Osaka, Dairen; b. Mar. 1881 at Hoya, Germany. Arrived in Japan 1903; founded own firm 1913. Address: 6-34, Aoyama Kita-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Counsellor U.S.S.R. Emb. Tokyo; b. 1897, Moscow; s. of Jacob Rayvid. Career: Attaché to Emb. Berlin 1925; 2nd Secr. same 1926-28; Asst.-Dir. 2nd Western Dept. Foreign Office Moscow 1928-30; Counsellor, Legation, Sweden 1930-31; Dir. 1st Western Dept. Foreign Office, Moscow. Address: U.S.S.R. Embassy, Tokyo.

M.A., Balliol College (Oxon), M.A. (London); Chev. of the Corona d'Italia; O.B.E.; Prof. of English Language and Literature, Taihoku Imp. Univ.; Royal Italian Consular Agent, Taihoku; b. Jan. 1892, Florence, Italy; s. of Pietro del Re, Capt. Italian Army, retired; m. H. Joan George. Career: Priv. Sec. to Italian Mil. Attaché, London 1916-19; Lecturer in Italian, Univ. of Oxford and King's Coll. London 1920-27; Prof. of Eng. Lit. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1927-30. Address: c/o Taihoku Imp. Univ., Taihoku.

B.D. (Yale Univ. 1926); A.M. (Univ. of Chicago 1933); Ph. D. 1937; Prof. Kwansai Gakuin Literary Coll. and Literary-Law Univ. since 1934; b. Aug. 1899, Sheldon, Missouri, U.S.A.; s of J. J. Reed, Christian minister; m. Josephine L. Reed. Career: arrived Japan 1921; Teacher Himeji and Tatsuno Middle Schs. 1921-23; Pastor First M. E. Church Yalesville Conn. 1925-26; Teacher & Dean Palmore Inst. Kobe 1926-31; author of "Facing Our Social World, 1929". Address: Kwansai Gakuin, Nishinomiya-shigai, Hyogo-ken.

Hon. Japanese Consul at Amsterdam; b. May 1898 at Amsterdam; m. Anna Maria Heldring. Career: grad. High Economic School 1917; visited Japan 1920; Secr. to Mgr. Nederland Royal Mail Line (Java Line) 1921; Second visit to Japan 1922; Secr. Head Office, same at Batavia 1923-25; Mem. of Hofmann, Schoffer & Co. in Holland 1930; Mem. Amsterdam Chamber of Com. 1931; connected with Holland-Steamship Co. since 1937. Address: Keizersgracht 517, Amsterdam.

B.A.; M.A.; L.H.D.; D.D.; Pres. Rikkyo Daigaku since 1912; Bishop and Educator; b. Nov. 1875, Frederick, Maryland, U. S. A.; n. American; s. of Charles David Reifsnider, railroad man. Career: grad. Kenyon Coll. and Bexley Theological Seminary; ordained Deacon 1900; Priest 1901; Rector, Christ Church, Hudson, Ohio 1900-01; Missionary to Japan since 1901; at Nara 1902-03; Fukui 1903-12; consecrated Bishop 1924. Address: Rikkyo Daigaku, Ikebukuro, Tokyo.

B.A.; M.A.; D.D.; LL.D.; Missionary & Educator; b. Sept. 1879, Jonesboro, Ill., U. S. A.; s. of Robert Reischauer; m. Helen Sidwell Oldfather. Career: grad. Hanover Coll.; Presb. Theol. Sem. Chicago; Grad. work at Univ. of Chicago and Union Theol. Sem. New York; Prof. Meiji Gakuin 1905-30; Nihon Shin Gakko 1930; Co-founder & Executive Secr. of Tokyo Joshi Daigaku 1917; lectured on Buddhism at various univs. in U. S. A.; Delegate Int'l Missionary Conf. Jerusalem 1928; author of "Studies in Japanese Buddhism," etc. Address: Tokyo Joshi Daigaku, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

B.A.; Ordained missionary; b. Nov. 1866, Toronto, Canada; s. of William Rennie. Career: grad. Toronto Univ. 1906; Christian ministry, Calgary 1906; Teacher, middle sch. etc. Hakodate 1906-12; independent missionary, Hakodate for 31 years. Address: 37 Hitomi-cho, Hakodate, Hokkaido.
French Consul at Harbin; b. Apr. 1884, Paris. Career: French Consular Service in the Far East for 29 years. Address: French Consulate, 11 Tsitsiharskaya St. Harbin.

Governor Chientao Prov.; b. in Chosen. Career: served Chosen Govt. for 30 years; Gov. Chuseinando Prov.; Mem. The Central Council of Chosen; present post since Sept. 1937. Address: Chientao Prov. Office, Chientao, Manchoukuo.

Pres. Taisei Fire & Marine Ins. Co. since 1925; b. Mar. 1897; bro. of Yucho Rin. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. and Econ. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1923; made inspection tour of Europe and America 1929. Address: 4 Onari-machi 3-chome, Taihoku City, Taiwan. (Tokyo home) 19 Shimo-Rokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; Barrister-at-law; b. Jan. 1868, London; s. of Sir John R. Robinson, editor & mgr. of The Daily News; m. Alice Maud Curtis of Harwich, England. Career: Westminster School, Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar 1896; practised 20 years patent law; came to Japan 1922 to Saga High Sch.; lectured 8 years Law & Lit. at Kyushu Imp. Univ. Address: Nishi Shirage Koji, Saga City.

n: RODRIGUEZ Y Jimenez de Acevedo, Carlos de
t: Ph, G.; C.a.L.; R.P.D.; Venezuelan Cons.-General in Japan since 1931; b. Aug. 1899, Upata Dto-Piar Bolivar-State, Venezuela, S. Am.; s. of Antonio Rodriguez, businessman; m. Carmen Herminia Delgado Perez. Career: Grad. Phar. Sch. Caracas 1921; Secr. Venezuela's 1st Criminal Court; Grad. Course at Law before supreme court of Venez. 1924; grad. Dr. of Polit. Sci. Central Univ. of Venez. 1924; Gen.-Mgr. Gen. Syndicate of Mica Bolivar State 1925-26; Prac. Lawyer 1926; Judge 1st Crim. Court; 1st Civil Ct.; Sup. Ct. 1927; Dir. Polit. & Adm. Dept. of Bol. Sta. 1928-30; Gen. Secr. a.i. of same Govt. 1930-31; Ven. Del. 15th Intl. Red Cross Conf. Tokyo 1935; 7th Educ. Intl. Conf. Tokyo 1937; author of "Venezuela" 1933 Tokyo and "Asia America." Club: American Club Tokyo. Address: 664 Marunouchi Bldg. Tokyo; P. O. Box 604 Central Tokyo; 20 Yamate-cho, Yokohama.

Charge d'Affaires of Colombia since 1937; b. Aug. 1898 at Bogota, Colombia; s. of Alberto Borda Tanco, former rector of the Tech. Univ. of Bogota; Hon. Prof. of Univ. of Colombia; Mem. Colombian Acad. of Sciences; m. Suzanne Weiprecht. Career: studied Civil Engrg. Nat. Univ. of Bogota; Secr. Comm. Attache, Paris, 1918-30; Dir. Gen. of Public Educ. for Bogota and Cundinamarca, 1930-33; Mem. Colombian Acad. of Educ.; 1st Secr. Colombian Leg. in Ecuador, 1933; Charge d'Affaires ad-interim to Ecuador, 1934-36; Comm. Orden del Merito of Ecuador. Address: Yusen Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Polish Minister to Japan since 1937; b. Dec. 1894; s. of Bronislaw Romer, prop. of land estate; married. Career: grad. Univ. Lausanne, Switzerland; 1st Secr. Embassy Paris 1919-21; assigned to Foreign Office Warsaw 1921: acting chief, Western Sec. 1923-25; chief of same, 1925-27; counsellor Embassy, Rome 1928-34; minister to Portugal, 1935-37. Address: 9 Mita Tsuna-machi, Tokyo.

Acting Netherlands Consul-General in Kobe since 1934: Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau; b. Feb. 1895 at Wageningen, Netherlands. Career: educ. course of Oriental studies, Univ. of Leyden; apptd. student-interpreter 1921; arrived in Japan 1921; 1st class interpreter 1926. Address: Meikai Bldg. 32 Akashi-machi, Kobe.
Dipl. Ing.; Engr.; b. Feb. 1894, Aachen, Germany. Address: 907 Magome-machi 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.
Hon. Consul for Estonia at Dairen; b. 1888, Estonia. Address: 54 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

L.D.; Acting Minister to Greece; b. Oct. 1888, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Shigeaki Horiuchi; later adopted by Kunitaro Saegusa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; entered Finance Office; Chief, Shimokyo Taxation Office; Commr. Tsingtao Garrison Civil Adm. Office 1915; Mem. of Suite, Japanese Delagation to 1st & 6th League of Nations Assemblies; 1st Secr. Legation, Stockholm; Chief, 1st & 2nd Secs. Cultural Work Dept. Foreign Office. Address: Japanese Legation, Athens, Greece.

Traffic Mgr. Gen. Direction of Rys. S.M.R.; b. Nov. 1889, Kobe; s. of Shigenori Sato; later adopted by Sahara family. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; entered Ry. Dept.; Councillor Ry. Bureau; Ry. Inspector; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Traffic Bureau; Secr. to Ry. Minister; Dir. Board of Tourist Ind. 1932-34; Dir. Harbin Ry. Adm. Bureau 1934-36. Address: c/o Yamato Hotel, Mukden.

Prof. Kobe Foreign Lang. Sch.; Lecturer on Indian. Asiatic & Int'l Problems; Editor, the "Voice of India;" Corr. Indian Journals; Hon. Gen.-Secr. Indian Trade Assn. Kobe; Organizer & Pres. Indian Nat. Cong. Committee of Japan, Indo-Japanese Young Peoples' Assn.; b. Sept. 1898, Bhagalpore, India; s. of Lal Mohan Sahay, landlord. Career: studied at Medical Sch.; gave up study to join struggle for Indian Independence 1920; worked 3 years under Indian Nat. Congress; arrived in Japan 1923; organized Japan Branch of Indian Nat. Congress 1928; Indo-Japanese Young Peoples' Assn. 1934. Address: 728/25 Shimosandanda, Uozaki-cho, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Poet; Prof. French Litt. Waseda Univ.; b. Jan. 1892, Tokyo; s. of Jubei Saijo, soap mfg. Career: grad. Litt. Course, Waseda Univ.; studied at Japanese Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to Europe by Waseda Univ. to study at Paris and Sorbonne Univs. 1924-26; then travelled to England and Italy; author of "Gold Dust," "Unacquainted Lover," "Beautiful Forfeiture," "Collection of Folk Songs," etc. Address: 377 Kashiwagi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Chief, Sanatorium, South Manchuria Railway Co. Dairen; b. April 1900 at Matsuyama; younger brother of Tadasu Saiki, Dir. Japanese Govt. Institute for Nutrition, Tokyo. m. Shigeko, d. of Takinosuke Amano. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1924; Dr. Kyoto Imp. Univ. Hospital; studied medicine under Prof. Thanhause and Prof. Stepp at Freiburg and Munich. Address: 43-11, Hoshigaura, Dairen.

Prince; Genro; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1849, Kyoto; s. of late Kimizumi Tokudaiji and later adopted by Morosue Saionji. Career: studied Law and Politics in France 1870-1880; published Tokyo Jiyu Shimbun 1880; went to Europe and America with late Prince Ito to investigate Parl. System 1882; Minister to Austria 1885; to Germany 1887; Grand Chancellor, Imp. Orders 1891-94; Vice-pres. House of Peers 1894; Privy Councillor 1894; Min. of Educ. 1894 and 1898; Foreign Min. 1895 and 1896; Finance Min. and Premier 1901; Pres. Seiyukai 1903; formed cabinet 1903 and 1911; Chief Delegate to World Peace Conf. 1919. Address: 5 Minami Kogacho, Surugadai, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Amb. to U.S.A. concurrently Min. to Cuba since 1934; b. Dec. 1886, Niigata-ken; s. of Shozaburo Saito. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Attaché, Wash. 1910; 3rd Secr. Emb. London 1918; Mem. of Suite, Delegation to Peace Conf. Paris 1919; 2nd Secr. Emb. London; attended 1st League of Nations Assembly Geneva 1920; Consul Seattle 1921; Consul-Gen. New York 1923; Dir. Information Bureau Foreign Office 1929; Councillor Emb. London 1930; Min. to Netherlands. Address: Japanese Embasssy, Washington, U.S.A.

Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Lecturer Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sci.; b. Feb. 1867, Iwate-ken; s. of Yonoshin Saito, scholar. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1888; Prof. of Alma Mater 1909; sent to Europe & Amer. 1909-11. Publications: "Geschichte Japans" etc. Address: 107 Hakusan Goten-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Yasuda Bank; Dir. Yasuda Trust Co.; b. Jan. 1878, Ehime-ken; s. of Yasuichiro Tomita; later adopted by Koji Saito. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Yasuda Hozen-sha; Vice-Chief Yokohama Branch 3rd Bank 1908; Chief Investigation Sec.; Mgr. Kyoto Bank 1909; again entered 3rd Bank 1914; Chief Osaka & Yokohama Branches; Vice-Mgr. Head Office 1922; went abroad for observation 1922-23; Chief Kofunacho & Kobe Branch Yasuda Bk. 1923-24; Asst. Gen. Mgr. Head Office 1925; Dir. 1927; Dir. Yasuda Trust Co. 1931. Address: 15 Nagazumi-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Gen.-Dir. North Chosen Ry. Direction of S.M.R.; b. June 1881, Yamagata-ken. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Course, Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1905; joined Ry. Dept., later S. M. R. Co.; Ry. Engr. Tsingtao Garrison; Engr. Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Chief Construction Sec., Ry. Bureau of Chosen; Engr. S.M.R. Co. 1933. Address: 11 Hokodo, Seishin, Chosen.

Chief Civil Engrg. Dept. Nippon Elec. Power Co.; Dir. Inaba Hydro-Elec. Co., Nippon Takugyo K. K.; b. Feb. 1887, Kochi-ken; s. of Risei Saito; m. Tomo. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Engr. Miyagi-ken; Chief Engr. Ominato Ind. Co.; Etchu Elec. Power Co.; Chief Designer Nippon Elec. Power Co.; Chief Kurobe Office. Address: 3 of 125 Shimochujo, Ibaraki-cho, Mishima-gun, Osaka-fu.

D.L.; Non-Commissioned Officer, Foreign Office; Adviser of South Manchuria Railway Company; b. November 1880; s. of Ryojun Saito. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Consul Foochow; Secr. Foreign Office; 2nd Secr. Emb.; Dir. Com. Bureau; Dir. S.M.R. Co. Address: 42 Shoto, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Gen.-Secr. Nat. Committee of Y.M.C.A. in Japan; Advisor to United Council Y.M.C.A. Manchuria; b. July 1886, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Isamu Saito. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Prof. 5th Higher Sch. 1911-17; Executive Secr. Inst. of Pacific Relations 1925-32; attended Y.M.C.A. World Conf. Mysore India 1937. Address: 62 Hayashi-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Aug. 1870, Hyogo-ken; s. of Hachiroemon Saito. Career: grad. Waseda Univ.; Yale Univ. 1904; joined the bar 1895; sent to Diet from Hyogo-ken 9 times since 1912; Parl Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; attended Int'l Parl. Conf. 1913; Dir. Legislation Bureau; Parl. Vice-Min. of Home Affairs 1932-34. Address: 315 Kitashinagawa 3-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Gunma Daido Bank; b. July 1878, Gunma-ken; s. of Matsugoro Saito, landowner. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; joined Bank of Japan 1905; Acting Business Mgr. of same; Mng.-Dir. Yokohama Credit Bank 1921-31. Address: 150 Takinoue, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Pres. Yonago Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. July 1883, Tottori-ken; s. of Toyojiro Inouye, later adopted by Heibei Sakaguchi. Career: grad. Law Dept. Waseda Univ. 1906; Chairman Yonago Muni. Assembly 1926-35; Dir. Hiroshima Elec. Co. and several other companies. Address: 29 Nishi-cho, Yonago City.

Mng.-Dir. Chosen Ry. Hotel; b. May 1882; s. of Korehae Sakai. Career: grad. English Course, Central Training Inst. of Railway Dept.; engaged in Hotel Business since 1911; Supervisor, Sanyo Hotel, Shimonoseki; Sawabumi Hotel, Kyoto; Station Hotel Shingishu; Fuzan Station Hotel;; Heijo Ry.
