Hotel; sent to U. S. A. to study hotel business for a year and practised at Hotel Ambassador, Pennsylvania and at other big hotels; Supervisor, Chosen Hotel, Keijo, 1927. Address: 87 Hasegawa-machi, Keijo.

Chief Adm. & Traffic Depts. Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Ry.; Councillor, S.M.R.; b. 1885, Gifu-ken. Career: grad. Chinese Language Dept., Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. 1908; entered S.M.R.; Chief Secretariat, Ry Dept.; Coucillor, same; Vice-Dir. Tsitsihar Direction of State Ry.; present post since Jan. 1936. Address: Gen. Direction of State Ry., Mukden.

Count; Mem. House of Peers; Dir. Daito Bunka Kyokai; b. 1893; adopted by Count Tadaoki Sakai. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; apptd. Secr. to Justice Minister and Ry. Minister; elected Peer 1923; travelled abroad 1929. Address: 12 Haramachi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha, Sanshin Bldg. Co.; b. June 1868, Aichi-ken; s. of late Hisashi Sakai. Career: grad. Rikkyo Univ.; Harvard Univ.; Secr. to Foreign Min.; Secr. to Premier; joined Mitsui Firm 1914. Address: 20 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Civil Engrg. and Bldg. Contractor; b. 1882, Hiroshima-ken. Career. grad. Tokyo Engrg. Sch. 1909; engaged in Chikwanshan Tunnel Work 1909-1911; Ssupingkai-Changchiatun Ry. Work 1916-17, established Anshan Steel Works foundation 1917-18; established Sakakiya Corp. 1921 and contracted various civil works as contractor of S.M.R. Co.; Chairman, Japan-Manchoukuo Civil Engrg. & Bldg. Assn. Address: 15 Noto-machi, Dairen.

Mayor of Osaka; b. Apr. 1886, Kanagawa-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; Chief, Police Dept. Toyama-ken; Chief, Home Dept. Kagawa-ken, Hyogo-ken; Gov. Kochi-ken; Dep. Mayor of Osaka. Address; Yamasumi, Ashiya, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Publisher: b. Mar. 1866, Kochi-ken; s. of Kihachi Sakamoto. Career: came to Tokyo in 1883; educated by Azusa Ono, who participated in founding Waseda Univ.; was charged with business of Toyokan Pub. Office under A. Ono; founded Fuzanbo 1886; Published 4,000 kinds of books including "Geog. Dict. of Japan," "Nat. Encyc." "Dai-Genkai." Address: Daibutsudani, Kamakura.

Chief Foreign Affairs Dept. of Taiwan; b. June 1894, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Momojiro Sakamoto, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; apptd. Secr. Embassy, U.S.A.; Consul, Buenos Aires; Consul at Amoy; Chief, 3rd Sec. Com. Bureau, Foreign Office 1923-33; Chief 2nd Sec. Amer. Bureau. Address: c/o Taiwan Sotokufu, Taihoku.

b. Oct. 1886, Osaka; s. of Genryo Sakamoto, M.D. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; joined Sumitomo Goshi Kaisha; Gen.-Mgr. Sumitomo Life Ins. Co. 1925. Mng.-Dir. same. Address: 1046 Tennoji-machi, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Resources Deliberation Committee; b. Oct. 1858, Nagano-ken s. of Daizo Sakamoto. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1882; apptd. Secr. to Navy Minister; Adjutant H. M. S. "Hiyei" and "Yoshino"; Staff Nav. Affairs Bureau Navy Office; Head Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; fought in Russo-Japanese War; Vice-Admiral 1898; ennobled 1907. Address: 32 Ichigaya Kora-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Chugoku Godo Elec. Co., Tottori Elec. Light Co., Katagami Ry. Co.; b. Nov. 1873, Okayama-ken; s. of late Hanjiro Sakano; m. Kiyono (deceased). Career: grad. Law College Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1898; entered government service 1899; Dir. Osaka Supt. Bureau, Dept. of Communications, 1910; Dir. Western Supt. Bureau of same 1913; retired 1915; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Elec. Light Co. 1915-18. Address: 1171 Kunotsubo, Ashia, Hyogo-ken.

Pres. Hanshin-Kokudo Bus Co.; Dir. Hanshin Harbour Co., Amagasaki Harbour Co.; Chief Dir. Osaka Econ. Soc.; Dir. Osaka Club; Mem. Intl. Sightseeing Committee; Statistical Committee of Dept. of Com. & Ind.; b. Dec. 1879, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Masaharu Sakata. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Gov. Ehime-ken, Kagawa-ken; Mayor of Takamatsu; Dir. Osaka Godo Spinning Co. Address: Mikage-machi, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Dir. S.M.R. Co.; b. 1892, Tokyo; s. of Baron Yoshiro Sakatani. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; entered Bank of Japan; Chief Finance Sec. Kwantung Govt.; Acting Dir. Colonial Bureau, Overseas Dept.; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Manchoukuo Finance Dept. 1932; Vice-Dir.-Gen. Gen. Affairs Boards, State Council 1932-35; Aud. Central Bank of Manchou. Address: c/o S.M.R Co., Dairen.

Baron; D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Adviser Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Pres. Central Statistics Committee, Senshu Univ., "Mikasa" Preserv. Soc., Imp. Aviation Soc., Gakushi-kai, Imp. Invention Assn.; Mem. Educ. Council; Dir. Saisei-kai, Tokyo Bay Reclamation Co., Hakone Hot Spring Supply Co., Asano Cement Co., Amagasaki Harbour Co., Oki Elec. Co., Iwaki Colliery Co., Sengokuhara Real Estate Co.; b. Jan. 1863, Okayama-ken; s. of late Roro Sakatani, scholar. Career. grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1884; entered Finance Dept.; Vice-Minister of Finance 1901; Fin. Min. 1906-08; Mayor of Tokyo 1912-15; attended Int'l Statis. Assn. Conf., World Econ. Conf. Switz., Allies Econ. Conf. etc. Address: 126 Hara-mati. Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt. Chief Research Dept. Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; b. Mar. 1887. Career: grad. Litt. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1910; joined Asahi Shimbun-sha 1913; toured Europe 1921-23; Lecturer Waseda Univ. since 1924. Address: 201 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Ambassador to Poland since 1937; b. February 1887. Kagoshima; s. of Jutaro Sakoh, businessman. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1911; Secr. Foreign Office; Chief, 2nd Section, Com. Bureau; Consul-Gen. Calcutta 1930; Councillor, Embassy, Moscow; Minister to Finland 1936. Address: Japanese Embassy, Warsaw, Poland.

M.P.; Lawyer; b. May 1887, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Ikujiro Sakuda, farmer. Career: grad Chuo Univ. 1915; elected M.P. 5 times since 1928; Parl. Councillor of Educ. 1936. Address: Kugenuma, Fujisawa-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

Int'l Committee of Kojunsha; Dir. Tokyo Econ. Assn.; b. Aug. 1867; s. of late Tikayoshi Sakurada. Career: studied at Doninsha of Keiu Nakamura; went to Holland & Belgium; studied Econ. & Law at Senshu Gakko; at Freiburg Univ. in Baden and Dijons Univ.; Litt. & Phil. at Brussels Univ.; Econ. & Law at Liege Univ. Belgium; joined Bank of Japan 1897. Address: 410 Daita 1-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Aug. 1880, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Genji Sakurai. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. 1911; elected M.P. 8 times; Parl. Vice-Min. of Overseas Affairs 1934-36. Address: 230 Higashi Osaki 4-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. LL.D.; Privy Councillor; Pres. Imp. Acad.; b. Aug. 1858, Kanazawa; s. of Jintaro Sakurai. Career: entered Daigaku Nanko 1871; studied Chemistry at Kaisei Gakko 1874-76; Univ. Coll. London 1876-81; Prof. Chemistry Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1882-1917; elected Mem. Imp. Acad. 1898; Mem. Nat. Research Council 1920; Mem. House of Peers 1920; Privy Councillor 1926; Pres. 3rd Pan-Pacific Sci. Congress 1926; Hon. Mem. Chem. Soc. of France 1923; Soc. of Chem. Ind. London 1923; Royal Inst. of Great Britain 1925; Amer. Chem. Soc. 1926; Acad. of Sci. of U.S.S.R. 1927; Chem. Soc. of Poland 1929; of London 1931; Delegate to Celebration of 9th. Jubilee, Foundation of Glasgow Univ. 1901, and to various int'l conf. at London 1907, Rome 1910. London and Paris 1922, Melbourne and Sydney 1923, Brussels 1928, Hague 1928, London 1937. Address: 3 Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Leader, Minseito; Pres. Izumo Elec. Power Co.; b. Aug. 1880, Shimane-ken; s. of Waichiro Sakurauchi. Career: studied at Waseda Univ.; Corr., Gifu & Aichi Shimbun; entered business 1903; elected M.P. 6 times since 1920; Minister of Com. & Ind. Apr.-Dec. 1931. Address: 34 Mita Matsuzaka-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Merchant; Chairman Sale & Co. Ltd. Tokyo; Chairman Sale Tilney & Co. Ltd. London; b. Oct. 1896 in Japan; s. of Charles Vincent Sale, merchant. Career: Mem. British Delegation to Int'l Pacific Relations Conf. at Kyoto 1929; Major commanding Middlessex Yeomanry (Territorial Army). Address: Sale & Co. Ltd. 14 Marunouchi 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo; Sale Tilney & Co. Ltd. 3 Lloyd's Avenue, London, E. C. 3.

Dir. Hypothec Bank of Japan; b. Dec. 1879, Tokyo; s. of Shotaro Ota; later adopted by Mitsu Sano. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; entered Finance Dept.; Secr., same; Chief, Provisional Building Sec.; Chief Bank Inspector 1930; Dir. Monopoly Bureau 1934. Address: [?]04 Shimo-ochiai 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Dean, Engrg. Dept. Nihon Univ.; b. Apr. 1880, Yamagata-ken; adopted s. of Seiichiro Sano, educator. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; apptd. Asst. Prof. 1906 and Prof. 1917, same studied in Europe & America 1911-14; Engr. Imp. Household Dept. & Finance Dept.; Dir. Tokyo Reconstruction Office; Pres. Tokyo City Building Bureau; Dean, Engrg. Dept. Nihon Univ. 1929; Adviser, Manchoukuo Capital Construction Bureau 1933. Address: 160 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Rear-Adm. (reserve); Dir. Japan Red Cross Soc.; b. July 1871; s. of late Count Tsunetami Sano. Career: Attache, Embassy Germany; Captain "Haruna," fought in Russo-Japanese War. Address: 2995 Magome-machi Nishi 4-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. (Cambridge); Clergyman; b. Jan. 1905, Streatham, London; s. of Cyril J. Sansbury; m. Ethelreda Wamsley. Career: grad. Peterhouse, Cambridge 1927; ordained Deacon 1928; Priest 1929; Curate of St. Peter's, Dulwich Common, London 1928-31; of Wimbledon 1931-32; S.P.G. Missionary at Numazu 1932-34; Prof. Central Theol. Coll. Ikebukuro, and Chaplain to British Community, S. Andrew's, Tokyo since 1934. Address: Seikokai Shingakuin, 1612 Ikebukuro, Tokyo.

K.C.M.G.; Com. Counsellor, British Embassy; b. Nov. 1883, London; n. British; s. of G. W. M. Sansom. Career, studied in France and Germany; entered consular service in Japan 1903; author of Historical Grammar of Japanese, Oxford Press 1928; "Japan. A Short Cultural History." Cresset Press, London 1931. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo.

Mayor of Nagasaki since 1934; b. Oct. 1885, Niigata-ken; s. of Kisaburo Sasai. Career: grad. Polit. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Commr. Wakayama-ken; Police Chief, Saga-ken; Chief, Peace Preservation Dept. Metropolitan Police Board; Chief, Accounts Dept. Reconstruction Bureau 1924; Gov. Nara-ken 1929; Ehime-ken 1930-32. Address: 118 Baba-machi, Nagasaki.

Pres. Yamaguchi Goshi Kaisha since 1934; Chairman Nippon Life Assurance Co., Kyodo Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. 110th Bank, Osaka Savings Bank, Sanwa Bank, Kansai Trust Co., Dainippon Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Toyo Linoleum Co.; Aud. Hotel New Osaka b. July 1873, Akita-ken; s. of Taemon Sasaki; later adopted by Fukuzo Sasaki. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. 1898; entered Yamaguchi Bank; Mng.-Dir. same. Address: 188 Kunotsubo, Sanjo, Seido-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

D.L.; Pres. Ritsumeikan Univ.; b. Mar. 1878; s. of Sozaburo Sasaki, Tottori-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1903; Asst. Prof. same Univ. 1906; went to Germany, France and England for study of adm. law 1909; Dean, Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; resigned Aug. 1933. Address: 1 Shimogamo Izumi-machi, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Major-Gen.; Comdr. Inf. 30th Brig. 16th Div.; b. 1886, Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1907; Mil. Attache Legation China Comdr. Inf. 18th Reg.; Chief Staff 9th Div.; Supreme Mil. Adviser of Manchoukuo. Address: 30th Brig. Hdqrs. Tsu City.

Mng.-Dir. Furukawa Mining Co., Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; b. Dec. 1881, Tokyo; s. of Naotsuna Sasaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; Chief, Gen. Affairs Sec.; Chief, Financial Sec. Furukawa Mining Co.; Dir. & Chief of Ashio Mining Office, same. Address: 270 Minami-Shinagawa, 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Toho Artificial Fibre Co.; Auditor, East Manchuria Rayon Pulp Co.; b. Aug. 1887 in Yamaguchi-ken. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Comm. Sch. (present Kobe Univ. of Commerce), 1908; Mgr., London Branch Bank of Taiwan; Mgr., Business Dep't.; Tokyo Branch, same; Dir., Suzuki Shoten; Teikoku Rayon Co. Address: 429, Kashiwagi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Vice-pres. House of Peers; b. July 1893, Tokyo; s. of Marquis Takayoshi Sasaki. Career: succeeded peerage 1910; grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; studied at Litt. Coll. of same. Address: 10[?] Aoyama Minami-cho 6 chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Niigata Iron Works; b. Aug. 1867, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Kichiro Sasamura. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1892; Chief Engr. of present firm 1897; Mng.-Dir. 1910. Address: 52 Suido-bata 2-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Pres. Japan-German Assn.; Pres. Sata Serum-Institut Osaka; b. Sept. 1873, Osaka; s. of Naomasa Sata. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; Lecturer Osaka Pref. Med. Sch. 1894; studied in Germany 1894-1900; rec'd deg. 1900; Pres. Osaka Pref. Med. Sch.; Dean Osaka Med. Coll.; Councillor Freiburg Univ. 1927. Address: 11 Dojima Kita-machi, Kita-ku, Osaka.

D.A.S.; Prof. & Dean of Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Tokyo Agr. Teachers' Coll.; Vice-Pres. Federation of Technical Educ. Associations, Federation of Society for Agr. Sci., Agr. Econ. Assns.; Dir. Central Union of Coop. Soc. b. Jan. 1879, Yonezawa; s. of Bantaro Sato. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1904; sent abroad for study 1918 20; Mem. Rice Control Committee, Raw Silk Export Control Investigation Com., Cultural Work Com. toward China, Tech. Educ. Inquiry Com.; Tech. Adviser to Employers' Delegate, 3rd Int'l Labor Conf. Geneva; Delegate, Int'l Econ. Conf. Geneva. Address: 440 Akatsutsumi-cho 2-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Sept. 1884, Sendai; s. of Noriatsu Sato, Judge. Career: grad. Litt. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1909; entered Ry. Dept.; Lecturer, Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1912; Secr. to Pres. Waseda Univ.; Chief Editor, Kyoiku Shimbun; Mng.-Dir. Japan Social Educ. Soc. 1920; Mng.-Dir. Inst. of Overseas People's Educ. 1933; elected M.P. 4 times since 1928; Parl. Councillor of Overseas Affairs. Address: 95 Suwa-cho, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Kagawa-ken since 1936; b. Sept. 1886, Fukushima-ken; s. of Kakunoshin Sato. Career. grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Commr. Taiwan Gov.-Gen.; Reconstruction Bureau; Chief, Educ. Dept. Hyogo-ken & Nagasaki-ken; Chief Police Dept. Akita-ken; Chief, Home Dept. Saitama-ken & Yamanashi-ken; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept., Harbin Muni. Office 1933-36. Address: c/o Gov.'s Residence, Takamatsu City.

ex-Minister for Foreign Affairs; b. Oct. 1882, Osaka; s. of Konroku Tanaka of Aomori-ken and later adopted by Aimaro Sato. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1904; Secr. Emb. Russia 1906-14; Cons.-Gen. Harbin 1914-19; Counsellor Emb. France 1921-23; Min. to Poland 1923; Dir. Japanese Bur., League of Nations 1926; Amb. to Belgium 1930; Japanese Del. to Assembly, League of Nations 1931-33; Japanese rep. at Council of League of Nations 1932; Japanese Delegate to Gen. Disarm. Conf. League of Nations 1931-34; Amb. to France 1933-37; Foreign Min. in Hayashi Cabinet 1937. Address: 4 Toriizaka, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Mem. House of Peers; Commr. Imp. Household Dept.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Academy; Chief, 2nd Dept., same; Chief, Medical Dept. Nat. Research Council; b. Oct. 1857, Gifu-ken; s. of Tadagoro Sato. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1882; studied Surgery in Germany 1883-86; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; rec'd deg. 1891; Dir. Medical Coll. Hospital 1893; Pres. Attached Medical Office 1901; Dean, Medical Coll. 1918. Address: 229 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

1st. Secr. Emb. France; b. Jan. 1894, Morioka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; 3rd Secr. Emb. France 1922; Commr. Foreign Office 1927; Chief 3rd Sec. Treaty Bureau 1931; 1st Sec. Emb. Manchoukuo 1934. Cons.-Gen. Harbin 1935-37. Address: Japanese Embassy, Paris.

Baron; D. Agr.; Ph. D.; LL.D.; Ex-Pres. Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; b. Nov. 1863; s. of Shozo Sato, samurai. Career: grad. Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; studied Agr. Econ. in John Hopkins Univ.; Prof. Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; Pres. Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; Gov. Rotary Int'l 70th Dist, 1937. Address: Higashi 7-chome, Kita Ichijo, Sapporo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. July 1865, Tsuruoka, Yamagata-ken; s. of Yasuyuki Sato. Career. grad. Nav. Acad. 1887; Staff, Nav. Gen. Staff; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; Pres. same; Vice-Admiral 1916; Commdr. Maizuru Nav. Port; elected Peer 1934. Address: 359 Kichijoji Hondenkita, Musashino-machi, Tokyo-fu.

Chief Engr. Muni. Adm. Office, Harbin; b. 1878, Okayama. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; served Canton-Hankow Ry. Adm. Office, 1905; Instructor, Ry. Sch. Hupei; joined S. M. R. Co. 1909; Vice-Chief, Ry. Dept. same 1928; resigned 1932; went to Europe & America for observation 1921. Address: 37 Hanazono-cho, Harbin.

M.D.; Imp. Court Councillor; b. August 1872, Nagoya; s. of Sanzo Sato. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; Surgeon-Sublieut. 1897; Instructor Mil. Med. Coll.; Chief Mil. Hospital, Keijo, Chosen; Chief, Med. Dept. Resident Garrison Chosen; resided in Germany 1907; Dir. Red Cross Hospital of Japan 1920; Surgeon-Gen. 1922; Chief Court Physician, 1927-37. Address: 14 Nagazumi-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Prof. Law & Letters Coll. Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. May 1877, Tsuruoka; s. of Hyozo Sato; m. Mineko, sister of Mikio Kato, lawyer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1903; apptd. Lecturer of same; Asst. Prof.; sent to Europe & Amer. to study politics 1908-12; Prof. of Politics & English Law; rec'd deg. 1913; again went to Europe & Amer. 1920. Address: 25 Higashi Niban-cho, Sendai.

Sr. Mng.-Dir. Daimaru Dept. Store; Governor 70th District (Japan and Manchoukuo) Rotary International; b. July 1878, Chiba-ken. Career: grad. Economics Coll. Keio Univ.; instructor, Keio Univ. 1903-06; joined Nippon Shokumin Kaisha, 1906; joined Mitsukoshi Dep't. Store as mng. head office, 1908; made tour of inspection of European and American dep't. stores, 1919; resigned from Mitsukoshi, 1920; Japanese del., Geneva Labor Conf., 1921; joined Daimaru Dep't Store, 1923. Address: 1,154, Oaza-shimo, Hamadera-cho, Osaka-fu.

n: SATOW, Mampei K. 佐藤万平
t: Hotel Mgr.; b. Apr. 1868, Nagano-ken; adopted s. of late Mampei Satow. Career: founder of Mampei Hotels at Karuizawa, Atami, Tokyo and Nagoya. Address: c/o Mampei Hotel, Atami, Shizuoka-ken.

Councillor, Japanese Emb. in Manchoukuo b. Oct. 1888, Tottori-ken; s. of Shingo Sawada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Chief Teleg. Sec. Foreign Office; attended Paris Peace Conf. Wash. Disarm. Conf. and Peking Customs Tariff Conf.; 1st Leg. Secr. Foreign Office; Secr. & Chief Teleg. Sec.; served Imp. Household Dept.; 1st Emb. Secr. England; Councillor Emb. France; Consul-Gen. New York. Address: c/o Japanese Emb. Hsinking.

Amb. to Brazil; b. Sept. 1884; s. of Shingo Sawada, Tottori-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Chief, Telegraph Section, Corr. Section, Translation Section; Councillor, Emb.; Cons.-Gen. New York; Dir. Japanese Bureau of League of Nations 1930; Dir. Japanese Bureau, Int'l Conf. Geneva 1933; Gov. Delegate to Simla Conf. 1934. Address: Japanese Emb. Rio-de-Janeiro, Brazil.

Major-Gen.; Mil. Attache, Legations, Poland & Rumania since 1935; b. 1887, Kochi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Academy, 1907; Mil. Staff Coll.; Instructor. Mil. Staff Coll.; attached to Kwantung Army Hdqrs.; Comdr. Field Artil. 24th Reg.; Chief Staff, Imp. Guards Div.; Comdr. Field Heavy Artil. 1st Brig. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Warsaw, Poland.

Consulting Engr. & Metallurgist; Repr. Demag, Duisburg; Otto Wolf, Koeln; b. 1882, Merseburg, Germany; s. of Julius Scheinhutte, Engr. Career: grad. Chemnitz K. G. A.; studied at Halle Univ.; Essen-Ruhr. Anaytical Chemist, 1906-09; Chief Chemist Affinerie Francaise, Lescure les Rouen; was in China as Metallurgist for Carlowitz & Co. 1910-19; in Japan for Otto Reimers & Co. Yokohama and Reimers Mining Office Tokyo 1920-22; Adviser Chinese Prov. Govt. Suiyuan 1922-34; Mgr. Behn, Meyer China Co. Peking 1927; Consulting Engr. & Metallurgist for Avg & Glenck 1931; Adviser Mining Adm. of Three Eastern Provs. 1928-31. Address: 46 Kaede-cho, Dairen.
German Vice-Consul at Kobe; b. Sept. 1898; s. of Georg S. Schmaltz, official. Career: entered German Diplomatic and Consular Service 1925. Address: German Consulate-General, Kobe.

Diplomvolkswirt; Dr. rer. pol. (Dr. of Economics); Prof. Saga Higher Sch. since 1929; b. May 1904, Sumatra. n. German; s. of Julius Schreiber, physician. Career: studied Law, Economics & History at Marburg, Kiel, and Vienna Univs. 1923-28; took deg. at Kiel Univ.; served at German Government State Record Office; came to Japan Sept. 1929. Address: Nishi-Shirage-Koji, Saga City.

Missionary; s. of late Samuel Scott, farmer; m. Annie J. McLellan. Career: grew up in North Dakota; grad. Hamline Univ. 1896, with degree of A.B.; received B.D. from Drew Theol. Seminary 1899; D.D. from Hamline 1923; came to Japan 1903; studied Japanese at Nagoya; was Presiding Elder of Kagoshima District 1905-06; Teacher, Chinzei Gakuin 1907-26; Aoyama Gakuin 1926-31; rec'd Gold medal from Nagasaki City for educ. service. Address: 683 Shiroyama-cho 1-chome, Nagasaki.

LL.B.; Lawyer; b. Nov. 1901, Baltimore, Maryland, U.S.A.; s. of Dr. Frank J. Sebald, physician; m. Edith Frances de Becker. Career: grad. from U. S. Nav. Acad. Annapolis, Md. in June 1922; served as commissioned officer in U. S. Navy; resigned in 1930 as Lt., U.S.N.; Japanese Lang. Officer attached to Amer. Emb. Tokyo 1925-28; grad. Sch. of Law, Univ. of Maryland; Mem. of Bar of State of Maryland; translated and annotated several books on Japanese law. Address: c/o de Becker, de Becker & Sebald, Meikai Bldg., 32 Akashi-machi, Kobe.

Chairman Mitsubishi Bank; Tokyo Bankers' Club; Dir. Showa Bank, 110th Bank; Aud. Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Permanent Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Sept. 1874, Nagano-ken; s. of Shichibei Sejimo; later adopted by Kiju Sejimo. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1893; entered Mitsubishi Bank. Address: 76 Kuruma-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Peers' Sch.; b. Aug. 1873, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Seiki Sekawa; m. Kukako, d. of late Baron Hikaru Inouye 1897. Career. succeeded family estate 1893; grad. History Course Toky Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Prof. Peers' Sch. 1901-30; taught at Mil. Staff Coll., Tokyo & Hiroshima Univs. of Lit. & Sc.; sent to Europe & Amer. 1906 & 19[?]3. Address: 107 Hanazono-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Rear-Admiral; attached Nav. Gen. Staff Office; b. 1886, Cotton Co.; Rep. Japan Cotton Spinning Assn.; b. Jan. 1884, Nara City. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Joined Osaka Spinning Co. 1908; toured Europe & America 1919-20; established Showa Rayon Co. 1928; Dir. Japan Horse Riding Assn.; went to Brazil as Mem. Japanese Econ. Mission to Brazil 1935. Address. 43 of 1876 Tantakabayashi, Sumiyoshi-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

D.E.; M.E. Cornell Univ. 1903; Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Tech.; b. Aug. 1875, Tokyo; s. of Toyojiro Sekiguchi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1896; Asst. Geneva; Chief 2nd & 3rd Secs. Information Bureau; Dir. same; Mem. Committee for Investigation of Cultural Work in China; Minister to Sweden, Norway & Denmark. Address: Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Author; b. Jan. 1884 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kenji Shirayanagi, shop-keeper. Career: entered Course of Philosophy at Waseda Univ. 1902; authority on Japanese history author of some 30 books including "Zaikai Taiheiki." Address: 4503 Takioji-cho, Oi-machi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Dir. Hsinking Postal Affairs Supt. Bureau since 1935; b. 1888, Osaka. Career: grad. Communications Dept. Training Inst. 1907; Vice-Commr. Com. Bureau, Kwantung Govt. 1927; Telegraph & Telephone Sec., Posts Bureau, Com. Dept. Manchoukuo 1932-35. Address: c/o Communications Dept. Hsinking.

Exchange & Stock Broker; Prop. Toyu Money Exchange Co. & Toyu Securities Dealing Co.; Pres. Dairen Gohin Daiko Co.; Auditor, Dairen Money Exchange & Trust Co.; Dir. Shusuishi Real Estate & Building Co., Dairen Kyosai-kai; Vice-Pres. Dairen Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. June 1890, Oita-ken; s. of Masuharu Shito. Career: served at Kwantung Govt. 1911-1914; entered Pohai Steamship Co. 1914; Mgr. Dairen Money Exchange & Trust Co. 1917-1923; Mgr. Hochengtai Money Exchange Co. 1923; founded Toyu Money Exchange Co.; Toyu Securities Dealing Co, 1932. Address: (Office) 81 Sakuramachi, Dairen, (Home) 18, Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

A.B.; Teacher of English; Mem. Asiatic Soc. of Japan; b. May 1910, Kyoto; s. of Prof. B. F. Shively; m. Beulah Feightner. Career: previously taught at Doshisha English Normal Sch., Ritsumeikan Univ. and Gifu Com. Sch.; now at Yamagata Higher Sch. Address: Koto Gakko Kansha, Kasumi-cho, Yamagata.

Pres. Nisshin Flour Mills Co.; Kotoku Flour Mills Co.; b. Feb. Gunma-ken; s. of Sakujiro Shoda. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1891; engaged by Soy brewing; established Tatebayashi Flour Mills 1901; established Nisshin Flour Mills 1907. Address: 22 Kobinatadai-machi 1-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Toyo Cotton Mills Co.; Vice-Pres. Showa Rayon Co., Yuho Spinning Co.; b. May 1873, Akita-ken; s. of Tomogoro Shoji. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1897; entered Dai-Nippon Spinning Assn.; sent to Bombay 1898; Chief Secr., same 1900; founded Osaka Spinning Co. 1912; Mgr., same; Mng.-Dir. Toyo Spinning Co. 1914; Vice-Pres. same. Address: 1876 Tantakabayashi, Sumiyoshi-mura, Hyogo-ken.

Pres. Yomiuri Shimbun; b. 1885, Toyama-ken; s. of Shojiro Shoriki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; served Metropolitan Police Board; Chief. Criminal Bureau, same; resigned 1924. Address: 1 Mita Shikoku-machi 2-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Hsingan South Prov.; Pres. Hsingan Coll.; b. 1885, Mongolia. Career: Adviser to Peace Preservation Office, Three Eastern Provs. 1924; Dir. Educ. Dept. Mongolia Frontier Supt. Office; Dir. Civil Affairs Bureau Mongolia Adm. Dept. Address: Governor's Residence, Wangyehmiao, Manchoukuo.
Dir. Decorations Bd. of Manchoukuo. Career: grad. Mukden Polit. Coll.; Councillor Fengtien Prov. Office; Dir. Land Bureau. Address: Decorations Bd. Hsinking.
Agent Louis Dreyfus & Cie Paris & Harbin; b. Jan. 1891, Zurich Switzerland. Career: 25 years representing interests of above firm in various countries. Address: 54 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

Prof. 2nd Higher Sch. since 1936; Dir. rer. pol. (Dr. Pol. Sc., Strassburg); b. May 1886, Magdeburg, Germany; s. of Max Singer. Career: Fin. Editor Hamburgischer Corr. 1913-16; Joint Editor Econ. Service, Hamburg 1916-28; Prof. Hamburg Univ. 1924-33; Visiting Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1931-34. Address 33 Kozenji-dori, Sendai.

Pianist; Prof. Tokyo Aacademy of Music, Ueno; b. 1885, Kiev.; n. Austrian. Career: grad. Coll. of Law 1908; Academies of Music in Kiev and Vienna; studied piano under Prof. Feruccio Busoni; gave concerts in cities of European countries; taught at Academy of Music, Poland and Vienna; present post since Apr. 1931. Address: 19 Hinoki-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
Portugese Consul at Harbin. Address: 44 Bolshoi Prospect, Harbin.
Soviet Ambassador to Japan since 1937; b. 1898; Consul-General at Harbin; arrived in Tokyo Aug. 25, 1937. Address: Mamiana-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

B.A. (Cambridge); Employee of Rising Sun Petroleum Co., Hon. Cosul for Netherlands at Taihoku; b. Jan. 1904, Westcliff-on-Sea. England; s. of Dr. J. C. Smellie. Career: came to Far East in service of the Shell organization in 1926. Address: c/o Rising Sun Petroleum Co., Taihoku.
B.A.; M.C.S.; Ph. M.; Teacher; b. June 1878, Illinois, U.S.A.; m. Charlotte Hess. Career: Teacher Kobe Higher Com. Sch. (now Univ. of Com.). Address: c/o Kobe Shoka Daigaku, Kobe.

M.P.; b. Aug. 1871, Fukui-ken; s. of Ryohei Soeda, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; Councillor, Hyogo-ken; Commr. Oita-ken, Kumamoto-ken, Shiga-ken and Yamanashi-ken; Gov. Saitama-ken, Yamanashi-ken and Yamagata-ken; Dir. Local Affairs Bureau. Home Dept. 1917; Councillor, Social Bureau; sent to Diet 5 times. Address: 301 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Kochu Koshi; b. Apr. 1884, Ehime-ken; bro. of Toranosuke Sogo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; entered Ry. Dept.; Dir. Reconstruction Bureau 1924; Dir. Finance Bureau, Ry. Dept.; Dir. S.M.R. Co. 1934. Address: 26 Yumi-cho 2-chome, Hongo-ku, Tokyo

M. of Sc.; Pres. Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co.; Chairman Meiji Confectionery Co., Showa Rubber Co.; Adviser Meiji Shoten; b. July 1869, Inuyama, Aichi-ken; s. of Ihori Tanaka. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Tech.; Univ. of Michigan; apptd. Prof. of Alma Mater; Engr. Taiwan Govt.; founded Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co. 1906, Meiji Confectionery Co. 1916, Showa Rubber Co. 1937. Address: 52 Isarago-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Monopoly Bureau, Finance Dept. and Monopoly Bureau, Taiwan Govt.-Gen.; Secr., Finance Dept.; Chief, Sales Sec. Monopoly Bureau, same; Advisor, Kwantung Army; Mem. Committee Meeting Manchuria Development Co.; b. July 6, 1898; 3rd s. Yuichi Kamite, samurai, and later adopted s. of Hanji Soma. Career: grad. Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1922; Financial Clerk, Finance Dept.; Surveyor of Taxes, same Bank Inspector, same; Vice-Councillor, Monopoly Bureau, same. Address: 225 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

n: SOUZA, Francisco Xavier da Silva e
t: Hon. Consul for Portugal, Kobe; merchant; b. Jan. 1867, Hongkong; n. Portuguese; s. of late A. J. Souza. Career: grad. Victoria Coll.; arrived in Kobe 1890 to join W. M. Strachan & Co.; Mgr. Kobe Office, Berrick & Co. from 1929 up to date; apptd. Hon. Consul for Portugal 1919; apptd. Repr. in Japan for Macao Govt. Bureau of Propaganda 1924; founded Portuguese Assn. 1920 and acted as Pres. for 3 years. Address: 17 Nakayamate-dori 2-chome, Kobe.

B.A. (Cambridge Univ.); b. Oct. 1872; s. of Taneomi Soyeshima. Career: Chamberlain to Taisho Tenno when he was Crown Prince; Dir. Anglo-Japanese Hydro-Elec. Co., Japan Steel Works, Central Reclamation Co., Hayakawa Water-Power Co., etc.; Pres. Keijo Nippo; Mem. Int'l Olympic Committee 1934. Address: 1321 Uyehara, Yoyogi, Tokyo.

Missionary; B. A. Cantab; Teacher & Librarian, Rikkyo Univ. since 1921; b. June 1882, London; s. of Henry Charles Spackman. Career: grad. Kelham Theological Coll. 1907; Caivs Coll. Cambridge 1910; Deacon 1910; Priest 1911; Teacher Central Theol. Coll. Ikebukuro 1914-21. Address: c/o Rikkyo Univ. Ikebukuro, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. (Boston Univ. 1925); D.D. (Syracuse Univ. 1932); District Supt. North Kyushu, Japan Meth. Church; Pastor Fukuoka Meth. Church; b. Nov. 1888, Nagasaki; s. of Dr. David S. Spencer; m. Evelyn W. McAlpine. Career: A. B. from Syracuse Univ. 1910; Asst. in Kyobunkwan Tokyo 1910-12; grad. B. D. Drew Theol. Sem. 1915; Pastorate in U. S. A. 1914-16; Assistant Board Foreign Mission M. E. Church New York 1916-17; Teacher Chinzei Gakuin Nagasaki 1917-19; subsequently country work, residence in Fukuoka; taught at Shyuyukan Middle Sch. and Kyushu Imp. Univ. Address: 21 Kego-hondori 1-chome, Fukuoka City.
Lawyer; b. June 1888, Philadelphia, Penn. U. S. A.; n. American. Address: 45 Yamashita-cho, Yokohama.

Hon. Consul for Japan at Oporto; Hon. Pres. Oporto Chamber of Com.; b. Sept. 1881, Oporto; s. of Antonio Spratley shipbroker; m. Stella Azevedo Pinheiro. Career: connected with shipping; later sub-mgr. of wine exporting firm; mem. of board of directors local railway co.; Mgr. Local Branch Bank of Lisbon & Azores; for 7 years Pres. Oporto Chamber of Com.; later Pres. Port-Wine Inst.; holder of decorations of Portuguese, Norwegian, Polish, French and Belgium countries. Address: 1361 Avenida da Boavista, Oporto, Portugal.

M.D.; b. Sept. 1896, Grossengottern, Germany; s. of Emil Stedefeld, Gutsbesitzer. Career: studied at Univs. of Freiburg, Kiel and Berlin; grad. Berlin Univ.; specialized in Ear, Nose, Throat & Eye diseases at Univ. of Berlin. Address: 67 Tansu-machi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Journalist; b. Apr. 1900; s. of Dr. R. Stein, Physician. Career: foreign corr. of "Berlin Tageblatt" in several countries; now of British and Continental-European papers in Tokyo. Address: c/o Domei Tsushin-sha, Ginza, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. K. K. L. Leybold Shokwan Tokyo & Osaka; merchant; b. Nov. 1886, Liegnitz; n. German; s. of S. Steinfeld, banker. Career: grad. Johannis Gymnasium Breslau; joined Simon, Evers & Co. Hamburg 190[?]; later was despatched to Japan by same and served as Sub.-Mgr. Kobe, Yokohama & Tokyo Offices; after World War became Partner and Mng.-Dir. of present firm. Address: 77 Sakuragaoka, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Hon. Cons.-Gen. for Austria in Japan; Gen. Mgr. for Far East of Bohler Steel Works, Vienna; b. June 1888, Budapest; n. Austrian. Address: Austrian Consulate, Teikoku Seimei Bldg. Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Dr. Juris (Univ. of Paris); Roumanian Minister to Japan since Apr. 1936; b. July 1886, Bucarest, Rumania; n. Rumanian; s. of Prof. George Stoicesco; m. Myra Nathan 1929. Career: Attaché Legation Constantinople; 3rd Secr. Berlin 1910; 2nd Secr. St. Petersburg 1911; Rome 1912; 1st Secr. Madrid 1917; Paris 1919; Councillor Paris 1920; served Foreign Office Bucarest 1926; Charge d'Affaires Tokyo 1929. Address: 55 Zaimoku-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo. Tel. Akasaka (48) 5061.

M.A. (Toronto Univ.); Missionary b. in Highgate, Ontario, Canada; s. of J. Frank Store, Agriculturist; m. Jean Gillespie, d. of Charles Gillespie. Career: grad. Toronto Univ. 1924; Emmanuel Coll. 1926; Teacher in St. Andrews' Coll. Toronto 1925; ordained clergyman United Church of Canada 1926; came to Japan as Missionary 1926; Language study, Tokyo till 1928; apptd. to Nagano 1928-31; Furlough & Post-Grad. study in Toronto Univ. 1931-32; apptd. to Hamamatsu 1932-34; Nagano 1934; specializing in Christian rural reconstruction. Address: 36 Minami Agata-machi, Nagano City, Nagano-ken.
M.A.; Missionary; b. Cardiff, Great Britain. Career: in Japan since 1926. Address: St. Francis Church, Meichiyama, Shimonoskei.

Dr. Phil.; Prof. Fukuoka Higher Sch. since 1935; b. July 1901, Dresden, Germany. Career: studied at Leipzig Univ. 1924-29; Asst. Museum of Ethnology, Leipzig; Asst. Inst. for Ethnol. & Anthropological Researches, Leipzig Univ.; took part in Ethnol. Expedition to Portuguese East Africa 1931. Address: Shioiri, Nishi-Shinmachi, Fukuoka City.

D.L.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Councillor, Social Bureau; b. Nov. 1888, Tokyo; s. of Ganseki Suehiro, judge. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; apptd. Asst. Prof. later Prof. of same Univ.; rec'd deg. 1920; Dean, Law Coll. 1933-36. Address: 971 Uenodai, Unane, Kinuta-mura, Tokyo-fu.

D.L.; Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. July 1874, Ehime-ken; s. of Shigeyasu Suehiro. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; studied in Europe 1901; Asst. Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ; sent to America 1913 & 1921. Address: 637 Sokokuji, Higashi Monzen-cho, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Admiral; Supreme War Councillor; b. June 1881, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Sokuro Suetsugu. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1899; Nav. Staff Coll.; Staff 1st Sqn.; Chief 1st Sec. Nav. Gen. Staff; Comdr. Submarine Sqn.; Dir. Educ. Bureau of Navy; Vice-Chief Nav. Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief 2nd Sqn.; Comdr.-in-Chief Combined Fleet & 1st Sqn, 1933-34; Yokosuka Nav. Stn. 1935. Address: 3-33 Nishiogikubo, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Chief Dir. Sendai Educ. Inst.; b. Jan. 18[?][?], Miyagi-ken; s. of Michizane Sugawara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; Dir. Hakodate Revenue Supt. Bureau; Dir. Marugame and Kobe Revenue Supt. Bureaus; Councillor and Secr. Finance Dept.; Dir. Revenue Bureau; Vice-Minister of Finance; nominated Peer 1916; Pres. Oriental Development Co. 1930-32. Address: 49 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Pres. Imp. Museum; b. Jan. 1873, Okayama-ken; s. of Ryotaro Sugi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; was in service in Finance Dept. and Board of Audit; Dir. Imp. Archives a Mausolea Bureaus. Address: 123 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Showa Cotton Co. since 1930; b. Oct. 1887, Shiga-ken; s. of late Arinobu Sugimoto. Career: joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha 1906; served in British India, England and China. Address: 52 Nango-cho, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Counsellor Asahi Shimbun; b. July 1872; s. of Shojiro Sugimura. Career: studied at Igirisu Horitsu Gakko & Senshin Gakuin; served Amer. Emb. Tokyo; joined Asahi Shimbun 1903. Address: 2210 Abiko-machi, Chiba-ken.

D.L.; Ambassador to France; s. of Fukashi Sugimura. Career: grad. Law College of Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1908; grad. Faculte de Droit de l'Université de Lyon 1912; Attaché, Emb. France 1912; 3rd Emb. Secr. 1914; 2nd Leg. Secr. China; Foreign Office Councillor 1919; Chief 2nd Sec. Treaty Bureau 1919; attended Wash. Conf. 1921; 1st Emb. Secr. France 1923; Emb. Councillor 1923; attended League of Nations Assemblies Geneva 1923-26; Dir. Japanese Bureau of League of Nations 1926-33; Under Secr.-Gen. & Dir. of Polit. Sec. of same 1927-33; Amb. to Italy 1934-37; Concluded Rome-Tokyo Accord 1936; Address: Japanese Emb. Paris.

Pres. Tokyo Stock Exchange; Dir. Chiyoda Securities & Investment Corp., Nichiei Brewing Corp.; b. Sept. 1870, Hirosaki-shi; s. of Yoshinaga Sugino. Career: joined Bank of Japan 1889; Asst. Mgr. Aichi Bank 1896; Mgr. later Dir. Nagoya Bank; engaged in broker business in Tokyo since 1907; joined as Partner Koike Goshi Kaisha 1910; established Yamaichi Securities Corp. 1926 and Pres. till Dec. 1935. Address: Daibutsu Keidai, Hase, Kamakura.

General; War Minister since Feb. 1937; b. Jan. 1880, Kokura City; s. of Tei Sugiyama. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1910; Chief Mil. Affairs Sec. War Dept. 1922-25; attended Disarm. Conf. League of Nations 1926; Vice-Minister of War 1928; Comdr. 12th Div. 1932; Chief Mil. Air Service Dept. 1933-34; Vice-Chief. Gen. Staff Office; Inspector-Gen. of Mil. Educ. Address: 33 Koenji 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Advisor Shakai-Taishuto; Pres. All Japan Farmers' Union; Dentist; b. Nov. 1885, Osaka-fu. Career: grad. Osaka Agrl. Sch. 1903; Asst. Engr. Agrl. Society of Wakayama-ken; grad. Theol. Dept. Tohoku Gakuin Sendai 1909; preached Chiristianity in Fukushima-ken; engaged in Farmer Movement with Toyohiko Kagawa; apptd. Chief Central Executive Committee. Labor & Farmer Party. Address: 55 Higashiajiro, Fuse-cho, Osaka-fu.

D.L.; Docteur Honoris Causa des Universités de Paris, de Lyon et de Bordeaux; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Vice-Chief Dir. Société Franco-Japonaise; Mng.-Dir. Maison Franco-Japonaise; Dir. Soc. Rapprochment Intellectual Fr.-Jap.; Councillor, Society for Int'l Cultural Relations, etc.; b. Jan. 1878, Tokyo; s. of Kanzo Sugiyama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; Lecturer of Civil Law, Peers' Sch., Hosei, Meiji, Nihon, Waseda Univs.; despatched to Europe to study Civil & Com. Laws 1905-8; Prof. Nagasaki Higher Com. Sch.; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; rec'd deg. 1917; sent to Europe & America 1926 & 1934; decorated by French Govt. 1922 & 1934. Address: 1 Sekiguchi Komai-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor Emb. Wash.; b. Sept. 1892, Akita-ken; s. of Yasohachi Suma. Career: grad. Law Dept. Chuo Univ. 1910; studied at Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Secr. Emb. Berlin; Secr. Leg. China; Consul Canton 1930 Cons.-Gen. Nanking 1933-37. Address: Japanese Emb. Wash., U. S. A.

Pres. Sumida Bussan Kaisha since 1927; Oriental Coffee Co.; Nanyo Coffee Co.; b. 1882, Hiroshima City; s. of Hatsuzo Sumida, farmer. Career: grad. Mid-Pacific Institute; established Sumida Shokai 1898; Oriental Coffee Co. 1922; Nanyo Coffee Co. 1926; rewarded by Nippon Sangyo Kyokai 1927; by Hiroshima-ken Kaigai Kyokai 1930. Address: 1429 Shironomae, Mikage-machi, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

D.Agr.; Prof. Tokyo Agrl. Coll. and Dir. Educ. Dept. of same; b. June 1890, Kumamoto-ken. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Engr. Taito Sugar Mfg. Co. 1915-18; Lecturer of above Univ. Address: 759 Komaba-cho, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

n: SUMITOMO, Kichizaemon 住友吉左衞門
t: Baron; Pres. Sumitomo Honsha Ltd.; Dir. Besshi Mining Co., Sumitomo Bank, Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Trust Co., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co.; b. Feb. 1909, Osaka; s. of late Baron Kichizaemon Sumitomo. Career: grad Peers' Sch.; studied at Kyoto Imp. Univ.; inherited family estate 1926. Address: 1 of 1876 Tantakabayashi, Sumiyoshi-mura, Hyogo-ken.

Vice-Admiral; Dir. Educ. Bureau of Navy since 1935; b. 1886, Tokyo. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1906; Nav. Staff Coll.; Aide-de-Camp to H.I.M. the Emperor; Captain "Haruna"; Chief Staff Kure Naval Station. Address: c/o Navy Office Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Manchuria Elec. Co.; b. 1894, Anhui Prov. Career: grad. Nihon Univ. Tokyo 1920; Secr., Ind. Dept. Kirin Prov.; Adviser Chinese Eastern Ry.; Dir. Ind. & Com. Bureau and Trade Mark Bureau 1932-34. Address: c/o Manchuria Elec. Co., Hsinking.

Manchoukuo Minister of Dept. of People's Welfare; b. 1881, Liaoyang-hsien, Fengtien. Career: grad. Higher Normal Sch. Tokyo; Chief, Educ. Dept. Heilungkiang; Chief, Finance Dept. Kirin Prov.; Chief, Chang-tao, Heilungkiang; Mem. Govt. Committee & Chief, Construction Dept. Kirin 1929; resigned 1931; Chief, Finance Dept. Kirin Govt.; Pres. Kirin Prov. Bank; Vice-Min. of Finance 1933; Gov. Heilungkiang Prov. 1933-34; Lungkiang Prov. 1934-35; Finance Min. 1935-37; Civil Affairs Min. May-July 1937. Address: Dept. of People's Welfare, Hsinking .

Dir. Pinkiang Revenue Supt. Bureau Manchoukuo; b. 1879, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: Comdr. 2nd Reg. Fengtien Army; Comdr. 30th Brig. North Eastern Army; Chief, Police Dept. Liaoning Prov.; Supt. Antung Customs; Chief Antung Monopoly Office. Address: Revenue Supt. Bureau, Pinkiang Prov.

Merchant; b. June 1893; s. of late Sun Yu-shan, merchant. Career: grad. Com. Sch.; Non-Commissioned Staff, S.M.R. Co.; Local Committee, Hsinking; Adviser, Exchange Brokers' Assn.; Non-Commissioned Staff, Manchoukuo Trade House at Osaka. Address: 1 Fuji-cho 4-chome, Hsinking.

Dir. Central Bank of Manchou since 1936; b. 1895, Kaiping, Fengtien Prov.; s. of Sun Hai-tung, scholar. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Peking Univ.; Gen. Mgr. Three Eastern Prov. Bank; Mgr. Mukden Branch, Central Bank of Manchou; Chief, Mint Sec. head office. Address: c/o Central Bank of Manchou, Mukden.

M.P.; Lawyer; Leader Seiyukai; b. Sept. 1885, Ehime-ken; s. of Shigeharu Sunada. Career: grad. Chuo Univ. 1904; elected to Diet 7 times; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry 1931. Address: 528, Kita Senzoku-cho, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

1st Secr. Legation, Austria; b. Sept. 1892, Yamagata-ken; s. of late Shimpachiro Suwa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; 2nd Secr. Legation at the Hague 1925; Consul at Medan, Sumatra, 1928; present post since 1934. Address: Japanese Legation, Vienna, Austria.

Former Prof. Hosei Univ.; Critic; b. Nov. 1896, Hiroshima-ken; m. Yoshiko Kikuchi. Career: grad. Aoyama Gakuin Coll. ; taught at Nihon Univ., Hosei Univ., Azabu Mid. Sch. for 17 yrs. till 1932; author of books on lit., phil. and religion. Address: 254 Setagaya 1-chome, Tokyo.

Adviser, Shakai Taishuto (Socialist People's Party); Chief Dir. Educ. Assn. for Laborer; b. Sept. 1885, Miyagi-ken; s. of Masuji Suzuki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; joined Shueisha Printing Office; Corr. Asahi Shimbun; went to America to inspect int'l labor movement; attended Int'l Labor Conf. as Laborer' Delegate 4 times. Address: Satakebori, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

Pres. Suzuki Shoten, Toshin Elec. Co., Showa Ind. Co.; Chairman Showa Fertilizer Co.; Dir. Tokyo Elec. Light Co.; b. Feb. 1875, Kanagawa-ken. Career: grad. Yokohama Com. Sch.; established Suzuki Shoten with his bro.; went to Europe & Amer. to inspect com. & ind. 1925-26; again visited Amer. partly on behalf Foreign Office 1931. Address: 9 Samban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.
Mng.-Dir. Nagoya Bank since 1933; b. Mar. 1875, Aichi-ken. Career: joined present bank 1907. Address: 10 Kitabata, Tashiro-cho, Higashi-ku, Nagoya.

Baron; Adml.; Privy Councillor; b. Dec. 1867, Osaka-fu; s. of late Yoshiaki Suzuki. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1887; Nav. Staff Coll. 1896; apptd. Sub-Lieut. 1889; fought in Sino-Japanese War as Captain, 6th Torpedo Boat; Staff Nav. Affairs Bureau; Staff Nav. Training Dept.; Instructor Nav. Acad. and Mil. Acad.; sent to Germany and apptd. Officer for bringing H.M.S. “Kasuga” home; fought in Russo-Japanese War as Comdr. “Kasuga” and 4th Destroyer Flotilla; Captain “Akashi,” “Soya”; Dir. Nav. Torpedo Sch.; Capt. “Shikishima,’ “Tsukuba”; Comdr. Maizuru Torpedo Flotilla; Comdr. 2nd Sqn.; Dir. Personnel Bureau of Navy; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr. Training Sqn.; Dir. Nav. Acad.; Comdr.-in-Chief, 2nd and 3rd Sqns., Kure Nav. Station, 1st Sqn.; Combined Fleet; nominated Supreme War Councillor; Chief Nav. Gen. Staff; Grand Chamberlain. Address: 40 Maruyamacho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Kyoto-fu; b. July 1889, Tokyo-fu; s. of Kwanji Suzuki. Career: grad. Polit. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Chief Educ. Affairs Dept. Nagasaki-ken; Police Dept. Fukuoka-ken; Pub. Peace Dept. Metro. Police Board; Gov. Toyama-ken, Kumamoto-ken; Hiroshima-ken. Address: Gov.'s Residence, Kyoto.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1867, Kanagawa; s. of Tomiemon Kawashima, and later adopted by Jiko Suzuki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1891; went to Europe & Amer. to study legislation; Judge Supreme Court; Pres. Tokyo District Court; Public Procurator Supreme Court; Vice-Minister of Justice; Public Procurator-Gen.; Justice Min. in Kiyoura Cabinet; Home Min. in Tanaka Cabinet; Justice Min. and later Home Min. in Inukai Cabinet; Pres. Seiyukai. Address: 6 Kudan 4-chome Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Nihon Chuzo K.K.; Mng.-Dir. Asano Shipbuilding Co., Oki Elec. Co.; Dir. Asano Family Co., Naigai Oil Co., Asano Kokura Steel Mills, Chosen Iron Mine Co., Keihin Canal Co.; b. 1880, Gifu-ken; s. of Yahei Daido; later adopted by Suzuki family. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1905; entered 1st Bank; Chief, Deposits Sec.; resigned 1913; established Haibara Co. Address: 9 Tamachi 6-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman Taifuku Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Mng.-Dir. Tokio Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Dir. Shinko Bldg. Co., Meiji Fire Ins. Co., Mitsubishi Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Nippon Salvage Co., Hull Underwriters' Union, Imp. Japanese Marine Corp., Ins. Business Research Bureau; Aud. Mitsubishi Econ. Research Bureau; b. Aug. 1887, Takamatsu, Kagawa-ken; e. s. of Ikuye Suzuki; m. Toyo, d. of Hikojiro Itami of Saga-ken. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1907; joined Tokyo Marine Ins. Co. (now Tokio Marine & Fire Ins. Co.) Mem. Japanese Econ. Mission to Europe & Amer. 1937. Address: 18 Naka-Tomisaka-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Japan Econ. Federation; Chairman Japan Savings Banks Assn.; Aud. Keio Univ.; b. 1866, Hamamatsu; s. of Takizo Suzuki. Career: grad Keio Univ. 1889; entered Yokohama Specie Bank 1892; Sub-Mgr. New York Branch 1895; Mgr. Tientsin, Peiping, Shanghai, Kobe Branches and Head Office; Gen.-Mgr. 1914; Dir. 1916; Vice-Pres. 1918-21; Pres. Int'l Trust Co. 1923; Bank of Chosen 1925; Ind. Bank of Japan 1927-30. Address: 116 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

General (reserve); Privy Councillor; b. Feb. 1865, Niigata-ken; s. of Takatsugu Suzuki. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1891, Mil. Staff Coll. 1896; Staff Gen. Staff Office; Sec. Chief same; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Comdr. Cav. 3rd Brig.; Cav. Inspector; Comdr. 4th and 5th Divisions; Comdr. Taiwan Army; Chief, Gen. Staff 1926; sent to Europe, America and Siberia; Pres. Imp. Assn. of Reservists. Address: 28 Kitayamabushi-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Kyodo Fire Ins. Co.; b. Apr. 1862, Nagano-ken; s. of Ryuzo Suzuki. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Corr. Jiji Shimpo; Pres. Yokohama Boeki Shimbun; entered Mitsui Bank, 1894; Mgr. Yokohama Branch 1896, Kobe Branch 1899; Mng.-Dir. Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; returned to Diet 5 times 1912-32. Address: 15 Hirakawa-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr.; Pres. Inst. of Scientific Research of Manchoukuo; b. Apr. 1874, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Shozo Suzuki, landowner. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; apptd. Asst. Prof. same 1900; sent to Europe by Educ. Dept. to study Physiol. Chem. 1901-06; Prof. Morioka Agr. Coll. 1906; awarded with Imp. Acad. Prize for his discovery of Oryzanin (Vitamin B) 1921; succeeded in preparing synthetic Sake (wine) 1925; Dean Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1927; Adviser Continental Inst. of Sc. 1935; Tech. Adviser to Sankyo Co. Address: Scientific Research Institute, Hsinking.

M.Sc.; B.A.; Architect; Consulting Engineer; b. 1885, Czechoslovakia; s. of J. Svagr, land owner. Career: studied at Univ. and Polytechnical Institute in Prague; worked in Czechoslovakia, Germany, Denmark, Russia, China and Japan. Address: 42-B Yamate, Yokohama.

Hon. Consul for Japan at Melbourne, Australia; Shipowner; b. 1876, Melbourne; s. of late David York Syme, shipowner; m. Jessie Mary Laycock, d. of Burdett Laycok. Career: educated at Scotch Coll., Melbourne and matriculated; Chairman & Mng.-Dir. Melbourne Steamship Co. and Hobson's Bay Dock & Engrg. Co. Pty.; Dir.: National Bank of Austrasia, Metropolitan Gas Co.; Mount Lyell Mining & Railway Co.; Australian Paint & Compositions Co.; Mount Pleasant Coke Co. Pty.; Commr. Melbourne Harbour Trust; was Mem. Commonwealth Central Shipping Committee and Deputy Controller of Interstate Shipping during War years; has been Chairman, Austrasian Steamship Owners' Federation; Mem. Board of Management Royal Melbourne Hospital. Address: 31 King Street, Melbourne, Austlaria.
Mgr. Far Eastern Agency of the Czechoslovak Export Inst. Harbin. Address: P. O. Box 37 Harbin, & P.O. Box 1845, Shanghai.

Sr. Mng.-Dir., Zenkoku Kobai Rengo-kai (Purchasing Union of Whole Country) since 1937; b. Dec. 1, 1888, Hyogo-ken; s. of Hikozaemon Tabuchi; Career: grad. Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; entered Agr. Bureau, Dept. of Agr. & For., same year; Dir., Stock Breeding Bureau, same, 1935; Vice-Dir., Horse Adm. Bureau, same, 1936; Dir., Sericulture Bureau, same, 1937. Address: 42, Honcho-dori 5-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Judge Permanent Court of Arbitration; Mem. Imp. Academy; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imperial Univ.; b. Mar. 1874; s. of Kaichi Tachi, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; studied Int'l Law in P.-G. Course; studied Diplomatic History in Germany, France and England; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; attended Paris Peace Conf. and Washington Conf. Address: 57 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. Jan. 1880, Tokyo; s. of Visct. Taneyuki Tachibana. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. 1904; Meiji Univ.; Cav. Lieut.; Parl. Councillor of Communications 1932-34. Address: 1922 Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Vice-Chief Gen. Staff Office and Dir. Mil. Staff Coll. concurrently; b. 1882, Miyagi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1904, Mil. Staff Coll; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Comr. Field Artil. 4th Reg; Chief Staff 16th Div.; attached to Kwantung Army during Manchurian Incident; Supreme Adviser Manchoukuo Defence Dept.; Comdr. Field Heavy Artil. 4th Brig, 1934; Garrison in China 1935; 11th Div. 1936-37. Address: Gen. Staff Office Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Apr. 1886, Chiba-ken; s. of Nenosuke Tada: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; elected M.P. 4 times since 1930; Parl. Councillor of Communications 1936-37. Address: 10 Imairi-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; D. E.; Dir. Mil. Sc. Research Office since 1936; b. 1882, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1904; Staff. Mil. Tech. Dept.; Chief, 1st Sec. Mil Sc. Research Office; Dir. Ordnance Bureau. Address: 3 Hyakunin-machi, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo,

M.P.; Pres. Meiji Gakuin; b. Oct. 1869, Saga-ken; s. of Setsuzo Tagawa, samurai. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Tokyo Senmon Gakko 1889; joined Yubin Hochi and Miyako Shimbun as Corr.; Mil. Interpreter; Asst. Mayor of Tokyo; Councillor, Justice Dept.; elected to Diet 7 times since 1908. Address: 25 Kobinata Daimachi 2-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo,

M.P.; Dir. Kyocho-kai; b. Nov. 1881, Iwate-ken; s. of Kanji Tago. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; entered Home Dept.; Chief Police Dept. Yamaguchi-ken; Sec. Chief Police Bureau Home Dept.; Sec. Chief Local Affairs Bureau; Chief 1st Sec. Social Bureau; Dir. Social Bureau; Gov. Mie-ken, elected M.P. 5 times; Parl. Vice-Min. of Ry. 1926-37. Address: 382 Kami-Osaki Nakanomaru, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Kishimoto Shoten, Indo-Japanese Trading Co., Indian Iron & Steel Co., Osaka Kozai K. K., Goyo Shosen Kaisha Ltd.; Hon. Secr., Osaka Assn. for Liberty of Trading; b. Mar. 1883, Gunma-ken; s. of Sakusaburo Taguchi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; joined Editorial Staff, Kokumin Shimbun; toured Europe, America and British India on business 9 times since 1919; decorated by the King of the Belgians. Address: 1315 Midarebashi, Zaimokuza, Kamakura.

Mng.-Dir. Asia Aluminum Co.; b. Sept. 1885, Saitama-ken; s. of Hanshichi Taguchi. Career: grad. Yokohama Com. Sch.; Dir. Takamine Hozen Co., Sumitomo Aluminum Co., Japan Bakelite Co., Harley Davidson Motor-cycle Sales Office. Address: 323 Gotenyama, Kitashinagawa, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; b. Sept. 1895, Kobe; s. of late Junkichi Taguchi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1923; practised law at Kobe for 8 years; came to Mukden and opened office 1932. Address: San Djin Loo. Pa Wei Loo, Mukden.

Pres. Mitsubishi Paper Mills Ltd.; Dir. Edogawa Chem. Works Ltd., Nihon Felt Co.; b. Mar. 1871, Hyogo-ken; s. of Masanari Tahara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895. Address: 36 Hachiman-dori 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman Tama Shipbldg Yard; Mng.-Dir. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. Feb. 1883, Gunma-ken; s. of Iwahei Tajima, farmer. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1905; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; served at New York Branch; apptd. Mgr. same Branch 1921; Dir. 1930; Mgr. Osaka Branch 1931. Address 71 Miyamura-cho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Engr. Dept. of Agr. & Forestry; b. Nov. 1885, Tokyo-fu; s. of Shintaro Tajima, agriculturist; m. Takeko, d. of Yozo Harashima. Career: grad. Mechanical Engrg. Dept. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1908; entered Dept. of Agr. & Forestry 1908 service in Fishery Bureau; sent to England and America for study 1916-18. Address: 1167 Ohara-machi, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Yokohama Com. Coll. since 1923; b. Dec 1876, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Eiji Tajiri, lawyer. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1901; completed Consular Service Course of same 1903; Prof. Nagasaki Com. Coll. 1908-20; Pres. of same 1920-23. Address: 1125 Masaka, Isogo-machi, Yokohama.

Pres. Takabane Shoten; Teikoku Brick Co.; b. July 1867, Aichi-ken; s. of late Sobei Takabane. Career: Vice-Chairman, Kojimachi Ward Assembly; Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 3 Kioi-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Dairen Steamship Co.; b. Feb. 1889, Fukushima-ken; s. of Seinosuke Takagi, public procurator. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1912; entered S. M. R. Co.; with present firm since 1920. Address: 256 Togendai, Dairen.

Pres. S. Manchuria Mining Co.; Vice-Pres. China-Japan Ind. Development Co. etc.; b. Oct. 1880, Fukui-ken; s. of Korenori Takagi. Career: studied at Niigata Com. Sch.; grad. Tokyo Com. & Tech. Sch.; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; was sent to China; served as Mil. Interpreter in Boxer Uprising; Japanese Repr. Han-Yen-Ping Iron & Coal Mining Co. 1911. Address: 28 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

b. Mar. 1892, Tokyo. Career: grad. Chuo Univ. 1914; entered Communications Dept. 1914; Chief, Sapporo Post Office; Chief, Bonds Sec. Savings Bureau; Chief. Pension Sec., same; Secr. Pension Bureau, Cabinet 1921; Commr. Imp. Household Dept. 1924; Councillor, same; Secr. to Imp. Household Minister; Commr. Prince Ri's Household 1934; Chief Secr. Privy Seal Dept. Address: 70 Yamato-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad. Nat. Research Council; b. Apr. 1875, Gifu-ken; s. of Kansuke Takagi. Career: grad. Mathematics Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied Maths. in Germany; rec'd deg. 1903; Dr. Honoris Causa (Univ. Oslo) 1929. Address: 24 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

D. Econ.; Prof. Hosei Univ.; Pres. Takagi Econ. Research Inst.; b. Apr. 1887, Toyama; s. of Kihei Takagi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; joined Fudo Savings Bank, later Masuda Bill Broker; Vice-Chief, Econ. Dept. Osaka Mainichi Shimbun. Publications: "Econ. Philosophy of Life," "Rush to East Asia Monroe Doctrine." Address: 39 Ueno Sakuragi-cho, Shitaya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Dec. 1889, Tokyo; s. of Baron Naibu Kanda; later adopted by Takagi family; m. Hideko Kawada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Asst. Prof. same, 1919; sent to America for study 4 yrs.; travelled Europe 1923; Prof. of Amer. Constitution, History & Dipl. 1924; Mem. Council of Inst. of Pacific Relations since 1925. Address: 282 Seijo, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

n: TAKAHASHI, Eijiro (Ichikawa Sadanji 5th) 高橋榮次郎
t: Kabuki Actor; b. Oct. 1880, Tokyo; s. of Ichikawa Sadanji, 4th. Career: made debut 1884; succeeded the name "Sadanji" after father's death 1906; visited Europe; went to Moscow to perform Kabuki plays 1928. Address: 6 Surugadai 3-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Toyo Kisen Kaisha, Taiyo Kogyo Kaisha; Vice-Pres. Tokai Shosen Kaisha, Toyo Shoji Kaisha; Mng.-Dir. Toyo Kaiun Kaisha; Dir. Yamashita Kisen Kaisha; b. June 1882, Sendai; s. of Kagenobu Takahashi; m. Fumiyo, d. of Kagetsugu Takahashi. Career: grad. Takushoku Univ.; joined N. Y. K.; Mgr. Taihoku Branch; Mng.-Dir. Kairin Koshi; Gen. Mgr. Toyo Kisen Kaisha. Address: 26 Nando-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Chairman Manchuria Invention Soc.; Chief Dir. Manchoukuo Life Ins. Co.; Dir. Manchou Light Metal Ind. Co.; b. Feb. 1891, Akita-ken; s. of Hyozo Takahashi; m. Miyo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; Commr. Agr. & Com. Dept.; despatched to Europe & Amer. 1918-19; to Manchuria, China & Siberia 1923; Dir. Tokyo Mining Inspection Bureau; Chief Judge Patent Bureau; Vice-Min. of Manchoukuo Ind. Dept. Address: 807 Hokuan Kodo, Hsinking.
Ex-Minister of Finance; died on Feb. 26. 1936. (See 1936 issue.)

Pres. Teikoku Refrigerator Co.; Tokyo Warehouse Co.: Director Nippon Dry-Ice Co., Hokkaido Railway Co.. Hayashi Iron Works, Nippon Fire Insurance Co.; b. September 1871, Miyagi-ken; s. of Heizaburo Takahashi, samurai. Career: grad. 2nd Higher Sch. and Fisheries Inst.; founded Iwate-ken Fishery Sch. by order of Educ. Authorities; apptd. Mng.-Dir. Chiba-ken Agri. & Ind. Bank; Mgr. Kobe Branch. Nippon Fire Ins. Co.; established Teikoku Refrigerator Co. Address: 2 of 532 Kamimeguro 8-chome, Meguro-ku. Tokyo.

M.P.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Agr. & For.; b. Oct. 1894, Saitama-ken; s. of Shuhei Takahashi. Career: grad. Saitama-ken. Normal Sch. 1916; elected M.P. 3 times since 1928; high tax-payer in Saitama-ken. Address: 34 Tsukudohachiman-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Dai Nippon Brewery Co.; Mng.-Dir. Manchuria Beer Brewery Co.; Dir. Chosen Brewery Co., Miyajima Hotel & Japan Beer Exporters' Assn.; b. July 1875. Ehime-ken; s. of Yoshihira Takahashi. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; studied in Germany. Address: 123 Komagome Kamifujimae-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Dir. Ordnance Central Depot since 1933; b. May 1887. Career: grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief, 3rd Dept. Mil. Tech. Dept.; Chief, Tokyo Mil. Arsenal; Chief, Kokura Mil. Arsenal 1933. Address: 6300 Mejiro 3-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral; War Councillor; b. Aug. 1882, Tokyo; bro. of Toyotaro Takahashi. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1901; Captain "Fuso"; Chief Staff Combined Fleet; Pres. Nav. Staff Coll.; Vice-Chief Nav. Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief 2nd Sqn. 1933-34; Combined Fleet. Address: 23 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr.; Ex-Dean and Prof. Agri. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1875, Nagano-ken; s. of Moemon Takahashi. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; Asst. Prof. same 1906; re'd deg. 1907; went to America for study 1916-19; Prof. 1922. Address: 327 Komagome Dozaka-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; M.D.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Nov. 1875; s. of Kanehiro Takaki, Peer. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; studied physics in England, Germany and Austria; grad. Kings Coll. Sch. and St. Thomas Hospital Medical Coll. London; served as House Surgeon at St. Thomas Hospital, London; Pres. Tokyo Hospital and Tokyo Charity Hospital; Head, Special Sch. of Tokyo Charity Hospital; sent to America to investigate medical education; became Pres. Japan and Kanto Rugby Union. Address: 13 Higashi-Toriizaka, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Japan Tourist Bureau; b. Feb. 1886, Miye-ken; s. of Jinsuke Takaku. Career: grad. English Dept. Tokyo Sch. of For. Languages 1908; M. B. A., Univ. of Penn. U.S.A. 1923; entered Ry. Dept.; Mgr. Foreign Affairs Dept. Traffic Bureau; joined present office 1928; sent to Europe & America. Address: 130 Horinouchi 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Pres. Musashino Girl's Sch.; Chief Dir. Japan-German Culture Inst.; b. May 1866, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Kanzo Sawai: later adopted by Magosaburo Takakusu. Career: grad. Shinshu Litt. Sch.; studied in England; grad. Oxford Univ. 1894; studied in Germany & France; Secr. to Communications Minister; Pres. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. same; rec'd deg. 1900; Mem. Imp. Academy 1912. Address: Hoya-mura, Tokyo-fu.

Mem. Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Prop. Shitei Shoten; High Taxpayer; b. Nov. 1889; s. of late Morosada Takamatsu, Aichi-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915. Address: 5 Naya-machi 1-chome, Naka-ku, Nagoya.

D.E.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; b. Sept. 1852, Tokyo; s. of Kahei Takamatsu. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1878; studied Chem. in England & Germany 1879-82; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch.; rec'd deg. 1888; Judge Patent Bureau 1890-1903; Pres. Tokyo Gas Co.; Pres. Tokyo Ind. Lab. 1914-24. Address: 13 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Chief, Preventive Sec. Sanitary Bureau, Home Office since 1922; b. Sept. 1884, Ibaraki ken; s. of Tohei Takano, landowner. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; became Staff, Infections Diseases Inst.; Mem. Kitazato Institute; Prof. Med. Dept. Keio Univ.; served Home Office; sent to Europe & America for study; rec'd deg. 1918. Address: 23 Minamitera-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

D. Agr. & D. L.; Pres. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. since 1933; b. 1871, Shimane-ken. Career: grad. Sapporo Agr. Coll. 1895; Asst. Prof. same 1897; studied in Germany 1900-1902; Dean Agr. Coll. Hokkaido Imp. Univ. 1928. Address: Nishi 12-chome, Kita Rokujo, Sapporo.

Admiral (retired); b. 1867, Miyazaki-ken; s. of Saneaki Takarabe, samurai. Career: grad. Naval Staff Coll. 1893; apptd. Staff, Naval Gen. Staff Office; Captain "Fuji"; Staff, 1st Squadron; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr.-in-Chief, 3rd Sqn. and Ryojun Naval Port; Comdr. Sasebo, Maizuru, and Yokosuka Naval Stations; Supreme War Councillor; Navy Minister in T. Kato, Yamamoto, K. Kato, Wakatsuki and Hamaguchi Cabinets; attended Naval Disarm. Conf. London 1929. Address: 519 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Oriental Can Mfg. Co.; b. Feb. 1885, Osaka-fu; s. of Matsunosuke Takasaki; m. Ito. Career: grad. Fisheries Institute 1906; joined Oriental Aquatic Products Co.; went to America and joined Intl. Fishery Co. 1911; founded present firm 1917. Address: Hibarigaoka, Kawabe-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Prof. Toyo Univ. & Rissho Univ.; Pres. Women's Higher Sch.; b. Oct. 1865, Tokyo; s. of Kinosuke Takashima. Career: Prof. Peers' Sch. 1889-96; Prof. Japan Women's Univ. 1897-1907. Address: 10 Nishikata-machi, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Toyo Paper Mfg. Co., Russo-Japanese Lumber Co., Nippon Rayon Pulp Co.; Vice-Pres. Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; b. May 1875, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Kikuzo Takashima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1890; entered business. Address: 14 Shimorokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

M.D.; Physician; Pres. Toyonaika Hospital and Nanko-in Sanatorium; b. Aug. 1861, Kyoto-fu; s. of Morimasa Masuyama, physician. Career: grad. Kyoto Pref. Med. Sch.; Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp Univ.; studied at Med. Coll. Berlin Univ.; Asst. Physician, Internal Dept. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890-96; Lecturer Internal Dept. Saiseigakusha Med. Sch. 1892-1902; representing Tokyo Medical and two other Societies, sent to Hongkong to visit Dr. T. Aoyama who suffered from Pest 1894; founded Toyonaika Hospital in Tokyo 1896; Nanko-in Sanatorium, Chigasaki, Kanagawa-ken 1889. Addresses: 15 Kudan 4-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo; Chigasaki-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; Mem. Imp. Academy; Adviser, Nisshin Life Ins. Co.; b. Mar. 1860, Tokyo; s. of Kohei Takata. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1881; Prof. Tokyo Tech. Sch.; Pres. same; elected M.P. 6 times; Dir. Com. Bureau, Foreign Office 1897; Councillor, Educ. Dept.; Dir. Higher Educ. Bureau; rec'd deg. 1901; went to Europe & America for observation 1914; Minister of Educ. 1915; Mem. House of Peers 1915; Pres. Waseda Univ. Address: 28 Komagome 1-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Prof. Econ. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Dec. 1883 Saga-ken; s. of Kiyoto Takata. Career: grad. Sociology Course, Litt. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1910; Prof. Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch. 1919; Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1920-24; Prof. of Econ. Kyushu Imp. Univ. 1925; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1929. Address: 428 Tonodan Yabushita-cho, Kyoto.

D.E.; Pres. Shomei Gaku-kai; Engr. Elec. Experimental Station & Patents Bureau; b. Feb. 1881, Yamagata-ken; s. of Koetomi Takatsu. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Govt. service; studied in America & Germany; rec'd deg. 1925. Address: 228 Amanuma 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Director of Taiwan Development Co. since 1936; b. Aug. 1892, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Seikichi Takayama. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Commr. same; Commr. Com. & Ind. Dept.; Chief, Registration Sec. Patent Bureau; Secr. Exploitation Bureau; Sec. Chief, same; Chief Secr. to Overseas Minister, 1933; Dir. Exploitation Bureau, Overseas Dept. 1934-36. Address: 18 Komagome Hayashi-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Law Coll. & Dir. Attached Library, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Pacific Relations Committee, Intl. Assn.; b. May 1887, Saitama-ken; s. of Kinzaemon Takayanagi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1912; apptd. Prof. of same 1920; went to Europe and America 1915 & 1923. Address: 253 Hisagi, Zushi-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

Pres. The Manchuria Public Information Assn. (Manshu Koho Kyokai); Lt.-Gen. (reserve); b. Dec. 1869, Kanazawa; s. of late Bunkichi Takayanagi. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. and Mil. Staff Coll.; Pres. Manchuria Daily News. Address: 19 Hatsune-cho, Dairen.

Dir.-Gen. Kwantung Bureau; b. Jan. 1893, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Naomatsu Takebe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; Commr. Home Dept.; Secr. Reconstruction Bureau; Chief, Documents Sec. same; Secr. to Home Minister; Chief, Accounts Sec., Home Dept.; Gov. Akita-ken 1932-35; Chief Polit. Affairs Dept. 1935-36. Address: c/o Kwantung Bureau, Hsinking.

D. Litt.; Dir. & Lecturer Tokyo Butsuri Gakko; Membre de l'Institute international de Sociologie; Mem. Amer. Acad. of Polit. & Social Sci.; b. Mar. 1871, Niigata-ken; s. of Sadao Takebe. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied in Europe & Amer.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer Tokyo Univ. of Com., Tokyo Higher Normal Sch., Waseda Univ., Mil. Acad. and Komazawa Univ.; M.P. 1923-28. Address: 902 Sendagaya 5-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Formosa Sugar Mfg. Co.; b. Apr. 1870, Tokyo; s. of Masamichi Takechi. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; studied Economics in Oahu Univ., Honolulu; established present firm 1900. Address: 13 Ichibei-cho 2-chome, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Dir. Restoration Bureau of National Monument "Horyuji"; Dir. Nat. Monuments Preservation Committee; b. Nov. 1872, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Naoyuki Takeda. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Architect Constr. Bureau Fin. Dept. 1907; Prof. Kyoto Higher Tech. Sch. 1913; Mem. Nat. Monument Preservation Com. 1917; Dir. Nagoya Higher Tech. Sch. 1918; Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1920; Standing Mem. Com. of Promotion of Sc. of Japan, 1933. Address: 4 Koyama Kamifusa-cho, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Dir. Nichinan Sangyo K. K.; b. 1897, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of [illegible] Takeda. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1922; entered Govt. service; Commr. Social Bureau; Chief 1st & 2nd Secs. Overseas Affairs Dept. 1929; sent to S. Amer. 1931 & 1935; Chief South Amer. Sec. Overseas Affairs Dept. Address: 111 Kitazawa-cho 2-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

A.M. (Columbia Univ.); Paymaster Rear-Admiral; Chief, Accounts Dept. Yokosuka Admiralty; b. Apr. 1887, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Matsutaro Takei. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1909; Columbia Univ. 1918; Attaché to Embassy in U. S.; Instructor Naval Academy; Head Instructor, Naval Paymasters' Sch.; Chief 2nd Sec., Gen. Affairs Dept. Naval Tech. Dept.; Chief Accountant Sasebo Naval Station. Address: Yokosuka Admiralty, Yokosuka.

Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; b. Oct. 1865, Saitama-ken; s. of Senzaburo Kiyono; adopted by Tohei Takekoshi. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; Corr. Jiji Shimpo, Osaka Koron and Kokumin Shimbun; Editor, "Sekai no Nippon," Monthly; apptd. Councillor and Secr. Educ. Dept. 1898; went to Europe 1899, and France, where founded Franco-Japanese Assn. 1906; sent to Diet 5 times; apptd. Dir. Imp. Compiling Bureau, Imp. Household Dept.; author "Economical History of Japan" (English). Address: 333 Arai-machi, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Minseito; b. Dec. 1855, Saga-ken; s. of Ryokitsu Taketomi. Career: studied English early; established Private Sch. 1878; Dir. Com. & Ind. Bureau, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Councillor, Finance Dept.; Chief Secr. Cabinet; Minister of Communications in Okuma Cabinet 1914; Minister of Finance, same; elected M.P. 13 times. Address: 13 Kaga-machi 2-chome, Ichigaya, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Amb. to Turkey since 1936; b. Dec. 1884, Saga City; s. of Tokitoshi Taketomi, Peer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp Univ. 1910; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer Legation Mexico; Secr. Leg.; Secr. and Commr. Foreign Office; Chief, 2nd Sec. Com. Bureau; Secr. Agr. & Com. Dept.; Secr. Embassy; Consul-Gen. France; America; Dir. Com. Bureau, Foreign Office 1927-32; Councillor Emb. U. S. A. 1933; Min. to Netherlands 1933-36. Address: Japanese Emb. Stamboul, Turkey.

Dir. Fuel Bureau; Ministry of Com. & Ind.; b. 1889, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Saijiro Takeuchi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Chief Agrl. Adm. Sec. Agr. Bureau; Secr. Com. & Ind. Dept.; Chief Ind. Adm. Sec. Ind. Bureau; Councillor Resources Bureau 1932; Dir. Ind. Bureau 1933-35; Japanese Commr. 6th Gen. Conf. Int'l Agrl. Assn. Rome 1922; Econ. Adviser Kwantung Army 1935-36; Dir. Patent Bureau; Vice-Min. of Com. & Ind. Address: 39 Mita Koun-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Governor Fengtien Prov.; b. 1888. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Chief Civil Adm. Office Dairen; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau Civil Dept. 1932-35; Chief Gen. Affairs Bd. Fengtien Prov. 1935-37. Address: Fengtien Prov. Office Mukden.

Painter of Japanese Style; Court Artist; Mem. Imp. Academy of Arts; b. Nov. 1864, Kyoto. Career: studied Painting with late Bairei Kono; grad. Kyoto Japanese Painting Sch.; Prof. Kyoto Fine & Applied Arts Sch.; same, Kyoto Municipal Painting Sch.; went to China, France and Europe for study 1900. Address: Kodaiji Minami-dori Masuya-cho, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto.

Univ. and Kansai Univ.; elected to Diet 7 times since 1917; Councillor, Meiji Shrine Construction Bureau; Secr. to Home Minister; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1932-34; Dir. Legislation Bureau 1937. Address: 106 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Imp. Acad.; Mem. Nat. Treasures Preservation Committee; Editor "Kokkwa," fine arts magazine; b. Dec. 1873, Tokyo; s. of Kwatei Taki, painter. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Non-Official Staff, Tokyo Imp. Museum; Lecturer Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof.; Commr. Crown Prince's Study; rec'd deg. 1914; went to Europe 1912 & 1926. Address: 226 Kamiosaki 4-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Chosen Match Co.; Chief-Dir. Kobe Exchange; Hon. Consul for Bolivia; Adviser Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Dec. 1874, Nara-ken. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Com. Sch.; Pres. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Address: 1 Sekimori-cho 2-chome, Suma-ku, Kobe.
Consul; b. Jan. 1884, Nagasaki-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; entered diplomatic service 1909. Address: Japanese Consulate, Antung, Manchoukuo.

Pres. Kyodo Fishery Co.; Dir. Kobe Elec. Machinery Co., Asahi Marine Ins. Co., Dairen Central Real Estate Co.; Acting Partner, Tamura Gomei Kaisha; b. Address: 83 Minami-cho, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Secr. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. June 1889, Tokyo; s. of Eijiro Tamura. Career: grad. Eng. Law Dept. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1914; immediately joined present firm. Address: 9 Kawada-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. of Forestry; Mem. National Park Committee; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Expert, Agr. & For. Dept. and Home Dept.; b. Sept. 1890, Okayama-ken; adopted s. of Kisaku Tamura. Career: grad. For. Course, Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Lecturer, Chiba Pref. Horticultural Sch. 1917; same, Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; Non-Commissioned Staff, Home Dept. 1920; rec'd deg. 1920; went to Europe and America to study landscape architecture 1932-34; Non-Commissioned Staff, For. Bureau, Agr. & For. Dept. 1924; Mem. & Mgr. Nat. Park Assn. 1931; Expert, Home Dept. and Agr. & For. Dept. 1933. Address: 225 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Dai-Nippon Drug Mfg. Co.; Prop. Tanabe Gohei Shoten (mfrs., importers and exporters of chemicals & drugs); b. May 1878, Osaka; s. of late Gohei Tanabe. Career: inherited family estate 1916. Address: 21 Dosho-machi 3-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

Vice-Pres. Manchoukuo Privy Council; b. Oct. 1878, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Yoshinobu Tanabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Master Niigata Post Office; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Osaka Communication Adm. Bureau 1911; studied in France; Secr. and Councillor Communication Dept. 1913; Councillor Kwantung Govt. 1915; Gov. Osaka-fu 1927-28; Manchoukuo Privy Councillor 1932; present post since 1937. Address: 11 Nishiki-machi 4-chome, Hsinking.

Painter of Western Style; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; b. Dec. 1886, Tokyo; s. of Shinnosuke Tanabe. Career: grad. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1910; Mem. Nikakai (Oil Painting & Sculpture Society) 1914; won Special Honour in Educ. Dept. Fine Arts Exhibitions; went to France 1923; Examiner, Imp. Academy Fine Arts Exhibition 1925. Address: 100 Tabata-machi, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Pres. Himegawa Electric Power Co.; Mng.-Dir. Keihin Elec. Power Co.; Dir. Kanto Gas Co., Fujigawa Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Toyo Muslin Co.; Fuji-Minobu Ry. Co.; b. Mar. 1879, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Shichibei Tanabe. Career: grad. Kofu Middle Sch.; elected to Diet 4 times; Parl. Vice-Min. of Agr. & Forestry 1936. Address: 19 Kamimeguro 1-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Supervisory Dept. Kwantung Bureau; Chief, Mil. Communications Supervisory Dept. Kwantung Army; b. 1885, Shiga-ken; s. of Prof. Nobushige Tanaka; m. Sizuko Arai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; entered Ry Dept.; Secr. same; Chief Personnel Dept.; Dir. Nagoya Region 1925-35. Address: 1 Yamabuki-cho 1-chome, Hsinking.

Pres. Taito Co. (Importers & Ins. Agents) Dairen; b. Dec. 1890, Yamaguchi-ken. Career: founded present firm 1924; Aud. Dairen Engrg. Works and Taito Nippo[illegible]; Dir. Chi Tung Tobacco Co., Keystone Tobacco Co., A. Lopato & Sons; travelled Europe & Amer. 1918 & 1922. Address: 51 Kokusekisho, Hoshigaura, Dairen.

Pres. Tokai Kogyo K. K., Nippon Kagaku Kogyo K. K., Yashiro Paper Mfg. Co., Fujigawa Elec. Light Co., Oshima Steel Works, Asano Cement Co.; b. Aug. [?]; s. of Shuzo Okawa; adopted by Ine Tanaka. Address: [?] Nezu Miyanaga-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Kyoto Elec. Light Co.; Dir. Kansai Kyodo Elec. Power Co., Daido Elec. Power Co.; b. [?], Kyoto. Career: Revenue Inspector; Dir. Kyoto Elec. Light Co. 1919. Address: 55 Higashiyama Kamitakano, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

D.L.; Pres. Waseda Univ. since 1931; b. Feb. 1876, Nagano-ken; s. of Shunosuke Tanaka. Career: grad. Polit. Dept. Waseda Univ. 1896; studied in Europe and America as student of Waseda Univ.; apptd. B.E.; Mgr. Yamato Hotel, Hoshigaura; b. Jan. 1895, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Y. Tanaka, dist. headman. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1920; joined S. M. R. Co.; went abroad for study 1923-24; Mgr. Yamato Hotel Hsinking 1927; Mgr. Dining Car Service (S.M.R.) 1931. Address: Bungalow 37 Hoshigaura Park, Dairen.

Dir. & Mgr. Kobe & Osaka Branches, Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; b. May 1886, Tokyo-fu; s. of Ginzo Tanaka, samurai. Career: joined Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; apptd. Dir. of same Jan. 1932. Address: 42 Shimoyamate-dori 8-chome, Kobe.

Dir. Finance Bureau Manchoukuo Fin. & Com. Dept.; b. 1899, Wakayama-ken. Career: served Finance Dept. Japan; went to Europe & America; Chief Kawasaki Taxation Office; Ryogoku Taxation Office. Address: 7 Nishiki-machi 3-chome, Hsinking.

D. Com.; M.P.; Prof. Meiji Univ.; b. Oct. 1891, Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Prof. Meiji Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1921; studied Economics & Social Problems in Europe & America 1921-22; rec'd deg. 1925. Address: 396 Kashiwagi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Secr. Text Book Compilation, Educational Sec., S. M. R. Co.; b. Sept. 1900, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Rosaku Tanaka; m. Sadako. Career: grad. Litt. Coll., Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Teacher, Middle Sch., Normal Sch. and later Girls' High Sch. Address: 1 of 8 Mimuro-machi 2-chome, Dairen.

Japanese Consul-Gen., Tsitsihar; b. July 1884; s. of Buheita Tanaka, agriculturist. Career: grad. Tung Wen Coll., Shanghai 1906; entered Foreign Service 1907; served in China, Manchoukuo, America, etc. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Tsitsihar, Manchoukuo.

President Central Bank of Manchou since 1936; b. Jan. 1889, Saga-ken; s. of Keiji Tanaka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Bank of Japan; Mgr.
