Pres. Chugai Shogyo Shimpo since 1934; b. Jan. 1877, Kyoto-fu; s. of Jinzaburo Tanaka. Career: grad. Consular Course, Tokyo Higher Commercial Sch. 1898; Consul at Singapore, Hongkong and Seattle; Secr., Foreign Office; Chief, 1st and 2nd Sec., Com. Bureau; Councillor, Embassy, Washington; Dir .Com. Bureau and Information Bureau, Foreign Office; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs; Pres. Japan Times; Ambassador to U.S.S.R. 1925-30; sent to Manchoukuo 1932. Address: 11 Konno, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Pres. Kokuchukai; Chairman Meijikai and Kokusei Bungei-kai; Prop. Daily Dai-Nippon; b. Nov. 1861, Tokyo; s. of Yoshiatsu Minamoto (popular as Genryu Tada), physician; m. 1897. Career: in 1877, after being tormented with sceptism was awakened to the fact of the spirit of nationalism having not sufficiently spread and then devoted himself to studies; in 1881 started propagation of nationalism and has worked in that cause by pen and speech for the past half century founding two patriotic societies "Kokuchukai" and "Meijikai" in the interval; in 1929 had Imp. Cup conferred upon him in recognition of his meritorious services in the cause of education and also certificate awarded by Education Department for the same; successfully conducted petition movement for 4 years for institution of the "Meijisetsu"; started campaign for upholding the cause of the national polity by taking the opportunity of the success of the said petition movement; on May 11, 1935 opened "New lecture on the National Polity of Japan" and started a monthly for the purpose; in June, 1935 went over to Manchoukuo and lectured on the national polity in the presence of the Emperor; after return home via Chosen set about editing "Shishiwo Zenshu." Address: c/o Shinkoen, Ichinoe-machi, Edogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Agric.; Prof. Agriculture and Economic Botany. Taihoku Imp. Univ.; b. Nov. 1885 at Osaka; s. of Tasitirô Tanaka, vice-pres. Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Stock Exchange. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Hon. fellow Royal Horticultural Soc. London; collaborator U. S. Dept. of Agric.; Dir. Tanaka Citrus Experiment Station; Mem. Botanical Soc. of America, France and India; Editor Studia Citrologica. Horticulture Tropicale; Scientific contributions "Citrus Studies," "Monograph of Satsuma Orange" (Agr. Assn. Prize), etc. Address: Hokuto Hot Spring, Taihoku, Formosa.

Dr. Sc.; Mem. House of Peers; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Nippon Rômazikwai; b. Sept. 1856; s. of Tôzô Tanakadate, samurai. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1882; studied Elec. and Magnetism at Glasgow Univ. and Berlin Univ. Address: 144 Zôsigaya-mati, Koisikawa-ku, Tôkyô.
M.P.; b. Aug. 1880; s. of Takazaemon Tange. Career: elected Representative 6 times from Aichi-ken; Parl. Councillor of Finance 1936-37. Address: 24 Kaga-cho 1-chome, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 6th Div. since 1935; b. 1882, Okayama-ken. Career: grad. Mil Academy 1904; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in England & France; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief Staff, 3rd Div.; sec. Chief, Gen. Staff Office; Imp. Army Delegate to the League of Nations; Chief, Research Dept. War Office; Comdr. 2nd Brig.; Comdr. Tokyo Bay Fortress 1934. Address: c/o 6th Div. Hdqrs., Kumamoto.

Minister to Austria & Hungary since April 1936; b. Feb. 1889, Kumamoto-ken; bro. of Masaichi Tani. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; apptd. Eléve-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer and Secr. of Embassy; after long service in Europe, apptd. Councillor, Foreign Office and Secr. to Foreign Minister; Chief 1st Sec. Asia Bureau; Secr. Emb. America 1927; Dir. Asia Bureau 1930; Councillor Emb. Manchoukuo 1933-36. Address: c/o Japanese Legation, Vienna, Austria.

Mem. Board of Council Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, Tokyo; b. Nov. 1885, s. of Hikosaburo Tanida; m. 1908. Career: grad. Kobe Com. Sch. 1902; joined Kobe Branch of present firm; Sub-Mgr. Kobe and Osaka; Mgr. Metal Dept. Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Mng.-Dir. Address: 1 Tango-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
Mng.-Dir. Osaka Yogyo Cement K.K.; Osaka Yogyo K.K.; Dir. Yingkow Yogyo K.K.; b. July 1879, Hyogo-ken. Address: 43 of 15 Ohama-Kitamachi, Sakai City.

Novelist; b. 1886, Tokyo. Career: grad. 1st Higher Sch. 1908; studied at Japanese Litt. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909-10; Adviser, Taisho Cinema Co. 1920-21; went to China 1918 & 1926. Address: 6 Shimomiyazuka 1-chome, Uchide, Seido-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

M.P.; b. Oct. 1867, Osaka; s. of Mataichiro Tomita; later adopted by Genshichi Tanomogi. Career: grad. Higher Sch.; Corr. Hochi Shimbun; Dir. & Business Mgr. same; Pres. Teikoku News Agency; elected M.P. 8 times since 1915; Communications Min. 1936-37. Address: 13 Higashi Misuji-machi, Asakusa-ku, Tokyo.

Afghan Minster to Tokyo since 1933; b. 1897, Kaboul, Afghanistan; s. of M. Zaman Khan Tarzi. Career. grad. Habibia Coll.; diplomatic service for 15 years; Minister to Paris 1927. Address: Afghan Legation, 7 Aoba-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
French Commercial Attaché, Tokyo; b. 1886 at Paris. Address: 1822 Kaijo Bldg., Tokyo.

LL.B. (Hastings Coll. of Law, Univ. of Calif.); Attorney-at-law in T.H.; Real Estate Broker; b. May 1904, Kauai, T.H.; s. of Ihachi Tashiro, merchant. Career: taught public elementary sch. in Hawaii, 1921-25; grad Hastings Coll. and rec'd deg. 1932; admitted to practise law in all courts of T.H. 1932; elected as Rep. from Kauai 1934; Mem. Legislature of Hawaii, 1935; Chairaman Rules Committee and Mem. Judiciary Committee; Pes. West Kauai Civic Club 1935-36; Pres. Kauai Japanese Baseball Ass'n. Address: (Office) Lihue, Kauai, Hawaii. (Residence) Hanapepe, Kauai, Hawaii.

Chief 1st Sec. Information Bureau Foreign Office; b. May 1896, Tokyo ; s. of Dr. Yoshinori Tashiro. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer Switzerland; Secr. Emb. Italy; Commr. Foreign Office 1926; Member 1st Sec. Asia Bureau; Consul Tientsin 1927; Hsinking 1929-33; Chief 3rd Sec. Information Bureau. Address: 10 Nishigoken-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Sculptor; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch.; Mem. Imp. Academy of Arts; b. Feb. 1880, Wakayama-ken; s. of Kisuke Tatehata. Career: grad. Address: 1040 Nippori Watanabe-machi, Arakawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Kaigai Kogyo K.K.; Dir. Peru Raw Cotton Co. and South America Real Estate Co.; b. Mar. 1874, Fukui-ken; s. of Seishin Tatsui. Career: grad. Univ. Course, Kyoto Bungaku-Ryo; studied at Sc. Address: 653 Kitasenzoku-machi, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

D.Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Mar. 1888, Tokyo; s. of late Dr. Kingo Tatsuno. Career: grad. French Law Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; Lecturer of French Litt. Keio & Waseda Univs.; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied in Europe 1921-23; rec'd deg. 1929. Address: 928 Komaba-cho, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Feb. 1872, Iwami; s. of Sukenobu Tawara; bro. of Magoichi Tawara. Career grad. Metallurgical Dept. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; studied in Germany 1899; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; rec'd deg. 1907; rec'd Imp. Academy Prize for study of Japanese Swords 1921. Address: 232 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Adviser Minseito; b. May 1869, Shimane-ken; s. of Sukenobu Tawara. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1895; Vice-Pres. Special Land Research Bureau, Chosen; Gov. Pres. Kobe Univ. of Com.; Adviser, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Mar. 1872, Nagasaki-ken; bro. of Shuzaburo Tazaki. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Pres. Nankai Ry. Co., Kishiwada Spinning Co.; Dir. Daido Elec. Power Co., Kyodo Trust Co., Osaka Elec. Power Co.; b. Dec. 1896, Osaka; s. of Jinyomo Terada. Career: grad Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. 1920. Address: 1 Uchide Hirono, Seido-mura, Hyogo-ken.

1st Secr. & Charge d'Affaires Legation to Argentina; b. Apr. 1892, Tokyo-fu; s. of Kogoro Terajima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; joined Mitsubishi Bank; apptd. Commr. n: TERAJIMA, Kozo (Onoe Kikugoro, 6th) 寺島幸三

Trade Bureau; Patent Bureau; Com. Affairs Bureau. Address: 105 Aoyama Kita-machi 4-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Inspector Kanto Branch, Canada Sun Life Ins. Co.; b. Feb. 1862, Fukui; s. of Jihei Terao, samurai. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Pres. Local Educ. Societies. Address: 541 Shimo-Meguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.
Mgr. Yamato Hotel, Mukden; b. June 1877; s. of Masaki Terasawa, samurai. Career: went to America to inspect hotel business; Dir. Nanman Ryokan. Address: 29 Naniwa-dori, Mukden.

Lawyer; Lecturer, Manchoukuo Law Coll.; Non-Official Staff, S. M. R. Tokyo 1911; Non-Official Staff, Tsingtao Army Commander-in-Chief's Hdqrs. 1922; joined the bar at Dairen 1924; Legal Adviser, Manchuria Bank. Address: Kirishima-cho, Dairen.

Count; General; Supreme Comdr. of Japanese Troops in North China; b. Aug. 1879; s. of Count Seiki Terauchi, ex-Prime Minister. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1900 and Mil. Staff Coll; Instructor Mil. Independent Garrison; sent to Germany 1912; Comdr. 4th Div. 1932-34; Taiwan Army 1934; War Min. 1936-37; Inspector-Gen. of Mil. Educ. 1937. Adress: 606 Yoyogi Hatsudai-machi, Shibuya-ku, Toko.

Dir. Audit Bureau; b. 1888, Saga-ken. Career; grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; entered Finance Dept.; Secr.-Gen. Sapproro Revenue Supt. Office 1931; Acting Pres. Manchoukuo Supervisory Council. Address: 501 Higashi Choyoro, Hsinking.

Mng.-Dir. Toshin Warehouse Co. since 1931; b. Sept. 1885, Kyoto; s. of Tomonori Teshima. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1906; served Mitsui Bussan Kaisha 1906-24; Mitsui Gomei Kaisha 1924-31; became Mgr. Immovables Dept. Address: 28 Higashi Shinano-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.
B.A.; B.D.; Missionary; b. Sept. 1888, Port Elgni, Ontario, Canada; s. of John M. Thede, labourer; m. Viola M. Wendt. Addrss: 500 Shimo-Ochiai 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

M.A. (Oxon); F.R.G.S.; Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc., Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. & Hosei Univ.; Literary Adviser, N.Y.K., Govt. Rys. and Board of Tourist Industry; b. May 1895, Wolverhampton England; s. of John Thomas. Career: studied at Univ. of Oxford 1920-23; Univ. of Paris 1923-26. Address: 7 Fujimi-cho 2-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

British Consul at Osaka since 1935; b. Apr. 1904; s. of H. C. Thomas, schoolmaster. Career: educated at Alleyn's Sch. Dulwich, Sidney; Scessea Coll. Cambridge; Yale Univ.; Student Interpreter, Japan 1927; Vice-Consul 1930. Address: c/o British Consulate-General, Osaka.
Swiss Minister to Japan; Diplomat; b. in Baden, Switzerland. Address: 1 Shimoniban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Manchuria Elec. Co.; b. 1886, Kaiping-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. Tokyo; Chief Foreign Affairs Dept. Mil. Hdqrs. Three Eastern Prov.; Gov. Fengtien Prov.; Chairman North Eastern Communications Committee 1931; visited Japan 1932; Communications Minister 1932-35; Ind. Min. 1935-37, accorded privilege of former post. Address: Manchuria Electric Co., Hsinking.

n: TINGE, W. S. Y. 丁士源
t: General; Auditor Central Bank of Manchou since 1935; Ex-Minister of Manchoukuo to Japan; b. 1876, Wu Hsien Chekiang, China. Career: studied at Tientsin Nav. Sch. 1893-96; joined Imp. Army commanded by Marshal Baron Sun Chin 1897-1901; studied at Lincoln's Inn London 1901-4; returned to Peking 1904 and organized 4th & 6th Divs with Marshal Ma Yukun and Tuan Chi-jui; Dept. Chief Imp. Army Council 1905-7; attended 2nd Hague Conf. as Chinese Imp. Mil. Delegate 1907-8; Life Mem. Royal Geog. Soc. London 1907; Judge Advocate Gen. Imp. Chi. Army & Navy 1907-11; Dir. Gen. Metro. Police & Gendarmerie Training Quarters 1908-11; Sup't. Customs Hankow 1912-16; Mng.-Dir. Peking-Suiyuan Ry. 1916-20; Mem. Defence Committee 1916-20; A.D.C. personal to the President of China 1917-20; Mng.-Dir. Peking-Hankow Rys. 1918-20; Chief Aviation Dept. 1918-20; Mil. Mission to Siberia 1919-20; Dir.-Gen. Lung-yen Iron Mining Co. 1916-20; Editor Tientsin Daily News 1922-24; Vice-Chairman Fin. Readjustment Commn. 1924-27; Chairman Domestic Loan Service 1924-29; Dir. Sino-Franco Bank and Exchange Bank of China 1926-30; Manchukuo Chief Executive's personal rep. in Europe 1932-33; Manchoukuo Min. to Japan 1933-35. Publications: World Navy 1909; Notes & Comments to the Rules and Regulations of War on Land 1911 etc. Decorations; Chevalier Legion d'Honneur 1906; 5th Order of Merit, Republic of China 1920; 2nd Class Excellent Corps 1914; 2nd Class, Civil Tiger, 1915; 2nd Class Presious Excellent Corps 1917; 2nd Order of Merit, Manchou Tikuo 1934. Address: (office) c/o Central Bank of Manchou, Hsinking.
Count; Fleet Admiral; died on May 30, 1934. (See 1934 issue).

Councillor of Communications; Parl. Vice-Minister of Educ. 1932-34. Address: 8 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Ambassador to Germany since October 1937; b. Dec. 1882, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Toshikazu Togo. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Eleve-Consul; 3rd Secr. Legation, Switzerland; 2nd Secr., Embassy, Berlin; Chief, 1st Sec., America & Europe Bureau, Foreign Office; 1st Secr. Embassy, Washington 1925; Councillor, Embassy Berlin; present post since 1937. Address: 15 Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Japan Wireless Telegraph Co.; b. July 1882, Tokyo; s. of Vice-Adml. Masamichi Togo. Career: grad. Law and Polit. Sci. Depts. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. House of Peers since 1911; Mem. Imp. Govt. Tariff Committee, Dumping Committee, Text Book Committee. Address: 66 Aoyama Minami-cho 2-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M.D. (1914); Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; b. Mar. 1877, Gifu-ken; s. of Doei Tohyama, physician. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; studied Dermatology at P. G. Course; Prof. Sendai Med. Coll. 1907; studied in Europe & America 1917; Prof. Tohoku Imp. Univ. 1918; despatched to Europe & America 1935. Address: 3481 Nerima Minami-cho 1-chome, Itabashi-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. Tokyo Stock Exchange; Chief Dir. Nagoya Raw Cotton Exchange; Pres. Tokabu Daiko Co.; Prop. Tohyama Shoten; b. Jan. 1885; Saitama-ken; s. of Chikazo Tohyama. Career: completed Keika Com. Sch.; engaged in present business since 1918; became Com. Councillor, Tokyo Stock Exchange; one of high taxpayers in Tokyo-fu. Address: 5 Sakamoto-cho, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo.

Lt.-Gen.; Chief Staff Kwantung Army; b. Dec. 1884, Tokyo; s. of Lieut.-Gen. Eikyo Tojo. Career: grad. Mil. Staff Coll. 1915; Aide-de-Camp War Office; Resident Officer Germany 1919; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll. 1922; Chief Mobilization Sec.; Comdr. Inf. 1st Reg.; Sec. Chief Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. 24th Inf. Brig. 1934-35 Gendarmerie Comdr., Kwantung Army 1935-37. Address: c/o Kwantung Army Hdqrs., Hsinking.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; b. Feb. 1892, Tokyo-fu; s. of Viscount Yoritomo Toki; adopted by Yoritoshi Toki Career: studied at Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; established Tokyo Provisions Co.; made inspection tour of Europe and America 1921-23; Mem. House of Peers 1922; Councillor, War Dept. in Inukai Cabinet 1931; Parl. Vice-Min. for War 1932-36. Address: 38 Nagasumi-cho. Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

ex-Amb. to Turkey; Hogakushi (B.L.); b. Mar. 1884, Tokyo; e. s. of Prince Iyesato Tokugawa. Career: grad. Peers' Sch.; Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. 1909; passed Diplomatic and Consular Service Exam.; Attaché, Embassy, London 1910-13; Secr. Foreign Office, Tokyo 1913-18; Priv. Secr. to Foreign Minister 1914-15; 2nd Secr. Legation, Peking 1918-19; 1st Secr. of same 1919-21; 1st Secr. Embassy London 1921-25; Councillor or same 1925; Consul-Gen. Australia and New Zealand 1925-29; Minister to Canada 1929-34; Mem. Japanese Suite to H.R.H. Duke of Gloucester, during latter's visit to Japan on Garter Mission May 1929; Amb. to Turkey 1934-37. Address: 330 Sendagaya 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Prince (cr. 1884); Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Board of Councillors, Peers' Sch.; Peers Club; Japan Red Cross Soc.; b. July 1863, Tokyo; s. of late Lord Yoshiyori Tokugawa, and became heir to the last of Shoguns 1908. Career: apptd. Gov. Shizuoka Clan 1869; resigned 1871; studied in England 1877-82; on return home apptd. Lord-in-Waiting Jako Hall; made inspection tour of Europe & Amer. 1910; Pres. Saiseikai (Imp. Gift Charitable Foundation); Delegate to Wash. Disarm. Conf. 1921; attended Int'l Parl. Conf. in London and Int'l Red Cross Soc. Conf. in Brussels 1930; Pres. House of Peers 1903-33; travelled abroad in 1933. Address: 330 Sendagaya 1-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Prince; Mem. House of Peers; Vice-Pres. Red Cross Society; b. Dec. 1886; s. of Marquis Tokuyasu Tokugawa. Career: attended Red Cross Society Assembly, Geneva 1920. Address: 34 Sarugaku. Shibuya-ku. Tokyo.

Baron; Lt.-Gen.; Comdr. Army Flying Corps; b. July 1884, Tokyo-fu; s. of late Count Atsumori Tokugawa; m. Chikako, sister of Viscount Tadaaki Matsudaira. Career: grad. Mil. Staff Coll. 1903; resided in Europe for study of aviation; apptd. Comdr. Aviation 1st Reg.; Dir. Akeno Aviation Sch.; Dir. Tokorozawa Aviation Sch. 1934-36. Adress: c/o War Office, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; Spec. Writer, Osaka Mainichi & Tokyo Nichi-Nichi; b. Jan. 1863, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Ikkei Tokutomi. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ.; established Minyu-sha; published "Kokumin-no-Tomo" 1887, and Kokumin Shimbun 1890; Councillor Home Dept. 1897; went to Europe and visited L. Tolstoy; nominated Peer 1911. Publications "National History of Japan in Recent Age" (in Japanese). Address: 2832 Sanno 1-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

Sr. Mng.-Dir. Konoshima Artificial Fertizer Co.; Jr. Mng.-Dir. Dai Nippon Kagaku Kogyo K.K., Dir. Nippon Oils & Fats Co.; Auditor Osaka Alkali Land Co.; Chairman Glycerine Sale Co.; Dir. Taiwan Fertilizer Co.; Nihon Sulphur Co.; b. Dec. 1880, Aomori-ken; s. of Kinjiro Tomabechi. Career: grad. Applied Chem. Course, Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch. 1903; joined Abe Paper Mfg. Co.; Osaka Sulphate Soda Co. 1904. Address: 4 Maruyama, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Emb. London; b. Aug. 1890, Tokyo; s. of Masaaki Tomii, Privy Councillor. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; 3rd Secr. Embassy, Washington; 2nd Secr. Emb. London; Consul-Gen. Ottawa; 1st Secr. Emb. Canada; 1st Secr. Emb. Berlin 1929; Chief, Documents Sec. Foreign Office; Consul-Gen. San Francisco 1934-36; attended Washington Conf. Address: c/o Japanese Emb. London.

b. October 1886, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Sueichiro Tominaga. Career: grad. Nagasaki Higher Commercial School 1909; entered Kawashima Textile Works; engaged in Textile Trade Business in Europe 2 years; established Nihon Ind. Drugs Co. 1916; entered Watanabe Trading Co. 1917; entered S. M. R. Co. 1919; went to Europe & America 1923; Councillor same; Dir. South Manchuria Electric Co.; Mng.-Dir. Showa Steel Works. Address: Suimeiso, Hoshigaura, Dairen.

M.P.; b. Oct. 1872, Kochi-ken; s. of Toraji Tomita. Career: studied Politics in Geiyo Gakusha; joined Democratic Movement under late Count Taisuke Itagaki; established Kochi Shimbun; Pres. & Chief Editor, same; elected M.P. 10 times since 1908; Chief Dir. Minseito; Pres. Teikoku News Agency; High Speed Steel Co.; Nihon Spinning & Weaving Machines Co.; Speaker House of Rep. 1936-37. Address: 22 Hachimandori 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Taido Electric Co. Ssupinkai since 1930; b. Feb. 1892, Hyogo-ken; s. of Yasukichi Tomita. Career: grad. Elec. Course, Tokyo Engrg. Univ. 1916; entered Elec. Dept. S. M. R. Co.; with South Manchuria Elec. Co. 1926-30. Address: Nishimon-uye, Hoshigaura Koen, Dairen.

Pres. Ind. Bank of Manchou; b. Aug. 1883, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Ichiro Tomita. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; entered Finance Dept.; went to Europe 1909; Mgr. Monopoly Bureau 1913; Chief Nat. Loans same; attended Wash. Conf. 1921; Dir. Fin. Sec. Fin. Bureau; Chief Nat. Treasury Sec. Finance Bureau 1924; Fin. Commr. in Eng. & Amer. 1934-36. Address: Ind. Bank of Manchou, Hsinking.

b. Apr. 1885, Aichi-ken; s. of Yasusaburo Tomiyasu. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; entered Communications Dept.; Commr. Savings Bureau; Secr. Com. Dept.; Chief, Documents Sec. Minister's Secretariat; Dir. Electric Bureau; Dir. Accounts Bureau 1931-35; Vice Minister of Com. 1936-37. Address: 1070 Ikebukuro 2-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Tokyo University of Litt. & Sc.; Prof. Nippon Women's Univ.; Lecturer Nihon Women's Univ.; Dir. Japanisch-Deutsches Kulturinstitut; b. Nov. 1876, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Hayami Tomoeda. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; went to England 1904; Prof. 5th Higher Sch.; Assi. Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; studied in America, Germany & England 1910; Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1914; Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; represented Shintoist at Preliminary Meeting of World Religions Peace Conf. Geneva, and stayed in Germany 1928; went to Europe as Japanese Dir. of Japaninstitut Berlin 1934; went to America 1935. Address: 24 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Nov. 1882, Tottori-ken; s. of Tazo Toyoda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Vice-Councillor, Hokkaido Ry. Adm. Bureau; Inspector, Ry. Dept,; joined the bar; elected M.P. 3 times; went to Europe & America 1924; Parl. Councillor, Finance Dept. 1934-36. Address: 271 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral; Dir. Mil. Affairs Bureau, Navy Office; b. May 1885, Oita-ken; s. of Susumu Toyoda. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1905; Nav. Staff Coll.; Comdr. "Kuma"; Mem. Tech. Council, Nav. Constr. Dept.; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; Captain "Yura"; Chief. 1st Sec., Educ. Bureau of Navy; Capt. "Hyuga," Chief Staff Combined Fleet; Dir. Educ. Bureau of Navy. Address: 518 Shimouma-machi 3-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Yasuda Trust Co.; Dir. Yasuda Hozensha; Vice-Pres. Trust Assn.; b. Feb. 1880, Yamagata-ken; s. of Shigemi Tozawa. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Teikoku Marine Transport Ins. Co.; went to Amer. to investigate ins. 1917; Chief Fire Ins. Dept. 1921; transferred to Yasuda Hozensha 1922. Address: 27 Morimoto-cho 1-chome, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Central Bank of Manchou since 1936; b. 1881, Shuangcheng-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad. Paoting Law Coll.; Chief, Adm. Dept. Heilungkiang Prov. 1915; Adviser, State Council, Peiping 1917; Chief, Finance Dept. Kirin Prov.; Pres. Yingkow Prov. Bank; Magistrate, Kichang-tao & Foreign Affairs Commr. Changchun, 1918; Magistrate Pinkiang-tao and For. Commr. Harbin, 1922; Chinese Repr. to Sino-Soviet Conf. 1929; Gov. Chientao Prov. 1934-36. Address: c/o Central Bank of Manchou, Hsinking.

Chief, Tsitsihar High Procurator's Office since 1935; b. Feb. 1883, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Kirin Law Coll. 1908; Chief Procurator Kirin District Court, 1911; Magistrate, Changling-hsien (Kirin Prov.), Lishou-hsien, Ningan-hsien, & Yenki-hsien (Fengtien Prov.), 1920-29; Chief, Kirin High Procurator's Office 1932-35. Address: c/o High Procurator's Office, Tsitsihar.

Pres. Manchoukuo Privy Council; b. 1884, Shenyang-hsien, Fengtien. Career: studied in Mil. Academy, Tokyo; Staff Officer, Military Gov.'s Office, Heilungkiang 1920; Chief Staff, Military Gov.'s Office, and Acting Gov. Kirin 1923; Councillor, General's Office, Fengtien 1926; Councillor, Public Peace Hdqrs. Three Eastern Provs. 1928; Gov. Mukden Arsenal, 1927; Chairman Govt. Committee, Liaoning Prov. 1930; Gov. Fengtien Prov. 1931-34; Minister of Civil Affairs 1932-35. Address: Privy Council, Hsinking.
Councillor, Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept. since 1937; b. 1861, Mongolia. Career: Inspector-Gen. Chekiang; Privy Councillor 1932-37. Address: Imp. Household Dept. Hsinking.

D. Sc.; Prof. of Petrology, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept. 1893, Tokyo; s. of Prof. Shogoro Tsuboi; m. Yuri Hirayama 1924. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917 apptd. Asst. of same; sent abroad for study 1921-23; Asst. Prof. 1921; rec'd deg. 1926; Prof. 1928; went to Canada and U.S.A. to attend Pacific Science Congress and Int'l Geological Congress 1933; rec'd Imp. Prize from Imp. Acad. for study on Genesis of igneous rocks 1934. Address: 423 Nakazato-cho, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Gov. Manshu Takushoku Kosha; b. June 1884, Saga-ken; s. of Buntaro Tsubokami. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1909; entered Foreign Office and served as Eleve-Consul, Attache, Cons-Gen., Secr. of Emb. attached to Consulate-Gen. in Tsitsihar, London and Hongkong; returned home 1923; Chief 2nd & 3rd Secs. Asia Bureau; Chief Fin. Sec. Foreign Office; Chief Cultural Work Dept. 1929-34; Vice-Min. of Overseas Affairs. Address: 14 Oyama-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Kanegafuchi Spinning Co.; b. 1881, Aichi-ken; s. of Yoshiroku Nishiyama, later adopted by late Oto Tsuda. Career: grad. Law Dept. Keio Univ. 1907; entered present firm; promoted to present post, 1930. Address: 32 Matsugae-cho, Chitose-mura, Mishima-gun, Osaka-fu.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Mar. 1883, Okayama-ken; s. of Daizaburo Tsugita. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Commr. Ishikawa-ken; Secr. Home Dept.; Councillor Ry Dept.; Supt. Home Dept.; Chief Health Ins. Dept. Social Bureau; Gov. Ibaraki-ken; Dir. Civil Engrg. Bureau, Local Bureau, & Police Bureau, Home Dept.; Vice-Minister of Home Affairs 1931; Dir. Legislation Bureau of Cabinet 1936-37. Address: 41 Otsuka Naka-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.
M.D.; Surgeon; b. Mar. 1886, Fukui-ken. Career: grad. Medical Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1911; Prof. same Univ. 1913-26; Consulting Surgeon. Address: 52 Kumochi-cho 2-chome, Fukiai-ku, Kobe.

Dr. Litt.; Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir. Historical Materials Compiling Bureau; Mem. Imp. Academy; Mem. National Treasures Preservation Committee; b. Apr. 1877, Tokyo; s. of Zenjiro Tsuji. Career: grad. Japanese Historical Course, Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; rec'd deg. 1909; went to Europe & America 1911. Address: 783 Totsuka-machi 4-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Pres. Hiroshima Univ. of Litt. & Sci. b. Sept. 1872; Hyogo-ken; s. of Hideo Tsukahara. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1902; studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Columbia Univs. 1902-05; apptd. Prof. Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch; Inspector, Educ. Dept. 1905-25; Dir. Shizuoka Higher Sch. 1925-27; Dir. Tokyo Higher Sch. 1927-34. Address: 15 Fujimi-cho, Hiroshima City.

Chief, 2nd Section, America Bureau, Foreign Office; b. June 1896, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Tohki Tsukamoto; m. Setsuko Masato. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1921; apptd. Commr. Foreign Office, service in Treaty Bureau 1922-25; Diplomatic Probationer, service in France 1925-28; 3rd Secretary of Embassy, Brazil 1928-31; Consul at Amoy 1933-35. Address: 467 Daita 1-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Bank of Japan since 1933; b. in Oita-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; Bank of Japan; went to America & Europe, 1920-22; Chief Inspection Sec. same; Dir. Business Bureau 1931. Address: 16 Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Adviser Nagoya Bank; Dir. Toyo Warehouse Co.; b. Mar. 1863, Aichi-ken; adopted s. of Yasuzo Tsunekawa, landlord. Career: grad. Aichi-ken Normal Sch.; joined Tsushima Bank 1901; became Dir. when it was merged into Nagoya Bank, 1907. Address: 2 Enaka-cho 1-chome, Nishi-ku, Nagoya.

Pres. Toho Gas Co.; Dir. Tokyo Gas Co., Tokyo Gas By-Products Co.; b. Mar. 1879, Oita-ken; s. of Otohei Tsuru. Career: grad. Doshisha Univ. 1900, Osaka Higher Tech. Sch. 1904; Dir. Keihin Cokes Co., Kyushu Gas Co., Godo Gas Co. Address: 52 Isarago-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Harbin since 1937; b. April 1895 at Shin-machi, Gunma-ken; s. of Yoshinari Tsurumi, businessman; m. Eiko, d. of Yuzuru Fujita. Career: entered Foreign Office 1922; Vice-Consul Tientsin, 1923; Los Angeles, 1924; Secr. Embassy Washington D.C. 1927; Secr. Foreign Office, 1929; Embassy, Hsinking 1932; Consul at Portland U. S. A. 1934. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Harbin.

Pres. Tokyo Mouselin-de-Laine Co.; Vice-Pres. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Imperial Invention Assn.; Dir. Nippon Oil Co.; b. September 1873, Kanazawa; s. of Arinari Tsurumi, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; Pres. Com. Museum, Agr. & Com. Dept.; Dir. Yawata Iron Yorks; Dir. Fisheries Bureau 1918; Dir. Com. Bureau 1920; Vice-Minister of Agr. & Com. 1924; Chief Secr. Italian Int'l Exhibition; toured Europe, America and China; Special Committee Mem. Allied Powers Econ. Conf. during World War. Address: 12 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M P.; Writer and Publicist; b. Jan. 1885, Okayama-ken; s. of Yoshinori Tsurumi. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; apptd. Secr. and Councillor, Ry. Dept.; sent to China, Europe and America; Chief, Gen. Affairs Sec. Traffic Bureau, Ry. Dept ; canvassed through Amer. on Anti-Japanese problems 1924; went again to America 1927; toured Australia 1937. Address: 38 Sakurada-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Gov. Bank of Japan; b. January 1888, Takamatsu City; s. of late Masami Tsushima. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; Councillor Fin. Ministry; Secr. to Fin. Min.; Mem. Delegation to Chinese Tariff Spec. Conf. 1925; Fin. Commr. stationed abroad 1927; Attaché, Embassies in England, France & U. S. A.; Mem. Delegation to 8th League of Nations Assembly Geneva 1927; Del. to Int'l Conf. for Abolition of Import & Export Prohibitions & Restrictions Geneva 1927 & 1928; Mem. Econ. Consultative Committee, League of Nations 1928; Mem. Delegation to London Nav. Conf. 1930; Delegate to Reparations Conf. at Lausanne 1932; Dir. Finance Bureau, Finance Dept. 1934; Vice-Min. of Finance 1934-36. Address: 62 Shimoniban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Polit. Affairs Bureau Manchoukuo Foreign Office; b. Nov. 1896, Chiba-ken; s. of Dr. Yaoju Tsutsui. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1920; joined Mitsubishi Trading Co. 1920; entered Japanese Foreign Office 1921; attached Embassy in Belgium; attended 5th & 6th League of Nations Assemblies Geneva; Chief, 2nd Sec. & 3rd Sec. Information Bureau 1930-34; 1st Sec. Information Bureau 1930-34; 1st Secr. Japanese Emb. 1934-35; entered Manchoukuo Foreign Office 1935. Address: Foreign Office, Hsinking.

Judge, Manchoukuo Supreme Court; b. Jan. 1885, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Toshichi Tsutsui; m. 1915. Career: grad. Chuo Univ.; entered judicial service 1915; Judge 1917; Judge Kumagaya Divisional Office of Urawa Local Court; Judge, High Court of Kwantung Govt. 1921; Dept. Chief of same 1923-33; Judge and Chief of Kirin High Court 1933, present post since June 1934. Address: 403 Keiminro, Dojigai, Hsinking.

Chief Imp. Guards, Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept. since 1934; b. 1886, Shanhuang. Career: grad. Fuchien Prov. Higher Sch.; Instructor, Amoy Middle Sch.; Peers' Law Coll.; Mil. Councillor; Staff of Gen. Staff; Chief Guards Corps, Chief Executive's Residence. Address: Imp. Household Dept., Hsinking.

M.A. (Univ. of New Zealand); Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Com. since 1921; b. June 1889, Epsom, Surrey, England; s. of Walter Robert Tytheridge, physician. Career: educated at Christ's Coll., Christchurch, New Zealand. and Canterbury Coll., Univ. of New Zealand; Staff Christchurch Press; Editor Fiji Times Suva; Editorial Staff The New East Tokyo. Address: Higashi Kaigan. Chigasaki-machi, Kanagawa-ken.

Japanese Consul-Gen. Foochow China since 1936; b. Aug. 1888, Yamagata-ken; s. of late Koretaka Uchida. official. Career: passed Diplo. & Consular Service Exam. 1920; apptd. Eleve-Consul, Antwerp, Belgium 1921; Japansee High Commissariat Constantinople 1922; Consul Swatow 1924-27; Mukden 1927-29; Chefoo 1929-32; Tsitsihar 1932-36. Address: Japanese Consulate-General. Foochow, China.

Dr. Com.; Mng.-Dir. Toa Ind. Co; Prof. Meiji Univ. since 1916; b. 1885, Chiba-ken; s of Heikichi Uchida. Career: grad. Meiji Univ. 1908; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; apptd. Govt. Com. Commr. to South China 1914; joined present firm 1918. Address: 19 Tenjin. Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

LL.D. (U.S.A.); Pres. Japan-Turkey Assn.; b. Jan. 1865. Fukuoka-ken; s. of Jinzo Uchida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; entered Foreign Office; served at Shanghai, Keijo, New York as Vice-Cons. and Cons.-Gen.; Minister to Brazil 1907; Minister Sweden, Norway, Denmark 1912-18; Amb. Turkey 1921-23; resigned 1924. Address: 15 Nampeidai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. Agr.; Ornithologist Agr. & Forestry Dept.; Lecturer Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Commissioned Staff Educ. Dept.; b. Dec. 1884, Tokyo; s. of Yasubei Uchida. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Commissioned Staff, Agr. & Com. Dept.; sent to Pan-Pacific Educ. Congress by Educ. Dept. 1927; sent abroad for study of ornith. by Dept. of Agr. & For.; Councillor Ornith. Soc. of Japan etc. Address: 8 Aoba-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Prof. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Kenchiku Kyokai; b. Feb 1885, Tokyo; s. of Yasubei Uchida. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; entered Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Asst. Prof. of Alma Mater 1916; rec'd deg. 1919; Prof. 1921. Address: 142 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

n: UCHIGASAKI, Sakusaburo 內ヶ崎作三郎
t: M.P.; Parl. Vice-Min. of Educ.; Lecturer Waseda Univ.; b. Apr. 1877, Miyagi-ken; s. of Sakutaro Uchigasaki. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901; studied at Oxford Univ. 1908; Prof. Waseda Univ.; made inspection tour of Europe, Amer. & China 1920; Dir. League of Nations Assn.; elected to Diet 6 times since 1924; Parl. Councillor Home Dept. 1929. Address: 1470 Sugamo 6-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Councillor Emb. France; b. Feb. 1890, Gunma-ken; s. of Iwakichi Uchiyama. Career: sent to Madrid as student of Foreign Office 1909; Secr. Legation Poland; Secr. to Foreign Minister; Commr. Foreign Office; Secr. Emb. Turkey & France; Consul Buenos Aires and Montevideo; Consul-Gen. Sao Paulo 1931-35; Councillor Emb. Brazil. Address: Japanese Emb. Paris.

Consul-Gen. at Manila; b. Aug. 1887, Tokyo; s. of Zenzo Uchiyama. Career: grad. Yokohama Com. Sch. 1907; apptd. Chancellor, Foreign Office 1917; Vice-Consul, Shanghai 1919; Consul, Chefoo 1921; Mukden, New York, Cuba; Seattle 1931. Address: Consulate-Gen. of Japan, Manila, P. I.

D. Agr.; Dir. Central Assn. of Coop. Soc. Pres. Joint Marketing Soc. of Japan; b. Mar. 1876 Kumamoto-ken; s. of Soryu Udo; m. Hatsue d. of Dr. Junzo Nakahara: Career: grad. Agr. College of Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1900; entered Agr. & Com. Dept; Chief Agr. Affairs Bureau; Chief Agr. Adm. Sec. same; retired 1933; despatched to Chosen 1904-05; Europe & Amer. 1910-12. Australia & New Zealand 1916. Address: 30 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

Gen.; Amb. to Manchoukuo; Commander, Kwantung Army; b. Mar. 1875, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1899; Comdr. 1st Cav. Reg.; 3rd Cav. Brig.; Japanese Garrison, China 1929; 9th Div. 1930; despatched to Shanghai 1932; Vice-Chief, Gen. Staff 1933-34; Comdr. Chosen Army 1934; War Councillor 1935. Address: c/o Japanese Emb. Hsinking.

Vice-Admiral; Dir. Nav. Constr. Bureau; b. Aug. 1884, Tokyo; adopted s. of Suzu Ueda. Career: grad. Nav. Engrg. Sch. 1905; Nav. Torpedo Sch., Artificers Sch., Nav. Staff Coll.; apptd. Instructor Nav. Engrg. Sch. and Nav. Staff Coll.; Chief Engr. Sasebo Nav. Stn.; Mem. Tech. Council, Nav. Constr. Bureau; Chief, Sci. Research Sec. Nav. Tech Inst.; Dir. Nav. Engrg. Sch. 1930-35; Dir. Nav. Supplies Bureau. Address: 3 Honcho-dori 6-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.
Pres Naniwa Gas Co., Imazu Hatsuden K. K.; Dir. Toyo Cement Co.; b. Feb. 1873, Oita-ken; bro. of Hiroshi Ueda; Pres. Kansai Trust Co. Address: Nagaomura, Kawabe-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Dir. Miye Higher Agr. & Forestry Sch. since 1922; 2nd Colonial Training Inst. since 1933; b. Jan. 1885, Yamanashi-ken; s. of Taneyori Uehara, farmer. Career: grad. Agr. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Chief, Agrl. Educ. Sec. Educ. Dept.; Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; made inspection tour of North & South America and Europe 1928. Address: Koto Norin Gakko Kansha, Tsu City.

Former Gen.-Mgr. The Japan Times; Rep. Partner Uehara Shokai; b. Apr. 1890, Ueda City; s. of Makitaro Uehara; m. Eiko; a s. and 3 d. Career: grad. Ueda Mid. Sch; went to China, England to inspect tailor's business; opened tailor shop 1915; Vice-Pres. Tokyo Tailor Assn.; Adviser Akasaka Tailors Assn.; Director Fed. Eastern Japan Tailors' Assn.; Committee Int'l Club; travelled Russia. Address: 545 Kamiuma-cho 1-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Asahi Shimbun-sha; b. Oct. 1882, Osaka; s. of Riichi Ueno, one of founders & shareholders of Asahi Shimbun. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; Mng.-Dir. Asahi Shimbun. Address: 5 Hirano 1-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

M.P.; Pres. Amazonia Ind. Co.; b. May 1890, Kumamoto-ken; brother of Hidekatsu Uetsuka. Career: grad. Kobe Higher Com. Sch. 1912; joined S. M. R. Co.; engaged in economic research in China, Manchuria, Mongolia, French Indo-China, South Seas as Non-Commissioned Official of Foreign Office and Dept. of Agr. & Com.; Secr. to Agr. & Com. Minister; same to Com. & Ind. Min.; attended Int'l Parl. Congress; Secr. to Fin. Min.; Parl. Councillor, Finance Dept. in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 155 Kogai-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Hon. Vice-Cons. for Jugoslavia; Pres. Ueyamayei's Japan Insect Powder Mfg. Co. Ueyama Trust Co, Osaka Traders' Assn.; b. Sept. 1889, Wakayama-ken; s. of Eiichiro Ueyama. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com Sch. Address: Okubatake, Morigu, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

General (reserve); State-Councillor; b. June 1868, Okayama-ken; brother of Tonahachi Ugaki. Career: grad. Military Staff College; Staff, of General Staff Office; Military Attache to Germany; Chief of Military Affairs Dept. War Office; Comdr. Inf. 6th Reg.; Chief, 1st and Gen. Affairs Depts., Gen. Staff Office; Pres Mil. Staff Coll.; Councillor, H. I. H. Crown Prince's Study; Comdr. 10th Division; Vice-Minister for War; War Min. in Kiyoura, Kato and Wakatsuki Cabinets; Supreme War Councillor 1927; War Minister 1929-31; Gov.-Gen. of Chosen 1931-36. Address: 1 Naito-cho 1-chome, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo.

n: UKON, Gonzaemon 右近權左衞門
t: Pres. Ukon Trading Co., Nippon Marine Ins. Co., Nikkai Ind. Co.; b. Nov. 1889, Fukui-ken; s. of late Gonzaemon Ukon. Career: grad. Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. 1914; entered bus.; High taxpayer in Fukui-ken;. Address: 14 Kita-dori 5-chome, Nishinagahori, Nishi-ku, Osaka.

3rd Head Umemoto House of Dancing; Dir. Takarazuka Music Opera Sch.; Hon. Fellow Imp. Soc. of Teachers of Dancing; b. Aug. 1897; s. of Sensho Umemoto II. Career: studied dancing with Father since 3 years of age; made debut at 5 years of age and danced "Harukoma"; grad. Imamiya Mid. Sch.; taught at Takarazuka Opera Sch. 1917-20; succeeded family estate upon his father's death 1927; despatched by Shochiku Opera Sch. and Educ. Dept. to Germany to study theory of dancing under Rudolf von Laban and to London classic ballet under Cecchetti; Hon. Fellow Imp Soc. of Teachers of Dancing London; returned 1934. Address: 52 Bakuro-machi 1-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

D.L.; Dir. Showa Steel Works since 1933; b. Feb. 1884, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Shunji Yasumoto; m. Tsuneko, d. of Takumi Seo, 1915. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1911; joined Govt. Steel Works; Chief, 1st Steel Mfg. Section, 1918; joined S. M. R. Co. 1919. Address: 3 Kamidai-machi, Anzan, Manchoukuo.

D. Litt.; former Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ., Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sci.; Prof. Toyo Univ., Daito Bunka Gakuin; Dir. Japanese-German Cultural Inst.; Toho Bunka Gakuin; Councillor Japan Phil Assn.; b. Nov. 1875, Kumamoto; s. of Jokuro Uno. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to China & Germany for study 4 years; is authority on Chinese Classics. Address: 517 Yoyogi-hatsudai-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Vice-Minister for War since Apr. 1936; b. 1882, Oita-ken; s. of Beiho Umetsu. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1904; Comdr. Inf. 3rd Reg.; Chief 1st Sec. Gen. Staff; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief Mil. Affairs Sec. War Dept.; Comdr. Inf. 1st Brig.; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Gen. Staff; Comdr. Garrison in China 1934-35; Comdr. 2nd Div. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.

Chief Judge, Supreme Court since 1934; b. Sept. 1878, Aomori-ken; s. of Seizaemon Uno. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904; apptd. Judge, Otsu, Urawa, and Tokyo Local Courts; Judge, Tokyo Court of Appeal; Chief Judge, same; Judge, Supreme Court; Pres. Yokohama Local Court 1920; Pres. Tokyo Local Court. Address: 13 Sakae-dori 2-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.
Corr. of Zentralverlag der N. S. D. A. P. for Japan; b. Oct. 1903; Hanau/Main; s. of H. S. H. Duke of Urach, General. Address: 166 Yoyogi Sanya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Dairen Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Dir. Dairen Oil & Fat Ind. Co., Dairen Exchange Trust Co.; Prop. Uritani Chozo Shoten; b 1881, Toyama-ken; s. of Nagamitsu Araki. Career: joined Sakai-Riki & Co. at Kobe and engaged in import of grains and fertilizers; later succeeded to the house of Mr. Uritani, then head of the above firm; came to Dairen and expanded his business. Address: 137 Yamagata-dori, Dairen.

Aud. Yamaichi Securities & Finance Co.; b. 1892 in Tochigi-ken; s. of Seirokuro Urushibara; m. Mon, e.d. of Naokichi Fukuda. Career: Grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1916, joined Koike Goshi Kaisha, precursor of Yamaichi Goshi Kaisha, 1917; became its councillor, same year; appointed Dir. upon reorganization of Yamaichi Goshi Kaisha as Kabushiki Kaisha in 1926; present post since 1933. Address: 125 Wakabayashi, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. May 1869, Yamagata-ken; s. of Katsusaku Usami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; Councillor, Tokushima-ken, same. Kyoto-fu; Secr. Home Dept.; Chief, Home Dept. Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Gov. Tokyo-fu 1921; Grand Chancellor Imp. Orders 1925; Dir. Resources Bureau 1927-32; Adviser, State Council of Manchoukuo 1932-34. Address: 444 Nakanomaru, Kami-Osaki, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. S. M. R.; Vice-Dir. Bureau of Rys. Manchoukuo; b. Jan. 1884, Gifu-ken; s. of Matazo Usami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Secr. Ry. Board Japan; Councillor same 1916; joined S. M. R. Co. 1919; Mgr. Traffic Office; went to Europe 1922-24; Gen. Mgr. Ry. Dept. 1927; Chief Harbin Office 1930; Mukden Office 1931; Gen. Dir. 1933. Address: Bureau of Rys., Dept. of Communications, Hsinking.

Lieut.-Gen.; Chief Aide-de-Camp to the Emperor since 1936; b. 1883, Kanagawa-ken; s. of Masaiye Usami. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief, Cav. Sec. Mil. Affairs Bureau War Office; Mem. Mil. Tech. Bd.; Comdr. Cav. 3rd Brig.; Dir. Cav. Sch.; Comdr. Cav. Corps in Manchoukuo; Cav. Inspector 1934; Comdr. 7th Div. 1935-36. Address: 11 Aoba-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Emb. Councillor; Cons.-Gen. at Geneva since Apr. 1937; b. Nov. 1893, Nagano-ken; s. of Kazutaro Usami. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; entered Dept. of Agr & Com.; Officer Foreign Office 1920; attended League of Nations Assembly; Consul Antung; Secr. Com. Bureau, Foreign Office; Consul-Gen. Foochow 1934-35; Mukden 1935-37. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen. Geneva.

Dir. Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. 1882, Gifu-ken; s. of Shinshichiro Ushimaru. Career: grad. Nav. Engrg. Sch. 1903; grad. Nav. Staff Coll. 1912; despatched to England 1918-20; Rear-Admiral 1925; Chief Engrg. Dept. Yokosuka Naval Arsenal; Chief 4th Sec. Nav. Tech. Dept. 1928; Vice-Adm. 1930; Dir. Stores Bureau of Navy 1932; attached Nav. Gen. Staff 1934. Address: 109 Omote-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mem. House of Peers; b. 1881, Shimane-ken; bro. of Tsunetaro Ushio. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; Commr., Secr. and Councillor, Home Dept.; Dir. Sanitary Bureau and Local Affairs Bureau; Vice-Home Min. 1928-31; against same 1932-34; Home Min. in Hirota Cabinet 1937. Address: 1070-2 Nakanobu-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Fukushima Cotton Mills Co.; b. Dec. 1880, Osaka; s. of Tameshichi Utsumi. Career: joined 34th Bank; entered Central Lab. S. M. R. Co.; Dir. & Mgr. Naniwa Warehouse Co.; Mng.-Dir. Teikoku Rayon Co. Address: 13 Tanaka Asukai-cho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

M.D.; b. Mar. 1883, Aichi-ken; s. of Jujiro Uyeda, educator. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; studied treatment of infectious diseases at Komagome Hospital under Prof. Miyamoto; Surgeon-Lieut. 1912; went to China, Australia, New Zealand, South Sea Islands; Surgeon-Lieut.-Comdr.; studied Internal Treatment at P.-G. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. under Prof. Inada 1919-21; sent to Germany to study at Berlin Univ., Kaiser Wilhelm's Institute 1922-24; rec'd deg. 1923; Surgeon-Inspector-Gen 1932-33. Address: 128 Kami-Ogikubo 2-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.
D.L.; Pres. Tokyo Univ. of Com; b. May 1879, Tokyo; s. of Akira Uyeda. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com.

Lit.-Gen.; b. 1885 in Kyoto. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1903; grad. Mil. Staff Coll; Staff, 5th Div.; attached Kwantung Army; Comdr. Inf. 48th Regiment; Chief Staff 4th Div.; attached to Kwantung Army; Chief 3rd Dept. Gen. Staff Office 1934-35; Dir. Personnel Bureau 1935-37; Dir. Mil. Affairs Bureau War Office. Address: War Office, Tokyo.

Ex-Mayor of Tokyo; b. Apr. 1879; Toyama-ken; s. of Tahei Ushizuka. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Communications Dept.; Secr. same; Secr. of Cabinet; Chief Statis. Bur. Cabinet 1916; Judge Court of Adm. Litigation; Vice-Chief Nat. Census Bureau; Gov. Iwate-ken, Gunma-ken, Miyagi-ken, Tokyo-fu 1929-31. Address: 19 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Fukushima Cotton Mills Co.; b. Dec. 1880, Osaka; s. of Tameshichi Utsumi. Career: joined 34th Bank; entered Central Lab. S. M. R. Co.; Dir. & Mgr. Naniwa Warehouse Co.; Mng.-Dir. Teikoku Rayon Co. Address: 13 Tanaka Asukai-cho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto.

M.D.; b. Mar. 1883, Aichi-ken; s. of Jujiro Uyeda, educator. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; studied treatment of infectious diseases at Komagome Hospital under Prof. Miyamoto; Surgeon-Lieut. 1912; went to China, Australia, New Zealand, South Sea Islands; Surgeon-Lieut.-Comdr.; studied Internal Treatment at P.-G. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. under Prof. Inada 1919-21; sent to Germany to study at Berlin Univ., Kaiser Wilhelm's Institute 1922-24; rec'd deg. 1923; Surgeon-Inspector-Gen. 1932-33. Address: 128 Kami-Ogikubo 2-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Pres. Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. May 1879, Tokyo; s. of Akira Uyeda. Career: grad. Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1900; apptd. Lecturer of same 1902; sent to Europe as Govt. Student 1905; Prof. 1919; Delegate to Int'l Econ. Conf. Geneva 1927. Address: 9 Momozono-cho, Nakano-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; Adviser Seiyukai; b. May 1877, Nagano-ken; s. of Shigetaro Uyehara. Career: grad. London Univ. 1910; Corr. Saihoku Shimpo in America; Pres. Nichibei Shogyo-sha, U. S. A.; Commr. English-Japanese Exhibition and Pacific World Exhibition, Panama; Lecturer, Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch.; Prof. Meiji and Rikkyo Univs.; returned to Diet 7 times since 1917; Councillor Communications Dept. and Foreign Office. Address: 12 Aoyama Takagi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; Finnish Minister to Tokyo; b. July 1894, Finland; s. of H. E. Wegelius, Dean. Career: entered Finnish Diplo. Service 1919; Charge d'Affaires Moscow 1921; Secr. Legation London 1921-25; Finnish Rep. Secretariat, League of Nations 1925; Secr. Leg. Berne 1926-28; served Ministry for Foreign Affairs Helsinki 1928-33; Chief Bureau for League of Nations 1928-29; Dir. Polit. & Com. Sec. 1930-31; Secr.-Gen. 1931-33; charge d'Affaires Rome 1929; Substitute Del. League of Nations Assembly 1925-28; Del. Int'l Labour Conf. 1926; Del. at several Int'l Confs. Address: c/o Finnish Legation 62 Tansumachi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Brazilian Ambassador to Japan since 1935; b. Jan. 1887 at Pindamonhagaba, Sao Paulo, Brazil; s. of Pedro Leao Velloso, Mem. House of Repr., writer, lawyer; m. Germaine Leao. Career: grad. Faculdade Livre de Sciencias Juridicas e Sociaes do Rio de Janeiro; attache Ministry For. Affairs 1907; 2nd Secr. Rome 1910; Paris, 1913; 1st Secr. Berne, 1916; Paris, 1918; charge d'affaires Copenhagen 1919; Counsellor Rome, 1921; Paris, 1923; Chief of Cabinet of Ministry For. Affairs 1926; Minister to China, 1931. Address: Brazilian Embassy 2 Omote-cho 3-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
French Vice-Cons. at Harbin; b. June 1906, Paris. Career: grad. Hautes Etudes Commerciales and Langues Orientales Vivantes Paris. Address: French Consulate, Harbin.

Painter of Western Style; Court Artist; b. Dec. 1874, Tokyo; s. of Hidetoyo Wada. Career: studied Western Painting under Kiyoteru Kuroda; grad. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1896; Asst. Prof. same 1896; studied in France 1897-1900; Prof. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1903; Mem. Imp. Academy of Fine Arts 1919. Address: 8 Kogai-cho Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Mem. Imp. Acad. since 1930; Dir. Historical Materials Compiling Bureau since 1907; Prof. Kokugakuin Univ.; b. Sept. 1865, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Gohei Wada. Career: grad. Japanese Classics Dept. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1888; Prof. Peers' Sch. 1899; won Imp. Prize for Research of Imp. Documents 1918; rec'd deg. 1921. Address: 538 Sendagaya 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Gov. Bank of Taiwan; b. Sept. 1889, Tokyo; s. of Hikojiro Wada, Peer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; entered Finance Dept.; Sec. Chief Nagoya Revenue Supt. Bureau; Bank Inspector 1928; Secr. Fin. Dept. 1929; Chief Ordinary Bank Sec.; same, Bank Inspection Sec.; Dir. Foreign Exch. Control Bureau 1934-36; Dir. Bank Bureau. Address: 25 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Painter of Western Style; Mem. Imp. Academy of Fine Arts; b. Mar. 1883, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Tokyo Fine Arts Sch. 1904; studied in France as student of Education Dept. 1910; visited India; Examiner, 10th Educ. Dept. Exhibition 1915-22; Examiner, Imp. Fine Arts Academy Exhibition 1924. Address: 1 Fukuyoshi-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.
Dir. Oriental Vacuum Ind. Co.; b. July 1897, Osaka; s. of Takahide Wada, businessman. Career: studied at Econ. Dept. Keio Univ. Address: 29 Kiyohori-cho, Higashi-ku, Osaka.

M. D.; Prof. & Councillor Osaka Imp. Univ.; Dir. Attached Hospital of Med. Coll. same; b. Aug. 1880, Osaka; 2nd s. of late Genji Wada, physician; m. Hisa. Career: grad. Osaka Pref. Med. Sch. 1899; served Russo-Japanese War; Prof. Osaka Med. Coll.; sent to Amer. & Germany 1909; afer returning home rec'd deg.; again to Europe & America 1929. Address: 175 Minami-Morimachi, Kita-ku, Osaka.

Hon. Con-Gen. of Czechoslovakia at Osaka; Partner of Liebermann Waelchli & Co.; b. Sept. 1882, Berne, Switzerland; s. of John Waelchli. Career: educated in England and Switzerland; engaged in business mostly in Manila; came to Japan 1912; established branch offices of his firm in Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo, Nagoya; decorated with Order of White Lion of Czechoslovakia IV. Address: 194 Kitano-cho 2-chome, Kobe.

Dr. jur.; German Cons-Gen. at Osaka & Kobe; b. July 1884, Wetterfeld, Hessen, Germany; s. of Heinrich Wagner, clergyman; m. Elisabeth Richly. Career: grad. Grammar Sch.; Geneva, Giessen and Berlin Univs. 1894-1903; Student Interpreter Legation Peking 1908; Acting Cons. Swatow 1913; served in Great War 1914-16; Vice-Cons. Geneva 1918; Secr. Legation Peking 1920; Acting Cons.-Gen. Canton 1921-23; Cons. Vladivostok 1923; Hongkong 1925; Counsellor Legation China 1928-29; Cons.-Gen. Canton 1929-34; present post since Apr. 1934. Address: German Consulate-Gen. 115 Higashimachi, Kobe.

M.D.; D.D.; Missionary; Mng.-Dir. Kyobunkwan; b. Apr. 15, 1863, Columbus, Ill.; s. of D. T. Wainright, preacher; m. Margaret Miller Todd. Career: Practised medicine in Missouri, 1886-88; Teacher in Govt. Middle Sch., Oita, 1888-90; Prin. Acad. Dept., Kwansei Gakuin, 1890-1907; Presiding Elder St. Louis District, St. Louis, Missouri, 1907-11; Pastor, Univ. Methodist Church, St. Louis, 1911-12; Gen.-Mgr., Christian Litt Soc. of Japan (Kyobunkwan) since 1912; Pres. at one time, American Association of Tokyo; American Peace Soc. of Tokyo; Asiatic Soc. of Tokyo, For. Auxiliary Nat. Temperance League, Tokyo; Mem. Executive Com. America-Japan Soc.; Author of books. Address: 2 Aoyama Gakuin, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Jan. 1875, Tokyo; s. of Seikai Wakamiya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; joined Communications Dept.; Vice-Minister of Com. 1922; Dir. Aviation Bureau 1923; elected to Diet 5 times since 1923. Address: 1 Omote-machi 4-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; LL.B.; Cons.-Gen. at New York; b. 1875; s. of Keishichi Wakasugi. Career: grad. Tung Wen Coll., Shanghai, Univ. of Oregon, New York Univ.; Attached to Consulate-Gen. Shanghai; 3rd Emb. Secr. France & England; attended 1st & 10th League of Nations Assemblies; Cons. Los Angeles; 1st Emb. Secr. England; Cons.-Gen. San Francisco; Shanghai. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen. New York.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Ex-Pres. Minseito; b Feb. 1866, Matsue City; s. of Senzaburo Okumura; later adopted by Kei Wakatsuki. Career; grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1892; joined Finance Dept.; Chief Revenue Officer of Ehime-ken 1894; Secr. and Councillor, Finance Dept.; Judge, Court of Adm. Litigation and Chief, Revenue Bureau, Finance Dept.; Vice-Minister of Finance 1906; Finance Minister in Katsura Cabinet 1912; same in Okuma Cabinet 1915; Home Minister in Kato Cabinet and Premier after Kato's death; attended Nav. Conf. London as Chief Delegate; Pres. Minseito 19[?]0-[?]4. Address: 129 Kamifujimae-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1929; Mem. Natural Monuments Preserving Committee; Pan-Pacific Sci. Research Council; Nat. Park Com.; Nat. Text Book Compiling Com.; Prof. Komazawa Univ.; b. Nov. 1867, Ogaki; s. of Kan-ichi Wakimizu. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1893; Asst. Prof. of same 1896; Prof. Geology and Pedology 1917-29. Address: 129 Denyen-Chofu 4-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

A,B,; M.A.; B.D.; S.T.M.; Missionary; b. Aug. 1889, New York City; n. American; s. of Dr. Oliver H. Walser, clergyman. Career grad. Albany Acad., Union Coll., Union Theol. Sem. Columbia Univ.; Dir. "Open Door" Student Centre; Associate Secr., "Fellowship of Reconciliation in Japan." Address: 9 Mita Tsuna-machi, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

M.A.; D.D.; Bishop of Hokkaido (Nihon Seikokai); b. Jan. 1880, County Donegal, England; s. of John Edward Walsh, barrister-at-law; m. Edythe Spence. Career: educated at Sutton Valence Sch. Kent, England and Trinity Coll. Dublin; ordained Deacon Belfast 1903; Priest 1904; worked in church of Ireland 1903-13; Rector of S. Peter's church, Athlone 1910-13; came to Japan 1913; worked as missionary at Tokushima, Hakodate, Asahigawa; consecrated Bishop of Hokkaido in Canterbury Cathedral 1927. Address: Bishop's House, Minami Junijo, Nishi 8-chome, Sapporo.

Mem. Hsinking Local Committee; b. Aug. 1878, Chinhsien, Chingchow Prov.; s. of Wan Yung-nien, merchant. Career: grad. Com. Dept., Mukden Prov. Tech. Sch.; succeeded to father's business and expanded it to Hsinking, Kirin, Harbin. Address: 5 Iwai-cho 4-chome, Hsinking.

Lt.-General; Dir. General Staff Bureau, Public Peace Dept. of Manchoukuo since 1936; b. 1893, Hsincheng-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Academy, Paoting; Chief Staff, 26th Div.; Comdr. 1st Brig. North Eastern Army 8th Div.; Chief, Kirin Prov. Guards Office; Chief, Mil. Research Dept.; Chief, Mil. Intelligence Dept. Address: c/o Public Peace Dept., Hsinking.

Gen.; Comdr. Manchoukuo 1st Military District; b. 1879, Chengteh-hsien, Fengtien. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Tokyo; taught Branch Sch. North Eastern Mil. Acad.; Chief Staff Nat. Defence Adm. Planning Office 1930; exerted in mediation between Ma Chan-shan & Japanese Army as Rep. of Ma; Acting Defence Minister; Vice-Min. of Defence & Dir. Horse Adm. Bureau 1932-34; Comdr. 5th Mil. Dist. (Jehol) 1935-37. Address: 1st District Army Hdqrs., Mukden.

Dir. Central Bank of Manchou since 1936; b. 1881, Tiehling-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: apptd. Chief Mgr. Three Eastern Prov. Bank; Sub-Mgr. Heilungkiang Prov. Bank; Mgr. Tsitsihar & Harbin Branches of present bank, 1934. Address: c/o Central Bank of Manchou, Hsinking.

Dir. Bureau of Constr. Manchoukuo Dept. of Ind.; b. 1887, Hsingching-hsien, Fengtien Province. Career: grad. Chem. Dept. Engrs. Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ.; Chief, Foreign Affairs Dept., Eastern Prov. Ry. Guards Hdqrs.; Chief, Powder-mill, Three Eastern Prov. Mil. Arsenal; Instructor, Mil. Engrg. Sch.; Councillor, Fengtien Prov. Office; Dir. Public Works Bureau, Civil Affairs Dept.; Mayor of Mukden 1935-37. Address: c/o Dept. of Ind. Hsinking.

Dir. Mil. Adm. Bureau, Manchoukuo Public Peace Dept. since 1937; b. 1898, Peicheng-hsien, Fengtien Province. Career: grad. Artillery Dept., Mil. Coll.; Staff, Suiyuan Adm. Office; Staff, Heilungkiang Mil. Adm. Office; Dir. Mil. Supply Bureau, Defence Dept. 1935-37. Address: c/o Public Peace Dept., Hsinking.

Gov. Chinchow Prov. since 1937; b. 1882, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. Tokyo; Chief Staff, 28th Div. Fengtien Army; Chief Staff Tartar Gen.'s Office Chahar; Councillor Fengtien Prov. Office; Gov. Antung Prov. 1934-37. Address: Governor's Residence, Chinchow.

Dir. Civil Affairs & Educ. Bureau of Fengtien Prov.; b. 1890, Haicheng-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Meiji Univ. Tokyo; Chief Prison Sec. High Procurator's Office Shansi Prov.; Prof. Shansi Univ.; Procurator Tientsin Local Procurator's Office; Vice-Chairman Registration Investigation Commn. 1932; Dir. Prison Bureau Justice Dept. 1933-37. Address: Fengtien Prov. Office, Mukden.

Mng.-Dir. Nippon Seimo Kogyo Co., Godo Keori K. K.; b. Sept. 1891, Hyogo-ken; s. of Mansuke Washio, sake brewer; m. Sue 1919. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1916; immediately joined Muslin Spinning & Weaving Co.; then joined Godo Keori Co.; went to Europe and America to inspect cotton industries 1922; director of Pacific Trading Co., Shirahama Hot Spring Hotel, etc. Address: 289 Kitabatake, Motoyama-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Ph.D.; Writer; b. Feb. 1883, Sumoto, Hyogo-ken; s. of Gensaku Washio; married. Career: studied phil. Harvard Univ.; obtained deg. 1911; studied in Berlin 1912; served Information Bureau Foreign Office 1919-22; went to Europe 1920; Secr. S. M. R. Co. 1922-23. Address: 33 Nishi-Takaido 2-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Chief of Research Sec., General Staff Bureau, Dept. of Public Peace, Manchoukuo; b. Dec. 1897, Saga-ken; m. in 1924. Career: grad. Tung Wen College, Shanghai. Address: 238, Dai-ichi Daiyo Kaisha (1st Official Residence), Giwa-ro, Hsinking Special Municipality, Manchoukuo.

Viscount; Mem. House of Peers; Director of Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; b. May 1876, Tokyo; s. of Chiaki Watanabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Mng.-Dir. Banque Franco-Japonais; Justice Min. in Hamaguchi Cabinet & Wakatsuki Cabinet 1929. Address: 69 Zaimoku-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Nippon Women's Univ.; b. Jan. 1875, Fukushima-ken; s. of Rinnai Watanabe. Career: grad. Higher Normal Sch.; worked as journalist and teacher. Address: 267 Shimohoya, Hoya-mura, Kitatama-gun, Tokyo-fu.
Former Inspector-General of Military Training; died on Feb. 26, 1936. (See 1936 issue).

Imp. Court Councillor; b. Jan. 1872, Okayama-ken; s. of Tokuichiro Watanabe, soy brewer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; Councillor Nara-ken; Commr. Kyoto-fu; Gov. Tokushima-ken; Dir. Local Bureau, Home Dept.; Gov. Niigata-ken & Nagasaki-ken; sent to Europe & Amer.; Mayor of Yokohama 1922; Pres. Oriental Development Co. 1925-28; Intendent to Prince Takamatsu. Address: 552 Shimo-Ochiai 1-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc. (1919); Prof. Tokyo Univ. of Engrg.; b. Sept. 1885, Tochigi-ken; s. of Tota Watanabe. Career: grad. Maths. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Prof. 8th & 1st Higher Schs.; Tokyo Univ. of Com. Address: 140 Totsuka-machi 2-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Dir. Japano-Australian Assn., Japano-Brazilian Central Assn., Japanese Traffic Assn., Japano-Argentine Assn., Japanese Seamen's Assn. for Mutual Aid; b. July 1881, Tokyo; s. of Heikichi Watanabe. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1905; entered N. Y. K. 1905. Address: 18 Dai-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Imp. Court Councillor; b. July 1872, Tokyo; s. of Naokatsu Matsudaira, feudal lord. Career: entered Imp. Household service; visited Europe & America as Subordinate to Princes and Princesses Higashi Fushimi, Fushimi, Nashimoto. Address: 9 Shitaya Kaya-cho 1-chome, Shitaya-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Chuo Trust Co., Aichi Bank; Dir. Okuma Iron Works; b. Sept. 1872, Aichi-ken; s. of Jin-emon Watanabe. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; entered Bank of Japan; invited to Aichi Bank. Address: 4 Shirakabe-cho 1-chome, Higashi-ku, Nagoya.

Lt.-Gen.; Attached to Gen. Staff Office; b. 1885, Tokyo. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1905; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in U. S. A.; Staff Gen. Staff Office & Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Mil. Attache Emb. U. S. A.; Chief Europe & America; Sec. Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. Inf. 6th Brig. attached 9th Div. Hdqrs.; Imp. Guards Div. 1935-36; Chief 2nd Sec. Gen. Staff Office 1936-37. Address: 543 Wakabayashi-cho, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Lecturer Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc.; b. Mar. 1873, Hyogo-ken; s. of Naokata Watari. Career: grad. 1st Higher Sch.; served as Lecturer, Attached Middle Sch. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1902; Lecturer Tokyo Univ. of Com. and Nihon Univ. Address: 45 Kobinata-Dai-machi 1-chome, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dr. phil.; b. Jan. 1879, Köln, Germany; n. German. Career: grad. Univ. of Munich, 1909; apptd. Prof. German Languages, Mil. Saff Coll. Tokyo 1922; Mil. Acad. 1929; Mil. Preparatory Sch. 19[?]5; Librarian, German East Asiatic Society. Address: 714 Matsubara-cho 2-chome, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Harbin; b. 1892, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Liaoyang Normal Sch. 1911; Sec. Chief Educ. Dept. Fengtien Prov.; Dir. Fengtien Prov. Educ. Soc.; Chief Educ. Dept. Fengtien Prov. 1932-37. Address: Muni. Office Harbin.

Dir. Manshu Kogyo Ginko (Ind. Bank of Manchou) since 1937; b. 1882 in Tehchow, Shantung; s. of Wei Nai-siang, govt. official. Career: Chief, Temporary High Court, Shantung 1915; Pres. Official Agri. Coll. 1913; Magistrate, Kianghun-Tao, Ichang-Tao, 1921; Chief, Ki-Hei Salt Transportation Office after Mukden Incident, 1931; Chief, State Salt Transportation Office, 1934-37. Address: Manshu Kogyo Ginko, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Captain; German Nav. Attache to Tokyo since 1933; b. Feb. 27, 1890; s. of Franz Wenneker. Career: entered naval service 1909; during World War was on board cruiser "Mainz" which sunk at the battle of Heligoland; after the War became gunnery officer and attached to the Staff of the Commander-in-Chief of the fleet. Address: 202 Yoyogi Sanya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

C.M.G.; Brit. Cons.-Gen. at Osaka; b. Sept. 1884, Newcastle-on-Tyne; n. British; s. of James White, merchant. Career: entered consular service 1903; Vice-Cons. 1913; Cons. 1920; Cons.-Gen. 1927. Address: Brit. Consulate-General, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir. M. S. Wiersum & Co., Yokohama; Consul for Netherlands, Yokohama; b. 1878, Kantens, Netherlands; n. Dutch; s. of L. Wiersum. Career: grad. Hoogere Burger Sch. Groningen; business practice at Groningen and Hamburg 6 years; at Shanghai, Hankow and Yokohama 1901-05; joined Simon, Evers & Co., Yokohama 1905; started business on his account 1915. Address: 25 Yamashita-cho, Yokohama.
D.L.; 1st Secr. Swedish Legation, Tokyo; b. April 1895 at Stockholm. Address: 451 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Tokyo.
Merchant; b. Oct. 1898, Hamburg, Germany; m. Liesel Krueger; n. German. Address: c/o Bergmann & Co., Hachiman-dori 3-chome, Kobe.

M.A. (Cambridge Univ.); Missionary, Priest of Nippon Seikokai; b. Mar. 1906, Osaka; s. of Rev. Charles Hampden Basil Woodd; m. Foss, Emily Hornby, 1936. Career: born in Japan; returned to England 1913; educated at Weymouth Coll. and Cambridge Univ. (Jesus Coll.); ordained Deacon England; came back to Japan 1933; with Momoyama Chugakko; Priest-in-charge of Fukkatsu Kyokwai, 1929; Priest 1930; 3 years Curacy in Tonbridge in Osaka. Address: 61 Asahi-cho 2-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka.

Dr. phil.; Kammersänger; Bass Singer; Prof. Imp. Academy of Music, Ueno since 1932; b. June 1884, Mühlhausen in Thüringen; n. German; s. of Franz Wucherpfennig, official. Career: grad. Univ. of Berlin 1922; studied singing under Prof. R. von Milde and Morattl of Milano, Italy 1912; sang 25 years in opera stages and concerts at Dessau, Nürnberg, Düsseldorf, Berlin, Karlsruhe, Frankfurt, Dresden, Cöln, Wiesbaden, Stuttgart; went to Norway, Hungary, South America and Italy for performance; kept private singing sch. in Karlsruhe 1922-30. Address: 1855 Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

D. Litt.; Prof. Taisho Univ.; b. Feb. 1879, Fukushima-ken; s. of Tomeshichi, farmer. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief, Tokyo Social Bureau 1925-26; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1924-35; sent to Europe and America 1913-16 and 1922-33. Address: 365 Takinogawa, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Fuji Life Ins. Co.; b. July 1883, Tokyo; s. of late Hideichi Yabuki, Lieut.-Gen. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; joined Yokohama Specie Bank; became Dir. of several firms; elected Peer 1918; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1925-27; of Navy 1929-31; of Foreign Affairs 1931; of Finance 1934-36. Address: 45 Nampeidai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Manchoukuo Privy Councillor since 1934; b. Dec. 1879, Shizuoka-ken; bro. of Shusaku Yada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; Elève-Consul at Canton, Hankow and Tientsin; Diplomatic Probationer in China; Secr., Embassy in Italy; Consul-Gen. at San Francisco, London and Shanghai; Minister to Switzerland 1929-33; attended Gen. Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1931. Address: c/o Sangifu, Hsinking.

Dir. Yalu Timber Co.; b. Feb. 1873, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Magohachi Yagi, merchant. Career: studied in China & Russia; Vice-Consul at several places; Consul, Tsingtao, China & New Orleans; Consul-Gen. Harbin. Address: c/o Yalu Timber Co., Antung, Manchoukuo.

Pres. Educ. Inst. of S. M. R. since 1934; b. Feb. 1885, Tottori-ken; s. of Eijiro Morimoto. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1908; Teacher Miye Pref. Girls' Normal Sch.; Prin. Anshan Primary Sch.; Dir. Fushun & Mukden Higher Girls' Schs. Address: 11 Aoi-cho, Mukden.

Pres. Japan Symphony Assn.; Composer; Adviser Takarazuka Opera, Columbia Gramaphone Co., etc.; b. June 1886, Tokyo; s. of Kenzo Yamada. Career: grad. Mid. Sch. Course, Kwansei Gakuin and Tokyo Academy of Music, Ueno; studied in Germany and grad. Composition Dept., Kaiser's Conservatoire, Berlin; conducted orchestras in America; founded Philharmony Society; composed songs, orchestras, symphonies and operas; founded Music-Drama Assn. and Composers' Assn. Address: 19 Goban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Shirokiya Dept. Store since 1927; b. Dec. 1885, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Masanari Namiyama, later adpt. by Ryuichi Yamada. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1905; established Yamada Shokai 1924; agent for Japan of Ford Motor Co.; founded Yamada Pub. Co. Address: 65 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 12th Div.; b. 1881, Nagano-ken; s. of Kaku Ichikawa; later adopted by Takayuki Yamada. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Instructor Mil. Cav. Sch.; Comdr. Cav. 26th Reg.; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Chosen Army Staff Office; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief, Educational Dept. Mil. Cav. Sch. 1930; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Gen. Staff Office; Dir. Mil. Acad. Address: 12th Div. Hdqrs. Kurume.

D.L.; Dir. Soc. for Int'l Cultural Relations; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov. 1869, Nara-ken; s. of Heizaburo Yamada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; studied in Europe & Amer. 1897; Prof. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901-30; Pres. Keijo Imp. Univ. 1931-35. Address: 172 Benten-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.
Chairman Shoko Glass Co., Asahi Glass Co.; b. Aug. 1870, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Ariyasu Yamada. Career: Dir. Takachiho Brick Refinery. Address: 103 Aoyama Minami-cho 2-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mint-Master Finance Office; b. Nov. 1893, Kochi-ken; s. of Chojitsu Yamada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; entered Finance Dept.; Chief Mito & Kyobashi Revenue Offices; Commr. Revenue Supt. Bureau; Chief Accounts Sec. Tokyo Revenue Supt. Bureau; Chief Indirect Tax Sec.; Bank Inspector; Chief Settled Accounts Sec. 1934-35; Mem. Cabinet Research Bureau 1935-36; Dir. Taxation Bureau 1936-37. Address: Zoheikyoku, Osaka.

Pres. Okura Bldg. Co.; Dir. Manshu Pulp Mfg. Co., Showa Steel Works, Ishikawajima Aircraft Co., Japan Wireless Telephone & Telegraph Co., Okura-gumi; b. Aug. 1870, Wakayama-ken; s. of Masamichi Yamada. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1894; Dir. Japan Trade Assn.; decorated by French Govt. 1928. Address: 4 Onden 4-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Documents Sec. Foreign Office; b. 1893, Ibaraki-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Elève-Consul, Hongkong 1918; Attaché, England 1919; attended Paris Peace Conf. and 1st League of Nations Assembly 1920; 3rd Emb. Secr. 1921; 3rd Leg. Secr., Sweden 1922; Foreign Office Secr. 1924; Chief, 2nd Sec., Europe & America Bureau 1926; Mem. Naval Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1927; Mem. Naval Conf. London 1929; 1st Emb. Secr. Belgium; Chief 5th Sec. Research Bureau 1934. Address: 13 Mikawadai-machi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Aud. Kirin Brewery Co.; b. May 1878, Tokyo; s. of Yubei Kitagawa, and later adopted by Kura Yamagishi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1898; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha 1898; Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Trading Co. 1922-29. Address: 146 Shirokane Imazato-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Ph. D.; Pres. Tokyo Elec. Co.; Dir. Daido Signal Co., Asahi Electrification Ind. Co., Tokyo Elec. Radio Co., Shibaura Engrg. Works; b. Jan. 1874, Tokyo; s. of Chozo Yamaguchi. Career: grad. Johns Hopkins Univ. Baltimore, U.S.A. 1902; Vice-Chief Mining Dept. later Mng.-Dir. Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; Mng.-Dir. Furukawa Elec. Co. 1920; Dir. Tokyo Elec. Co. 1918; Mng.-Dir. and Vice-Pres. of same 1921. Address: 260 Minami Shinagawa 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Prof. Applied Mechanics, Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1926; b. Mar. 1891, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kyujiro Yamaguchi. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ.; Asst. Prof. same, 1916-26. Address: 1127 Ohara-machi, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Operation Office, Operating & Mech. Engrg. Dept. Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Ry. since 1936; b. Mar. 1889, Fukui-ken; s. of Rizaemon Yamaguchi. Career: Vice-Councillor Ry. Dept. 1927; Commr. same; Chief Wagon Service Dept. Traffic & Operation Bureau, Ry. Dept. Address: 28 Kobai-cho, Mukden.

Trader; Pres. Yamatake & Co.; b. July 1869, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Hikoshichi Yamaguchi. Career: grad. Tokyo Tech. Sch. (now Tokyo Univ. of Tech.); served Patents Bureau; Mgr. Hakodate Dock Co.; established Yamatake & Co. 1903, Teikoku Spinning Machine Mfg. Co., Nihon Seiko K. K., Japan Oxygen Co. Address: 7 Shoto-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

n: YAMAJI, Tosataro 山地土佐太郎
t: Pres. Sumatra Takushoku K. K.; Yamaji Steamship Co.; Meiji Bussan K. K.; Dir. Borneo Gum Co.; b. Dec. 1878, Tokyo; s. of Junkichi Yamaji. Career: Chairman Nanyo Planters' Assn.; Mng.-Dir. Tokyo Riding Club. Address: 5 Nakarokuban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Dec. 1873, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kagenori Yamakawa, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; apptd. Councillor, Navy Office 1899; Interpreter of same 1900; Dir. Ry. Dept.; Instructor Nav. Staff Coll.; attended 2nd Int'l Nav. Conf. Hague 1907; Int'l Naval Conf. London 1908-09; Peace Conf. France 1919; Dir. Special Peace Treaty Bureau; Dir. Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office 1920; Dir. Legislation Bureau 1925-27; nominated Peer 1926; attended Lodon Naval Conf. 1929. Address: 5 Oyama-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Apr. 1889, Tottori-ken; s. of Tomozo Yamamasu. Career: grad. Meisei Com. Sch., Osaka; Teacher, Primary Sch.; grad. Litt. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1917; went to Europe & America 1921; elected M.P. 3 times; Parl. Councillor, Dept. of Educ. 1934-36. Address: 24 Komagome Akebono-cho, Hongo-ku, Tokyo.
Admiral on the Reserve list. (See 1936 issue).

Vice-Admiral; Vice-Min. of Navy; b. Apr. 1884, Niigata-ken; s. of Teikichi Takano; later adopted by Tamashi Yamamoto. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1904; fought in Russo-Japanese War; Chief Instructor Kasumigaura Nav. Air Corps; Nav. Attaché Emb. Wash.; Captain "Isuzu" and "Akagi"; attended London Conf.; Chief Tech. Sec. Nav. Tech. Dept.; Japanese Delegate Nav. Disarm. Pourparler London 1934; Chief Nav. Aeronautic Dept. Address: 14[?]5 Kamikawara, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

M.P.; b. May 1881, Nagano-ken; adopted s. of Kyuemon Yamamoto. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1903; elected M.P. 7 times; Councillor Ry. Dept. 1929; Parl. Vice-Min. of Educ. 1936-37. Address: 26 Wakamiya-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Nisshin Spinning Co.; b. Nov. 1884, Hyogo-ken; s. of Sadashichi Miki, and later adopted by Motosaburo Yamamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; joined present firm 1912. Address: 11 Kita-machi Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; M.A. (Wisconsin); Emeritus Prof. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Jan. 1874, Miye-ken; s. of Shohei Yamamoto. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ., Kyoto Imp. Univ., Columbia, Wisconsin, Halle and Berlin Univs.; Prof. Econ. Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Dean Econ. Coll.; resigned Feb. 1934; despatched to China, Manchuria, Siberia, South Seas, Europe & America. Address: 1 of 31 Koyama Shimofusa-cho, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Pres. Manshu Arsenal since 1934; Pres. Manshu Ind. Soc.; b. May 1873, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Morihide Yamamoto, banker. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; joined Kawasaki Dockyard Co.; apptd. Chief, Works Dept. 1909; Dir. 1920; Mng.-Dir. 1928-33. Address: 4 Asama-cho, Mukden.

Pres. Seisen Godo Elec. Co.; Dir. Chosen Elec. Transmission Co., Chosen Radio Corp.; b. May 1886, Hyogo-ken; s. of Kichijiro Yamamoto. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; Secr. Legislation Bureau; Chief, 1st Sec. Leg. Bureau; toured in Europe & America for Inspection 1922-23; Commr. Chosen Govt. 1924; Dir. Communications Bureau, Chosen Govt. 1928-33. Address: 7 Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Nissan Automobile Sales Co.; Dir. Nissan Motorcar Co.; b. Oct. 1888, Niigata-ken; s. of Meijiro Yamamoto; m. Tokuko Ito. Career: grad. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. 1912; Factory Mgr. Kubota Iron Works 1917; Purchasing Mgr. Toyo Steel Mills Co. 1917; Business Mgr. Kyoritsu Kigyo K. K.; Dir. Tobatta Foundry Co. 1927; Dir. Dat Jidosha K. K. 1931; Mng.-Dir. Jidosha Seizo K. K. 1933. Address: 32 Denyen-Chofu 3-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

D.E.; Dir. Waseda Univ.; Chief, Sc. Dept., same; b. June 1881, Kochi-ken; s. of Chujiro Yamamoto; later adopted by Tadahide Yamamoto. Career: grad. Elec. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1905; entered Shibaura Engrg. Works; studied in Germany, 1909; Prof. Sc. Dept. Waseda University; received degree 1917; attended Int'l Motive Power Conf. London 1924. Address: Edogawa Apmts. Shin-Ogawa-machi, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Minseito; b. Mar. 1856; s. of Kaku Yamamoto, samurai. Career: studied at Keio Univ. and Mitsubishi Com. Sch.; Mgr. Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Business Mgr. Bank of Japan; Dir. Yokohama Specie Bank; Pres. Bank of Japan; same, Hypothec Bank of Japan; Finance Minister in 3rd Saionji Cabinet; Com. & Agr. Min. in Yamamoto Cabinet and Hara Cabinet; Home Min. in Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: [?] Kaminiban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Territorial Comdr. Salvation Army Japan; b. Aug. 1872, Okayama-ken; s. of Sahachi Yamamuro, farmer. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ.; in 1895 entered Salvation Army, to which work has devoted his whole life; commencing as Lieut., has now reached highest rank in S. A.; served as Corps Commanding Officer; Training Sch. Prin.; Editor Chief Secr. for Japan; travelled extensively in Europe & Amer.; Mem. High Council of S. A.; noted preacher and teacher of Christianity. Address: (office) Jimbo-cho, Kanda-ku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 11th Div.; b. 1881, Kumamoto-ken; bro. of Sobun Yamamuro, banker. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1903; Instructor, Field Artil. Sch.; Comdr. Field Heavy Artil. 4th Reg.; Staff Mil. Tech. Dept.; Chief 3rd Sec. Mil. Tech. Dept.; Dir. Field Artil. Sch. 1932-36; Artil. Inspector 1936-37. Address: 11th Div. Hdqrs. Zentsuji, Kagawa-ken.

Chairman Mitsubishi Trust Co.; Dir. Mitsubishi Bank. Trust Assn.; Aud. Mitsubishi Jukogyo K. K.; b. Oct. 1880, Kumamoto-ken; s. of Soi Yamamuro. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1907; studied in Europe & Amer.; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Vice-Chief Bank Dept.; Business Mgr. London Branch; Mgr. Osaka Branch; Spec. Mem. Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Bank 1929-36. Publications: "Japan's Money Market," etc. Address: 10 Mukoyama, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. of Library, Taiwan Govt.-Gen.; b. Oct. 1882, Fukui City; s. of Rainosuke Yamanaka; m. Miyoshi, d. of Gentatsu Suzuki, physician. Career: Teacher Nara Tech. Sch.; Miyagi-ken Higher Girls' Sch.; Librarian Miyagi Pref. Library; Chief Niigata Pref. Library. Address: 127 Nishiki-cho, Taihoku. Tel. Taihoku 2398.

Pres. Kyoto Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; Aud. Radio Corp. of Japan; b. Feb. 1882, Tokushima-ken; s. of Bunkichi Yamane, agriculturist; m. Hisano, sister of Jun Kimura 1913. Career: joined Kobe Yushin Nippo and then Kobe Shimbun and sarted his pressman life; became General Manager Kyoto Nichi-Nichi; Mng.-Dir. Kobe Shimbun; Dir. Osaka Jiji Shimpo; Nagasaki Shimbun; Santo Godo Shimbun-sha; Mng.-Dir. Osaka Broadcasting Station; Dir. Radio Corp. of Japan; travelled in Europe and America to inspect newspaper business and broadcasting works 1932. Address: Somedono-cho, Hirokoji-agaru, Nashikicho-dori, Kamikyo-ku, Kyoto.

Aud. Toyo Cotton Mills Co.; A.M.S.T.; b. June 1876, Otsu, Shiga-ken; adopted s. of late Takeo Yamanobe. Pres. of above firm. Career: grad. Textile Dept. Muni. Sch. of Tech. Manchester; has been with present firm since 25 years ago; authority on cotton spinning ind. in Japan. Address: 19 Dogashiba-cho, Tennoji-ku, Osaka.
Hon. Consul for Uruguay at Yokohama; Mgr. Yokohama Branch O. S. K.; b. June 1887; s. of Tokunojo Yamanoi. Address: Uruguayan Consulate, 22 Honmachi 2-chome, Yokohama.

M. Sc. (Columbia Univ.); Mng.-Dir. Kurosaki Ceramic Co. since 1936; b. Aug. 1886, Fukuoka-ken; s. of Hanzaburo Yamauchi, landowner. Career: grad. Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch. 1908; entered S. M. R. Co. 1909; sent to Europe & Amer. 1919-21; Acting Traffic Mgr. Head Office; resigned 1931; Inspector & Aud. Subsidiary Cos. of same; Dir. Dairen Fire & Marine Ins. Co. 1933-36. Address: 654 Sonoda-machi 1-chome, Ohkura, Yawata City.

Lt.-Gen. (retired); Adviser S. M. R. Co.; b. Aug. 1876, Kyoto; s of Kakudo Yamanouchi; adopted by Masaaki Yamanouchi. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1897, Mil. Artil. Sch. and Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Instructor Mil. Acad.; Adjutant Field Telegraph Dept. Imp. Hdqrs.; Instructor Artil. Sch.; Sec. Chief, Mil. Tech. Dept.; Chief Mil. Fortification Dept.; Pres. Manchuria Tel. & Telegraph Co. Address: 370 Taizanton, Dairen.

D.L.; Mem. House of Peers; b. Apr. 1876; s. of Tsuruji Kosaka; later adopted by Toyo Yamaoka. Career: grad. Nippon Horitsu Gakko 1899; Judge Tokyo District Court; studied criminal law in Germany; Councillor Justice Dept.; Dir. Penal Bureau same; Police Bureau Home Dept.; Gov.-Gen. Kwantung Govt.; Pres. Nihon Univ.; rec'd deg. 1919. Address: 20, Shinsen, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Asst.-Dir. Kirin District Office, Manchoukuo State Railway; b. Apr. 1886, Saga-ken; s. of Seisai Yamaryo. Career: grad. Kumamoto Higher Tech. Sch. 1909; enetred S.M.R. Co.; studied in Europe & America 1919-21; Chief, Construction Sec., Railway Department 1930; Chief, Construction Dept., Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Railway 1933; Vice-Dir. 1934-35. Address: c/o Kirin District Office, Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Railway, Kirin.

Former Consul; b. May 1888, Kyoto; s. of Tanomu Yamasaki, officer. Career: grad. Com. Coll. Meiji Univ. 1908; resigned from diplomatic service in 1933 after 26 years' service in China, America, Australia and South Africa; Secr. to For. Min. 1921-23; Secretary to Japanese Delegate to Washington Nav. Limit. Conf.; accompanied Prince Iyesato Tokugawa in his tour through Europe and America 1934; Secr. to Japanese Econ.
