Mission to Brazil 1935. Address: 658 Kunitachi Tokyo-shigai.

Consul at Swatow; b. Feb. 1880, Kochi-ken; s. of late Keikichi Yamasaki. Career: grad. Dobun Shoin; Chancellor at Chientao, Newchwang; Consul Tsitsihar, Kalgan, Manchouli, Chefoo. Address: Japanese Consulate, Swatow, China.

M.P.; b. June 1886, Ibaraki-ken; s. of Tadashi Yamasaki. Career: Mayor of Mito; Priv. Secr. to Educ. Minister & Justice Min.; elected M.P. 6 times since 1924; Parl. Vice-Min. of Agr. & For. 1936-37. Address: 307, Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Major-Gen.; Comdr. Inf. 40th Brig. since 1936; b. 1886, Kochi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1907; Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in Germany & Poland; Mil. Attache, Embassy, Austria & Hungary; Comdr. Inf. 3rd Reg.; Chief, Mil. Affairs Sec. War Office; attached to Mil. Arsenal; Chief, Mil. Research Dept. 1935-36. Address: c/o 20th Div. Hdqrs. Keijo, Chosen.

Pres. Yamashita Kisen Kaisha; Hanshin Harbour Co.; b. Apr. 1867, Ehime-ken; s. of Genjiro Yamashita. Career: studied at Meiji Law Sch.; engaged in coal & marine business. Address: 47 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Hitachi Ltd.; b. Apr. 1881, Ehime-ken; s. of Kosaku Yamashita. Career: grad. Engrg. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; entered S. M. R. Co.; Engr. same; sent to Europe & America 3 years; Engr. Imp. Govt. Ry. 1916; Mgr. Oi & Omiya Works; Cheif, Factory Sec. Engrg. Bureau 1925; Dir. 1929. Address: 507 Koyama-cho, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Author; b. Nov. 1876, Miyazaki-ken; 2nd s. of Morinori Yamashita; m. Fumiye. Career: grad. Eng. Polit. Coll., Waseda Univ., 1901; Secr., Revenue Bureau, Finance Dept.; Bible Transportation Reviser; Account Mgr., Rising Sun Petroleum Co., Ltd.; Japanese Accountant, same; Attorney at International Law, Yokohama; founded the Universal Foundation Spirit Assn. of Japan, 1926. Author: "The Way for Our Emperor," "Japanese Spirit and Three Imp. Treasures," "National Foundation Spirit," "Meiji Emperor's Songs, Omiyagokoro," etc. Address: 18, Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Major-Gen.; Dir. Resources Mobilization Bureau War Office since 1935; b. 1886, Aichi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1907; Mil. Staff Coll.; resided in Poland; Staff; Gen. Staff Office; Aide-de-Camp to late Marshal Uehara; Sec. Chief Gen. Staff Office & Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Comdr. Inf. 22nd Reg.; Chief 1st Sec. Mil. Training Dept.; Mil. Attaché Legation Poland. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.

Pres. Peru Assn.; b. Jan. 1882, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kazuyasu Aida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer, Secr. of Legation, at Canton, Spain, France, America and Argentina; Secr. Foreign Office and Agr. & Com. Dept.; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Treaty Bureau; Chief 3rd Sec., Europe & America Bureau; Councillor Emb. U.S.S.R., Brazil; Minister to Argentina. Address: 122 Taishido, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. Chuo Univ.; b. June 1868, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Tokujiro Yamazaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1889; studied econ. in Germany; Prof. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch.; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof. same; resigned 1929; Commr. Imp. Household Dept. 1926-1930. Address: 126 Hara-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

D.L.; Prof., Keio Univ.; b. July 1890, Wakayama City; e. s. of Eijiro Yamazaki, merchant; m. Mutsu, d. of Churyo Morita. Career: grad. Polit. Coll. Keio Univ. 1914; joined Jiji Shimpo-sha 1917; Special Staff, Peace Convention Bureau, Dept. of For. Affairs, 1919; sent to Europe and America for study from Alma Mater 1924; returned 1926; obtained D.L. degree, 19[?]6. Publications: "Outline of Constitutional Law," "Proportional Representation System and Majority Preferential Voting System," "Science of Constitutional Law," etc. Address: 1502 Takagi-cho, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. June 1880, Tokyo; s. of Motoyoshi Yamazaki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1906; apptd. Official and Councillor Taiwan Govt.; Secr. and Councillor Educ. Dept.; Dir. Common Educ. Bureau; Parl. Vice-Minister of Educ.; elected to Diet 6 times; Chairman Polit. Affairs Inquiry Committee Seiyukai; Agr. & Forestry Minister 1934-36; again same 1936-37. Address: 2570 Nishi Sugamo 2-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.
Lieut.-Gen. on the Reserve List. (See 1936 issue).

Pres. Dai-Ichi Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Dir. Niko Co. & Denki Kagaku Co.; b. 1862, Nagano-ken; s. of Yasoki Yanagi. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1889; joined Jiji Shimpo; Mng.-Dir. Maebashi Spinning Works Ltd.; Mgr. Shinmachi Spinning Works 1895; joined Mitsui Bank 1899; Mgr. Shimonoseki, Hiroshima and Nagasaki Branches; Chief, Real Estate Dept. same 1909; established Dai-Ichi Fire & Marine Ins. Co. and became Mng.-Dir. 1917. Address: 37 Honmura-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Adviser Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; b. July 1875, Chiba-ken; adopted s. of Naohei Yanagida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; Councillor, Legislative Bureau 1902; Secr. Imp. Household Dept.; Secr. of Cabinet; Chief Secr. House of Peers 1914. Address: 3272 Kitami, Kinuta-mura, Tokyo-fu.

Mayor of Tsitsihar since 1935; b. 1878, Wutsin-hsien, Chiangsu Prov., China. Career: grad. Lungcheng Coll., Chiangsu Prov.; studied in Japan; Teacher, Fengtien 2nd Higher Sch.; Mgr. Sino-Japanese Cultural Assn.; Prof. North Eastern Univ.; Secr. Fin. Dept. Fengtien Prov.; Secr. Mukden Mun. Office 1932-5. Address: Muni. Office, Tsitsihar.

Minister to Spain; b. 1884, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Attaché, Emb. in England 1914; Foreign Office Secr. 1919; Attaché, 1st Secr. Polit. Affairs Bureau 1920; Mem. 1st League of Nations Assembly; 2nd Legation Secr. China 1921; 1st Emb. Secr. Belgium 1924; Consul-Gen. Canton 1928; Secr., Taiwan Govt.; 1st Leg. Secr. China 1930, Minister to Chile 1933-36. Address: c/o Japanese Legation, Madrid, Spain.
M.P.; b. Jan. 1886, Kagawa-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Meiji Univ.; Police Commr. Kagawa-ken; Chief Kida-gun, Kagawa-ken. Address: 5 Mita Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co.; Pres. 1st Mutual Savings Bank; b. Dec. 1865, Okayama-ken; s. of San-eki Yano. Career: grad. 3rd Higher Sch. 1889; apptd. Physician, Nippon Life Ins. Co.; made inspection tour of Europe and America 1895-97; Commr. Ins. Dept. Agr. & Com. Dept.; Examiner, Statistics Bureau of Cabinet 1900; established 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co. 1902 and 1st Mutual Savings Bank 1922. Address: 126 Denyen-Chofu 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

A.M. (Columbia Univ.); Pres. Hikone Com. Coll.; b. July 1886, Kochi-ken; s. of Seikichiro Yano, businessman. Career: grad. Yamaguchi Com. Coll.; Columbia Univ.; apptd. Prof. Yamaguchi Com. Coll.; Sch. Inspector Educ. Dept. Address: 26 Konki, Hikone, Shiga-ken.

Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Sch. of For. Lang.; b. Sept. 1876, Shimane-ken; s. of Toshi Yasugi. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; studied in Russia; apptd. Prof. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang.; made inspection tour of Russia with late Count Shimpei Goto 1927. Address: 19 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Ex-Minister of Educ.; b. Sept. 1890, Tokyo; s. of Juzo Yasui. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1916; entered Home Dept.; Chief Adm. Sec. Local Affairs Bureau; Secr. to Home Minister; Chief Public Peace Sec. Police Bureau; Gov. Okayama-ken; Chief Labour Sec. Social Bureau; Dir. Local Affairs Bureau 1932-35; Gov. Osaka-fu. Address: 775, Sendagaya 4-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Exploitation Bureau, Overseas Dept.; b. Mar. 1893, Okayama-ken; s. of Takeji Yasui. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1917; Police Chief Hyogo-ken & Fukuoka-ken; Dir. Sanitary & Social Bureaus Tokyo Mun. Office, 1920; Chief Secr. Chosen Govt.; Commr. same 1932; Dir. Monopoly Bureau 1934-36; Gov. Keikido Chosen. Address: Overseas Affairs Dept. Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Yasukawa Electric Works Ltd.; b. June 1886, Fukuoka-ken; s. of late Keiichiro Yasukawa; m. Matsuko, d. of Sadakichi Tsuruhara. Career: grad. Elec. Engrg. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1912; founded present firm 1915. Address: 1052 Nakabaru, Tobata, Fukuoka-ken.

Pres. Oriental Development Co.; b. Apr. 1870, Kyoto-fu; s. of Tarosuke Yasukawa. Career: grad. Osaka Higher Com. Sch. 1889; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr. Kobe, Tientsin and Dairen Branches; Business Mgr. Tokyo Head Office; Mng.-Dir. of same 1918-33; Dir. Mitsui Gomei Kaisha 1932; Pres. Toyo Rayon Co. went to Siam as Chairman Econ. Mission to Siam 1936. Address: 59 Sekiguchi Dai-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

M.P.; b. Dec. 1879; s. of Jinroku Yatsunami, Oita-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1909; Secr. to Communciations Minister 1915; elected to Diet 5 times; Councillor Justice Dept.; Chairman Executive Committee of Minseito; Parl. Vice-Minister of Justice 1932-34. Address: 1 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Dir. Sumitomo Honsha Ltd.; Chairman Sumitomo Bank; Dir. Sumitomo Trust Trust Co., Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co., Osaka North Harbour Co.; Aud. Sumitomo Bldg. Co., Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd.; b. Sept. 1872, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Tadashi Yatsushiro; m. Fumiko, d. of Saiji Amano. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; joined Sumitomo Bank 1905. Address: Kannonbayashi, Sumiyoshi-mura, Hyogo-ken.

Dir. Cultural Works Bureau Foreign Office; b. Mar. 1884, Fukui-ken; s. of Kanshiro Yedo. Career: grad. History Course Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Foreign Office 1918; Vice-Consul Tientsin 1918; San Francisco 1920; Consul Kiukiang 1921; Tsingtao 1922; Liverpool 1927-30; Vancouver 1930-31; Chief 2nd Sec. Cultural Works Bureau 1931-33; Chief 1st Sec. same 1933-35; Cons.-Gen. Hamburg. Address: Gaimusho Tokyo.

Captain; Chief Staff Manchoukuo River Patrol Fleet; b. 1898, Changtu-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Tokyo Mercantile Marine Sch.; Chief, Mil. Tribunal; Vice-Dir. Tungsheng Sec. District Gendarmerie Inst.; Chief River Transport Dept. of Navy; Captain, Gunboat "Kiangching," "Lisui." Address: c/o River Patrol Fleet Hdqrs., Harbin.

Gov. Kirin Prov. of Manchoukuo; b. 1896, Chinchow-hsieng. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined S. M. R. Co. 1926; Mem. Dairen Muni. Assembly 1928; Councillor Fengtien Prov. Office 1931; Mayor of Mukden 1932-35; Gov. Pinkiang Prov. Address: Governor's Residence Kirin.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr.-in-Chief Manchoukuo River Patrol Fleet; b. December 1886, Chichianghsien, Hunan Prov. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Mercantile Marine Sch. 1910; Naval Gunnery Sch. 1911; Capt. Gunboat 'Litsi," "Kiangping," "Li Tsieh," "Kiang Hsiang',; Acting Comdr. River Patrol Fleet 1929; Comdr. 1931; Vice-Admiral, Aug. 1935. Address: River Patrol Fleet Hdqrs., Harbin.

Reserve Major-Gen.; Dir. Mongolian Hall in Hsinking; b. Dec. 1882, Tokuyama City; s. of Eiji Naganishi; later adptd. by Yoda Family. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1904; Mil. Staff Coll. 1015; Chief Staff 4th Div. 1929; Comdr. Inf 38th Brig. 1931; Vice-Minister Hsingan Gen. Adm. Office 1933-34; Dir. Hsingan Coll. 1935-37; Vice-Min. of Mongolia Adm. 1934-37. Address: 362 Chokei-kodo, Higashi Junji-ro, Hsinking.

b. 1884, Akita-ken; s. of Yuki Yokoyama, samurai. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial University 1909; entered Home Dept.; Gov. Hiroshima-ken, Ishikawa-ken; Dir. Police Bureau 1928; Gov. Kyoto-fu 1931; Kanagawa-ken 1932; Tokyo-fu; Metro. Police Chief 1937. Address: 21, Maruyama-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Admiral; Navy Minister since February 1937; b. 1880; Iwate-ken, s. of Ukemasa Yonai. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1901; Captain "Fuso," "Mutsu"; Chief Staff 2nd Fleet; Staff Nav. Gen. Staff Office; Comdr. Chinkai Nav. Port; Comdr.-in-Chief 3rd 1929; Sasebo Nav. Stn. 1933-34; 2nd Fleet 1934-35; Yokosuka Nav. Stn.; Combined Fleet. Address: 28 Takeshita-cho, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Cons. at Hailar since 1933; b. Feb. 1888, Aomori-ken; s. of Kanjo Yonaiyama. Career: grad. Tungwen Coll. Shanghai 1911; sent to Peking as student of Foreign Office; attached Japanese Consulates at Tsinan, Canton; Consul, Hangchow, China 1928. Address: Japanese Consulate, Hailar, Manchoukuo.

Spec. Mem. Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Feb. 1868, Tokyo; s. of Takezo Wada; adopted by Tozaburo Yoneyama. Career: grad. Aoyama Gakuin; studied in America 8 years; joined Nippon Ry. Co.; joined Mitsui Bank; Mgr. Osaka and Yokohama Branches; Mng.-Dir. same 1909; Chairman Mitsui Trust Co.; Pres. Trust Assn.; Pioneer of introducing trust business into Japan. Organizer of Rotary International movement in Japan. Address: 116 Aoyama Minami-cho 6-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Kyodo Trust Co.; b. 1876, Saga-ken; s. of Asakichi Yoshida, farmer. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Commr. Revenue Supt. Office; Chief Customs House; Secr. Home Dept.; Commr. Imp. For. Bureau; Chief Communications Dept. Taiwan Govt. Address: 442 Matsumoto, Sanjo, Seido-mura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

D. Litt.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Feb. 1874, Yamagata-ken; s. of Eijiro Yoshida. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1900; went to Germany and France for study of Ethics; Prof. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. and Tokyo Women's Higher Normal Sch.; attended World Econ. Conf. Belgium. Address: 110 Hakusan Goten-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Chief Bureau of Civil Engineering, Navy Dept.; b. Mar. 1884 in Kyoto. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Dept. Sapporo Agric. Coll.; joined the Navy Dept.; travelled abroad 1928-29. Address: 2324 Midorigaoka, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Amb. to England; b. Sept. 1878; s. of Tsuna Takeuchi, M.P.; later adptd. by Kenzo Yoshida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; 3rd Secr. Emb. Italy; Secr., Chosen Govt.; 2nd Secr. Emb. U. S. A.; attended Peace Conf.; 1st Secr. Emb. England; Cons.-Gen. at Tientsin; at Mukden; Minister to Sweden; Vice-Min. of Foreign Affairs 1928; Amb. to Italy 1930-32. Address: c/o Japanese Emb. London.

Mem. House of Peers; b. 1885, Oita-ken; s. of Kamejiro Yoshida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; Commr. Miye-ken; Secr. Home Dept.; Secr. Meiji Shrine Constr. Bureau; Asst.-Mayor Tokyo; Dir. Shrine Bureau; Social Bureau; Mng.-Dir. Institute for Harmonization of Capital & Labour; Chief Secr. of Cabinet 19[?]4; Dir. Cabinet Investigation Bureau. Address: 1600 Mejiro 2-chome, Toshima-ku, Tokyo.

Physician; M.D.; Mem. Taihokushu Conf.; Mem. Taiwan Central Sanitation Committee; b. 1875, Hyogo-ken; s. of Shigeru Yoshida, physician. Career: grad. Govt. Med. Coll., Okayama 1899; studied Bacteriology in Ishigami Lab. Osaka; Sea-Port Quarantine Physician, Taiwan Govt. 1901; Asst. Prof. Med. Coll. Taiwan 1905; studied in Germany 1907; Prof. 1910; Chief Physician & Vice-Pres. Red Cross Soc. Hospital, Taiwan; rewarded by Taiwan Educ. Soc. 1922; established Yoshida Hospital in Taihoku 1922. Address: Tsukiji-machi, Taihoku.

Director of Japan Sugar Mfg. Co., Japan Iron Works; b. December 187[?], Sakai; s. of Nobuyuki Yoshida. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1894; Adjutant, War Office; Secr. to War Minister; attached, Ordnance Bureau; Sec. Chief, same; Dir. Mil. Heavy Artil. Sch.; Dir. Mil. Ordnance Bureau; went to Europe 1899-1903; Pres. Mil. Arsenal; went to Europe & America 1918; Chief, Mil. Tech. Dept. 1928; Pres. Manchuria Elec. Co. Address: 1248 Shimo-Ochiai 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Former Vice-Gov. Bank of Taiwan; b. May 1883, Ehime-ken; s. of Minoru Yoshida. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; entered Bank of Taiwan; Secr. & Chief, Documents Dept.; Mgr. Osaka Branch. Address: 216 Kago-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr. 2nd Sqn.; b. Feb. 1885, Saga-ken; adopted s. of Yujiro Yoshida. Career: grad. Nav. Acad. 1904; Staff 3rd Sqn.; Instructor Torpedo Sch.; Staff Training Sqn.; Chief, 2nd Sec., Educ. Bureau of Navy; Captain 'Hirato"; Gen. Staff Maizuru Nav. Port; Chief 1st Sec. Tactical Affairs Bureau; Captain "Kongo" & "Mutsu"; Staff Combined Fleet; Chief Staff 1st Sqn.; Dir. Tactical Affairs Bureau 1933-35; Commdr. Training Sqn. Address: 397 Kakinoki-zaka, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Pres. Fuji Elec. Co.; Repr. Dir., Furukawa Mining Co., Furukawa Forestry Co.; Furukawa Coal Mining Co.; b. March 1886, Tokyo; s. of Shobei Kimura; later adopted by Yoshimura family. Career: grad. Keio Univ. 1908; studied in Halle & Berlin Univs.; Vice-Pres. Furukawa Mining Co. Address: 44 Takanawa Minami-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo.

Min. Com. & Ind. Dept.; b. Sept. 1888, Miyagi-ken; s. of Toshizo Yoshino. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; entered Agr. & Com. Dept.; Secr. same; Secr. to Min. of Agr. & Com.; Com. & Ind. Dept. 1925; Chief, Documents & Statistics Bureaus; Dir. Industrial Bureau 1928; Vice-Minister of Com. & Ind; Pres. Tohoku Kogyo K.K. Address: 54 Kamiyama, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo.

Non-Commissioned Officer; Nippon Camphor Co.; b. May 1878, Ibaraki-ken; s. of E. Yoshioka, educator; m. Seiko, sister-in-law of Shunji Miyao, 1908. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Resident Official in London 1912; Gov. Tainan-shu, Taiwan; Chief, Monopoly Bureau, Taiwan Govt.; Gov. Taihoku-shu. Address: 990 Naka-Meguro 3-chome, Meguro-ku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral (reserve); Dir. & Chief of Shipyard, Kawasaki Dockyard Co., Ltd.; b. Feb. 1880, Tottori-ken. Career: grad. Naval Engrg. Sch. 1903; despatched to England to bring home H.M.S. "Kongo" 1911; served World War; resided in England to inspect naval affairs 1917-18; Chief Engineer, 1st Torpedo Flotilla; same, 3rd Squadron; Chief, 2nd, Sec., Engrg. Bureau of Navy; Chief Engr. Training Sqdrn.; Chief, Tech. Dept. Yokosuka Nav. Station; Chief, Gen. Affairs, Sec. Naval Tech. Dept.; Dir. Sasebo Nav. Arsenal; Dir. Nav. Fuel Depot. Address: 151 Rikyu-mae, Suma, Kobe.

Mng.-Dir. Kogyo Koshi since 1934; Councillor, Oriental Development Co.; b. Mar. 1889, Wakayama-ken; s. of Matsunosuke Asai, merchant, later adopted by Ginji Yoshioka; m. Mitsue, niece of Kenkichi Sakaeda. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imperial Univ. 1917; joined Fujita-gumi and served at Kosaka Mines; entered Oriental Development Co., serving at its General Affairs Dept., Keijo and Moppo Branches; Asst.-Mgr. Keijo Branch; Mgr. Fusan Br.; Chief Work Dept.; Mgr. Shariin and Heijo Br.; besides served as Special Mem. of several local agr. assns. in Korea; Auditor, Totaku Mining Co. and Chosen Fertilizer Co., etc. Address: 64 Hanazono-cho, Dairen.

Mem. House of Peers; b. Jan. 1874, Niigata-ken; s. of Joryo Yoshizawa, banker. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1899; apptd. Attaché, Foreign Office; Dir. Polit. Affairs Bureau; same, Asia Bureau; 1st Secr. Emb. in England; Min. to China; Amb. to France; Foreign Minister in Inukai Cabinet; nominated Peer 1932. Address: 22 Kasumi-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

D. Sc.; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. Nat. Research Council; b. Apr. 1874, Yamagata-ken; s. of Masaki Yosie. Career: grad. Maths. Course Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1897; Prof. Sc. Coll. of Alma Mater 1909-35; studied in Germany 1899; Commr. Crown Prince's study 1898. Address: 1991 Kitizyôzi, Tôkyô-hu.

Newspaper Management; b. July 1903, Rushville, Ill., U.S.A.; s. of James H. Young, banker; m. Marjorie Willis. Career: Student Univ. of Ill. and Johns Hopkins Univ.; Priv. Secr. late E. W. Scripps of Scripps-Howard Newspapers; United Press Assn. New York 1926-27; since 1928 in Japan; Mgr. Japan Advertiser and Tokyo Corr. for Hearst's Int'l and Universal News services. Address: 2 Hiroo-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

C.B.; Secr. Chinese Embassy at Tokyo; b. July 1891, Hopei Prov.; n. Chinese; s. of T. T Young. Career: studied at Law Course, Pei-Yang Univ. Tientsin; grad. Com. Dept. Meiji Univ. Tokyo; apptd. Prof. Tientsin Law Coll.; passed Diplomatic Exam. 1921; diplomatic service in Tokyo since 1924. Address: Chinese Emb. Azabu, Tokyo.

Dir. Harbin Customs since 1932; b. 1888, Tahsing-hsien, Hopei Prov. Career: grad. Chinese Eastern Ry. Russian Language Sch.; entered Harbin Customs; Chief, Manchouli Branch Customs. Address: Customs House, Harbin.

Magistrate, Poli-hsien, Sankiang Prov.; b. Sept. 1895, Wuchang-hsien, Kirin Prov.; s. of late Yu Sung-sheng. Career: grad. Peiping Higher Educ. Training Inst.; Secr., Educ. Dept., Kirin Prov.; Educ. Inspector, Wuchang-hsien, Kirin; Mem. Nat. Repr. Conf., Kirin Prov.; Commr. Supply Dept. Chinese Eastern Ry. (North Manchuria Ry.); Secr. Kirin Bandit Suppression Hdqrs. Address: 10 Nan-kang-fang-yin-kai, Harbin.

Field-Marshall; Manchoukuo Minister of Public Peace; b. 1882, Taian-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: Comdr. Garrison Army 1932-35; Defense Min. 1935-37. Address: Dept. of Pub. Peace Hsinking.

Chief Central Hdqrs. Manchoukuo Concordia Assn.; b. 1898, Liaoyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Swiss Mil. Acad.; Prof. North Eastern Univ.; Staff Tungsheng Ry. Guards Corps Hdqrs.; Councillor Tungsheng Spec. Dist. Gov.'s Office; Chief Fengtien Self-Govt. Training Inst.; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Hsieh Ho Hui 1932; Councillor Emb. Tokyo. 1933-37. Address: c/o Kyowakai, Hsinking.

Commr. Polit. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Foreign Office; b. September 1889, Kiangsu Prov., China; s. of Yu Jung-kao, official. Career: grad. Chuo Univ. Tokyo; Chief, Foreign Affairs Commissioner's Office, Tsitsihar; Chief, Dairen Office, Dept. of Foreign Affairs; sent to Tehhua. Address: Dept. of Foreign Affairs, Hsinking.

General; Gov. Sankiang Prov.; Comdr. 4th District Army; b. 1878, Kirin Province. Career: Comdr. 10th Brig. Kirin 1922; Comdr. Manchoukuo Ambassador to Tokyo; b. 1894, Tiehling-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. South Manchuria Med. Coll. 1919; studied in Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1921; Pres. Mukden Hospital 1923; Commr. Chief, Harbin Revenue Supt. Office; b. 1894. Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Shenyang Higher Normal Sch.; Chief, Elec. Light Office Changchun; Chief, Revenue Supt. Office, Harbin. Address: c/o Rev. Supt. Office Harbin.

Manchoukuo Lord Keeper of Privy Seal; b. 1870, Liaoyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: Dir. Grand Keeper of Imp. Seals; b. Feb. 1874, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Koan Yuasa, doctor. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1898; Councillor Shiga-ken & Hyogo-ken; Chief, Police Dept. Vice-Governor Pinkiang Prov., Manchoukuo; b. 1894, Yamagata-ken; s. of Tamijiro Yuki, farmer; m. Sonoko. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined S. M. R. Co.; Chief Gen. Affairs Bureau Manchoukuo Supervisory Council; Capital Constr. Bureau. Address: Pinkiang Prov. Office, Harbin.

Gov. Bank of Japan; Mem. House of Peers; b. May 1877, Yamagata-ken; s. of Yaemon Yuki. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1903; joined Bank of Japan; served at London; Mng.-Dir. Major-Gen.; Attached to Mil. Horse Supply Dept since 1935; b. 1883, Miyagi-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Academy 1905; Instructor, Mil. Cavarly Sch.; Comdr. Cav. 14th Reg.; Chief, Sanbongi Branch, Mil. Horse Supply Dept. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.
